title: A tap in the step files a verdict, because the click lands after the card is back
description:
Frank, on his phone: "when we're in the state screen, the buttons are still
getting clicks. I've had several Falses when I was tapping to go back."

The buttons are NOT on screen at depth. renderStep() is the whole page and
renderCard(), which owns the three answers, is not drawn. So this is not a
chrome defect and chromeAt() is right.

It is the synthesized click. One touch produces touchend AND a click. The tap
is handled at touchend, render() runs synchronously inside it, clear(v.root)
removes every child the touch began on, and the card comes back with
.swipe-answers near the bottom because the dock carries margin-top: auto. THEN
the browser dispatches the click, which hit-tests the page as it is now and
lands on a button that did not exist when the thumb went down. SWIPES is
["right", "left", "down"], so false is the MIDDLE column of a 3-column grid,
which is where a thumb tapping the lower middle of a model screen lands.

tla-7xql.18 introduced it. Before the step was the whole page the dock stayed
on screen under the step, so nothing moved under the thumb and the ghost click
landed on what it started on.

isControl(ev.target) does not catch it. That reads the touch's own target, and
the touch began on the model, not on a button.

Files: swipe/reader/swipe.js, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh, swipe/README.md

RED: INVARIANT: a click whose touch began on an element the render removed is
dropped before it reaches a control. clickIsTail(null) is false,
clickIsTail({isConnected: true}) is false, clickIsTail({isConnected: false}) is
true. The click listener is bound on root in the CAPTURE phase and calls both
preventDefault and stopPropagation, so a ghost on <a class="swipe-link"> cannot
navigate either. The arm is set in touchend only on the paths that call
gesture(), which means after the flash guard and after the isControl guard, and
it is cleared in touchstart so a deliberate press can never be eaten.
close_reason: Merged at 4ff0480, worker commit 110e2c6. Frank: tapping to go back out of a model filed several Falses. The buttons were never on screen: renderStep() is the whole page since tla-7xql.18 and renderCard() is not drawn in that branch, so chromeAt() was right and needed no change. One touch produces a touchend AND a synthesized click. The tap is handled at touchend, render() runs inside that handler, clear() removes every child the touch began on, and the card comes back with .swipe-answers near the bottom edge because .swipe-card carries margin-top auto. Only then does the browser dispatch the click, which hit-tests the page as it stands now and lands on a button that did not exist when the thumb went down. SWIPES is right,left,down over a 3-column grid, so false is the MIDDLE column, which is where a thumb tapping the lower middle of a model comes down. That the symptom was Falses rather than a scatter is the corroboration. isControl() cannot catch it: it reads the touch's own target, and a touch sequence keeps one target throughout where the synthesized click does not. tla-7xql.18 introduced it, since before the step was the whole page the dock stayed on screen underneath and nothing moved under the thumb. Rule: clickIsTail(arm) is Boolean(arm) and arm.isConnected === false, where arm is the element the touch began on, held only when that touch filed a gesture, cleared in touchstart. No window, no timer, no timestamp, because a deliberate press begins with a touchstart. The swallow is a capture-phase listener on root calling preventDefault for menuLink's anchor and stopPropagation for every button. Both touch listeners stay passive: central rejected dropping passive to preventDefault the click at source, because that rests on the browser honoring a cancel and no gate on this box can drive it. WORKER CAUGHT ITS OWN CHECK PASSING GREEN UNDER THE FIRST MUTATION: the Part 5 awk range terminated on the listener's own closing line, so deleting the capture argument deleted the terminator and the range ran to end of file. It ends on bindGestures()'s closing brace now. Worker also found harness/test-spelling.sh has no 'cancelling' entry and slipped two British forms past a green run, corrected by hand; the -ing siblings of the -lled pairs are worth a pass. Verified: reader gate 292/0 up 6 from 286, --static 290 with 1 skipped, eight worker mutations each red on the check it covers, plus central's own independent mutation of the capture argument. Registry 49/49 in 1099.6s. pipefail 25, spelling 20, lint clean over 146.

title: A drag on the model files a verdict, because the decline reads where you started
description:
Files: swipe/reader/swipe.js, swipe/reader/swipe.css, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh, swipe/README.md

RED: INVARIANT: a drag anywhere inside .swipe-screen that moves the model's own scroll position files no verdict, and a drag that moves nothing is still a gesture.

## Frank, 2026-10-19

"Scrolling up and down in the model is being read as a navigation swipe."

Down files "not a claim". So this writes wrong verdicts into his record, which
is the same defect class as tla-7xql.16 and the third time this epic.

## Measured, Chrome at 390 wide with innerHeight 730

730 is what a real phone gives at 844 with its URL bar showing, and it is the
height Frank's screenshots show. Geometry of the step view, model step open:

    .swipe-step          10-720
      .swipe-step-head   29-81     LIVE
      gap                81-93     LIVE
      .swipe-screen      93-669
        .swipe-screen-head  94-138 LIVE   <- THE MODEL'S OWN NAME
        gap                138-153 LIVE
        .swipe-screen-body 153-653 declined, but only when it overflows sideways
        bottom padding     653-669 LIVE
      gap                669-681   LIVE
      .swipe-hint        681-701   LIVE
      tail               701-720   LIVE

220 of 730 pixels take a gesture, which is 30% of the view. 143 of them sit on
or immediately around the model box, so they LOOK like the model. A thumb that
lands on the model's name and drags down files "not a claim".

## The root cause, which is architectural rather than a bad number

`scrollerDeclining()` decides from WHERE THE TOUCH STARTS. The regions that
look like the model are not the scroller, so a region test can never cover
them. It also tests the wrong thing on the right region: it asks whether the
box COULD overflow on one axis, not whether the drag actually moved anything.

Second measurement, same height. Four screens scroll vertically at a 500 px
body: 1:Ledger, 2:Contention, 1:Shelves, 1:Break. One of them, 2:Contention,
fits sideways and so is not declined at all, which means a vertical drag there
scrolls the model AND navigates in one stroke.

At 844 that count is one screen and no conflict, which is why the gate in
tla-7xql.19 reads green. The gate pins the 844 case only.

## The fix, in two parts, and both are needed

**P1. Decline the whole `.swipe-screen` box, not just its body.** Nothing that
looks like the model is a gesture surface. That removes the name row, both
gaps inside the box and the bottom padding.

**P2. Test what MOVED, not what could overflow.** Record the scroller's
`scrollTop` and `scrollLeft` at touchstart and compare them at touchend. If
either changed, the reader scrolled and no verdict is filed. If neither
changed, it is a gesture.

P2 is the same delegation the flash already relies on, where the browser
raises a click after a tap and suppresses it after a scroll. The comment in
`scrollerDeclining()` says so: "The discrimination is the browser's rather
than this file's." Extend that reasoning rather than inventing a rule.

P2 also preserves D4 of tla-7xql.18, that a swipe right at the model step
still files true with no button on screen. A model with nothing to scroll
sideways keeps its horizontal gestures, and one with nothing to scroll down
keeps its vertical ones. The region test cannot do that: it kills both axes
whenever either one could move.

## Why the listeners allow this

The touch listeners are `{ passive: true }` and must stay that way. Passive
means this file cannot cancel the browser's scroll, which is correct: the
browser should scroll. All this bead decides is whether to ALSO fire a
gesture, and a scroll-position delta answers that after the fact with no
guessing.

## The gate

`harness/test-swipe-reader.sh`, split `--static` (3.0 s) and full (22.0 s).
Both budgets stay.

The decline table in part 6 drives `scrollerDeclining()` through fake
scrollers. It needs to become a table over (start element, scroll delta)
rather than over (start element, overflow). Keep every existing row's
intent and say in a comment which rows changed meaning and why.

ADD THE TWO CASES THIS BEAD EXISTS FOR:
  - a drag starting on the model's name row files nothing
  - a drag inside the body that moved the scroll position files nothing,
    and one that moved nothing still files

AND ADD THE SHORT VIEWPORT. The gate's screen scan pins 844. Pin 730 as well,
with the four screens that scroll vertically there named, so the next person
to change the type size sees both heights.

Watch every new assertion FAIL first.

## Do not change

The gesture table, meaning what each gesture does. `chromeAt()`.
`answersLive()`. `cardHint()`. `{ passive: true }` on the listeners.
`harness/Gate.tla` and `harness/verdict.sh` are centrally owned. `docs/` is
generated from `module-docs/`. `puzzles/` is v1. No payload field changes.

## Ordering

tla-7xql.20 is in flight on the same four files. This bead starts from
whatever .20 lands, not from 271b7c2.
close_reason: Merged at f665b11, worker commit c19ab88 plus central's 13bd2db. Frank: scrolling in the model was read as a navigation swipe, and down files not-a-claim, so this wrote wrong verdicts. Cause was architectural: the decline read WHERE THE TOUCH STARTED, and at innerHeight 730 (a real phone at 844 with its URL bar) 220 of those pixels took a gesture, 143 of them on or around the model box including the model's own name row. The gate pinned 844 only, which is why this shipped green. It pins 730 now with the four vertically-scrolling screens named. Fix is two rules: a region rule for inside .swipe-screen and outside its body, dead whatever the thumb does, because the name row fits its own content so every measurement of it answers 'nothing moves' and files. Then per-axis capacity for a swipe and a scroll-position delta for a tap: var takesIt = axis ? overflowsOn(at.el, axis) : movedFrom(at). Central specified delta for everything and that was wrong, because at a scroll limit nothing moves and the stroke files, which the bottom of 1:Shelves reaches. A tap has no limit case, so movement is honest there and capacity is honest for a swipe. tla-7xql.18's flaw was the BOX, not the capacity. Also: the +1 tolerance removed on the worker's asymmetry argument, and a tap that moved nothing now steps back on all 24 screens. CENTRAL CAUGHT TWO '| head -1' PIPES in the new ordering check, the exact pipefail hazard, inside the one check pinning this bead's defect; fixed with parameter expansion and verified by mutation rather than by the green run. Verified: 286/0 in 13.6s against 22.0, 284/1 in 1.5s against 3.0, up 37 from 249, spelling 20, pipefail 25, lint clean over 146, swipe.js parses, footprint exactly the four declared files. Registry 49/49 in 1161.6s with zero failures.

title: The recall rung cannot be worked: the only way to read a prompt is to read its answer
description:
The recall rung has no way to work a session, and the only route into it
shows you the answer before you try.

MEASURED on the DELIVERED tree at ~/tla-practice/recall on 2026-10-16, after
tla-1sh7.10 landed and the channel was delivered.

The only invocation is `recall/recall.sh [OPTIONS] <rep-id> <answer>`, and
--help names no mode that serves a rep. So working a rep means:

  1. open REPS.tsv
  2. read a prompt
  3. note its id
  4. run the command with that id and your answer

Step 2 and step 3 happen on the same tab-delimited LINE as field 6, the
canonical answer:

  R001 | for each track, the wagons standing on it, with the per-track lookup
         given a name of its own rather than written out twice
       | LET Occupants(t) == {w \in Wagons : Parking[w] = t} IN
         [t \in Tracks |-> Occupants(t)]

So the only way to find out what a rep asks is to read the answer to it.

THIS IS TWO FAILURES, AND THE SECOND IS WORSE.

It is unusable at flow speed, which was the whole complaint that started this
epic: "When you're drilling multiplication tables, you should never be
stopping for 10 minutes to figure out 8 * 7. You do a thing, check, move on."
Opening a TSV, scanning for a row and retyping an id is not that.

And it defeats the rung. Retrieval practice needs an attempt before the
answer. Exposure without one buys very little durability, which is the
finding the whole corpus is built on and which drill/study/CLAUDE.md cites.
A rung where reading the question hands over the answer is the lookup this
corpus exists to replace.

WHAT IT NEEDS. A session loop. Serve a rep: print the prompt and nothing
else, read the answer from stdin, grade it, show the feedback block that
already exists, move on. Several reps in a row without retyping anything.

Points to settle, each with a reason to think about rather than a default to
take:

- WHICH REP COMES NEXT. Random is the cheap answer and it is probably wrong:
  tla-1sh7.2 wrote several differently-phrased reps per construct precisely
  so the fact gets retrieved rather than the sentence, and interleaving is
  measurably stronger when consecutive items are SIMILAR. So drawing within
  a construct, or within a family, likely beats drawing uniformly. Read what
  the epic tla-1sh7 records about interleaving before choosing.
- WHETHER PROGRESS IS KEPT. The drill channel has PROGRESS.tsv and
  LAST-SERVED. If recall grows one, it becomes the first learner-owned file
  in a channel whose delivery is always-overwrite by design, and
  scripts/deliver-recall.sh says in its own header that no file here is
  learner-owned. That claim would stop being true and the delivery has to
  change with it. Say which you chose and fix the header if you add state.
- HOW A SESSION ENDS. A count, a clean exit on EOF, or both.

WHAT NOT TO DO. Do not add a mode that prints the rep table. That is the
leak wearing a flag.

RED: INVARIANT: a session mode prints a rep's prompt without its canonical answer being reachable from anything the session prints or from any file the session tells the reader to open, grades what is typed on stdin, and serves a further rep without the reader naming an id.

Files: recall/recall.sh, recall/README.md, harness/test-recall-runner.sh, harness/fixtures/recall/
close_reason: Merged at 490ca33 (worker commits f9af055 and 890393c) and DELIVERED. Central verified the acceptance test in a tree holding only what the delivery names with no repo above it: two reps, each prompt printed WITHOUT its answer, answers read from stdin, exit 0, tree byte-identical after. Then ran a real session in ~/tla-practice/recall after delivering. THE P0 IS CLOSED: before this the only invocation took a rep id and an answer together, so learning what a rep asked meant opening REPS.tsv where field 5 shares a line with the canonical in field 6. REP ORDER IS MEASURED, NOT RANDOM: the next rep comes from a construct within two positions and never the same construct, because two phrasings of one construct back to back is lag 0 where the second is recognition. Position means file order and that was measured: 120 reps, 37 constructs, four unbroken family runs, 33 of 36 adjacent construct pairs sharing a family, which is why the walk needs no INVENTORY.md in a delivered tree. PROGRESS IS NOT KEPT, keeping deliver-recall.sh's always-overwrite justification true rather than quietly falsifying it, and the worker gated the session's half of that claim. IT ADOPTED tla-vo5l's FIX RATHER THAN SHIPPING ITS OWN: its red run hit the same mutate() defect, it found commit 8ccd384 naming this very file as follow-up, dropped its own sentinel-file fix and took that mechanism. THAT CLOSES tla-w91v. Two of its own assertions were wrong and it watched them being wrong, one having passed -- to grep as the pattern. 170 to 233 assertions, 36 FAILs watched first, piped and interactive transcripts byte-identical under script(1), a session rep at 328 ms against 310 ms alone.

title: Fix the hint one-shot: inject hint.md and flip the tiebreak
description:
Repair the hint one-shot. This is the defect that cost Frank the hour on
2026-10-16 and it is independent of the recall rung, so it lands first.

WHAT HAPPENED. Frank ran ./drill --hint with this text: "I'm confident that it
involves setting up a function from tracks to sets of wagons, but I'm fuzzy on
creating functions this way, please give a high level description of how this
is done in general, not this specific application." He got a rung of the
ladder and the sentence "Explaining the general syntax would do the item's work
for you."

TWO CAUSES, both fixable here.

1. The worked cases are unreachable. drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md
   carries the mechanism-versus-content classification with worked examples and
   the tiebreak. The one-shot runs claude -p --tools "" so it has no file
   access, and drill/drill.sh injects STYLE.md into the style prompt but never
   injects hint.md. The model classified on the four-sentence summary in
   drill/study/CLAUDE.md with no examples and no stated tiebreak.

   FIX: inject hint.md into the hint prompt the way STYLE.md already goes into
   the style prompt. drill/drill.sh around line 205 documents that injection
   and the code that does it is the model to copy.

2. The tiebreak is wrong for this corpus. hint.md reads "When you can't tell
   which kind you're looking at, treat it as the item's content and ladder it."
   The corpus is indexed by construct, so the construct Frank is fuzzy on is
   why he is stuck, which puts nearly every real hint question in the
   ambiguous band. The conservative default therefore fires almost always and
   bills an hour each time.

   FIX: flip it. An unclassifiable question gets the mechanism answered flat.
   Keep the ladder for what his rule should assert. Say in the file that this
   is sound here because the sheet makes syntax free (sibling bead), and that
   it would want revisiting if this corpus ever had readers other than Frank,
   which is tla-byyo.

   The prohibition in drill/study/CLAUDE.md on naming the construct that is
   MISSING from his rule is untouched. This is about notation he needs to run
   the model at all.

HAZARD. drill/study/CLAUDE.md and the two command files are DELIVERED to
~/Study/tla-drills/ by scripts/deliver-drill.sh. Editing the repo copy does not
reach Frank. Three waves merged on 2026-10-15 without re-delivering and none of
it reached him. Re-deliver and verify, and NEVER touch ~/tla-practice or
~/Study without a verified backup first: a guessed manifest deleted 39
delivered files on 2026-10-02.

RED: Given a --hint invocation, When drill.sh builds the prompt, Then the prompt carries the full text of drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md, the same way a --style invocation carries STYLE.md.

Files: drill/drill.sh, drill/study/CLAUDE.md, drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md, harness/test-drill-runner.sh
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the merge commit is 321fec4, not 0e4d1e4. Worker commit 91f7123 is right. 0e4d1e4 names nothing in this repo and was written from nothing rather than read from git log.
close_reason: Merged at 0e4d1e4 (merge of worktree-agent-a8256fe49e7fdb352, worker commit 91f7123). drill.sh now cats hint.md into a hint prompt at the four sites the STYLE.md injection uses, gate decided before the checker so a missing sheet never spends a TLC run, hint-only. Tiebreak flipped to flat at hint.md:73 and stated in CLAUDE.md:170. The construct-naming prohibition is untouched: the CLAUDE.md diff is one hunk at 166 and that section is not in it. RED watched: 12 rows failed against the unmodified runner, including a sheetless hint that exited 0 and spent the checker. GREEN 378 assertions, re-run by central. Four worker findings filed: tla-x0he (check.md has the same defect), tla-vo5l (mutate cannot fail the suite), tla-dhsu (prompt cost), tla-7s2l (delivery outstanding). Stale assertion label fixed inline in test-deliver-drill.sh.

title: CI is red again: --changed-only reports CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN wherever it cannot resolve the jar
description:
CI IS RED ON main AT 3471c9f. Central caused it and verified narrower than CI
runs, for the second time in one session.

  gh run view 38346111046 --log-failed
    FAIL  --changed-only: rc 0 on the first run — rc=99, want 0
    FAIL  --changed-only: rc 0 on the second run — rc=99, want 0
    FAIL  real tree, changed-only at -P8: drill-gate.sh returned rc=99 over drill/
    test-drill.sh: 131 passed, 9 failed
    FAILED: 1 of 26 suite(s) in 407.0s

Every --changed-only assertion returns 99, CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN. All nine pass
locally. The difference is the toolchain layout, which --changed-only reads by
construction, so this could not have been caught by running scripts/test on
the author's box.

TWO DEFECTS. The second is the one that matters.

D1 resolve_jar READS ONE WRAPPER SHAPE AND TWO EXIST.

harness/drill-gate.sh:554 resolves the jar by parsing a JAR= line out of the
`tlc` wrapper:

  v="$(awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*JAR=/ { sub(/^[^=]*=/, "", $0); print; exit }' "$w")"
  [ -n "$v" ] || return 1

scripts/setup writes a wrapper that has one. THE CI WORKFLOW WRITES ITS OWN
WRAPPER INLINE AND DOES NOT (.github/workflows/verify-puzzles.yml:130-132):

  exec java -XX:+UseParallelGC -cp "$HOME/lib/tla2tools.jar" tlc2.TLC "$@"

$HOME is already expanded there, because the heredoc is unquoted <<EOF. So
resolve_jar returns 1 on every CI run.

Parse the -cp argument too. Keep the JAR= path, since the local wrapper uses
it, and read both rather than replacing one with the other. Do NOT hardcode a
path: the comment above resolve_jar explains why, and it is right.

D2 FAILING TO RESOLVE THE JAR EMITS UNCHECKED, WHICH ESCALATES TO rc 99.

harness/drill-gate.sh:1251-1253. The intent is sound and the gate's own
comment states it: caching against an unknown build is the one failure this
cache must not have. The IMPLEMENTATION conflates two different things.

  "I cannot cache safely"  ->  run every job, cache nothing, say so, exit 0
                               if every job verified
  "I could not check"      ->  rc 99

NOT CACHING IS NOT A FAILURE TO CHECK. On a CI run every job ran and every
recorded rc reproduced. The gate did exactly what it was asked and then
reported CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN, which is false.

So the correct behavior when the jar will not resolve: run every job, write no
state file, print a line saying the cache is off and why, and let the run's
own findings decide the exit code. That is a non-escalating report. The gate
already has the vocabulary for this distinction, `declared` at :345, for a
check it categorically cannot run as against one that failed today.

D1 alone would make CI green and leave a landmine: the next box with a
different wrapper turns --changed-only into a hard failure again. Fix both.

CONTROLS. Watch each fail before believing it.

  A wrapper carrying only a -cp path, no JAR= line, resolves. Build the
  fixture from the CI workflow's exact line.
  A wrapper that resolves to nothing declines to cache, says so, and the run
  still exits 0 over a clean corpus.
  A wrapper that resolves to a MISSING file does the same.
  The resolved jar still enters the key, so a different jar invalidates.

Files: harness/drill-gate.sh, harness/test-drill.sh

RED: GIVEN a `tlc` wrapper of the CI workflow's shape, with the jar in -cp and
no JAR= line, WHEN harness/drill-gate.sh --changed-only runs over a clean
corpus THEN it exits 0 and caches. GIVEN a wrapper naming no resolvable jar
THEN it exits 0, caches nothing, and says the cache is off. A cache that
reports CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN because it could not cache is the defect; one that
caches against an unknown build is the worse fix.
close_reason: Landed in c315101. Two defects fixed. D1: resolve_jar at harness/drill-gate.sh:585-621 now reads both wrapper shapes, JAR= first then -cp/-classpath, in pure bash with no awk fork. The order is measured, not assumed: a -cp-first pass reads the local wrapper's '-cp "$JAR"' as a literal path and declines. D2: a failed resolution calls declared rather than unchecked at :1316-1318, so it does not escalate, plus an epilogue block saying no cache was consulted and why. Central verified all three cases independently against a CI-shaped wrapper built from .github/workflows/verify-puzzles.yml:132 with the jar in -cp and no JAR= line: cold 5 jobs verified rc 0, warm 5 from cache rc 0, and an unresolvable wrapper giving 1 declared, 0 findings, 0 unchecked, VERDICT OK, rc 0, with no state file written. The local shape still returns a byte-identical JAR_PATH, proven by 236 of 236 jobs reading back from a state file the old code wrote. 25 new assertions in part 2e, watched red at 147 passed 11 failed before the fix and 158 passed 0 failed after. Control 4 is the one that keeps the cache sound: a jar with one byte appended changes the key and the jobs re-run as stale. Gates: bash scripts/cibuild --skip-docs green through phases 1, 2, 3 at 26 suites in 288.8s, 3b, and 5 at 107 passed, ending OK: cibuild passed. Fork budget still 168 against a ceiling of 300.

title: CI is red: the drill gate admits a skip the indeterminate census cannot see, and exits 0 on one it should
description:
CI IS RED ON main RIGHT NOW. Central caused it and did not catch it.

  gh run list --branch main
    808d806  CI  success
    807fe9a  CI  failure

807fe9a is tla-0eis.2. Central verified it with harness/test-drill.sh,
scripts/lint and harness/test-pipefail.sh, and SKIPPED the full scripts/test
because another worker was taking timed measurements and central did not want
the CPU contention. That trade is what shipped the red. The full suite was the
one gate that would have caught it.

THE FAILURE. harness/test-indeterminate.sh part 2 is a census: every
harness/*.sh that is not a test suite gets its comment-stripped source scanned
for SKIP_VOCAB, and an instrument that can admit a skip and is not driven by a
row of that suite FAILS.

  FAIL  UNREGISTERED instrument(s) can admit a skip
  harness/drill-gate.sh
          1924:  echo "A CACHED JOB IS VERIFIED, not skipped: same TLC build, ...

That is the ONLY line in drill-gate.sh that matches, confirmed with the
suite's own ERE against the file. So the census currently reaches the gate
through a sentence that DENIES a skip, which is a false positive.

AND THE FALSE POSITIVE IS HIDING A TRUE ONE. Do not just reword it.
drill-gate.sh has four real non-run paths and the vocabulary misses all four:

  the EXTENDS-helper SKIP line        "SKIP" is not "skipped"
  UNCHECKED                           "cannot run" is not "could not run"
  DECLARED                            categorically cannot run, says neither
  --static-only                       "no TLC ran", "NOT CHECKED HERE"

--static-only IS THE SERIOUS ONE. It exits 0 while stating it reproduced none
of 237 recorded rcs. A success code carrying a skip admission is the exact
property part 3 exists to forbid. It passes today only because its wording
dodges nine fixed English phrases, which is hole C in that file's own header.

harness/reading-gate.sh has the same gap, and its author already acted on it:
it REWORDED its skip messages to "the check was not run" so the census can
see it, rather than dodging. That is the right instinct and it is why the
census now names two instruments instead of one.

WHAT TO DO. Three things, and the second is the one with judgment in it.

1 REGISTER BOTH GATES in harness/test-indeterminate.sh. Add them to
  REGISTERED at :203 and add driving rows. Read :193-230 for the registry and
  :735-760 for part 6's counter check, which obliges EVERY registered
  instrument to have at least one row that did NOT return success. A
  registered instrument with only passing rows fails as "registered and never
  exercised".

  The cheap honest non-pass rows already exist in both gates: --no-tlc over a
  real or fixture tree returns 99, CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN, which IS the skip path.
  Follow the run_row idiom at :578-584. Keep the rows cheap: that suite's
  budget is 7.4s and it is already the tightest thing near the tier boundary.

2 MAKE --static-only's ADMISSION VISIBLE AND WAIVED. Two halves, both needed.

  Reword its block so SKIP_VOCAB reaches it. The vocabulary is at :175.

  AND name the waiving flag IN PARENTHESES so the parenthetical rule marks
  the skip as voluntary. WAIVED_VOCAB at :176 is

  correctly, because an unwaived admission on a success code is the defect.

  This is the existing convention applied rather than a new one invented. Read
  the PARENTHETICAL RULE in that file's header before you write the wording.

  Then fix the :1924 false positive, by rewording so the sentence does not
  carry a SKIP_VOCAB phrase while denying a skip.

  1c and part 3 drive TLC's model checker, which is that file's stated

title: The load vector is retired and its gates still run
description:
Frank ruled on 2026-09-05 that difficulty is one 1-to-5 scale assigned after a problem exists, and retired the load vector. Commit 9e94239 (2026-09-05 20:10) closed 54 beads unfixed and its message names "the load vector" among them. PRACTICE-PLAN.md:166 lists "The load vector and the ramp rule" under What is retired. Epic tla-h2cg, which built them, closed at that same moment (2026-09-06T03:10Z).

The retirement was never carried out in the harness.

EVIDENCE
- scripts/test:196 runs harness/test-vector.sh on every full gate.
- scripts/test:201 runs harness/test-sequence.sh on every full gate.
- 13 VECTOR.md records sit under authoring/ and pilot/, last written 2026-09-05.

- git log --since=2026-09-05 over harness/sequence.sh, harness/test-vector.sh, harness/test-sequence.sh and authoring/VECTOR-FLOOR.md returns nothing. Not one commit since the ruling.
- The load vector is written down in V2-PLAN.md section 2.5, by tla-h2cg.1, and V2-PLAN.md is superseded history.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The gate is green and looks authoritative. It is green because the 7 numbered problems carry records from 2026-09-05 and nothing new has entered ORDER. It will hard-fail exit 2 on the first prose problem added to ORDER, which is what fencing hit and what started the 09-21 design cycle.

The design cycle drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0721f0abe841f73eb9def38d, opened 2026-09-21 and handed off 2026-10-01, reads the load vector as "locked in the difficulty-progression cycle and not reopened". It was reopened and retired 26 days before that cycle opened. Four decisions and five beads rest on it. Epic tla-kv2d and children tla-gdka, .1, .3 and .4 all carry the false premise. Only D2 survives.

THE DECISION IS FRANK^S AND IT IS ONE OF TWO.
1. The load vector comes back as the ramp placement authority. This reverses the 2026-09-05 psychometric ruling, which was that people cannot reliably grade on finer detail than 5 points and the six dimensions claimed thousands of distinguishable states. If this is the answer, tla-kv2d stands as designed and this bead closes by un-retiring the rule in PRACTICE-PLAN.md.
2. The gates retire with the rule. harness/test-vector.sh, harness/test-sequence.sh and the vector clause in harness/sequence.sh come out of scripts/test, the 13 records stay as history, and ORDER carries a plain order with no record requirement. If this is the answer, tla-kv2d is rewritten around the 1-to-5 scale and four of its five children die.

A third shape exists and works under either answer: keep the gate scoped to batch 2 packages that already carry records, and declare prose problems outside the ramp. That is close to what tla-kv2d.1 already emits. It is a narrowing, not an answer, so it does not settle this.

DO NOT WORK tla-kv2d UNTIL THIS CLOSES.

notes:
MY READ, 2026-10-01, and it is a recommendation rather than a finding. Frank rules.

I would retire the gates (option 2). Three reasons, weakest first.

1. Nothing has maintained them for 26 days. Not one commit since 2026-09-05 touched harness/sequence.sh, harness/test-vector.sh, harness/test-sequence.sh or authoring/VECTOR-FLOOR.md. A gate nobody maintains is a gate nobody believes.
2. The psychometric argument has not changed. People cannot reliably grade on finer detail than 5 points, and six dimensions at four levels each claims thousands of distinguishable states. Nothing measured since 09-05 bears on that, so re-adopting would be reversing a ruling on no new evidence.
3. The ramp exists to answer whether problem N is reachable from N-1, and the K=1 rule is what answered it. That question is real and retiring the gates leaves it unanswered. So option 2 is not free. It costs the reachability check, and the 1-to-5 scale cannot replace it, since a sort order over five buckets does not say which dimension moved.

That third reason is the one that would change my mind. If the reachability check matters more than the grading precision does, option 1 is right and the psychometric objection is a cost worth paying.

The third shape in the description is the cheap move and I do not think it settles anything. Scoping the gate to batch-2 packages keeps a green gate over 7 problems that are themselves withdrawn-and-replaced history, and declares every future problem outside the ramp. That is option 2 with extra machinery.

WHAT I WOULD NOT DO: cite Frank picking "Author a VECTOR.md for it" on 2026-09-30 as support for option 1. He picked from options I built on the false premise and was never told the vector was retired.

title: Source problems from documented failures and prose specs, and measure difficulty by spiking
description:
Frank, 2026-09-06: the curated set does not help. Search problems are interesting as
computer science and bear almost no relation to the systems he actually has to model.
He asked for software engineering scenarios instead of TLA+ problems.

The corpus cannot supply those at any level. 30 of the 45 usable rows at levels 3 and 4
are consensus, replication, broadcast, leader election or mutual exclusion. Of the other
15, two are puzzles and three are memory interfaces from Specifying Systems. About a
dozen rows in 143 look like ordinary application engineering. Levels 1 and 2 are search
puzzles. That is what people publish specifications about, so curation from published
TLA+ inherits it.

The constraint that made curation look necessary is not real. The direction-change
drawer says the failure was never modeling, that every reference was correct, and that
the problem was design taste plus review steps grading material against assumptions the
same process authored. So authoring was never what broke. What curation bought was an
artifact from outside the process, and a published spec turns out to be the wrong source
of that.

DECIDED with Frank. Source from both:

1. Documented failures. Jepsen reports, engineering postmortems, DDIA case studies. A
   real system, a named invariant, a documented violation.
2. Prose behavioral specifications. RFCs, Kafka KIPs, isolation-level documentation, API
   contracts. Bigger supply, ordinary mechanisms, no built-in counterexample.

OPEN, and the reason this is P0: how hard a source will be to model cannot be read off
the source. Measured over the 143 rows, variable count barely separates the levels.
Medians run 3, 2, 6, 7, 8, levels 1 and 2 are inverted, and level 1 spans 1 to 87
variables. Spec length separates the 2/3 boundary, INSTANCE marks level 5 at 51% against
under 10% elsewhere, and liveness predicts nothing at 58, 59, 46, 94, 60.

Every one of those is measured from a specification, not from a description. The deeper
point is that the variable count is the answer rather than a fact about the problem,
which is why one level spans two orders of magnitude of it. Asking a prose source how
many variables it needs is asking it for the representation, and the representation is
what the set exists to train.

So measure instead of predicting. Spike each candidate: an agent models it against TLC
until it checks, and reports variables, actions, distinct states, depth, wall time, and
whether it needed liveness or a history variable. The spike is also the example
implementation, which replaces what published specs were supplying.

The prediction line matters and is easy to cross. Predicting difficulty is safe for
choosing and ordering candidates. It must never reach the statement author, because
scoping a statement is the lever that lets someone hit a number, and that is the
load-vector failure coming back through a different door.

Pipeline: source document, then spike, then a statement written from the source alone
and never seeing the spike, then the consistency check. Statement and spike are written
independently from the same external document, so a disagreement is a finding.

title: NEXT SESSION STARTS HERE: the problem set has no difficulty axis
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: a planning session with Frank, not dispatchable work.

Frank, 2026-09-04, after reading seat 01 cold: "let's shift what the first priority will be for the next session to a planning session to revise what we're doing so it's actually a set of graded problems from raw neophyte up to experienced modeller. If we foul that up, it doesn't matter how good my grading is."

That last sentence is the whole argument, and I think it is right. Two days of harness work closed three grading holes. All of it is downstream of a problem being the right difficulty for the learner who meets it. A perfectly graded problem three levels too hard produces a stalled learner and no telemetry.

## The structural finding, verified rather than asserted

The v2 design has no progression dimension. Checked:

- §2.1 is a two-axis grid, situation (S1-S9) by task shape (A-F). Neither axis is difficulty.
- Ordering is the diagonal walk, which exists to serve interleaving.
- `tla-kl5.19` is the ONLY ordering bead in the plan: "interleave ordering and back-load pure TLA+". Two rules, neither of them difficulty.
- Every occurrence of "difficulty" in `V2-PLAN.md` is about WHERE difficulty lives (abstraction choice against state-space size against gap location) or about §7.1's refine-broken-not-hard policy. None of it orders anything.

So problems are placed by coverage and sequenced by interleaving, and nothing asks whether problem N is reachable from problem N-1.

Two consequences already measured. Seat 01 asks for a from-scratch model of a 14-day two-party system with ten properties and a liveness obligation, as first contact after chapter drills that top out at five short exercises (`tla-avvo`). And its author suspected exactly that, wrote it down, and deferred to a blind panel of fluent agents that could not test it.

## Why interleaving does not substitute for a ramp

The interleaving evidence is strong and should be kept: Rohrer et al. 2020, 61% against 38%, d=0.83, and the mechanism is that interleaved practice makes you CHOOSE a strategy rather than execute one. But choosing among strategies presupposes having some. Interleaving orders a set whose members are all reachable; it does not make an unreachable one reachable.

I suspect the two rules compose rather than conflict — a ramp fixes the floor, interleaving orders within it — but that is the design question, not its answer.

## What the session is

An above-bead planning session, `/design-a-cycle` shaped rather than a bead. Likely questions, not a plan:

- What is the difficulty axis actually made of? Candidates seen so far: number of properties to render, whether the representation is suggested or has to be invented, state-space size and therefore debug-cycle length, whether history has to be modelled, and whether liveness is in scope.
- Does it become a third axis of the grid, or an ordering constraint over the existing two?
- What is problem 1 for someone who has just finished the grammar? Nothing in the current set was designed to be that.
- How does a ramp get VERIFIED, given the finding that an agent-run pipeline cannot measure first-contact difficulty (`tla-rrwl`)? This is the hard one. The blind panel cannot answer it, and Frank is n=1 and gets used up: once he has worked a problem he is no longer first-contact for it.
- What happens to the 5 problems already authored and the 55 unauthored?

## Read first

- `tla-avvo` — seat 01's calibration, with the author's own quoted suspicion.
- `tla-rrwl` — an agent-run pipeline cannot test the human interface. Same blind spot, and it bounds how a ramp can be validated.
- `tla-y8tb` and `tla-nyrb` — column C's two structural findings, since a redesign should not leave them behind.
- `V2-PLAN.md` §2.1 (the grid), §3.4 and §8.2 (interleaving), §7.1 (refine broken not hard).
- Drawer `drawer_tla_puzzles_milestones_6690c9b5783d90c5f0e1eb9f` for the session this came out of.

## What NOT to do

Do not open this by reordering seats. The seat order is a symptom. Frank asked for the set to be graded from raw neophyte to experienced modeller, which is a design question about what the set IS, and answering it with a permutation of what exists would be the cheap move that looks like progress.

title: Lane A ships the answers next to the problems, which is the pilot's worst defect repeating
description:
Lane A delivers "statement + frozen reference + commented reference" as one bundle. Nothing says
WHERE Frank receives any of it, and no bead covers delivery.

**This is the pilot's worst defect, repeating.** The answer key sat in the critic-readable
directory carrying the words "Never show this to a critic", built by the same session that had
quoted §6b.1 two hours earlier. §6b.1: "Telling an agent not to look at the answers does not work.
Isolation must be structural." §2.4 says the `tla-practice`/`tla-answers` split "is a leak defense,
not a preference, so it does not get simplified into two directories of this repo later."

in the next paragraph." §7.4 records the ENSEEIHT counter-technique, withhold practice solutions,
which the plan ignores.

Frank gets ONE first contact per problem, ever. With the reference and commentary a `ls` away, in a
repo he owns and debugs in, the first impasse becomes a peek. §9.9's "read the commentary after
attempting" then has no enforcement but willpower, which is exactly what §6b.1 rejects. Batch-1
telemetry, which is the entire reason §7.0 batches, is contaminated at the source.

**Fix, and it needs no Stage 4 machinery.** A statements-only delivery point outside this repo (or
`tla-practice/` scaffolded as a bare directory), with reference and commentary released per problem
only after an attempt is recorded. Two directories and one rule.

**Blocks shipping any problem to Frank.**

title: The drill checker reads TLC's error line and prints run=ERROR instead of it
description:
Hit by Frank 2026-10-22 on sets/01-any-healthy-upstream. He was blocked, the
hint system was blocked, and the line that answered the question was in the
checker's hands and thrown away.

WHAT HE SAW. './check' reported 'rc=75 distinct=1 run=ERROR' and nothing else.
'./drill --hint' then said, correctly and honestly, 'Your checker output does
not include TLC's error message' and 'I cannot tell you the cause from the
module text. I would be guessing.' It told him to re-run TLC by hand.

WHAT THE CHECKER HAD. drill/study/check copies the modules into a scratch
directory, runs TLC, reads the log for the distinct-state count, and DELETES
the copy. Its own comment at :84-90 states that every measured failure path
opens a line with 'Error:', including the JVM's own class-not-found. So it
knows the shape of the line, it has the line, and it prints a three-letter
token.

THE ERROR IT DISCARDED, verbatim, and it names the cause outright:

  Error: Attempted to apply the operator overridden by the Java method
  ... Integers.DotDot(IntValue,IntValue), but it produced the following error:
  Cannot cast tlc2.value.impl.SubsetValue to tlc2.value.impl.IntValue

Plus a nested-expression list whose last entry was 'Line 11, column 26 to line
11, column 46', the exact span of the defect. The cause was 'SUBSET 1..N'
parsing as '(SUBSET 1) .. N', a precedence bug now recorded as bd memory
subset-binds-tighter-than-dotdot-so-parenthesize.

WHY THIS IS P1. The drill channel's whole design is attempt, then failure, then
IMMEDIATE feedback, citing Kornell/Hays/Bjork 2009 and Hays/Kornell/Bjork 2012
on delayed feedback mostly not carrying the effect. A checker that withholds
the diagnostic line converts immediate feedback into a manual re-run, and the
hint system's only remaining move is to tell him to go get it himself. That is
the feedback loop this corpus is built on, broken at its narrowest point.

IT IS ALSO THE MEMORY a-gate-over-what-the-code-computes-never-sees, exactly.
That memory says a gate over what the code computes never sees what the reader
is shown, and that when a channel has a human on the other end you assert on
the TRANSCRIPT and not only the exit code. Here the transcript is missing the
one line that matters.

WHAT TO DO, and the second half is the part that lasts.

Show the 'Error:' line on any non-clean run. Not the whole log, which is noisy
and carries trace states that would leak an answer on a violation. The first
'Error:' line plus the nested-expression list's LAST entry is the diagnosis,
and the last entry is the deepest position, which is the one worth reading
first.

CHECK THE LEAK BOUNDARY BEFORE WIDENING IT. On rc 12 the log carries a
violating state, and drill/study/check:92-95 already handles that case
deliberately, showing the last state rather than the whole trace. An error line
on rc 75, 76, 150, 151 or 255 carries no state, so those are safe. Decide per
code rather than printing the log.

AND FIX THE HINT SHEET'S FALLBACK. It told him to run
'java -cp /path/to/tla2tools.jar tlc2.TLC -config Balancer.cfg Balancer.tla'
when 'tlc' is on his PATH as a wrapper. That is a worse instruction than
'tlc -config Balancer.cfg Balancer.tla', and it asks him to find a jar path he
has no reason to know. Filed together because the sheet's fallback only exists
because the checker is silent.

Files: drill/study/check, drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md, harness/test-drill-check.sh
Acceptance: a non-clean run shows TLC's first Error: line and the deepest
nested-expression position, the per-code leak decision is written down beside
the code that makes it, a suite asserts the line appears on an rc 75 fixture
and does NOT appear with a trace state on an rc 12 one, and the hint sheet's
manual fallback names the wrapper on PATH.

title: Exit 151 has at least five meanings and tonight's fix records three
description:
Found 2026-10-22 by the tla-9y4s.6 author, about twenty minutes after
tla-ry2y landed at def9a79. THIS CORRECTS WORK I DID TONIGHT: my fix is
partial, and the way it is partial is the way I said a future reader should
not let happen.

WHAT def9a79 RECORDS, three readings of 151, each measured:

  INVARIANT NoSuchOperator   'The invariant NoSuchOperator specified in the configuration file'
  INVARIANT DiffSet          'The invariant of DiffSet is equal to FALSE'      -> INVARIANT_FALSE
  PROPERTY  DiffSet          'The property of DiffSet is equal to FALSE'       -> PROPERTY_FALSE

TWO MORE, both reproduced by the temporal page author:

  PROPERTY BareAct, where BareAct == tick' = tick + 1
    rc 151, 'Error: The formula BareAct ... is an action-level formula ... Only
    temporal-level (or state-level) formulas are allowed under PROPERTY or
    PROPERTIES.'
    The module DEFINES the operator, so nothing about the config-error reading
    applies.

  An operator named Any
    rc 151, 'Error: The invariant of Any is equal to <Java Method: public
    static tlc2.value.impl.Value tlc2.module.TLC.Any()>'
    Reproduced on a NINE-LINE fixture with NO EXTENDS AT ALL, control operator
    Mine at rc 0. Any == CHOOSE x : TRUE is at TLC.tla:119 inside the jar, and
    the Java override table appears to be keyed on the OPERATOR NAME rather
    than on the declaring module. That is a second finding inside this one and
    it is worth its own measurement: any spec is one unlucky operator name away
    from this.

WHY MY FIX IS PARTIAL AND NOT MERELY INCOMPLETE. The 151 arm in
harness/verdict.sh matches two needles and DEFAULTS TO CONFIG_ERROR on anything
it does not recognize. I wrote that default deliberately and recorded the
reason: 'An unrecognized 151 message is the documented meaning until somebody
measured otherwise, which keeps this arm from inventing a verdict for text it
has never seen.' That reasoning still holds. The consequence is that both
readings above report as a broken configuration when the configuration is fine,
which is exactly the harm tla-ry2y was filed on, surviving its own fix for two
more cases.

So the default is right and the needle set is too small. Those are different
problems and only the second one is a bug.

THE GATE IS WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE TO EXTEND. harness/test-verdict.sh now counts
matcher sites and requires each to be a permitted needle over $LOG, checked as
a pair. Adding needles means widening that pair DELIBERATELY, with the count
changed and its reason written next to it, rather than by accident. Do not
loosen the pair into a range.

A NAMING QUESTION THAT IS NOT OBVIOUS. INVARIANT_FALSE and PROPERTY_FALSE say
an assertion came out false. Neither new reading is that: one is a malformed
obligation and one is a name collision with the standard library. A token like
OBLIGATION_REFUSED would cover both and would NOT be a fourth flavor of false.
Decide it rather than extending the FALSE family by reflex.

AND THE TABLE-WIDE QUESTION, now asked for the third time in two days. 151 at
five meanings, 76 at two (tla-x90i), and 11, 75 and 76 absent from
run-all.sh's comment block. Every row was built from the codes this project
happened to run, so each is a claim about the corpus rather than about TLC.
Related: tla-v8ev (two more copies of this table), tla-x90i (76's second
meaning).

Files: harness/verdict.sh, harness/test-verdict.sh
Acceptance: all five readings of 151 are distinguished and pinned by a fixture,
the token naming decision is recorded with its reason, the matcher-site count
in test-verdict.sh is widened deliberately, and the CONFIG_ERROR default is
either kept with its reason restated or replaced with something that is not a
false statement about an unmeasured message.

title: TLC 151 means two things and verdict.sh records one, so a false invariant reads as a broken config
description:
TLC exit 151 has two meanings and this project records one. Found 2026-10-22 by
the tla-9y4s.3 author and verified independently in the main tree before that
page merged.

THE DOCUMENTED MEANING. Two places record it and both say the same thing:

  harness/verdict.sh:68              151  CONFIG_ERROR  .cfg names something
                                          the spec does not define
  core-language-docs/snippets/run-all.sh:39   151  the .cfg named something the
                                          module does not define

THE SECOND MEANING. A declared invariant with no variable in it, evaluated
FALSE, also exits 151. Measured on TLC 2026.07.31.184830 against
core-language-docs/snippets/sets/Girder.tla with Girder.cfg:

  rc 151
  Error: The invariant of SameSet is equal to FALSE

No state, no trace, no "Invariant X is violated" line. The cfg is correct and
every name in it resolves, so nothing about the documented meaning applies.

A TRUE invariant of the same shape exits 0 and reads like any ordinary pass.
The same module's Arity case does exactly that. So only the failure channel
differs, which is why this was never noticed: the shape only misreports when
it is wrong, and a corpus of passing fixtures never exercises it.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE PAGE IT CAME FROM. harness/verdict.sh is the
shared TLC invocation path for every component in this project, by the
dispatched-agents rule's own centrally-owned-files table. Anything reading its
classification sees CONFIG_ERROR for what is actually a false assertion. A
grader or a gate deciding "the configuration is broken, so this run
established nothing" would discard a real refutation.

The exposure is narrow and worth measuring rather than assuming. It needs a
declared obligation whose body mentions no variable, which is unusual in a
written spec and NOT unusual in a corpus that seeds wrong answers on purpose.
harness/seeded-bugs.sh and the drill verify/ trees are where to look.

WHAT TO DO, and the second half is the part that lasts.

Separate the two readings in verdict.sh. The discriminator is in the output
rather than the code: the config error names a symbol the spec does not define,
and this one reads "The invariant of <name> is equal to FALSE". Match the text,
do not guess from the code alone.

Then ask the completeness question of the whole exit-code table rather than of
this one row: which code in it carries a second meaning nobody has met yet?
The table was built from the codes the corpus produced, so every row is a claim
about what this project happened to run, not about what TLC can do. Three
codes turned up today that the table does not list at all, 11, 75 and 76, found
by the tla-9y4s.2 and .4 authors. That is four findings against one table in
one day.

Files: harness/verdict.sh, harness/test-verdict.sh
RED: a fixture with a false variable-free invariant, asserted to classify as a
violation rather than as a config error. Watch it classify as CONFIG_ERROR
first, since that is the behavior being corrected.
Acceptance: both readings of 151 are distinguished by output text and both are
pinned. The exit-code comment block says 151 has two meanings rather than one.
close_reason:
Fixed in merge commit ef6b0c7, implementation def9a79.

151 carries THREE meanings on TLC 2026.07.31.184830, not the two the bead
named. Reproduced each directly against the new fixture
harness/fixtures/verdict/InvariantFalse.tla:

  INVARIANT NoSuchOperator  'The invariant NoSuchOperator specified in the configuration file'
  INVARIANT DiffSet         'The invariant of DiffSet is equal to FALSE'
  PROPERTY  DiffSet         'The property of DiffSet is equal to FALSE'

New tokens INVARIANT_FALSE and PROPERTY_FALSE. Not SAFETY_VIOLATION, which
would have replaced one false statement with another, since a caller reading
it goes looking for a trace and there is none. CONFIG_ERROR stays the default
for unrecognized 151 text, so the arm never invents a verdict for a message
nobody measured.

THE ARCHITECTURAL CONFLICT, resolved rather than ignored. verdict.sh opened by
promising it never reads TLC's output, and test-verdict.sh enforced that with
a blanket ban on text matchers. The bead's RED line required a text match. The
resolution: the ban is scoped, not lifted. Text may only subdivide a single
code already measured to be ambiguous, never move a verdict between codes.
The structural assertion now counts matcher sites and requires all of them to
be the permitted needles over $LOG, so a third matcher or a different needle
breaks it. Checked as a pair because either half alone is satisfiable by the
wrong file.

RED watched honestly, and the first attempt at it was worthless: a stray token
in the reverted arm broke the parse and all 43 assertions failed at rc 2,
which says nothing about behavior. Redone cleanly, exactly 3 failed and both
new behavioral assertions reported got 'CONFIG_ERROR'.

Exposure measured rather than assumed, as the bead asked. A transitive scan of
1,425 cfg files resolving 2,693 obligations found variable-free bodies live in
the swipe corpus and the reference-page snippets, some seeded FALSE on purpose.
The scan's first version said 582 and was wrong for a reason worth keeping: it
did not close the body's identifier set over the module's own definitions, so
an obligation reaching state through a defined operator read as variable-free.

Green: verdict 53, grader 158, refinement 46, spelling 21 (run after git add),

title: Extend the refutation instrument to the temporal family, where reading is the whole check
description:
Measured 2026-10-21, after tla-0i0l landed harness/refute.sh with a reach of
40 of 64 items.

THE TEMPORAL FAMILY IS THE ONLY PLACE WHERE READING IS THE WHOLE CHECK.
Running the checker's own claim scanners over all 64 prompts, lifted verbatim
from drill/study/check rather than reimplemented:

  family             items  count  possible?  runnable
  control-state          8      0          5         8
  core                   8      8          0         8
  functions-records      8      8          0         8
  modules                8      8          0         0
  sequences              8      3          0         8
  sets                   8      8          0         8
  state-space            8      8          0         0
  temporal               8      0          0         0

Intersecting the no-count list with the not-runnable list gives exactly 8
items and all 8 are temporal. modules and state-space have pass 1. So on the
temporal family, passes 1 and 2 are dead by construction and pass 3 has no
instrument, which is the configuration that cost Frank a day on
sequences/01-triage-board. That item at least had a prompt table to argue
from. Temporal has nothing.

AND TEMPORAL IS THE EASIEST FAMILY TO INSTRUMENT, NOT THE HARDEST. This
reverses what tla-0i0l's commit and test comment say, and that wording should
be corrected when this lands.

All 8 temporal items carry two files no other family has:

  verify/MODULE   one line, the base module's name
  verify/MATRIX   a tab-separated manifest, one row per run, carrying the cfg
                  body verbatim, for example
                  answer-prop-buggy  -  SPECIFICATION Spec;PROPERTY AnswerProp
                  n3-buggy  -  \* MODULE: PipelineRefused;SPECIFICATION Spec;PROPERTY N3

Measured: MATRIX and MODULE exist in 8 of 8 temporal items and 0 of the other
56. drill/temporal/gen-cfgs.sh generates the per-run wrappers from MATRIX.

That manifest is structured where every other family's ANSWER.md rc table is
prose in three dialects. It names which SPECIFICATION each run uses, so the
buggy machine and the fixed one are identified without reading any prose.

WHY refute.sh REJECTS THEM TODAY, and the current comment gets this wrong. It
skips any module declaring no VARIABLES of its own. The *Run.tla wrappers
declare none, since each is two lines that EXTEND the base. But the BASE
module does declare them: Pipeline.tla:7 reads VARIABLES stage, artifact,
retries. So the state is declared, one level down, and the filter is looking
at the wrong file rather than at a family that composes state away.

The probe shape does not change. What changes is where the machines come from:
a named SPECIFICATION inside one module rather than a module of its own.

  V == INSTANCE <MODULE>
  Spec == V!<the SPECIFICATION the MATRIX row names>
  Ob == L!<the learner's obligation>

THE ONE REAL COMPLICATION, AND IT IS NOT THE MANIFEST. 7 of the 8 base
modules carry a fairness conjunct:

  PrintJob 2, Heartbeat 2, CommitTrace 1, Steps 1, LinkLassos 7,
  DeskLassos 5, Turnstile 1, Pipeline 0

.claude/rules/tla-practice.md records that a fairness conjunct over an action
[][Next]_vars forbids leaves no behavior at all, and TLC then exits 0 on every
temporal property including one no behavior can satisfy. Measured there on
this build: rc 0 where the same property without the conjunct reads 13.

So on this family an rc 0 is not evidence of anything until vacuity is ruled
out. A silent column would read exactly like a correct obligation. That is the
same false-reassurance failure the whole instrument exists to remove, so it
must be closed here rather than noted.

harness/vacuity.sh already exists and already reads the two codes this needs,
as VECTOR 4. Pair each temporal probe with it and report three states rather
than two: refutes, silent, or vacuous. Never fold vacuous into silent.

Files: harness/refute.sh, harness/test-refute.sh
RED, and both watched failing first:
  1. Point refute.sh at temporal/07-pipeline-halt. It must enumerate machines
     from MATRIX rather than reporting none.
  2. Build a probe over a spec whose fairness conjunct leaves no behavior, and
     confirm it reports vacuous rather than silent. Watch it report silent
     first, since that is the failure being closed.
Also: correct the reach comment in harness/test-refute.sh part 2b and the
wording in tla-0i0l's commit, which say these families compose state away.
That is true of the wrappers and false of the base module.

Temporal machines are named SPECIFICATIONs read from verify/MATRIX. rc 0 is now paired with harness/vacuity.sh on that family, since 7 of 8 base modules carry a fairness conjunct and a conjunct over an action Next forbids makes TLC exit 0 on every temporal property. Four cell states now: refutes, silent, vacuous, did-not-run. The author built a fixture with that shape, switched the pairing off, watched a column of silent zeros that reads like a correct obligation set, then watched it read vac. Three defects found on the way: a refused module printing a column of 150s, an INSTANCE-only dependency never copied so one item was nine columns of 150, and a grep piped under pipefail in its own new code that test-pipefail.sh caught. WHAT IS LEFT. ./drill --check runs from the delivered tree at

reads the repo. So the runner needs a repo root, it needs to refuse cleanly
when there is none, and its output has to join the checker's on the way into
the check prompt.

THE REPO DEPENDENCY IS THE DESIGN QUESTION, and it is new to this channel.
Every other thing ./drill does works from the delivered tree alone, which is
why the tree is delivered at all. Three routes, and I would take the first.

Take a DRILL_REPO_ROOT environment variable, defaulting to unset, and have a
check run say in one line that the refutation table was not produced because
no repo was named. That keeps ./drill working everywhere it works today and
makes the richer report opt-in on the one box that has the repo. Cheapest, and
it never half-runs.

Or have drill.sh discover the repo by walking up from its own delivered
location, which it cannot do, since the delivered copy is not under the repo.
Rejected, recorded so nobody re-derives it.

Or deliver verify/ to the study root. REJECTED and it must stay rejected.
drill/study/CLAUDE.md names verify/ as one of three things withheld on
purpose, and a variant module is a working spec for the item. Putting one
within reach of a model that has tools in a typed /check session hands over
most of the exercise. The instrument exists precisely so the machines can be
RUN without being READ.

THE OUTPUT SHAPE IS ALREADY DECIDED and part 4 of the suite asserts it: no
machine name, no ANSWER.md prose, machines numbered. Do not widen it while
wiring.

ALSO FOR THIS BEAD. check.md gains a pass that reads the table, and that pass
has to say what silence means. TypeOK reading 0 against a wrong doctor is
correct rather than a finding, since TypeOK is not about the picking rule.
Silence means silent against THAT machine. A count of refutations would call a
correct obligation a failure, which is the error the current check already
makes in prose.

AND THE REACH HAS TO BE SAID OUT LOUD. 40 of 64 items are in range. On the
other 24 a check run must say the table was not produced, never print an empty
one. The modules, state-space and temporal families are the 24.

harness/test-drill-runner.sh
RED: Serve sequences/01-triage-board and run ./drill --check with no repo
named. The report must say the refutation table was not produced and why.
Then name the repo and run again: the table must carry rc 13 for
GreatestSeverityAlwaysPicked. Watch the first fail before wiring the second.

title: Build the refutation instrument: run his obligations against the machines an item ships
description:
Found 2026-10-21, reading nine ./drill --check runs Frank made against
sequences/01-triage-board over one day, on an item budgeted at ten minutes.

WHAT WENT WRONG. The check produced a fresh prose finding on every run and
repeated one that is false. Across runs 2, 3 and 6 its headline finding was
that GreatestSeverityAlwaysPicked "would never catch a doctor who broke the
rule". Measured against the wrong doctor the item itself ships, with his eight
obligations spliced onto verify/TriageFifo.tla, one TLC run each:

  obligation                        rc
  GreatestSeverityAlwaysPicked      13   REFUTES the wrong doctor
  BoardEitherGrowsOrShrinksByOne    13   REFUTES the wrong doctor
  TypeOK                             0
  BoardDoesntExceedMaxSize           0
  PatientAlwaysPickedFromBoard       0
  TreatedListOnlyGrowsByOne          0
  RemovedPatientIsAlwaysTreated      0
  TreatedPatientIsAlwaysRemoved      0

Two mutations of his own PatientTreated confirm it from the other side.
board[i] >= board[j] reads rc 13 at 35 states, \E patient \in 1..Len(board)
reads rc 13 at 36 states, both naming GreatestSeverityAlwaysPicked.

THE EVIDENCE ALREADY SHIPS, AND IT SHIPS FOR ALL 64 ITEMS. ANSWER.md:105 and
:121 record the reference rule refuting TriageFifo at rc 13 over 50 states, so
the item's author ran this before shipping. verify/ holds thirteen runnable
files for this item, and every one of the 64 items has a verify/ directory,
from 4 files to 54. check.md restricts reading to the delivered prompt tree
and deliver-drill.sh:263 withholds ANSWER.md, META.md and verify/ from every
route, so the check re-derives a question the repo has already answered, and
got it backwards.

WHY A RUN RATHER THAN A BETTER READING. A prose reading has no fixed point.
Nine runs produced nine findings because the instrument generates text, so
there is always another sentence available. An rc table is deterministic and
it terminates: each shipped wrong machine is either refuted by one of his
obligations or it is not.

NO NEW LEAK, AND drill/study/CLAUDE.md ALREADY ARGUES THE DISTINCTION. It says
deliver-drill.sh "enforces a delivery boundary rather than an access boundary"
and that the prohibition on reading verify/ is the only thing in front of it.
That prohibition is on the MODEL. A script that runs the variants and prints
exit codes keeps the model further from them than today, because its output is
a table rather than a module. In one-shot mode the model has no tools at all,
so it cannot reach a variant whatever the script did. In typed /check mode the
exposure is exactly what it is today.

THE CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS FRANK'S. The day was educationally valuable: he
learned a large amount about writing TLA+ working through it. So this is NOT a
bead about making the check finish sooner. The iteration is where the value
was. What has to change is that each iteration be true, and that the end be
visible. Do not add a path that shortcuts the attempt.

REPORT PER VARIANT, NEVER AS A SCORE. TypeOK reading 0 against a FIFO doctor
is correct rather than a finding, since TypeOK is not about the picking rule.
Silence means silent against THIS wrong machine. The item ships two axes:
TriageFifo is wrong about the rule, and TriageSelect is wrong about the table
(ANSWER.md reads it rc 0 on the full model, rc 13 as TriageSelectAdmits), so a
learner's picking rule is right to be silent on the second. A count of
refutations would call that a failure.

THE RISK THAT DECIDES THE SCOPE. Splicing his obligations onto a variant needs
his variable names to match the variant's. They did here, by luck. Measure how
many of the 64 reference variants use names a learner would plausibly land on
before promising this works corpus-wide. The honest v1 runs where the names
match and says plainly when they do not, rather than reporting silence that is
really a name mismatch. A reported 0 that means "could not substitute" is the
same class of lie as a green gate that read no files.

THE REPO DEPENDENCY IS NEW. ./drill runs from the delivered tree, which has no
verify/. The instrument needs the repo root, so it refuses cleanly when the
repo is absent, the way deliver-drill.sh --verify skips an absent study root.
Every box but Frank's is in that case.

Files: drill/drill.sh, drill/study/.claude/commands/check.md
RED, and watch both fail first:
  1. Run the instrument on Frank's Triage.tla against verify/TriageFifo with
     the obligation list hardcoded empty. It must report 0 of 0 and say the
     substitution did not happen, not report a clean run.
  2. Then with his eight obligations. It must print rc 13 for
     GreatestSeverityAlwaysPicked and rc 13 for BoardEitherGrowsOrShrinksByOne.

Reproduces the rc 13 on GreatestSeverityAlwaysPicked that nine check runs said was impossible. Reach pinned at 40 of 64 items. Wiring into --check moved to tla-p29t, which is why this bead was retitled to what it delivered rather than closed on its original claim.

title: Nothing routes a drill reader to chapter/refinement.md, and the hint sheet names no source
description:
Reported by Frank on 2026-10-20 as "what it means is I'm lacking an actual
lesson on the thing I'm drilling on", working drill/modules/01. The lesson
exists and is published. Nothing points at it.

THE LESSON. chapter/refinement.md is 816 lines, published at
/tla-puzzles/chapter/refinement/ since tla-jaob.5 closed on 2026-10-08. Its
section "Substituting for variables" at line 223 opens:

  One gap to close first. The modules chapter taught INSTANCE ... WITH for
  constants, which is the common case. The refinement case substitutes for
  variables, and the rule is the same one with a wider target: every variable
  of the instantiated module gets replaced by an expression over the
  instantiating module's state.

Lines 243 to 245 print the exact SANY error Frank spent the evening on, with a
different variable name: "Substitution missing for symbol takings declared at
line 9, col 10 to line 9, col 16 of module Till and instantiated in module
MissingSub."

THREE SEARCHES, run 2026-10-20:

  grep -rl 'chapter/' drill/                 ->  0 files
  grep -rn 'refinement' exercises/ch13/*.md  ->  0 matches
  drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md       ->  121 lines, no source material named

So no PROMPT, META, ANSWER or README under drill/ mentions the chapter
directory at all, the cheatsheet whose own SOURCE GAP note records the hole
does not say the hole is closed, and the hint sheet gives its agent no
instruction to search repo lesson material before answering from its own
knowledge.

THE CONSEQUENCE, OBSERVED RATHER THAN PREDICTED. Frank ran ./drill --hint and
the returned answer to his mechanics question was generic TLA+ about initial
predicates. It was correct and it did not point at the section that prints his
error message verbatim. He called it "not helpful" and suspected it was wrong.
It was not wrong, it was unsourced.

AND ONE OF OUR OWN RULINGS PREDICTED IT. exercises/ch13/COVERAGE.md, section
"The excluded row": "Material the chapter never gave the reader isn't material
to test the reader on." That ruling excluded variable substitution from the
ch13 exercise set, because learntla's modules.rst:137 is a .. todo:: marker
reserving the parameterize-over-a-variable technique the chapter never
delivers. The drill family then built modules/01 and modules/02 on exactly that
technique. Three artifacts, each defensible alone, none of them aware of the
other two.

THE FIX, three cross-references.

1. The modules family gets a prerequisite pointer at chapter/refinement.md's
   "Substituting for variables". There is no family-level README under
   drill/modules, so it goes either in each of the eight META.md files under a
   new heading or once in drill/README.md. Check which the drill gate tolerates
   before choosing.
2. exercises/ch13/CHEATSHEET.md's SOURCE GAP note gains "closed in
   chapter/refinement.md", so the next reader of that note stops looking.
3. drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md tells its agent to search the repo's own
   lesson material before answering a mechanics question from its own
   knowledge, and to cite what it found.

ONE CONSTRAINT ON ITEM 3, and it has to be written out or the next author will
read it as a conflict. The hint sheet is a refusal contract that forbids the
session from reading this repo's drill tree, per drill/README.md. chapter/ is
not the drill tree. It carries no answers to any drill item, so citing it widens
nothing. Say so in the sheet rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

GATE IT, DON'T ADVISE IT. A cross-reference that rots silently is the shape this
bead is about. Candidate: for each drill family, at least one tracked file names
a chapter/ path, with a per-family floor so a typo reddens instead of passing
quietly. Same pattern harness/test-spelling.sh already uses for its roots, and
the same failure this project has now hit four times, three of them recorded in
.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md under the gate-that-never-read-the-tree
hazard.

notes:

The bead asks hint.md to tell its agent to SEARCH the repo's lesson material. A

And pointing at a lesson spends no rung, EXCEPT where the page you would name

title: Vacuous is not the same as not a claim, and the reader says it is
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: needs Frank's ruling before anything is built.

Frank, on L0-T1-14 on his phone: "this feels flawed, while it is vacuously
true, it is still a true assertion. (and all the elephants in my pocket are
pink)"

THE CORPUS AGREES WITH HIM IN ITS OWN NUMBERS. All 30 level 0 vacuous items
measured (0, 0), and the verdict table in swipe/README.md reads that pair as
"the claim holds, swipe right". bake.sh then overwrites it, because field 6 is
derived from the authored kind in field 5 and vacuous maps to down.

L0-T1-14 contradicts itself on screen. Its flash reads "The left side is false,
so the implication holds whatever the right side says", which is an argument
for true, under a verdict of "not a claim".

The contract page already concedes the merge and defends it: "Merging them is
forced rather than chosen: without the merge a vacuous item has no correct
swipe." That premise is false. The correct swipe is right.

SCALE. 46 of 432 items are vacuous: 30 at level 0, 12 at level 1, 4 at level 2.
down also carries illformed (37), unparsed (13) and wronglevel (12), and those
three are genuinely not claims. Only the vacuous ones are being told they are
not true.

O1, vacuous bakes right. Truth stays truth and down means only "it does not
mean anything". Costs: the level 0 mix per template goes 18/18/12 to 24/18/6,
the base rate for true goes 0.375 to 0.500, and the stem-blind probe floor, the
power table in swipe/README.md and the level 0 gate constants all move with it.
Vacuity stops being scored.

O2, the mapping stands and the words stop lying. down becomes "says nothing",
which is true of all four kinds under it and never contradicts a truth value,
and the ask stops being yes/no shaped: "does this hold" becomes "what does this
line say", answered true, false or nothing. No corpus row changes, no bake, no
probe re-run. Eight files carry the "not a claim" string: authoring/laytime and
authoring/river-call DESCRIPTION.md, swipe/README.md, swipe/reader/swipe.js,
scripts/deliver-drill.sh, scripts/build-docs.sh, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh,
harness/test-build-docs-reading.sh.

O3, ask both questions of every claim, so neither ask leaks the kind and both
lessons get scored. Roughly doubles the stream and adds a per-ask verdict
column.

CENTRAL RECOMMENDS O2. The objection is about what the screen asserts rather
than about what is scored, and O2 removes the false assertion for the price of
a label and two prompts. Spotting vacuity is the skill the rest of the project
is built around, see harness/vacuity.sh and "Vacuity is measured, not
asserted", so O1 pays for a wording defect by dropping the lesson. O1 wins if
this rung is meant to be pure truth evaluation at fingertip speed, where any
item whose honest answer is true and whose scored answer is not trains
hesitation.

THE OPEN LEVEL 2 RULING RIDES ON THE SAME ANSWER. swipe/README.md, "The
stuttering reading is the vacuous kind, and that is a ruling Frank has not
taken", shipped vacuous against central's read and is still unruled.

Files: depends on the ruling. O2 touches the eight files above and no corpus
row. O1 touches swipe/level0/bake.sh, the three ITEMS.tsv files and the level
gates.
notes:
RULING 2026-10-20, Frank: "I agree, let's build." O2 it is.

THE LOCKED DESIGN.

D1 Two maps, because a button and a sentence are two jobs. LABELS stays the
button text and becomes right true, left false, down nothing. VERDICT is new
and holds the sentence form: right "it is true", left "it is false", down
"it says nothing". One map doing both gives "It is says nothing".

D2 The three sentence sites read VERDICT. renderFlash's hit and miss lines and
renderExplain's line, which is where Frank saw "You said true. It is not a
claim." They become "Right. It says nothing.", "No. You said true and it says
nothing." and "You said true. It says nothing."

D3 The help rows read VERDICT too, so the panel says what each gesture
asserts rather than naming it.

D4 No prompt is yes/no shaped any more, because there are three answers and a
yes/no question has two. All six become noun phrases: holds "what this line
says", implies "what this implication says", enabled "what this says about
firing here", terminal "what this says about stopping here", step "what this
says across the step", always "what this says all the way".

D5 The contract page says the quiet part. Down covers four kinds, and the
fourth is a line that holds for a reason that leaves it empty. A vacuously
true line IS true, and it still tells you nothing, which is what the question
asks for. Frank's own sentence is the best statement of it and goes in: all
the elephants in my pocket are pink.

D6 The gate pins the new words, because the words ARE the fix. LABELS.down,
VERDICT.down, every PROMPTS value starting with "what ", and the contract
page's two new passages.

WHAT DOES NOT MOVE. No corpus row, no bake, no kind field, no verdict channel,
no mix, no base rate, no probe re-run. Field 11 already explains the vacuity
per item and now agrees with the frame instead of contradicting it.

KIND STAYS BEHIND. The flash frame cannot distinguish vacuous from illformed,
because swipe/reader/emit-items.sh keeps field 5 off the page on purpose: it
is the answer in a sharper form than field 6 gives it. The per-item field 11
already carries the why, so the frame does not need it.

THE REAL FOOTPRINT IS FOUR FILES. The other four hits on "not a claim" are
coincidental English: authoring/laytime/DESCRIPTION.md is about a constant,
authoring/river-call/DESCRIPTION.md about a step rule, scripts/deliver-drill.sh
about a delivery, harness/test-build-docs-reading.sh about a floor. Leave all
four alone.
