title: The claim leaves the step, and the model stops being collapsible
description:
Files: swipe/reader/swipe.js, swipe/reader/swipe.css, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh, swipe/README.md

RED: INVARIANT: the step view renders no .swipe-step-claim and the model screen renders no collapse control, and every model screen except 1:Shelves fits its body without vertical overflow at 390x844.

## Frank's ruling, 2026-10-19 afternoon

THE CLAIM LINE AT THE FOOT OF THE STEP GOES. This reverses D2 of tla-7xql.18,
which Frank ruled that morning and revised the same day after reading a model
on his phone: "I think we will be better off having to flick back and forth
for the problem." To re-read the claim you tap back to the question and swipe
up again.

He accepted the sideways scroll in the same breath, "the phone screen is going
to be tight", so this bead does not try to remove it.

## What the claim costs, measured

Chrome at a true 390x844 against the published build, model step open on
1:Fences. Setting the claim line to `display: none` and re-reading:

    model body with the claim      480.0 px
    model body without it          613.9 px
    returned                       133.9 px

Line metrics read off the served stylesheet in the same pass: 21.28 px per
line, 12 px of bottom padding, 10.825 px per character, 318 px of client
width, so 29 characters fit across.

## What that buys, over all 24 screens

Computed from the emitted payload against the two measured heights:

    vertical overflow WITH the claim        5 of 24
    vertical overflow WITHOUT the claim     1 of 24

The one that still overflows is 1:Shelves at 29 lines, which needs about
629 px against 613.9. It is over by roughly 15 px and will scroll a little.
Leave it scrolling rather than shrinking the type for one screen.

## Also in this bead: the collapse control is a leftover

`renderScreen()` draws a `.swipe-screen-head` button that toggles
`v.collapsed[key]` and prints "hide" or "show". That earned its place when the
model shared the resting view with the card. The step IS the model now, so
collapsing it leaves the step with a head and nothing else, which is very
likely what Frank saw when he reported "It isn't showing the model".

REMOVE THE CONTROL AND THE STATE. `v.collapsed` is initialized in the view and
reset by forget, and both go. Keep the model's NAME on screen: it is the one
label that says which model you are reading. A non-interactive head is the
shape to reach for.

## Do not change

The gesture table. `chromeAt()`. `answersLive()`. `scrollerDeclining()`, whose
sideways reading of `.swipe-screen-body` stays exactly as tla-7xql.18 left it.
`harness/Gate.tla` and `harness/verdict.sh` are centrally owned. `docs/` is
generated from `module-docs/`. `puzzles/` is v1. No payload field changes.

## The gate

`harness/test-swipe-reader.sh`, split `--static` (3.0 s) and full (22.0 s).
Both budgets stay. tla-7xql.18 added an assertion that the claim line is
PRESENT in the step view; it has to flip rather than be deleted, so the gate
records that this was decided twice.

Add a corpus assertion over the emitted screens: at the measured line height
and the measured body height, exactly one screen overflows vertically and it
is 1:Shelves. That is a gate over what the reader is SHOWN rather than over
what it computes, which is the hole bd memory
`a-gate-over-what-the-code-computes-never-sees` names. Put the measured
constants in one place with a comment saying where they came from, so the next
person who changes the type size sees what they invalidate.

Watch every new assertion FAIL first.

The claim left the step: model body 480.0 to 613.9, vertical overflow across the 24 screens 5 to 1, the survivor 1:Shelves at 29 lines wanting 629.1 and staying scrolled by Frank's ruling. The model stopped being collapsible, control and v.collapsed state both removed, model name kept. Three figures from tla-7xql.18 corrected in place: the 660 estimate was 180 over a measured 480.0, the corpus DOES reach vertical overflow, and 438 was a correct reading of 1:Alternation at 20 lines mislabeled as the tallest and propagated into four files. New measurement nobody had: 29 characters fit at 318px client width and 10.825px per character, so 22 of 24 screens overflow sideways and the conditional decline frees two, not most. The gate grew a scan over what the reader is SHOWN, constants in one block with an invalidation note. Verified: 227/0 in 14.5s against 22.0, 225/1 in 1.3s against 3.0, spelling 20, pipefail 25, lint clean over 146, footprint exactly the four declared files. Registry 49/49 in 1133.4s with zero failures. Open and left to Frank: the step hint still promises a tap on 22 of 24 models, filed as tla-7xql.20.

title: A step is the whole page, and the menu stops eating the premise
description:
Files: swipe/reader/swipe.js, swipe/reader/swipe.css, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh, swipe/README.md

RED: INVARIANT: with v.depth > 0 the rendered root holds exactly one .swipe-step and one .swipe-claim, and no .swipe-card, no .swipe-controls and no .swipe-status.

## The defect

Frank, on his phone, 2026-10-19: "It isn't showing the model."

The model IS rendered. It is given 66 pixels of the 438 its content wants.
Measured in Chrome at a true 390x844 against the published build, with a
record present and the model step open:

    counts          29.6
    the step       276.4   the only flex-shrink child, so it absorbs the deficit
    the card       304
    the menu       172
    padding+gaps    62
                   844 exactly

Hide the menu and the step goes to 462.4 and the model screen from 66.3 to
252.3. The payload is not at fault: 24 screen keys against 24 non-zero bucket
keys, 2:Handover among them, nothing missing.

## Frank's ruling, 2026-10-19

A STEP IS THE WHOLE PAGE. Swiping up from the question REPLACES the view with
the premise rather than stacking a panel above the card.

D1  At v.depth > 0 the card, the menu and the counts row are not drawn. The
    step keeps its head, its back button and its hint.
D2  ONE LINE OF THE CLAIM STAYS, pinned at the foot of the step view. Not the
    card: no tag, no ask prompt, no answer buttons. At level 2 the reader is
    checking a one-line claim against a step in front of them, and holding it
    in their head is friction rather than the exercise.
D3  The menu collapses behind ONE control at rest too. Eight controls touched
    once a session against one touched every item. Ruled alongside D1 and
    still wanted, since D1 only covers the stepped view.
D4  THE GESTURE TABLE IS UNCHANGED AND THIS BEAD MUST NOT TOUCH IT. Right,
    left and down answer, up is deeper, tap is back. A swipe right at the
    model step still files "true" with no button on screen. answersLive() is
    unchanged, and the buttons going away removes the affordance, not the
    answer.

## R1, which this bead creates and must solve

bindGestures() declines every touch starting inside .swipe-screen-body,
unconditionally, at swipe.js:1626. Today that body is 66 of 844 pixels, so
almost the whole page still answers gestures. Full-page it becomes most of the
screen, and the back button would be the only way out of a view filling the
phone. That is the ambiguity Frank reported on 2026-10-19 pointed the other
way.

MITIGATION, ruled by Frank: decline only when the line ACTUALLY overflows
sideways. The pattern already sits twelve lines below it in the same function,
where the .swipe-step-body decline reads

    body.scrollHeight > body.clientHeight + 1

The screen body wants the horizontal form, scrollWidth against clientWidth.
Watch it decline on a wide model and NOT decline on a narrow one before you
believe it.

## Room after the change

844 less 20 page padding, about 29 step padding, 40 head, 25 hint, 30 claim
line and 38 screen head leaves roughly 660 for the model body against the 438
the worst one wants. It fits, so most models stop scrolling vertically at all,
which is the other half of why R1's mitigation is safe.

## A third defect in the same footprint

The card hint is the depth-0 line at every depth. At the model step it still
reads "up for the pinned state". D1 removes the card at depth so this closes
itself, and the gate should pin that rather than leave it to inference.

## Do not touch

harness/Gate.tla and harness/verdict.sh are centrally owned. docs/ is
generated from module-docs/. puzzles/ is v1. No payload field changes:
swipe/reader/SCREENS.tsv and swipe/reader/emit-items.sh are settled, and this
bead changes presentation only.

A step is the whole page: chromeAt(depth, panel, flash) decides the counts row, the resting box and the menu, render() asks it once, and the model gets 824 of 844 instead of 66. Claim line at the foot of the step on the card's own type, withheld at the explanation step where the answers are dead. R1 mitigated: the screen body declines only on actual sideways overflow, watched failing both ways (6 FAIL unconditional, 3 FAIL with no decline). Menu behind one control, 120px back to the flash and the panels. Gesture table untouched. Verified: reader gate 216/0 in 13.9s against 22.0, static 214/1 in 1.19s against 3.0, spelling 20, pipefail 25, lint clean over 146, footprint exactly the four declared files. Registry 49/49 in 1178.3s with zero failures. Open finding recorded in the gate: a model that overflows VERTICALLY is not declined, which is Frank's ruling rather than an oversight and is unreachable at 844.

title: The reader is a widget in a scrolling page, so a scroll files a verdict
description:
The reader is a widget in a scrolling page, so a scroll files a verdict

Files: swipe/reader/swipe.js, swipe/reader/swipe.css, scripts/build-docs.sh, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh, swipe/README.md

FRANK HIT THIS ON HIS PHONE ON 2026-10-19, minutes after tla-7xql.15 shipped:
"I'm not sure whether a swipe is going to scroll through the page or send a
message. I've now accidentally sent multiple responses." His record has
verdicts in it he never gave.

THE MECHANISM. bindGestures binds touchstart and touchend to the reader root
with { passive: true }, so the handler CANNOT cancel the scroll. A vertical
drag that starts inside the reader scrolls the page AND fires gesture(). Down
is "not a claim", so a scroll files a vacuity verdict on a real claim. That is
the exact failure the single-meaning gesture table was built to prevent,
arriving through the page's own scroll rather than through a mode.

Chrome Android's pull-to-refresh is the same hazard a second time. A downward
drag near the top of the document is a browser gesture before it is ours.

MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER at a true 390x844 on 2026-10-19, against the live
site after tla-7xql.15:

  the document is 3266px and the viewport is 844
  387px of chrome sits ABOVE the reader: Material header 48, the h1, the
    intro paragraph, the status callout
  1944px of contract prose sits BELOW the controls
  the card is position: sticky at the viewport bottom
  a level 2 step opens 471px tall. 133px of it is visible and 338px sits
    BEHIND the card
  scroll down 339px and it fits exactly: step 48 to 520, card top 521, zero
    hidden, 1px of margin

So the room exists and nothing takes the reader to it. That is tla-7xql.15's
bug returning through a different door: 198px of occlusion became 338px.

WHAT WORKS, measured the same way, so this bead does not reopen it. Synthetic
touch events drove the whole stack: rest, pin 471px, model 449px, explanation
189px with the three buttons disabled, up clamped at the top, taps walking back
out one at a time. The gesture layer and the stack are correct. The page around
them is not.

FRANK RULED O2 on 2026-10-19: the reader owns the viewport on its page. Not a
scrollIntoView call on the step, which was the one-line option and which he
turned down. His words: "the Design is deeply ambiguous."

THE DESIGN

D1. THE READER FILLS THE VIEWPORT and the page does not scroll. No Material
header, no h1, no intro, no prose, no footer. html and body get overflow
hidden and overscroll-behavior none under a class, which kills pull-to-refresh
as well. Use dvh rather than vh so mobile browser chrome is accounted for.

D2. THE CLASS GOES ON AT RUNTIME, FROM swipe.js, NOT FROM A MKDOCS TEMPLATE.
mkdocs.yml runs navigation.instant, which replaces the document's content
without reloading, so a per-page template is not known to apply when the reader
arrives from the nav. swipe.js already subscribes to window.document$ for
exactly this reason and boots on every instant navigation. Reusing that
mechanism is the one route proven to work on this site. THE CLASS MUST COME OFF
when the observable fires on a page that is not the reader, or every other page
on the site loses its header.

D3. THE CONTRACT PROSE MOVES TO ITS OWN PAGE. 1944px of it cannot live under a
reader that owns the viewport. The reader's menu links to it. One URL is the
reader and one is the contract, so there is no mode to be in.

D4. touch-action IS THE DECLARATIVE FIX AND IT NEEDS CARE. With the page no
longer scrolling, a vertical drag on the reader root has nothing to scroll, so
the ambiguity is gone at the root. The tla-7xql.15 author deliberately set no
touch-action because the property intersects up the ancestor chain and a wrong
value risked killing the model screen's sideways scroll. That reasoning still
holds. Set it per element rather than broadly, keep the step body scrollable in
both axes, and SAY WHAT YOU MEASURED rather than what you expect.

D5. THE MENU GETS A FORGET BUTTON. There is no way to clear the record and
Frank needed one tonight. Clearing site data is the only route today and it
takes the theme preference with it. Put it behind a confirm, and make it write
nothing if the reader declines.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT TOUCH. The gesture table, the stack, stepsFor,
depthAfter, answersLive, cardHint and the level tags all measured correct and
stay as they are. The payload fields are settled. harness/Gate.tla and
harness/verdict.sh are centrally owned.
close_reason:
Landed at merge 14177bc. The reader owns the viewport on its page and the page does not scroll, so a drag can no longer file a verdict while it scrolls. Pull-to-refresh stops competing for the same reason.

The bead's own mechanism was wrong and the worker measured it rather than believing it: .swipe-card has carried touch-action pinch-zoom since tla-7xql.15, so the DOCK was never the panning surface. What panned was everything else at auto, the counts, the menu, the gaps and the reader root.

The class goes on from swipe.js rather than a page template, because navigation.instant replaces content without reloading. It comes off in applyViewport(), one function with one caller, first statement of boot() ahead of every early return. Proven against real instant navigation by mapping the published hostname to a local mirror, since the theme matches its sitemap on protocol and hostname but never on port.

The contract prose moved to its own page. The menu gained a forget button behind a confirm, which did not exist and which Frank needed.

THE SAMPLE WAS THE BUG IN OUR OWN MEASUREMENT, and this is the part worth carrying. The flash overflow shipped as 28 of 40 in two files and 35 of 40 in two others. The stream draws at random from unanswered items, so answering 40 of a 48-item rung SAMPLES it: three runs of one tree read 35, 31 and 29. Re-measured over every item of the rung: 39 of 48 at level 2, worst 111px, 0 of 144 at level 1, identical twice. The 93px figure was a pre-fix reading that reached two of four files.

Verified by central: footprint exactly the 5 Files-line files across both commits; reader gate 161 passed full 13.3s against 22.0s and 159 passed static 1.19s against 3.0s with neither budget moved while the suite grew 33 assertions; spelling 20, pipefail 25, shellcheck clean over 146 files, docs suites 314/94/47; every tracked file on the branch searched for the stale figures. Full registry 49 of 49 in 1107.2s, 0 failures.

NOT READ ON A PHONE. dvh against real browser chrome and overscroll-behavior against pull-to-refresh are taken from the specs, because headless has none to measure.

title: The reader serves level 0 only, and 192 items just shipped behind it
description:
tla-7xql.12 built the published reader and was scoped to level 0 on purpose, because level 1 did not exist when it was briefed. Level 1 now ships 144 items over three templates and level 2 ships 48. NONE OF THEM REACHES A READER.

That is the same shape as tla-rrwl and as tla-7xql.12 itself, for the third time in this project: the artifacts ship and the interface does not. Worth naming because the pattern is now a habit rather than an accident.

WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM LEVEL 0. A level 0 item is a single line and needs no model screen at all, which is why the epic built that level first. A level 1 item pins a STATE and a level 2 item pins a STEP, and both need the model on screen with the obligations stripped, which is decisions D2 and D7 on the epic.

THE MEASUREMENTS THAT CONSTRAIN THE LAYOUT, from tla-7xql.4 and verified in its merge:

  model screens, the level 1 pilot's 7 models   4 to 21 nonblank lines
  model screens, all 33 reading/ models         0 to 22 nonblank lines
  shortest   Fences 4, Brackets 11, Contention 18, Break 21

AND ONE MODEL RENDERS ZERO LINES. Ring's actions live in the PlusCal translation block under names the shown-roots rule does not reach, and Collatz's screen carries vars and the BEGIN TRANSLATION comment. Both follow from the rule rather than breaking it. A reader has to do something defined when a screen is empty, and PlusCal screens are separate work.

THE PHONE IS THE ONLY TARGET, which Frank settled on 2026-10-18. A 21-line model screen plus a pin plus a claim plus the swipe affordances has to fit a phone viewport without the reader scrolling to find the question. That is the real design problem in this bead and nobody has looked at it.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND SHOULD BE REUSED. swipe/level1/render.sh and swipe/level2/render.sh compute the shown set, forward from the actions, as the transitive closure of every level 2 definition except Next and the SPECIFICATION formula. The gates assert the screen is closed under use and that a claim may only name a definition the screen shows. swipe/reader/emit-items.sh is the ONE place that decides which fields may ship, and harness/test-swipe-reader.sh holds that line.

THE WITHHELD FIELDS DO NOT CHANGE. kind, rc_claim, rc_wf and vacuity stay in the repo at every level. The baked swipe ships because a page with no server cannot grade without it. A level 1 pin is field 13 and it SHIPS, since the reader cannot pose the question without it, and the stem-blind gate already treats the pin as part of the surface while the model stays the premise.

Files: swipe/reader/emit-items.sh, swipe/reader/swipe.js, swipe/reader/swipe.css, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh

RED: INVARIANT: the published reader serves an item from every shipped level, a level 1 or 2 card shows its model screen with no stripped definition and no obligation, and a model whose screen renders empty is reported rather than served.
close_reason:
Merged at 96e44e25855179fecef80cefb32f69c04e982c4f. The reader serves all three rungs: 432 items, 24 level-and-model screens, payload 52,461 to 138,987 bytes.

The brief's assumption that screens could be rendered at publish time was wrong, and the worker found why: pages.yml installs Python and mkdocs-material and nothing else, so there is no Java on the deploy runner, and render.sh needs SANY's semantic tree to read a definition's level. Screens are baked into swipe/reader/SCREENS.tsv (373 rows) and the gate re-renders all 24 and diffs byte for byte. That split the registry row: fast 3.0 --static, slow 22.0 for the freshness pass.

NO BROWSER READ THE LAYOUT. Chrome would not complete a headless load in the authoring sandbox, four ways. The design stopped depending on the measurement instead: the question is docked sticky at bottom 0, so its position is an invariant rather than an arithmetic result. The layout numbers in the merge commit are computed from the shipped CSS and marked INFERRED. That gap is real and the next reading that settles it is Frank's own phone.

Central corrected one thing on the way in: the suite header and its part 8 notes claimed a headless Chromium reading at 390x844 that nobody took, contradicting the author's own report and swipe/README.md. Both now say so and point at the merge commit. Two stale part numbers went with it (f85ef24).

title: Level 1 templates E2 and E3: take the ENABLED rung to the full set
description:
FRANK SIZED IT 2026-10-18: 'I'm ok with doing the full set.' That is the tla-7xql.4 worker's proposal, taken as proposed: THREE templates at 48 each, 144 items, and stop there.

E1 SHIPPED with tla-7xql.4 at merge 11960de. Does this action fire here, 48 items over 7 models, 18 right 18 left 12 down, base rate 0.3750.

E2, PARAMETERIZED ACTIONS AND QUANTIFIED ENABLED. The bead measured 37 parameterized actions, several instantiable ways each, and E1 spends only 5 items on them. The distinct trap is three claims that look alike and are not: \E p \in S : ENABLED Take(p), \A p \in S : ENABLED Take(p), and ENABLED Take(c) for a fixed c. Empty-range vacuity lives naturally here. Supply named by the worker: Break, Key, Quorums, Tickets, Chips, Matching, Shelves, Alternation.

E3, TERMINAL AND STUCK. E1 has 7 terminal items and they are its thinnest ask. 79 of 337 published configs in this project's corpus survey set CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE on purpose, so telling stuck from finished is the lesson rather than a footnote. It wants items where several actions are each disabled for a DIFFERENT reason, which E1 does not supply.

TWO FAMILIES THE WORKER ARGUED AGAINST, with the measurement behind each, and they stay out.

The empty-guard family. MoveA == a' \in 1..b has an enabling condition even with no guard conjunct, which is real and worth teaching. Under the TypeOK pin rule it can never be DISABLED, because TypeOK forces b \in 1..N, so the family has true items and no false ones without new models. Fences is almost its entire supply in reading/. It stays a thread inside E1.

A fourth or fifth template. Level 0's five split by TLA+ subject area. At level 1 the subject is one question kind, so the split has to be by claim shape, and the worker could name three shapes a reader experiences differently. A fourth would be the same question in new clothes.

MIX: hold 18 right, 18 left, 12 down per template. The base-rate argument is about the SWIPE mix and it carries. The kind mix under down was 4 vacuous, 3 illformed, 3 wronglevel, 2 unparsed in E1, and it moves only if a template's subject supplies a kind more naturally.

COST, AND IT IS THE REASON THE REGISTRY ROW NEEDS SPLITTING. A level 1 item cannot batch: each costs a claim run plus the auxiliary type run, and a vacuous one a third. E1 is 100 JVMs over 48 items and its gate measures 69 to 70 s on a quiet box. Three templates in one row is roughly 210 s, which would be the second-largest row in the registry behind test-recall-gate.sh at 215. The worker's suggestion, and central agrees: scope bake.sh --check per template and carry three registry rows, so one template's growth does not move the whole row.

STILL CENTRAL'S RULE AND NOT FRANK'S: a pinned state must satisfy the model's own type invariant and need not be reachable. 31 of 33 models name one, both exceptions are PlusCal, and it costs one extra run per item.

Files: swipe/level1/ITEMS.tsv, swipe/level1/TEMPLATES.tsv, harness/test-swipe-enabled.sh, scripts/test

RED: INVARIANT: every level 1 template ships 48 items at 18 right, 18 left and 12 down, every kind in the level 1 channel table is shipped or recorded as unshipped with its reason, and the stem-blind probe reads clear on each template at the level 1 surface.
close_reason:
Landed at merge 4f07dd5. Frank sized it on 2026-10-18 as the full set, and it ships three templates at 48 each, 144 items, with the mix held per template so the base rate and the power table are unchanged.

RECOVERED RATHER THAN REPORTED, and the recovery needed two gate repairs. The corpus survived the power cut fully baked with zero unmeasured fields. The gate did not.

REPAIR 1: the file was left with 'if want_corpus; then' opened at line 1152 and no matching fi, so the suite died at PARSE time and not one assertion ran. Its tail was complete, so it read as whole on inspection and only bash -n found it. That is the failure shape worth remembering and it is filed as a bd memory: the corpus was finished and correct, and the only broken thing was the instrument that would have said so.

REPAIR 2, and it found a real defect rather than just restoring the file. The premise-leak check scans the stem file for every model name. Key is a module name in this corpus, reading/state-space/04-key/Key.tla, and ALSO a CONSTANT declared by Overlay.tla and Ledger.tla, which seven E2 and E3 items quantify over. A level 1 claim cannot be written without naming its own model's vocabulary, so an identifier in a stem is necessary rather than gratuitous. The scan now skips a model name that any corpus model declares and PRINTS what it skipped, since a silent exclusion is how that check would stop covering the one thing it is for. The declaration scan gained CONSTANTS to make it possible. Key.tla declares CONSTANT Staff and no constant of its own name, so nothing about it ever reached a judge.

THE PER-TEMPLATE REGISTRY SPLIT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR WAS NOT DONE, deliberately, and 8880ad6 records why. The bead estimated three templates in one row at about 210 s and wanted four rows so one template's growth could not move the whole row. Measured on a quiet box: combined 152.5 s against split 185.4 s, being --machinery 24.0 plus E1 52.5, E2 55.3 and E3 53.6. The split is SLOWER by 33 s because each template run repeats setup the combined run does once, so the premise did not hold. One row, re-based 74.0 to 165.0. The suite already takes --template ID for iteration, which is where that scoping pays.

title: The swipe rung has no reader, which is tla-rrwl happening a second time
description:
FRANK RULED 2026-10-18: PUBLISHED. 'I would go with Published myself.' The reader is a page on the docs site rather than a file delivered into ~/tla-practice. He asked the question himself, having imagined the channel as a website and then seen a JVM mentioned.

THE SPLIT, SO NOBODY RE-ASKS. TLC runs ONCE, at bake time, on a dev box. swipe/level0/bake.sh writes the measured exit codes into ITEMS.tsv fields 6, 7 and 8 and never runs again. The phone reads a baked table: claim text, swipe direction, flash. No model checker, no JVM, no round trip. swipe/README.md:6 already states it and the epic's mechanic paragraph does too.

THE GAP, measured 2026-10-18. git ls-files returns ZERO files matching html, js, css, jsx, ts or tsx in the whole repo. swipe/ is four files: README.md, level0/ITEMS.tsv, level0/TEMPLATES.tsv, level0/bake.sh. There is no deliver-swipe.sh among the six delivery channels. The epic has 11 children, 8 of them closed, and not one is the thing a person touches.

THAT IS tla-rrwl'S SHAPE, which is open and P1 and says 'the problems shipped without the interface a person uses to work them'. Same failure, second channel, and this time the corpus is 240 items that nobody can read. Worth noting that the tracker recorded everything about this epic except that it had no reader.

WHERE IT GOES. mkdocs-material, site_url https://fkberthold.github.io/tla-puzzles/. docs/ is GENERATED and gitignored (.gitignore:28), produced by scripts/build-docs.sh. The precedent is the reading channel: tla-fwkz.1 gave reading/ its own section in that script, at scripts/build-docs.sh:942, and its bead title was 'publish it phone-first'. Follow that shape.

WHAT IS NEW AND HAS NO PRECEDENT HERE. Every page this site has ever published is markdown. This one needs JavaScript, because a swipe is an interaction rather than a link. Two hazards follow.

1. The theme runs navigation.instant (mkdocs.yml features), which is SPA-style page loading. A naive inline script runs once on first load and never again when the reader navigates to the page. mkdocs-material documents the subscription hook for this. Do not discover it by hand.
2. tla-9t76 is OPEN: nothing in this repo runs mkdocs build --strict, so a broken internal link ships green. A page that is mostly a script is worse under that gap than a markdown page is.

THE CORPUS IS A TSV AND THE PAGE NEEDS IT AS DATA. 240 items at five reader-facing fields is roughly 60 KB. Embedding it in the page or emitting a JSON beside it are both fine and the choice is the author's. What is NOT fine is the page reading field 5, the kind, or field 10, the vacuity witness. The stem-blind gate already asserts that no witness and no flash text reaches the stem file, and the same separation has to hold here or the answer is in the page source.

OPEN, AND NOT FOR THIS BEAD TO SETTLE ALONE: level 1 items need a MODEL SCREEN and a PIN, which level 0 items do not have. Central rendered one by hand on 2026-10-18 to settle the epic's T2 thread and it ran about 14 lines for the simplest usable model. tla-7xql.4 is measuring real model-screen line counts and will report them. A reader built for one-line items will not carry a model screen, so read .4's numbers before fixing the layout.

Files: scripts/build-docs.sh, swipe/ (new reader assets), mkdocs.yml

RED: INVARIANT: the published swipe page serves an item from the shipped corpus, records the reader's swipe against the baked verdict, and its source carries neither field 5 nor field 10.
notes:
2026-10-18, FRANK ASKED FOR A BOOKMARK: 'It would likely be useful to have some way to bookmark where I was on a course of study with it.'

THAT IS NOT A CONVENIENCE, IT IS tla-7xql.6'S INPUT. .6 asks whether the swipe rung moves the recall rung, and its own description calls it the question the whole epic exists to answer, one the literature could not settle. Answering it means correlating swipe performance against recall performance over time. Recall already keeps that record: ~/tla-practice/recall/REPS.tsv at 293 lines and MISSES.tsv at 181. Drill keeps PROGRESS.tsv and LAST-SERVED. EVERY CHANNEL IN THIS PROJECT RECORDS PROGRESS AS A TSV IN THE PRACTICE TREE.

AND A PUBLISHED PAGE CANNOT WRITE THERE, which is the cost of the Published ruling arriving before this request did. A static page on GitHub Pages has no server and no filesystem. Its only durable store is browser localStorage, which is per-device, per-browser and per-origin: a bookmark made on the phone does not reach the laptop, and clearing site data clears it.

CENTRAL'S READ, and it is cheap enough that it should just be built this way. Two layers.

1. localStorage is the LIVE state. It is what makes the page resume where he left off, and it needs no interaction.
2. A one-click EXPORT writes a SWIPE.tsv in the same shape the other channels use, which he drops into ~/tla-practice/swipe/. A Blob download is an ordinary browser capability and needs no server.

That keeps the published ruling, gives him the bookmark he asked for, and leaves .6 answerable without anybody hand-transcribing a browser's storage.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOULD HOLD, so one table serves all three uses: item id, timestamp, the swipe he gave, and whether it matched the baked verdict. Resume reads the last row. A review queue reads the mismatches, which is D4 and L2 on the epic extended past one session. .6 reads the whole thing. Recording only a resume point would serve the smallest of the three.

NOT SETTLED HERE: whether the export is manual or whether something later reconciles it into the practice tree automatically. Manual is the honest starting point, and scripts/verify-delivery.sh deliberately has no opinion about a file the repo does not generate.
2026-10-18, FRANK AMENDED CENTRAL'S READ AND IT IS BETTER: 'I would suggest instead having that, but with an import to local state, this will only ever be used on a phone browser.'

So the round trip is EXPORT AND IMPORT, not export alone. Central had the export as a one-way feed into tla-7xql.6's measurement. Adding the import inverts which side is authoritative.

WHAT THAT CHANGES. localStorage stops being the record and becomes a CACHE. ~/tla-practice/swipe/SWIPE.tsv becomes the durable store, which puts this channel back inside the convention every other channel follows rather than beside it. A cleared browser, an evicted origin or a new phone all stop being data loss and become an import.

THREE THINGS THE PAGE NOW OWES THAT IT DID NOT BEFORE.

1. It must render correctly with localStorage EMPTY and say so, because empty is now an ordinary state rather than a first run. The import control has to be reachable from that state.
2. THE EXPORTED FORMAT IS A CONTRACT RATHER THAN A DUMP, because the page reads back what it wrote. It needs a version marker and an import that refuses a file it cannot read instead of silently starting over. Silently starting over is indistinguishable from working, which is the failure shape this project keeps finding.
3. Import must tolerate a hand-edited file. The practice tree is where Frank works and a TSV sitting in it will get opened.

AND THE PHONE IS THE ONLY TARGET, stated plainly: 'this will only ever be used on a phone browser.' That settles the per-device worry central raised, since there is one device. It also fixes the LAYOUT target. tla-7xql.4 is measuring model-screen line counts right now and those numbers are to be read against a phone viewport, not a desktop one. A model screen that fits a laptop and scrolls on a phone fails this channel, because the whole rung is built on running at flow speed.

Browser file input works on both mobile platforms, so the import needs no server either.
close_reason:
Landed at merge eee9555, registry row and README section added at 8148330.

Frank ruled published rather than delivered, localStorage with BOTH export and import, and the phone as the only target. This is the one rung that puts no files in ~/tla-practice.

SIX FIELDS SHIP AND FOUR DO NOT. Central verified independently rather than reading the report: the emitted payload is 52461 bytes, carries zero occurrences of kind, rc_claim, rc_wf and vacuity, and zero of the 30 vacuity witness texts. The baked verdict ships and is the answer, because a page with no server cannot grade without it.

THE RECORD IS A FILE AND THE BROWSER IS A CACHE, which was Frank's amendment to central's read. SWIPE.tsv carries its SWIPEFMT version as DATA rather than a comment so it survives a hand edit that strips comments. The import refuses a file it cannot read, names the line and the reason, and MERGES on item and timestamp so local work is never destroyed.

A LOCAL SERVER CANNOT TEST THIS PAGE, and that is the finding to carry. The theme's instant navigation matches a clicked link against its sitemap after overwriting protocol and hostname and never the port, so on 127.0.0.1 nothing matches and every link falls through to a full document load. Three local runs looked fine and said nothing. mkdocs serve has the same hole. The real reading came from headless Chromium serving the actual site_url.

TWO OF THE GATE'S FIVE RED RUNS CAUGHT DEFECTS IN THE GATE RATHER THAN THE PRODUCT, and both generalize. The shape check selected on a line starting with the id, so an item that gained a key AHEAD of the id stopped matching the selector and was never examined, and its own negative control walked through it. And a grep for document$ over a file whose header explains at length what document$ is for stayed green when the subscription was deleted. A TEXT GATE OVER A WELL-COMMENTED FILE MEASURES THE COMMENTS.

mkdocs build --strict is clean over the whole site, three runs. That bears on tla-9t76, which is open: wiring --strict into cibuild phase 4 costs one flag and nothing else today.

SCOPED TO LEVEL 0 ON PURPOSE. Level 1 items need a model screen and tla-7xql.4 measured those at 4 to 21 nonblank lines, 0 to 22 across all 33 models. The reader leaves room for one without designing it. That is the follow-up.

title: The level 0 corpus has no unparsed item, so the fourth channel row ships unexercised
description:
Follows tla-7xql.10, where Frank ruled on 2026-10-18 that rc 150 is a
down-swipe item with its own field 5 value. That bead builds the CHANNEL:
bake.sh maps 150, swipe/README.md states the row, and the gate proves it
through a fixture. It deliberately ships no corpus item of the new kind.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT RATHER THAN DONE AT ONCE. The shipped mix is 18 true, 18
false, 6 vacuous, 6 illformed per template. That is n 48 and a 0.3750 base
rate, and the stem-blind power table in swipe/README.md is computed from
exactly those numbers. Adding a fifth kind moves the mix, the base rate and
the detection floor together. The last time n moved it broke four gate
assertions, every one of them mine, so this is not a theoretical worry.

THE QUESTION. Does the shipped corpus gain unparsed items, and if so how many
per template and what happens to the mix?

Three shapes:

1. NONE. The row stays a mapping the bake supports and no reader ever meets.
Cheapest. The row is then a fixture-backed path with no shipped instance.

2. REPLACE RATHER THAN ADD. Convert some illformed items to unparsed, keeping
6 down-kind items per template and the 0.3750 base rate fixed. No arithmetic
moves anywhere, and the corpus teaches the distinction.

3. ADD. The mix becomes 18/18/6/6/N, n rises, the base rate and the detection
floor both move, and every number in the README power table needs recomputing
along with the four gate assertions keyed on them.

MY READ, and it is a read. Shape 2. It keeps every gate number fixed while
putting the lesson in front of a reader. The six items the tla-7xql.7 author
replaced are the obvious source, since each was a real precedence trap that
went one step further than intended. T2 is the operator-precedence family and
is where they belong.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS. A generator working T2 will meet
parse failures constantly, which is the argument tla-7xql.10 already makes. A
channel row with no shipped instance has never been read by anybody, so
nothing says the explanation column reads well for that kind, and the first
reader to meet one meets it in generated output.

Files: swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv, swipe/README.md, harness/test-swipe-level0.sh, harness/test-swipe-stemblind.sh

RED: INVARIANT: every kind named in the channel table has at least one shipped item, or is recorded in the table as deliberately unshipped with its reason.
notes:
2026-10-18, FRANK RULED: SHAPE 2, CONVERT. 'I'm ok with convert.' So the corpus gains unparsed items by converting existing illformed rows rather than adding new ones. Down stays at 12 per template, the base rate stays 0.3750, and no gate number moves.

CENTRAL'S CALL ON THE COUNT, which Frank did not take and which is reversible: one per template, five in total, leaving 5 illformed plus 6 vacuous plus 1 unparsed per template. Where a template cannot carry a genuine parse trap in its own subject matter without becoming a T2 item wearing another label, it is recorded in the channel table as deliberately unshipped with its reason, which the RED line allows.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH, and it is why convert was the cheap shape. illformed and unparsed both bake to down, so field 6 is unchanged for every row. The stem-blind gate reads field 6, so its per-template base rates and the whole power table in swipe/README.md should be byte-identical after the conversion. The no-perfect-correlation invariant also correlates on field 6 and is likewise untouched. A reading that MOVED is a finding, not a pass.

THE MACHINERY WAS ALREADY BUILT BY tla-7xql.10 and this bead adds no plumbing. bake.sh maps (150, 150) to unparsed at line 451, runs unparsed items singly at line 406 because SANY refuses the whole module rather than one row, and controls both directions: a typo inside an item declared true reddens the holds batch, and an item declared unparsed whose claim parses reddens its own probe. So this bead is corpus authoring plus one gate assertion.

Dispatched to a worker 2026-10-18 with the RED line to gate: every kind named in the channel table has at least one shipped item, or is recorded as deliberately unshipped with its reason. The assertion reads the real ITEMS.tsv, which section 10 of harness/test-swipe-level0.sh deliberately does not.
close_reason:
Landed at the merge of worktree-agent-acd3e9877a4e50cfb into main, commit baa7506 on the branch. Frank ruled convert on 2026-10-18 and all five templates carried a parse trap in their own subject matter, so the unshipped escape the RED line allows went unused.

The mix is 18 true, 18 false, 6 vacuous, 5 illformed, 1 unparsed per template. Right, left and down stay 18, 18 and 12, so the 0.3750 base rate did not move and neither did the power table.

CENTRAL VERIFIED THE NO-MOVE CLAIM rather than reading it off the report: harness/swipe/stemblind.sh probe run on main and on the worker's tree. base, best, feature and null95 identical in all five templates, verdict clear, flagged 0 both times. Three p-values and two feature counts moved, which is correct, since those read the claim text and five claims were replaced.

T4's ITEM IS A JUXTAPOSITION ERROR, NOT A PRECEDENCE TRAP, and the worker flagged it as a deviation from the brief. Head <<1, 2, 3>> fails because TLA+ has no juxtaposition. There is no precedence trap in T4's own vocabulary: \o associates and parses at rc 0. Central accepted it, since the RED line prefers a genuine item to a T2 item wearing another label.

ONE THING LEFT UNGATED ON PURPOSE, reported by the worker. The assertion is at the kind level, which is what the RED line says. The per-template spread is printed and not asserted, so an author who drops T3's unparsed item keeps the suite green on the strength of T1's. All five ship one today. If per-template coverage is wanted it is a small follow-up and the printed spread is the key to hang it on.

title: 16 items per template cannot decide whether a swipe template has an artifact
description:
Measured 2026-10-18 by the tla-7xql.1 author while building the stem-blind gate. The gate works and its arithmetic says it cannot see what it was built to see at the corpus size that exists.

THE NUMBERS, printed by harness/swipe/stemblind.sh power on every run rather
than asserted from a tolerance somebody picked:

  items  crit  critacc  tolerance  detectable at 0.80 power
     16    10   0.6250     0.2500                    0.6900
     32    18   0.5625     0.1875                    0.6190
     48    25   0.5208     0.1458                    0.5705
     64    31   0.4844     0.1094                    0.5295
     80    38   0.4750     0.1000                    0.5160

At 16 items a judge needs 10 right, which is 25 POINTS over the 0.3750 base
rate, and an artifact has to make the label 69.0 percent predictable before
the gate fires at 80 percent power. Gururangan's own result was 67 percent
against a 34.3 percent baseline, so THE PUBLISHED FINDING THIS GATE EXISTS TO
CATCH WOULD SIT RIGHT AT THE EDGE OF WHAT 16 ITEMS CAN DETECT.

AND IT IS ALREADY BITING. T5 reads 0.6250 on the token 17, which is 25 points
over its floor, with a cause the author could name. The gate cannot call it
because 0.6250 is under the 69.0 floor. So the instrument is seeing a signal
it is not allowed to report, which is exactly the state this bead fixes.

THE FIX IS ITEMS, NOT A LOOSER TOLERANCE. 48 per template gets the tolerance
to 14.6 points, which is where a Gururangan-sized artifact becomes detectable.
That is 240 items against today's 80.

AND POOLING IS NOT THE FIX, although it is tempting. Pooling all five
templates reaches a 10.0-point tolerance immediately, and tla-7xql.1's bead
forbids it for a stated reason: the artifact is template-local, so a pooled
number hides a bad template behind good ones. Doing it would trade the thing
the gate measures for a number that looks better.

ORDER. This should land before any swipe corpus ships to a phone, and before
.4 or .5 author their own items, because those will be authored at whatever
size this bead settles. The epic's own L9 says the gate must exist before any
corpus ships; this is the other half of that, which is that the gate must be
able to decide.

Files: swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv, swipe/level0/TEMPLATES.tsv, swipe/level0/bake.sh

RED: INVARIANT: every generator template ships enough items that the
stem-blind gate's detectable-at-0.80-power figure is at or below the accuracy
a published premise-blind classifier reached on the task it was copied from.
close_reason: Merged at 76ae1ed, gates repaired at 9b70733. 240 items, 48 per template against 16, so the stem-blind tolerance goes 25 points to 14.6 and detection 0.6900 to 0.5705, which puts Gururangan's 0.67 clear of the floor rather than at the edge. Mix holds at 18/18/6/6 so the 0.3750 base rate does not move. THE PROBE IS NOT WHAT CAUGHT THE AUTHOR'S OWN HABITS, which is the finding: it was clear through every draft, and tla-7xql.8's RED line read directly found four violations, two on the corpus that had already shipped including a 3-item perfect correlation in T2 nobody had written down. So that invariant is stricter than the gate at n=48 and is wired to nothing, filed as tla-7xql.9. The vacuity sentinel was REMOVED rather than varied, which is better than the brief asked for, since five varied sentinels is five rules. Planted signature re-measured at both sizes: a token must be about half as widespread at 48 before the probe can call it. Nine of 160 items contradicted the author's field-5 prediction, six of them parse failures at rc 150 which is not a row in the level 0 channel, filed as tla-7xql.10. Every T5 dividend is non-negative so no item needed a div caveat.

title: recall-gate.sh check 4 validates a field-7 pattern that is there and cannot see one that is missing
description:
Measured 2026-10-18 by the tla-1sh7.7 author, which reported rather than edited because harness/recall-gate.sh was outside its footprint.

harness/recall-gate.sh:940 reads

  [ -n "$req" ] || continue

So check 4 validates every field-7 pattern that IS present and skips every
row that carries none. The worker proved the consequence on a mirror rather
than reasoning about it: stripping R023, R045 and R110 back to six fields
leaves 99 six-field rows, and the gate still reports '0 finding(s), VERDICT
OK'.

TWO THINGS GO UNNOTICED BECAUSE OF IT.

1. This adoption being undone. Twenty-four rows now carry a pattern and
nothing would report their loss.
2. A NEW rep in K001, K007, K009 or K071 to K076 landing with no pattern,
which is the likelier of the two and the one that matters more. The whole
point of field 7 on those families is that value equality cannot see the
construct, so an ungated row in them is a rep a wrong answer passes.

WHAT I WOULD BUILD. A seventh check in harness/recall-gate.sh that holds a
list of construct ids requiring a pattern and fails on any REP row in one of
them with an empty field 7. The list is the gate's own, not derived from the
table, because deriving it from the table is what makes an omission
invisible.

THE ALTERNATIVE is to invert check 4's skip so an empty field 7 is a finding
everywhere. I would not take that: 96 of the 120 rows legitimately carry no
pattern, since value equality is sufficient for them, and a gate that fires
on all 96 is a gate somebody switches off.

Files: harness/recall-gate.sh (CENTRALLY OWNED, report not edit), harness/test-recall-gate.sh

RED: INVARIANT: a REP row whose construct is in the requires-a-pattern list
and whose field 7 is empty is a finding, and the gate names the row id.
close_reason: Closed at d3cc895, with its assertions corrected at 35357e2. harness/recall-gate.sh now emits REQUIRES-ABSENT when a REP row's construct needs a field-7 pattern and has none, so the 24-row adoption from tla-1sh7.7 is gated in both directions. Measured on a mirror: stripping R023, R045 and R110 back to six fields gives three findings and VERDICT FINDINGS where the gate previously reported 0 findings and VERDICT OK. KEYED ON THE INVENTORY'S CONSTRUCT NAME, not its id, because the first version was id-keyed and called the suite's own clean control a finding: drill/INVENTORY.md reads K001 as Operator definition and the fixture inventory reads it as Set literal. The name list carries a rename tripwire that emits UNCHECKED when a listed name stops resolving, with a total miss treated as a different inventory rather than a rename, which is what keeps the fixture green. 245 assertions to 253, including two controls and one assertion I had to correct after watching it fail: the accept-control run exits 99 for the tripwire rather than 0, and 99 is the stronger claim.

title: Subscript items: the one lesson nobody can state and everybody writes
description:
Frank's third pick, and the framing both he and central started with was
WRONG. Worth stating because it is the kind of mistake that survives into a
corpus.

NOT AN ITEM: "insert a stuttering step, does the formula survive". Inserting a
stutter changes the truth value of nothing expressible in TLA+. That is
stutter invariance and it is a theorem, so the answer is always yes.

WHAT IS GENERABLE IS THE SUBSCRIPT, and it is sharp. Measured on one step,
(7,7,7) to (9,7,7), where a heap GREW so Take does not hold:

    [][Take]_<<a, b, c>>   rc 13   the whole tuple moved, Take must hold
    [][Take]_<<a>>         rc 13   a moved, the subscript does not excuse it
    [][Take]_<<b>>         rc  0   b did not move, a stutter on b, vacuous
    [][Take]_<<b, c>>      rc  0   neither moved, still a stutter
    [][Take]_<<a, b, c>>   rc  0   over a whole-tuple stutter

FOUR ITEMS ON ONE STEP WITH THE SUBSCRIPT AS THE ONLY VARIABLE, and two of
them are true for a reason the reader has to find.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST VALUABLE OF THE THREE. The corpus survey in
.claude/rules/tla-practice.md section 2 measured 1,182 subscript sites across
334 published modules and found 906 of them, 77 percent, are the bare token
`vars`. Almost everyone writes the safe default. Only 16 box sites in the
entire corpus use a proper subset, and the rule that makes them sound is
stated in Specifying Systems at p.123: a narrower subscript is sound when v
covers every variable the action mentions. That is exactly what these four
items teach, and nothing else in this project drills it.

A BONUS KIND FROM THE SAME MACHINERY: which of these is even a formula.

    []Take     (box of a bare action)        rc 150 PARSE_ERROR
    []TypeOK   (box of a state predicate)    rc 12

The two look identical in shape and one is not TLA+. That belongs under the
down swipe, which D3 already merged.

COST. 439 distinct (action, non-empty-subscript) pairs exist across the 33
models, each about 0.35 s singly or riding a batch.

Depends on step pinning: Ini fixes the state, Nxt fixes its successor, the
claim is [][A]_v declared as a PROPERTY. Hazard H1 on the epic applies, read
{12, 13} as one answer.

Files: swipe/ (new), harness/test-swipe-subscript.sh, scripts/test
close_reason:
Landed at merge eeb301f. 48 items at 18 right, 18 left, 12 down, base rate 0.3750, kind spread under down matching level 1's at 4 vacuous, 3 illformed, 3 wronglevel, 2 unparsed. Gate is 79 assertions, read 57.6 s on a quiet box against an 81.0 budget.

SIX EXIT CODES, AND 151 APPEARS WHERE LEVEL 1 CANNOT REACH IT: 0, 12, 13, 75, 150 and 151. Level 1's write-up records that 151 never shows there, because a level 1 claim is state-dependent and TLC cannot fold it. A level 2 claim can. Both 12 and 13 appear, which is hazard H1 doing exactly what the epic warns about.

RECOVERED RATHER THAN REPORTED. A power cut killed the authoring session before it committed, and the branch sat at its base SHA so git showed nothing. The work was whole in seven uncommitted worktree files: the corpus fully baked with zero unmeasured fields, and the gate passed 79 assertions on the first run central gave it. Central committed and merged it as the author's integrator, and the commit body says so.

One finding in its comment block that outlives the bead: a div by zero inside a STEP formula reads rc 255, where every other evaluation failure at this rung reads 75. Registered in harness/div-sites.tsv with that reason.

title: ENABLED items: does this action fire here
description:
Frank's second pick. It asks whether a transition is POSSIBLE rather than
whether a predicate holds, and people routinely conflate "the guard is true"
with "the action can fire". Nothing else in this project's five rungs touches
it.

MEASURED. 72 arity-0 actions swept over state grids:

    usable, 20 to 80 percent enabled   24
    lopsided but mixed                 13
    enabled everywhere                 35
    failed to run                       0

THE 35 DEGENERATE ONES ARE ALMOST ENTIRELY `Next`. ENABLED Next is false only
at a terminal state, so it is a structural dud and the generator should skip
it by name rather than filtering it by balance.

What is left is good: Terminating in PlusCal models at 2.9 to 19 percent,
individual labels (s0, s1, k0, k1 in Contend at 33.3 percent), TaskTake and
PollTake in Contention at 20 and 40 percent, Pop and Push in Brackets at 44
and 54 percent.

PARAMETERIZED ACTIONS WORK, arity 1 and 2, and so does quantifying over the
parameter:

    ENABLED read(w1)              13 / 84
    ENABLED write(w2)             24 / 84
    ENABLED Pass(p1, p2)          50 / 120
    ENABLED Enter(p1)              2 / 26
    \E q \in Proc : ENABLED Enter(q)   4 / 26

That adds 37 parameterized actions to the 72, each instantiable several ways.

A SIBLING ITEM KIND THAT COMES FREE: is this state terminal, which is
~ENABLED Next. One line, and the concept is already live in the corpus, since
79 of 337 published configs in the survey set CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE on purpose.
Distinguishing stuck from finished is a real skill.

Honors D7 on the epic: show the definitions, the CONSTANTS and the state. Do
not show Init, Next or Spec.

Files: swipe/ (new), harness/test-swipe-enabled.sh, scripts/test
close_reason:
Landed at merge 11960de, with the registry wiring and a correction at 8148330. Pilot template E1 ships 48 items over 7 models at 18 right, 18 left, 12 down, so the base rate stays 0.3750 and the power table transfers unchanged.
