title: The stem-blind gate: prove an item needs its model
description:
THIS BLOCKS SHIPPING ANY CORPUS. Build it before or with the first generator,
not after.

A machine-generated false item leaves a signature in how it was generated, and
a reader who detects the signature scores well without reading the model. The
accuracy metric cannot tell the difference.

MEASURED, on a task with this exact label set. Gururangan, Swayamdipta, Levy,
Schwartz, Bowman and Smith, 2018, NAACL: a classifier that NEVER SEES THE
PREMISE scored 67 percent on SNLI and 53 percent on MultiNLI against a 34.3
percent majority baseline. The giveaways were habits of the people writing the
items, negation correlating with contradiction and so on. Poliak and others
found the same across 10 NLI corpora the same year. All had passed expert
review. Their conclusion was that reported progress on the task had been
substantially overestimated.

THE GATE. Hide the model, show only the claim and its tag, predict the label.
Whatever that scores above the chance floor is the CEILING on how much of the
measured accuracy reflects reading the model.

RUN IT PER GENERATOR TEMPLATE. The artifact is template-local, so a pooled
number hides a bad template behind good ones.

The chance floor is not 1/3 in general. It is the base rate of the most common
label in that template's output, which is what the 34.3 percent above is.
Compute it from the corpus rather than assuming a uniform mix.

A classifier is not required for v1. Central or Frank judging a sample is a
real measurement if the sample size is stated and the judge has not seen the
items before. The point is the comparison, not the instrument.

This is gate-don't-advise, which this project already insists on. An advisory
script nobody runs is how the drift comes back.

Files: harness/test-swipe-stemblind.sh, scripts/test

RED: INVARIANT: for every generator template, a label predicted from the claim
alone scores no better than that template's own most-common-label base rate,
within a stated tolerance, and the gate fails when it does better.
close_reason: Merged at ae0895c. 46 assertions over harness/swipe/stemblind.sh, registered fast at 6.5 s, and it starts no JVM. THE BEAD'S DESIGN DOES NOT SURVIVE A LEVEL 0 CORPUS, since a level 0 claim is self-contained and there is no model to hide, so the brief carried the adaptation: the question becomes whether the label is predictable from the claim's SURFACE without evaluating it, which is what Gururangan's finding was always about. Hiding the model was never the leak here, the ID was, because ids run in kind order inside a template. The worker's own hash reproduced that kind order exactly on its first emit and it caught that itself. Deterministic half runs with no judge: a per-template decision stump scored by leave-one-out against a permutation threshold, with the token bag deliberately not hand-picked. Planted artifact goes 0.5000 to 0.7500 at p 0.0090 and flags one template with its signature named. A 16-defect mutation sweep found two real defects in the worker's own suite, one of which COULD NOT FAIL. No template is flagged. Two findings filed: tla-7xql.7 because 16 items per template cannot detect a Gururangan-sized artifact, and tla-7xql.8 because T5 and the vacuity sentinel already carry a signature the gate can see and is not allowed to report.

title: [epic] The swipe rung: a phone recognition channel graded by TLC
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: epic, and its children have ordering constraints the detector cannot see.

Promoted 2026-10-17 from the exploration in
drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_c738cb682d1cd0cf1754921e, which carries the
measurements, the literature and the prior art. Read it before working any
child. This description is the contract, not the reasoning.

## The mechanic

A model, then a stream of single lines. Per line the reader swipes right for
true, left for false, down for not-a-true-or-false-claim, up to review. Ten to
twenty lines per model. Verdicts are baked at generation time so the phone
runs no model checker.

## Decisions locked by Frank, 2026-10-17

D1  The CONSTANTS stay visible. They change every answer.
D2  The model is shown with its INVARIANT and PROPERTY declarations stripped,
    from the .cfg and the .tla both. A model that ships its obligations
    asserts its own answers. Questions carry their definitions inline.
D3  Vacuous and ill-formed share the down swipe. Forced, not chosen: without
    merging, a vacuous item has no correct swipe at all.
D4  Swipe up carries the long explanation of the last WRONG answer, below the
    model, held until the next wrong one. AMENDED by the literature: the
    one-line correction goes in the flash as well. See L2 below.
D5  The item's kind is tagged in the question. It makes the question
    well-posed and it is where D3's lost discrimination goes.
D6  Build level 0, ENABLED and subscript items first.
D7  A pinned item shows the model's definitions, its CONSTANTS and the pin. It
    does NOT show Init, Next, Spec or the fairness conjunct. Showing the
    machine invites a reachability check that is not the question, is not
    graded and has no feedback channel.

## The two axes

LEVEL, what gets pinned. TLA+'s own level calculus:

  0  constant     pin nothing, no model screen at all
  1  state        pin a state
  2  action       pin a STEP
  3  temporal     pin a LASSO

QUESTION KIND, what is asked: does it hold, is it ENABLED, is this terminal,
is this reachable, does P imply Q, is it vacuous, is it well formed.

## Three hazards every generator carries, all measured

H1  NEVER predict rc 12 against 13. The split holds only for specs without a
    fairness conjunct and a pinned behavior is fair by construction. Read
    {0} = holds, {12, 13} = refuted. Bead tla-vzu3 is open on this.
H2  A pinned behavior needs a genuinely temporal satisfiability probe. An Init
    admitting nothing passes EVERY liveness check silently, including
    []<>(i # i). This is the only measured failure mode that ships a WRONG
    item rather than a boring one.
H3  Pinning needs exactly one V-changing successor per state. A stuttering
    self-loop is harmless. One real branch means a SET of behaviors was pinned
    and TLC finds the member that refutes you.

## What the literature changed

L2  The bare verdict sits on the measured floor of feedback effectiveness.
    Measured on this task shape: falsehood reproduced later at .19 with no
    feedback, .15 with a bare verdict, .04 with the verdict plus the
    correction. So the correction goes in the flash.
L3  Rowland 2014: without feedback, practice at or below 50 percent success
    gives g = 0.03. With feedback, g = 0.73 at any success rate. Feedback is
    what makes this format work, not an enhancement to it.
L7  The mix must carry true and false substantively. A true-heavy corpus
    transfers back to recognition and nowhere else.
L9  The stem-blind gate. See the child bead. This is the one that must exist
    before any corpus ships.

## Open threads carried from the exploration

T2  Nobody has looked at a RENDERED item. D2, D7 and the pin interact and are
    consistent on paper only.
T3  The item mix has no number in the literature and the exploration found
    none. It is a generator constraint somebody has to choose.
T4  "Is this state reachable" is a different item type with its own verdict
    channel, not a swipe. Out of scope here. File it if it is wanted.

## What this reopens, and it is not neutral

tla-fwkz.2 was settled by Frank on 2026-10-13: "CONSTRUCT EXPOSURE, not
recognition practice. So NO comprehension question and NO answer key." Both
tla-fwkz and tla-fwkz.2 are open P1. This epic takes that channel's models,
its phone bound and its delivery surface and puts a question on them. Two
findings in the read/write split drawer also run against it: single-line units
showed no correlation with code writing, and production-trained learners beat
recognition-trained ones on receptive measures too. The argument in favor is
that a baked verdict is the only channel here that cannot be self-scored by a
faculty that is already miscalibrated.

Files: (per child)
notes:
2026-10-18, central. H1 AND H2 BOTH MOVED. tla-lj1n and tla-vzu3 are closed at db5f869 and the measurement widens both hazards.

H1 AS WRITTEN UNDERSTATES IT. The contract says the 12/13 split holds only
for specs without a fairness conjunct. It is any LIVENESS conjunct. WF, SF and
a bare []<>(s = 1) all move the same claim from 12 to 13, and only one of the
three is a fairness operator. The instruction the contract gives is unchanged
and still right: read {0} = holds and {12, 13} = refuted, never predict which.

THERE ARE THREE CHANNELS, NOT TWO, and the third one matters for item design.

1. The invariant channel, 12, and nothing moves it. A box over a state
   predicate gets lifted outright and prints 'Invariant P is violated' even
   for a .cfg that said PROPERTY []P.
2. The safety channel, 12, and any liveness conjunct takes it away.
3. The liveness channel, 13, everything else, INCLUDING A BARE STATE
   PREDICATE UNDER PROPERTY refuted by the initial state.

CELL 3 IS THE ONE A GENERATOR WILL TRIP ON. A level-1 item pins a state and
asks whether a state predicate holds there. Written as PROPERTY P it reads 13,
written as PROPERTY []P it reads 12, and written as INVARIANT P it reads 12.
Same question, same answer, three codes. So the generator must fix one form
and keep it, and the exploration's F1 already picked the INVARIANT route for
pinned states. That pick now has a second reason behind it.

H2 HAS A SECOND ROUTE AND A SHIPPED DETECTOR. The exploration found the
hazard through an Init admitting nothing. WF over an action that
[][Next]_vars forbids gets to the same place with a healthy state space and a
configured model. harness/vacuity.sh's VECTOR 4 is already the probe and
reads the same two codes, so .4 and .5 should drive that rather than writing
a third satisfiability probe.

AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES H2 WORTH GATING RATHER THAN NOTING. An empty
spec exits 0 on every temporal property, including []<>FALSE, while still
exiting 12 on a lifted invariant. A corpus checked only through lifted
invariants looks healthy while every liveness obligation on it is vacuous.

ONE MORE CELL WORTH AN ITEM. A safety-shaped temporal conjunct inside
SPECIFICATION is refused at 255, pointing at the conjunct's own source span
with 'TLC cannot handle the temporal formula'. That is a down-swipe item with
a real lesson in it, and it reads as an author typo rather than as TLC
declining the shape.

The grid is in harness/verdict.sh and eleven of its cells are pinned in
harness/test-verdict.sh.
2026-10-18, central, after .2 and .3 landed. FOUR THINGS FROM HAVING REAL ITEMS IN HAND, and three of them are decisions only Frank can take.

ONE: D5 AND D3 CANNOT MEAN THE SAME FIELD, AND AS WRITTEN THEY DO. D3 puts
vacuous and ill-formed on one swipe and says the cost is that the swipe stops
distinguishing two mistakes, so 'the item's kind must be kept in the data'.
D5 then says to tag the kind in the question. But the KIND IS THE ANSWER:
tagging 'this one is false' in the stem gives the item away and the accuracy
measurement collapses to nothing.

The .2 author split it into two fields and shipped that way: 'ask' is what the
reader sees and takes two values, holds or implies, while 'kind' is what the
data keeps and takes four, true / false / vacuous / illformed. I think that is
what D5 meant and it wants rewording rather than reversing, but which field D5
named is Frank's call and the corpus already depends on the answer.

TWO: LEVEL 0 CANNOT SETTLE T2 AT ALL, and shipping the first corpus reads like
progress on it. T2 is 'nobody has looked at a RENDERED item, D2 and D7 and the
pin are consistent on paper only'. A level 0 item has NO MODEL SCREEN, no pin,
nothing to strip and no CONSTANTS, so it exercises none of the three. T2 stays
open until .4 or .5 renders an item with a model on screen, and D1's 'the
CONSTANTS stay visible' is satisfied by construction here rather than by
display: the generated modules declare no CONSTANT and no VARIABLE, and the
gate asserts both keywords are absent.

THREE: L2's .04 MAY NOT TRANSFER TO A TRUE ITEM. L2 measured the verdict plus
the CORRECTED CLAIM, tracking whether a falsehood is reproduced later. The 30
false and 20 down items have something to correct. The 30 true ones have no
corrected claim, only a reason they hold. The author wrote every flash field
as 'the one line that gets it right' and said plainly it would not assume .04
carries. Worth a decision about what the flash says on a true item, because
'correct' is not a thing you can do to a true statement.

FOUR, AND THIS ONE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN A DECISION: D3's MERGE CUTS ACROSS
THE EXIT CODES AND NOTHING HAD WRITTEN THAT DOWN. At level 0 the channel is a
pair of ASSUME runs. Vacuous and ill-formed SHARE the down swipe with
DIFFERENT pairs, (0,0) against (10,10), while vacuous and plainly-true share
a pair with DIFFERENT swipes. The two partitions cross and neither refines
the other. That is why every item carries a per-item VACUITY WITNESS: a second
level 0 expression holding exactly when the item is vacuous, run in its own
batch, so the vacuous label has a TLC run behind it rather than an author's
word.

AND THE HAZARD LIST GAINS ONE. H1, H2 and H3 are all about pinned behaviors.
Level 0 pins nothing and still has a hazard: an evaluation error inside a
batched ASSUME aborts the WHOLE batch at rc 10, not 75, and only the items
before it print. So batch the well-formed and run suspected-ill-formed ones
singly. The .2 gate does that, 13 JVMs over 80 items.

READ FOR .1, WHICH IS NOW BUILDABLE. .2 ships five templates and bake.sh
--stats computes the most-common-label base rate per template from the corpus
rather than assuming uniform. It reads 37.5 percent in all five, close to the
34.3 percent SNLI baseline .1 cites. The uniformity is a property of authoring
to a 6/6/2/2 mix and NOT a measurement, so .1 should recompute it rather than
take the number.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING. .3's harness/levels/levels.sh landed after .2's corpus was
built, and it is a better instrument for .2's 'no variable, no prime' clause
than the text scan .2 shipped. Not wired, recorded in swipe/README.md. .2's
own text scan found 103 level 0 candidates in reading/ against this epic's 49,
so it used them to pick calibration targets rather than as a count, and .3's
semantic-tree reading says 49 is right for DEFINITIONS while 103 counts
something looser.
2026-10-18, FRANK SET THE PRIORITY: 'I want to prioritize getting the swipe system working, and getting it fully right.' The epic and .4, .5 and .11 moved P2 to P1. .6 stays P2 because it measures whether the rung moves the recall rung, which cannot run until the corpus has been used for a while. tla-mv4b stays P3: it touches the div tripwire inside harness/test-swipe-level0.sh and is a docs wording question, not channel work.
2026-10-18, FRANK RULED ON ONE AND THREE from the note above. Landed at 8ceac0d.

ONE, the two kind fields. The split stands and D5 wants rewording rather than reversing. Field 4 is the reader-visible ask, field 5 is the data's kind. The corpus has been built that way since .2, so the ruling changed the contract's wording in swipe/README.md and swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv and no row.

THREE, what field 11 says on a true item. It is now the FLASH rather than the correction: the correction on a false, vacuous or illformed item and the reason the claim holds on a true one. 90 of the 240 items are true and already carried a reason rather than an imitation correction, so the content was right and the contract was wrong. L2's .04 is now stated as covering 150 of 240 rows, since it measured whether a falsehood comes back. The field stays required on every row and the number no longer travels with it. Renamed in harness/test-swipe-level0.sh and harness/test-swipe-stemblind.sh, variable and control fixtures both. Nothing parses field 11 by name.

TWO stays as written: level 0 cannot settle T2 and shipping the first corpus is not progress on it.

ALSO 2026-10-18, AN ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION FROM FRANK that applies to every bead in this epic. He supplies ideas and takes decisions. The prose around them is central's. So a line reading 'Frank's D5 says X' is wrong twice over when X is central's wording of his decision, which is exactly how ONE above came to contradict itself. Write 'D5 as recorded' or 'the epic's D5' and keep the decision separate from the sentence carrying it.
2026-10-18, A POWER CUT KILLED TWO AUTHORING SESSIONS MID-FLIGHT, and both bodies of work survived. Recorded because the recovery shape is reusable and the diagnosis order mattered.

NEITHER WORKER HAD COMMITTED. Both worktree branches sat at the base they were cut from, d5338b0, so git showed nothing. The work was entirely in uncommitted worktree files: 4 files for tla-7xql.13 and 7 for tla-7xql.5.

WHAT SURVIVED INTACT, in both cases, was the CORPUS. Both were fully baked with zero unmeasured fields. tla-7xql.5 had 48 items at 18/18/12. tla-7xql.13 had 144 items at 48 per template across E1, E2 and E3. The bake is the expensive part and it was done.

WHAT DIED WAS THE INSTRUMENT, in one of the two. harness/test-swipe-enabled.sh was left with 'if want_corpus; then' opened at line 1152 and no matching fi, so the suite died at PARSE time and not one assertion ran. The file's tail was complete, so it read as whole on inspection and only bash -n found it. THAT IS THE FAILURE SHAPE TO REMEMBER: the corpus was finished and correct, and the only broken thing was the gate that would have said so.

THE DIAGNOSIS ORDER THAT WORKED, and it is worth following next time: git state first (nothing committed), then uncommitted file counts (substantial work), then the CORPUS measured directly with awk rather than through its gate (mix, counts, unbaked rows), and only then the gate. Running the gate first returns a syntax error that tells you nothing about whether the work is salvageable.

AND THE REPAIRED GATE THEN FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN ITSELF. Its premise-leak check scans the stem file for every model name. Key is a module name in this corpus, reading/state-space/04-key/Key.tla, and it is ALSO a CONSTANT declared by Overlay.tla and Ledger.tla. Seven E2 and E3 items quantify over that constant. A level 1 claim cannot be written without naming its own model's vocabulary, so the scan now skips a model name that any corpus model declares and PRINTS what it skipped. Key.tla declares CONSTANT Staff and no constant of its own name, so nothing about it ever reached a judge.

Both merged at eeb301f and 4f07dd5 with central as committer, and both commit bodies say so.

title: The wrong-answer report prints a TLC error on 84 of 120 reps
description:
Frank, 2026-10-17, working R018 in the delivered tree. He typed
`Parking["a"] = 3 /\ Parking["c"] = 3` where the row wanted b and c, so the
grade is right. What he was shown is not.

    you typed   Parking["a"] = 3 /\ Parking["c"] = 3
      FALSE
      Attempted to compute cardinality of the value
      FALSE
      (no count: TLC will not count that value, so it is not a set)

The value appears twice and a TLC error sits between the two copies. Nothing
went wrong. The second FALSE is TLC's echo of the operand inside its own error
message, not a second value.

## The mechanism

write_value_module (recall/recall.sh:1486) ends every probe with
`ASSUME PrintT(Cardinality(Shown))`. On any value that is not a set TLC emits
three lines:

    Error: Evaluating assumption line 7, col 8 to line 7, col 33 of module P failed.
    Attempted to compute cardinality of the value
    TRUE

printed_region (recall/recall.sh:1513) drops the first line on purpose and
keeps the other two. show_value then appends the parenthetical. So a reader
gets an error sentence and a duplicated value on every non-set answer.

## How many

84 of the 120 REP rows. Measured by building the probe module for each row's
canonical answer and recording TLC's exit code: 36 answers are sets, 84 are
not. The 36 are R003 R039 R041 R043 R044 R045 R060 R061 R062 R063 R066 R067
R069 R073 R074 R075 R076 R077 R078 R079 R080 R081 R082 R083 R084 R085 R086
R093 R094 R095 R096 R097 R098 R107 R108 R109.

The learner's own answer is probed separately and fails the same way
independently, so a boolean rep answered with a boolean shows the noise twice
over.

## Why the comment above printed_region argues the other way

It says the cardinality sentence "is the part that says what went wrong, and
it stays." That reasoning holds for an answer that was meant to be a set and
is not. It is wrong for a boolean or a string, where the count was never
meaningful and nothing went wrong, and that is 84 of 120 rows.

The parenthetical has the same problem. Telling a learner that TRUE "is not a
set" is true and useless.

## What I would do

When the probe exits nonzero, print the value and stop. Drop the TLC sentence,
drop its operand echo, drop the parenthetical. Keep the count only where it
succeeded, which is where it says something.

## Why no gate caught it

402 assertions and a 197 s corpus gate both green. Same shape as bd memory
a-gate-over-what-the-code-computes-never-sees: the gates check the exit code
and the grade, and nobody asserted on the block of text a wrong answer puts on
the screen.

Files: recall/recall.sh, harness/test-recall-runner.sh

RED: INVARIANT: a wrong-answer report for a rep whose value is not a set
contains no line matching 'Attempted to compute cardinality' and shows the
value exactly once.
close_reason: Duplicate of tla-1sh7.8 (filed by Frank 2026-10-16, same defect). Created by central 2026-10-17 before finding the existing bead; the 84-of-120 measurement was appended to tla-1sh7.8's notes rather than kept here. No work was done against this id and nothing references it, so there is no capture to file.

title: A rep asks for a name you cannot guess and a shape it never states
description:
Found by Frank on 2026-10-17 after tla-1sh7.12, working R119. Two things a
rep does not tell you that it has to.

1. THE NAMES IN SCOPE ARE UNGUESSABLE AND THE SESSION NEVER SHOWS THEM.

R119's prompt is "the balance after two has been paid into ann's account on
top of whatever was already there". The environment defines Balance,
Accounts, Kinds, Amounts and Entries. A reader has to produce `Balance`
exactly, and nothing in the prompt says it is capitalized that way.

Frank's own words: "there's no way I'd know it was capitalized, and in fact
it's more common for variables to be lowercase."

He is right that he could not know, and the corpus says his instinct is
backwards for TLA+ specifically: drill/study/STYLE.md measures constants at
134 of 140 CamelCase or ALLCAPS, snake_case 0, short-lowercase 6. So the
CONVENTION is learnable, and the specific names still are not guessable.

MEASURED: all 120 reps name an environment, 83 shunting and 37 ledger, and a
session prints the prompt alone. So this is every rep, not one.

SHOWING THE NAMES IS NOT A LEAK, and that is the whole reason this is
cheap. The names are the vocabulary, not the answer. Knowing that `Balance`
exists does not tell you to reach for EXCEPT, any more than the shunting
yard prompt naming wagons and tracks tells you to reach for a function set.
The thing that must stay hidden is field 6, and it stays hidden.

So print the environment's definitions with the prompt, or print them once
at the head of a session and name the environment per rep when it changes.
Prefer whichever reads better at seconds a rep, and say which you tried.
Note the env files are FRAGMENTS carrying their own comments, so the
comments probably want stripping.

2. NOTHING SAYS THE ANSWER IS AN EXPRESSION.

Frank read "the balance after two has been paid in" as asking for the
change, and wrote a primed assignment. His own reading of that: "a
reasonable person could argue that was a failure to understand the problem,
it doesn't say to update, just the pure value".

I think the prompt is defensible and the channel is not. Every one of the
120 reps goes into a scaffold as `Answer == <what was typed>`, so an action
can never be right anywhere at this rung, and nothing anywhere says so. That
makes it a property of the channel to state once rather than a wording
problem to fix 120 times.

One line at the head of a session is probably enough. Do not add it to each
prompt: the prompts are deliberately short and the constraint is global.

The deeper half of this is already recorded and is not for this bead: a
primed variable with an equals sign is an ACTION, and reaching for it is the
documented false friend for somebody arriving from a language where x = e
updates something.

DEPENDS ON tla-03ep.1, which owns recall/recall.sh, and will likely land
alongside tla-1sh7.12, which is the other session-display defect in the same
file. Read both before starting.

RED: INVARIANT: a session shows the names in scope for the rep it is serving, with no part of field 6 reachable from what it prints, and states once that an answer is an expression rather than an assignment.

Files: recall/recall.sh, recall/README.md, harness/test-recall-runner.sh, harness/fixtures/recall/
notes:
FRANK PROPOSED BACKTICKING THE NAMES INSIDE THE PROMPT, 2026-10-17:

  R119  the `Balance` after two has been paid into `ann`'s account on top of
        whatever was already there

The instinct is right and the form does not survive measurement. Central
measured both.

IT IS A REWRITE OF 96 PROMPTS, NOT A FORMATTING CHANGE. 96 of the 120 reps
have a canonical that uses an environment name, and ZERO prompts contain
every name they need, verbatim and case-sensitive. R119 is not an exception:
its prompt says "balance" where the identifier is `Balance`.

AND THE PLURAL MISMATCH BREAKS THE ENGLISH ON MOST OF THEM. R107's prompt is
"every possible parking of this yard, each wagon on exactly one track" and
its canonical is `[Wagons -> Tracks]`. The English wants the singular member
because it is talking about members; the identifiers are plural because they
are sets. Backticking gives "each `Wagons` on exactly one `Tracks`", which
is ungrammatical, or a paraphrase that reads worse than what is there. That
shape is most of the 96.

One concern of mine that does NOT hold, recorded so nobody re-raises it:
naming the identifiers does not leak the direction of a function set. R107's
English already says "each wagon on one track", and no reversed-direction row
appears in MISSES.tsv.

TAKE THE ROSTER INSTEAD, which keeps what Frank was after at a thousandth of
the cost. One line under the prompt:

  R107  every possible parking of this yard, each wagon on exactly one track
        in scope: Capacity Parking Tracks Train Wagons
  >

Measured: both environments carry exactly five names and the longest roster
is 39 characters. ledger is Accounts Amounts Balance Entries Kinds, shunting
is Capacity Parking Tracks Train Wagons.

It is one change rather than 96, it inflects nothing, and it shows all five
rather than only the ones this rep needs, which does not narrow the search
the way a subset would.

Whether the roster repeats per rep or prints once per environment and again
when the environment changes is a judgment about reading at seconds a rep.
Try both and say which you shipped. Strip the fragment comments either way.

THE ROSTER IS WRONG AND FRANK'S "ann" QUESTION IS WHY. Print the DEFINITIONS,
not the names. Measured 2026-10-17.

A roster lists top-level definitions. "ann" is a string literal INSIDE one,
so a roster hides it, and R119 needs `!["ann"]` with the quotes and the
lowercase exactly.

MEASURED: 32 of the 120 reps need a quoted literal that only a definition
shows. 13 of those need an account name, the rest need a wagon name or an
entry kind. So the roster fails on a quarter of the corpus.

THE DEFINITIONS COST FIVE SHORT LINES, NOT ONE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PRICE.
Both environments are five lines, comments stripped, widest line 38
characters:

  Accounts == {"ann", "bo"}          Wagons == {"a", "b", "c"}
  Kinds == {"deposit", "withdraw"}   Tracks == 1..3
  Amounts == 1..4                    Parking == [a |-> 1, b |-> 3, c |-> 3]
  Balance == [ann |-> 3, bo |-> 0]   Train == <<"c", "a", "b">>
  Entries == <<2, 5, 1, 5>>          Capacity == 4

AND THE FULLER FORM TEACHES THE THING MOST LIKELY TO CONFUSE, which the
roster could never show. These two sit in one environment:

  Accounts == {"ann", "bo"}
  Balance == [ann |-> 3, bo |-> 0]

The same name is quoted in one and bare in the other, because a record
literal writes its field names bare while a record's DOMAIN is strings. That
is why `Balance["ann"]` works, and seeing both lines together is the only way
to learn it. A roster reading "Accounts Amounts Balance Entries Kinds" hides
exactly the distinction a reader needs.

So: print the definitions, comments stripped. Whether they repeat per rep or
print once and again when the environment changes is still a judgment about
reading at seconds a rep, and five lines makes that question sharper rather
than settling it. Try both.

This supersedes the roster paragraph above it. The measurement that ruled out
backticking still stands, so neither of the two cheap forms survives and the
five-line one is what is left.

title: A typo spends the rep, and the parse error points at a scratch file the reader never saw
description:
Found by Frank on 2026-10-17, working a real session. Two defects stacked,
and his own diagnosis is the fix: "it should either let me fix that error, or
point out what it is."

He typed, for a rep asking for a balance after a payment:

  acct' = acct EXCEPT !["ann"] = @ + 2

and got

  rep=R119 rc=150 token=PARSE_ERROR grade=parse-error
  that did not parse, so nothing was graded about whether it is right.
    Encountered "EXCEPT" at line 17, column 24 and token "acct"
    Was expecting "==== or more Module body"

then the session moved straight on to the next rep.

DEFECT 1: A TYPO SPENDS THE REP. Reproduced by central with --count 1: the
session reported "1 rep, 1 not graded" and never read the second line of
input. A parse error is not a wrong answer, so the retrieval attempt the rung
exists for never happened. At 0.32 s a rep the cost of re-prompting is
nothing.

So on rc 150 the session should re-prompt the SAME rep rather than advance.
Cap it, because an answer that will never parse must not loop: two or three
attempts, then show the answer and move on, saying that is what happened.
Decide the cap by trying it rather than by picking a round number.

Note this is a session-mode change only. A single-rep invocation returning
150 is correct as it stands and the gate drives that path.

DEFECT 2: THE MESSAGE POINTS AT A FILE HE NEVER SAW. "line 17, column 24" is
a line of a scratch module in a mktemp dir that is deleted before he reads
the message, and "Was expecting ==== or more Module body" is about module
structure rather than about his expression. Neither helps.

THE TRANSLATION IS MECHANICAL, MEASURED BY CENTRAL. The scaffold writes his
answer after the literal prefix "Answer == ", which is 10 characters. SANY's
column 24 minus 10 is column 14 of what he typed, and character 14 of
`acct' = acct EXCEPT !["ann"] = @ + 2` is the `E` of `EXCEPT`, which is
exactly the error site. So echo his line back with a caret under the
translated column:

    acct' = acct EXCEPT !["ann"] = @ + 2
                 ^

Drop the "Was expecting" line, or replace it. There is precedent for dropping
a SANY line on exactly this reasoning: the runner already strips
"Error: Evaluating assumption line N ... of module Yours failed" because it
cites a scratch module already deleted. Follow that, and say in the code that
the two have the same justification.

CHECK THE OFFSET RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT. 10 is what the current scaffold
gives and the scaffold is yours to read. If a multi-line answer or a
different code path changes it, the caret must not point confidently at the
wrong character, which is worse than no caret. When the arithmetic does not
land inside the typed text, print the line without a caret and say the
position was not recoverable.

DEPENDS ON tla-03ep.1, which owns recall/recall.sh right now for the temporal
row kind. Do not start before it merges, and re-read the session loop
afterwards, because a second row kind may parse differently.

RED: INVARIANT: in session mode a parse error re-prompts the same rep up to the cap and only then advances, and the message echoes the typed line with a caret at the translated column, or without one when the translation does not land inside the typed text.

Files: recall/recall.sh, recall/README.md, harness/test-recall-runner.sh, harness/fixtures/recall/

Merged at 169d53a (branch commit 5d3f844).

A parse error no longer advances the session. It hands the same rep back, up to three goes, then shows the answer and says that is what happened. Keyed on rc 150 alone: 255, 151 and 75 are reports about the run that retyping cannot fix, so a retry over one would be a loop with no exit. Three rather than two was run both ways over R119 (at two the reader is handed the answer over a second slip; at three it scores 1 rep, 1 right), and a whole session of unparseable answers costs 638 ms at three against 429 at two. Session only: a single-rep invocation returning 150 is correct as it stands and the gate drives that path.

The parse error now prints the typed line with a caret under the column SANY named, and drops the location that pointed at a deleted scratch module, along with the Was expecting line about module structure. The offset comes from whichever module writer ran rather than from a constant: ANSWER_PREFIX is 10 wide on a REP row, 0 on a SPEC row whose answer fills a line. The line number is a guard, not an input, so an unbalanced bracket reported on the following line yields no caret and says so.

title: The recall suite has the same vacuity guard defect, and it erases the evidence
description:
harness/test-recall-runner.sh carries the same vacuity-guard defect tla-vo5l
just fixed, and here it leaves no trace at all.

MEASURED. mutate() at harness/test-recall-runner.sh:395 is byte-identical to
the one tla-vo5l fixed: it calls nope and returns 1 when a mutation changed
nothing, then prints the path to stdout. Central confirmed it on main, and
confirmed all 8 call sites.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE ONE ALREADY FIXED. Every call site here reads

  M1=$(mutate name 'script') || M1=""

so the `|| M1=""` clears the FAIL text as well as the path. In the drill
runner the message at least survived as a bogus path and surfaced as a cp
error. Here it is simply gone.

The tla-vo5l worker measured the consequence on a copy with one pattern
broken: 151 passed, 0 failed, rc 0, against a 153 baseline. The ONLY signal
is two assertions that silently stopped running, and nothing in the project
looks at an assertion count.

THE FIX IS THE ONE ALREADY TAKEN NEXT DOOR. harness/test-drill-runner.sh:1930
now lands the path in a global and the verdict in the return code, with all
call sites as `if mutate ...; then`. That was chosen over a nameref because
run_drill and three siblings already report that way. Check whether this file
has the same idiom before copying the choice rather than the reasoning.

BLOCKED UNTIL tla-1sh7.11 LANDS. That bead owns harness/test-recall-runner.sh
and is building the session loop in it. Do not start before it merges, and
re-measure the call sites afterwards, because a session loop may add its own.

RED: INVARIANT: with one sed script edited so it matches nothing, harness/test-recall-runner.sh exits nonzero and names the vacuous mutant in a FAIL row, rather than returning 0 with a reduced assertion count.

THE SWEEP IS DONE AND THESE TWO ARE THE WHOLE SET, measured rather than
asserted. 82 shell files selected by shebang across harness/, scripts/,
drill/ and recall/, each function body checked for a reporter call and for
capture in $( ) anywhere in that file set. The reporter list was itself
measured: a pass over the tree found 39 functions that increment a failure
counter or set a failure flag, yielding assert_rc, assert_source,
assert_verdict, bad, fail, nope, shape_arm and st_bad.

Two stated limits on that negative, both from the worker. The scan is one

slip past. And a first pass produced a false positive from a body extractor
running past a one-line definition, which was found and fixed before the

title: Pull the inventory from the drill delivery, and make the cold list land once
description:
Two rulings from Frank on 2026-10-16, after tla-wn0z landed all three
reference files as always-overwrite.

RULING 1: PULL drill/INVENTORY.md FROM THE DELIVERY.

It hands over META.md. Field 8 is drill item slugs, so inverting the file on
a slug returns every construct that item drills. Measured by the tla-wn0z
worker against core/06-can-pyramid: 22 constructs out of the inventory,
exactly the 10 plus 12 that drill/core/06-can-pyramid/META.md declares. The
same scan found SHEET.md and COLD-LIST.md name 0 of 64 item slugs while
INVENTORY.md names 64 of 64, so the inventory is the only one of the three
that leaks and the other two are clean.

META.md is withheld by name because reading it answers the question the drill
asks. The worker's defence was harness/test-deliver-drill.sh:1766, which says
the withholding is a delivery boundary rather than an access boundary. That
is true of a file one absolute path away in the repo. It is not true of one
sitting in the directory he practices in.

So: drop INVENTORY.md from the manifest, restore its assert_absent, and keep
the three rows that assert SHEET.md and COLD-LIST.md name no item slug.
Those rows lose their control, since the inventory was the positive arm, so
give them a new one rather than deleting it: a fixture file that does name a
slug, which the check must still catch.

RULING 2: COLD-LIST.md LANDS ONCE AND IS NEVER OVERWRITTEN.

Its first line asks him to tick every construct he could write from a blank
page, which makes it the one of the three he has a reason to edit. Always-
overwrite on a file the learner is invited to edit is the shape that deleted
39 delivered files on 2026-10-02.

The script already has a never-overwrite class, the prompts, so this reuses a
mechanism rather than inventing one. Read how a prompt's skip is reported and
match it, because a silent skip is the half of this that goes wrong: he has
to be able to see that a newer cold list exists and was not written.

The cost is real and he accepted it: a regenerated cold list will not reach
him without a flag. drill/README.md currently says a tick does not survive a
delivery. That sentence is now wrong and is in your footprint.

WHAT STAYS. SHEET.md keeps always-overwrite. It is the file he actually
needed, it names no item slug, and he never edits it.

Watch each change fail first. An assert_absent restored without being seen
red is not evidence, and neither is a never-overwrite path that was never
handed an existing file to refuse.

RED: INVARIANT: a delivery lands drill/SHEET.md always, lands drill/COLD-LIST.md only when absent and reports the skip when present, and never lands drill/INVENTORY.md.

title: Second slice: temporal, three holes, 20 constructs
description: Build first: 20 constructs at 0.94x the cost of a recall rep for two of the three holes. Read the parent epic's body for the measured contract and tla-1sh7.9's report for the scaffolds. The property hole is the one with real design in it: a single run cannot grade it because a weaker property also holds, so the key is an rc vector over two or three specs, and even two sides misses a near neighbour. Measure every wrong answer you record against the battery you ship. Files: recall/, harness/recall-gate.sh, harness/test-recall-runner.sh

title: Second slice: the 68 constructs value equality cannot reach
description:
The recall rung reaches 37 of 105 constructs. tla-1sh7.9 measured the other
68 and ALL FOUR SHAPES WORK. This epic builds them.

MEASURED 2026-10-16 on TLC2 2026.07.31.184830, costs taken against a
same-pass baseline because the box carried foreign JVMs at load 12 to 14, so
the RATIO is the honest figure and absolute times are inflated.

  baseline, a real recall rep        1.00x
  state-space                        0.80x
  modules                            0.81x
  temporal, fairness hole            0.94x
  temporal, action hole              0.96x
  pluscal                            1.27x
  temporal, property battery         2.84x  (three runs)

Nothing belongs in the completion channel. PlusCal is NOT the one to drop: it
is 31 of the 68 constructs and the translator costs 90 to 130 ms, not a
second JVM.

THE FOUR SHAPES, AND WHAT EACH NEEDS. Full scaffolds, exit codes and
alternates are in tla-1sh7.9's returned report. What follows is the part a
corpus author must not re-derive.

TEMPORAL IS THREE HOLES, NOT ONE. My framing in tla-1sh7.9 said one hole
conjoined into Spec, which reaches 4 of the 20 constructs. Three reach all 20.

  A1 fairness hole, one run, keyed on rc. WF_ and SF_ and three more correct
     alternates all pass at 0; TRUE and a wrong subaction give 13. Two traps:
     WF_vars(Init) returns 255 rather than 13, and <>(x = 2) conjoined as if
     it were fairness PASSES at 0. The field-7 construct gate closes the
     second. K098 needs a second environment with two subactions, one always
     enabled, or WF_vars(Next) and WF_vars(Step) are the same formula.

  A2 property hole, A BATTERY, NOT A RUN. A property weaker than the
     canonical also holds, so []TRUE passes. Two specs catch too-weak and
     too-strong; a third is needed because <>(x = 1) has the same two-sided
     profile as the canonical. The key is the rc VECTOR.

  A3 action hole, one run, keyed on the state-graph fingerprint read through
     TLCGet in a POSTCONDITION. THE FINGERPRINT ALONE COLLIDES: swapping
     which variable moves gives an isomorphic graph and passes. The contract
     is fingerprint AND an invariant naming the variable the prompt is about.

     TLCGet("level") returns 0 in a postcondition and is NOT the depth.
     TLCGet("diameter") is. That cost the spike a wrong fingerprint.

STATE-SPACE, cheapest of the four. The answer is a .cfg line, the key is
TLCGet("distinct") in a POSTCONDITION, and wrong answers land on rc 10 which
is already what recall.sh means by incorrect. Three cautions: a VIEW must
mention a variable or it is 151; the key is one integer so two wrong answers
sharing a count silently false-pass; and a deadlock rep needs the runner to
forward -d, which recall.sh never passes.

MODULES, two scaffold variants because EXTENDS must be the first line. The
design move to copy: two sibling modules defining the SAME NAME at different
values, so a wrong import is false at 10 rather than unparseable at 150.
Without it the grade table says "nothing was graded" about a check that did
happen.

PLUSCAL, and three things gate it. An unbounded wrong answer ran the whole
budget and returned 124 TIMEOUT after 60.3 s, so every rep ships a type
invariant capping the state space and the runner passes a short budget.
--fair algorithm plus PROPERTY Termination is what catches a non-progressing
answer. And pcal.trans exits 255 on a syntax error, which collides with
TLC_EXCEPTION in verdict.sh's table, so a translation failure must report as
99 CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN instead.

Roughly 7 of the 31 pluscal constructs ask what the TRANSLATION produces, so
their answers are ordinary TLA+ expressions and they belong on the existing
value-equality rung with the translated module as the environment. INFERRED
by the spike from construct names, not measured.

EVERY SHAPE HAS A FALSE PASS, found by looking for one: <>(x = 2) as a
fairness conjunct, []TRUE as a property, a swapped variable under the action
fingerprint, and x := 3 in PlusCal. Three are closed by the field-7 construct
gate or an invariant. The fourth is closed only by measuring the wrong
answers you intend to record. A row that was never submitted wrong is not
evidence.

THE GATE NEEDS ITS OWN CHECKS. Every guard in both recall gates is
$1 == "REP", so a second row kind under a different marker is invisible
rather than mis-handled. The prompt's forbidden-character rule also bites
here: harness/test-recall-runner.sh:678 forbids braces and a backslash in a
prompt, which a temporal prompt must respect while describing a temporal
operator. And the three reserved scaffold names become roughly thirty across
the four shapes.

ONE THING THAT GETS BETTER. recall-gate.sh check 1 submits each canonical
against itself and its own header says that proves only that the canonical
parses. A spec row has no self-grading form: the canonical goes into a
scaffold whose other half is a declared expected rc, so the analogous check
is strictly stronger. Take it.

title: Record the self-matching pgrep wait loop, which never exits
description:
A wait loop written as `until ! pgrep -f PATTERN; do sleep N; done` can never
exit, because the waiting shell's own command line contains PATTERN and
pgrep -f matches full command lines.

MEASURED 2026-10-16. Seven such shells were found spinning, up to 64 minutes
old, all from one finished dispatched worker. Direct proof:

  pgrep -af 'measure.sh'

returned four processes, and every one of them was a waiting shell whose
command line read `eval 'until ! pgrep -f measure.sh ...'`. The loop sees
itself, so the condition is permanently false. The work it was waiting on had
finished long before.

The seven, by the pattern each waited on: red-static.sh, measure.sh (twice),
bash .wk-scratch/measure.sh (twice), bash scripts/test, scripts/test.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE. Each shell burns almost no CPU and shows up only as a
shell slot, so the symptom is "this session has eight shells and I only
started one", not a slow box. Frank spotted it from the shell list; nothing
in the harness or the gates would have.

TWO SHAPES, AND THE SECOND ONE HIDES THE FIRST. A loop that waits on a file
AND a pgrep, `until [ -f X ] && ! pgrep -f Y; do ...`, is stuck for the same
reason even when X appears. Two of the seven were that shape.

WHAT TO WRITE INSTEAD, in order of preference.

1. Do not poll. A background Bash call notifies on completion and a
   dispatched agent notifies when it returns. A poll loop around work the
   harness already reports on is pure waste, and this is the failure it
   produces.
2. If you must wait, wait on a SENTINEL FILE the work itself creates as its
   last act, never on a process pattern. A file cannot match the waiter.
3. If a process check is genuinely unavoidable, exclude self and ancestors:
   `pgrep -f PATTERN | grep -vx $$` is not enough, because the match is the
   shell's parent as often as the shell. Prefer a pidfile written by the
   work.

WHERE IT GOES. .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md, next to the ugrep-wrapper
and pipefail-SIGPIPE hazards. It is the same family: a shell construct that
returns a plausible wrong answer rather than an error. The file already says
a worker's own measurements are what the briefs rest on, and a worker stuck
in one of these produces no measurement at all while appearing to work.

Lineage: found by Frank from the shell list, diagnosed and the seven killed
by central, 2026-10-16.

Files: .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md
close_reason: Written into .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md at commit d74b657, alongside a second hazard from the same day. The pgrep entry carries the measurement (seven shells, oldest 64 minutes, all from one worker that had already returned), the one-command proof (pgrep -af came back with four waiting shells whose own command lines hold the pattern), why nothing caught it (they burn no CPU, and a ps grep for bash misses them because they run as zsh -c eval), the second shape that hides the first (until [ -f X ] && ! pgrep -f Y stays stuck after X appears), and three remedies in order with the reason each is ranked where it is. The second entry records that every worker running the full gate makes every reading worse: 420 to 560 s on a quiet box against 1.5x to 4x over budget at load 12 to 14 with four concurrent runs, and names it a brief defect rather than four worker mistakes, since a worker handed no guidance reasonably runs the gate.

title: The delivered recall runner cannot grade: verdict.sh is not beside it

title: Measure the spec-scaffold shapes for the 68 constructs value equality cannot reach
description:
The recall rung reaches 37 of the 105 constructs. This is the other 68.

MEASURED on main 2026-10-16. recall/REPS.tsv names 37 distinct construct ids,
all in the four value-producing families. By drill/INVENTORY.md field 3:

  functions-records  11 of 11      modules       0 of  8
  sets                9 of  9      state-space   0 of  8
  core               15 of 16      temporal      0 of 20
  sequences           2 of  2      pluscal       0 of 31

TEMPORAL AT 0 OF 20 IS THE POINT. That is fairness, WF_, SF_, box and
diamond. It is the one family with no Haskell analog at all, so nothing
transfers into it, and it already has the thinnest production coverage in the
corpus: 8 drill items across six inventory rows, two of which have none,
against 38 reading exposures. Recognition-heavy on the only thing that cannot
be recognized from somewhere else.

WHY THEY ARE NOT IN THE FIRST SLICE, and it was a correct call. The first
slice grades by value equality: the answer is dropped into a scaffold and
compared against a canonical with ASSUME. A temporal formula, a config
keyword and a PlusCal statement are not values, so none of them can be
compared that way.

THE SHAPE THAT SHOULD WORK, and this bead's job is to measure whether it
does before anyone authors a corpus against it. A small spec where the
construct is REQUIRED, and the recorded exit code or distinct-state count is
the key. Four sub-shapes, because the answer lands in four different places:

  temporal      an expression conjoined into Spec, keyed on rc.
                A spec with no fairness fails its liveness property at rc 13
                and passes at rc 0 once the fairness conjunct is there. So
                "the fairness condition that makes this eventually reach the
                third state" grades on the code alone.

  state-space   a line in the .cfg, keyed on the distinct-state count.
                SYMMETRY, VIEW and CONSTRAINT all change the count and not
                the verdict, so the count is the key and rc is the guard.

  modules       a module-level line with a second module present, keyed on
                rc. EXTENDS, INSTANCE and WITH.

  pluscal       inside an --algorithm block, so the translator has to run
                before TLC. The biggest lift of the four and the one most
                likely to come back not worth it. 31 of the 68 constructs.

WHAT TO DELIVER. Measurements, not a corpus. For each of the four, build the
smallest scaffold that works, submit a right answer and at least two wrong
ones, and record every exit code and count. Then say which of the four are
worth building and what each would cost. A sub-shape that cannot separate a
right answer from a wrong one by rc or count is a finding, and saying so is
worth more than a corpus built on a guess.

Report the scaffold for each shape that works in enough detail that a corpus
author can build against it without re-deriving it, the way tla-wekw's
contract was handed to tla-1sh7.2.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING. This rung runs at seconds a rep. A
grading run in the first slice is 0.32 s. Measure the wall time of every
scaffold you build and report it. A shape that needs five seconds a rep
belongs in the completion channel instead, and saying so is a real answer.

DEPENDS ON tla-1sh7.4, which is writing the gate over recall/REPS.tsv right
now. A second row kind may need that gate extended, so do not start before it
lands and read what it built.

Files: (none; the deliverable is the measured report and whatever scratch scaffolds prove it)

The results are carried in epic tla-i7uz and its four children, and the reparenting of those children is commit 08b3bd3. THE ANSWER: all four spec-scaffold shapes separate a right answer from a wrong one on an exit code, and three cost LESS than a recall rep. Measured against a same-pass baseline on a box at load 12 to 14, so the ratio is the honest figure: state-space 0.80x, modules 0.81x, temporal 0.94 to 0.96x, pluscal 1.27x, and only the three-run property battery above at 2.84x. Nothing belongs in the completion channel, and PlusCal is not the one to drop because the translator costs 90 to 130 ms rather than a second JVM. THREE FINDINGS THAT CORRECTED MY FRAMING: temporal is three holes not one, since mine reached 4 of 20 constructs where three reach all 20; the property hole cannot be graded by a single run because a weaker property also holds, so the key is an rc vector over two or three specs and even two sides misses the near neighbour; and the action hole's fingerprint collides, because swapping which variable moves gives an isomorphic state graph, so the contract is fingerprint AND an invariant. Also measured: TLCGet('level') returns 0 in a postcondition and diameter is the depth key, which cost the worker a wrong fingerprint, and an unbounded PlusCal answer ran 60.3 s to a timeout before a bounding type invariant turned it into 692 ms. Every one of the four shapes has a false pass the worker found by deliberately looking, three closed by the existing field-7 gate or an invariant and the fourth closed only by measuring the wrong answers you intend to record.

title: The cardinality probe's failure prints the value twice under the right answer
description:
When the cardinality probe fails, the value prints twice and TLC's raw error
text sits between the two copies.

MEASURED on main. recall/recall.sh R001 'Wagons', where R001's canonical is a
sequence rather than a set, prints under "the answer":

  <<{"a"}, {}, {"b", "c"}>>
  Attempted to compute cardinality of the value
  <<{"a"}, {}, {"b", "c"}>>
  (no count: TLC will not count that value, so it is not a set)

Four lines where two carry the information. The value is correct, the gloss
on the last line is correct and is the one worth keeping, and the two middle
lines are TLC's own message with its subject repeated.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE LINES. The gloss reads as a complaint, and here
it is attached to the RIGHT answer rather than to the learner's mistake. Any
rep whose canonical is a function, a sequence or a record hits this, which is
a large share of the functions-records and sequences families. Somebody at
seconds a rep sees an error message under the heading "the answer" and has to
work out that nothing is wrong.

WHAT IT SHOULD PROBABLY READ. One line for the value and one for the gloss,
with the gloss phrased as a fact about the value rather than as a failed
attempt:

  <<{"a"}, {}, {"b", "c"}>>
  (a sequence, so there is no count)

CHECK BEFORE WRITING THAT. The runner already drops one line of TLC's output,
the "Error: Evaluating assumption line N" line, for the reason that it cites
a scratch module already deleted. So there is a precedent and a place to do
this. Read how that drop is implemented before adding a second one.

Do not drop TLC's text when it is the EXPLANATION rather than noise. On a
wrong answer, lines like "Attempted to evaluate a CASE with no conditions
true" and "A non-function (an integer) was applied as a function" are the
feedback, and tla-1sh7.3 measured both. The cardinality probe is different
because it is the runner's own probe failing on a value that is perfectly
fine, rather than TLC reporting on what the learner wrote.

Files: recall/recall.sh, harness/test-recall-runner.sh
notes:
2026-10-17, central. Frank hit this again on R018 in the delivered tree, this
time under "you typed" rather than under "the answer", so it lands on both
halves of the report.

EXACT REACH, measured rather than estimated. Built the probe module for each
of the 120 REP canonical answers and recorded TLC's exit code. 36 answers are
sets, 84 are not. So 84 of 120 rows show this under "the answer", and the
learner's own answer is probed separately and fails the same way, so a boolean
rep answered with a boolean shows it twice in one report.

The 36 set-valued rows: R003 R039 R041 R043 R044 R045 R060 R061 R062 R063 R066
R067 R069 R073 R074 R075 R076 R077 R078 R079 R080 R081 R082 R083 R084 R085
R086 R093 R094 R095 R096 R097 R098 R107 R108 R109.

This is wider than the note above reads. It is not mainly functions-records and
sequences. It is every boolean, string and number too, which is the bulk of
the core family. R018's report carries it on a plain conjunction of two
equalities.

ONE THING THE NOTE ABOVE PROPOSES THAT I WOULD DROP. The suggested replacement
gloss, "(a sequence, so there is no count)", still spends a line telling a
learner something about a value that was never in question. On a boolean it
would read "(a boolean, so there is no count)", which is noise with better
manners. I would print the value alone when the probe fails and keep the count
only where it succeeded.

PRIORITY. Filed P2 on 2026-10-16 when the reach read as two families. At 84 of
120 on the rung's primary feedback surface I would put it at P1. Frank's call.

A duplicate of this, tla-9gdb, was filed by central the same day before
finding this bead. Closed as a duplicate; its measurement is the paragraph
above.
2026-10-17, central. The fix I proposed, keying the drop on VERDICT_RC != 0,
is WRONG. Prior-art pass flagged it and I measured it.

WHY IT IS WRONG. rc 10 holds three different things (harness/recall-gate.sh:
215-231). Two of them produce no value at all, and for those TLC's sentence is
the only feedback there is. The same printed_region carries that sentence and
the cardinality noise, so a drop keyed on the exit code strips the explanation
from exactly the rows that need it. tla-1sh7.3 established that and it is
written into tla-1sh7.4 rather than into .3's close reason.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, MEASURED. write_value_module plants three ASSUMEs: the
sentinel, Shown, and Cardinality(Shown). Which one failed is visible in the
log, because a value that evaluates prints BEFORE the error and a value that
does not prints nothing.

  Shown == Parking.b = 3          "@@S@@" / TRUE / Error: ... line 22 /
                                  Attempted to compute cardinality / TRUE
  Shown == 1 + "a"                "@@S@@" / Error: ... line 21 / Attempted to
                                  apply the operator overridden by ...
  Shown == Train[9]               "@@S@@" / Error: ... line 21 / Attempted to
                                  access index 9 of tuple ... out of bounds
  Shown == CASE Parking.a = 2 -> 1  "@@S@@" / Error: ... line 21 / Attempted
                                  to evaluate a CASE with no conditions true

The last three are the tla-1sh7.3 cases and all three print no value. The
first is the noise and it prints one.

So the rule is NOT about the exit code. It is: if a value printed between the
sentinel and the first Error line, drop everything from that Error line on,
because the count failed and nothing else did. If nothing printed, keep all of
it, because the sentence is the whole feedback.

The line number in the Error line would also discriminate, 22 against 21, but
printed_region already drops that line for the reason in its own header, so
the printed-or-not test is the one to use.

TWO GREEN ASSERTIONS PIN THE CURRENT SHAPE AND HAVE TO BE REWRITTEN ON PURPOSE.
harness/test-recall-runner.sh:294 asserts that TLC's sentence about the refused
count is part of the explanation, and mutant M4's control at :511 rests on the
same claim. Part 4's heading says "explanation and not failure", which is the
claim this bead reverses for the cardinality case only. Reverse it for that
case and leave it standing for the other three, which is what the discriminator
above buys.

RED: INVARIANT: a report for a value that evaluates shows that value once and
no TLC error text. A report for a value that does not evaluate still carries
TLC's sentence about why.

title: Wire the sheet entry and the misconception row into the runner's feedback
description:
The feedback has four layers in the design and the runner shows one.

MEASURED on main at 6a46418: grep -c MISSES recall/recall.sh is 0, and
grep -c SHEET is 0. So recall/MISSES.tsv (30 rows, tla-1sh7.3) and
drill/SHEET.md (105 entries, tla-ucbs) both exist and nothing puts either in
front of a learner. Only layer 1, the two values side by side, is wired, and
that is because the runner was built before the other two files existed.

DEPENDS ON tla-1sh7.5, which owns recall/recall.sh right now. Do not start
until it lands.

WHAT THE FOUR LAYERS ARE, cheapest first, from the epic:

  1 both values printed       WIRED
  2 the sheet entry           file exists, not wired
  3 the named misconception   file exists, not wired
  4 one model call            not built

LAYER 2. On a wrong answer, print the drill/SHEET.md entry for the rep's
construct. The rep's field 3 is a K id and SHEET.md is keyed on the same ids,
so this is a lookup with no matching. One entry is three lines.

LAYER 3. If what was typed matches a MISSES.tsv row for this rep, print its
explanation. Field 3 of that file is the wrong answer verbatim. Decide and
write down whether the match is exact text or normalized for whitespace: 30
rows is small enough that exact is defensible and a learner who types the
same mistake with different spacing then gets nothing, which is the case to
think about rather than to discover.

LAYER 4 IS A SEPARATE BEAD AND NOT THIS ONE. It is the model call for a wrong
answer with no row, and it is safe at this rung only because the answer is
already on screen, so there is nothing to withhold and no ladder applies.
90 of the 120 reps have no miss row, so layer 4 is the common case rather
than the fallback, and it deserves its own measurement of what a one-shot
costs here. Note the cost that already exists: a hint one-shot measured 6.7 s,
against 0.32 s for a grading run.

ORDER ON SCREEN. Layers 2 and 3 both explain, and they explain different
things: the sheet says what the construct IS, the miss row says what the
wrong answer SAYS. I think the miss row goes first when there is one, because
it is about what the learner just did. Read a few real blocks before fixing
that, and say which you read.

WATCH THE LENGTH. tla-1sh7.5 is already cutting a 40-line feedback block down.
Do not undo that by adding two more sections without measuring the result. A
wrong answer should still fit on a screen.

RED: INVARIANT: a wrong answer to a rep whose construct has a SHEET.md entry prints that entry, a wrong answer matching a MISSES.tsv row prints its explanation, a wrong answer matching no row prints neither and says nothing false, and the whole block fits the budget tla-1sh7.5 set.

title: Recall runner: accept a leading dash, and gate that a construct was written
description:
Two things the runner cannot do that the rep corpus now needs.

1. AN ANSWER BEGINNING WITH A DASH IS READ AS A FLAG.

Reproduced by central on main:

  recall/recall.sh -q R012 '-4'      -> "recall.sh: unknown option: -4", rc 2
  recall/recall.sh -q R012 -- -4     -> rep=R012 rc=0 token=OK grade=correct

R012 is "a thermometer reading of four degrees below zero" and R075 is a
negative integer interval. Negative integers are ordinary answers at this
rung, and K005 and K015 both want them, so a learner typing the right answer
gets a usage dump instead of a grade. The -- escape works and
recall/README.md never mentions it.

FIX: once a rep id is in hand, stop treating the next argument as a flag.
Documenting -- is the weaker option and should lose, because this rung is
supposed to run at flow speed and an escape nobody can guess costs more than
the parser change.

2. NO WAY TO REQUIRE THAT A CONSTRUCT WAS ACTUALLY WRITTEN.

Value equality grades the value, so it cannot see how the value was reached.
Two consequences, both measured by the tla-1sh7.2 worker:

- K008, bullet-point boolean notation, has NO rep at all. A canonical of
  (/\ TRUE /\ 1 = 1) = TRUE scores rc 0 exactly as the infix form does, and a
  tab-delimited row cannot carry the line breaks the layout is made of
  anyway.
- The seven definition forms (K001, K071 to K076) DO have reps and they grade
  rc 0 wrapped in a LET, but a learner who computes the same value without
  writing a definition passes. Those rows drill the construct without gating
  it.

FIX: a seventh TSV field carrying a pattern matched against the RAW ANSWER
TEXT before grading. A row with no pattern behaves exactly as today, so this
is additive and no existing row changes.

Watch out for the obvious trap: a pattern strict enough to require a LET is
also strict enough to reject a correct alternate spelling, and accepting any
correct form is the property that makes this rung gradeable without a model
in the loop. Keep the pattern to the construct's own token and never to the
shape of the whole answer. Measure a correct alternate against every pattern
you add.

K008 gets its rep once this exists, and it still needs a decision about line
breaks in a one-line field.

RED: INVARIANT: recall/recall.sh grades an answer beginning with a dash without the -- escape; and a rep carrying a requires pattern scores rc 10 or a distinct code when the answer evaluates correctly but does not match the pattern, while a row with no pattern behaves exactly as it does today.

Files: recall/recall.sh, recall/README.md, harness/test-recall-runner.sh, harness/fixtures/recall/
notes:
3. THE VALUE BLOCK IS TOO LONG TO READ AT FLOW SPEED.

Measured by central on main. One wrong answer to R107, which is the
function-set confusion this whole rung exists for:

  recall/recall.sh R107 '[w \in Wagons |-> Tracks]'   ->  40 lines

27 of those lines enumerate the 27 functions in [Wagons -> Tracks], one per
line, and the count that makes the point sits on line 40 underneath them. The
contrast a learner needs is between a record of three ranges and a set of 27
functions, and the enumeration pushes the two halves apart instead of putting
them side by side.

This rung is supposed to be seconds a rep. A block that scrolls the terminal
costs more attention than the mistake did.

FIX: cap the enumeration and keep the count. Two or three elements, an
ellipsis, then the count:

  the answer  [Wagons -> Tracks]
    { [a |-> 1, b |-> 1, c |-> 1], [a |-> 1, b |-> 1, c |-> 2], ... }
    27

A flag for the whole value is worth having for the case where somebody wants
it, and the default should be short. Pick the cap by reading a few real
blocks rather than by choosing a round number, and say which reps you read.

Do not cap the WRONG answer's value the same way without checking: that one
is usually small, and it is the half the learner has to recognize as theirs.

All three defects fixed and verified by central on the branch: a bare -4 grades rc 0 where it used to exit 2 with a usage dump; R107's feedback block is 40 lines down to 17 with the count still last and --full offered; and rc 4 CONSTRUCT_NOT_WRITTEN sits inside the 3-to-7 band harness/vacuity.sh:320 reserves for statements about the submission, absent from verdict.sh's own table which runs 0, 10-14, 75-77, 124, 150, 151, 255 plus the project's 99. CORRECTION TO MY BRIEF: I wrote that the typed value should not be capped because it is usually small. The worker measured R108's typed value at 27 lines and R109's at 16, because the characteristic mistake in that family swaps domain for range and gives a set exactly the size of the right answer. Both halves are capped. The cap shape came from reading twelve real blocks plus two measurements: TLC wraps at about 80 columns rather than at a member count, and a nested value does not print one member per line, so the cap counts lines. The field-7 trap was measured rather than reasoned about: against \bLET\b a renamed operator, a changed body and a whole function defined all score 0, where a pattern anchored on the operator's spelling would have refused two of three correct answers. 76 to 113 assertions with 18 rows watched failing first, full gate 37 suites green in 464.1s. Adoption in the 120 live rows is tla-1sh7.7. Two gaps reported: the suite is still unregistered (tla-1sh7.4) and recall/ is outside scripts/lint's roots.

    nope "mutant $name changed nothing, so its control below is vacuous"
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$out"

Every call site captures stdout: mutant=$(mutate NAME 'script'). nope writes
its FAIL text to stdout, so the message lands in the variable instead of the
report, and the fail_count increment happens in the subshell and dies with it.
The caller then proceeds with the failure message as a file path, which
surfaces as a cp error rather than a FAIL row.

WHY IT MATTERS. Each sed script puts a literal line of drill.sh's source on
both sides of a substitution. When that line changes, the mutation stops
matching, the mutant is byte-identical to the runner, and its control passes
because the unmutated runner behaves correctly. The suite goes green with a
dead control, and the thing the control exists to catch is unguarded. That is
the gate-that-enforces-nothing shape, and this file carries eleven of them.

The suite's own M7 comment claims "mutate() caught it and said so", which is
true only in the sense that the downstream cp error is loud.

THE FIX. Send nope's output to stderr, or have mutate() write the path to a
variable by nameref rather than to stdout, or check the mutation before the
subshell. Whichever route, the RED is the same: break one sed script so it
matches nothing and watch the suite go RED on the vacuity row rather than
green or noisy.

CHECK THE OTHER SUITES FOR THE SAME SHAPE while here. A helper that both
reports a failure and returns a value on stdout is a general hazard, and this
is the first instance anyone has looked for. A grep for a function called
inside $(...) that also calls nope or fail is the search.

RED: INVARIANT: with one sed script edited so it matches nothing, harness/test-drill-runner.sh exits nonzero and names the vacuous mutant in a FAIL row.

title: check.md is unreachable to a --check one-shot, same defect as hint.md
description:
check.md is as unopenable to a one-shot as hint.md was, and tla-1sh7.1 fixed
only the hint half.

drill/study/CLAUDE.md tells a MODE: check run to "Work the passes in /check in
the order they're written, and hand back everything its last section asks
for". That file is drill/study/.claude/commands/check.md, 4778 bytes. The
one-shot runs claude -p --tools "" so it has no file access and cannot open
it. So a --check run is working from a summary of a document it was told to
follow in order.

This is the same defect tla-1sh7.1 just closed for hints, found by that bead's
worker and left alone as out of footprint.

THE FIX IS THE SAME SHAPE and the code to copy now exists on main. drill.sh
cats $STUDY_ROOT/.claude/commands/hint.md into a hint prompt at four sites:
the header read-list, the -r gate in coach(), the banner line, and the cat
block, with the gate decided before the checker runs so a missing file never
spends a TLC run. Do the same for check.md in a check prompt.

ONE THING TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING IT. hint.md is 121 lines and check.md is
comparable, so a check prompt would carry both the register and the full pass
list on top of the checker output and every attempt file. Measure the prompt
size before and after. If it is large, the question is whether check.md's
passes want to be in the prompt or whether CLAUDE.md should carry the passes
directly and check.md become the interactive-only wrapper. Either answer is
fine; guessing is not.

RELATED, from the same worker: the delivery suite's assertion on the hint
tiebreak matches the phrase "can't tell which kind" without asserting which
way the rule points, so it stayed green across a reversal of the rule. Worth
strengthening in the same pass.

title: Recall: gate, deliver and register the channel
description:
Gate the recall channel, deliver it, and register it.

DEPENDS ON the runner and the rep table, which fix both file formats.

THE GATE. harness/recall-gate.sh, modelled on harness/completion-gate.sh:

1. Every REPS.tsv canonical answer scores rc 0 through the runner.
2. Every MISSES.tsv wrong answer scores rc 10 against its own rep.
3. Every construct id resolves to a drill/INVENTORY.md row.
4. Every environment named by a rep exists under recall/env/.
5. No prompt contains the notation it is asking for. This is the telegraph
   check that drill-gate.sh CHECK 1 does for drill prompts, and it is the one
   that keeps a rep from being a transcription exercise.

Checks 1 and 2 together are the mutation bar applied to this channel: a
canonical answer that scores anything but 0 is wrong, and a miss that scores 0
is not a miss.

DELIVERY. scripts/deliver-recall.sh, modelled on scripts/deliver-completion.sh.

NEVER TOUCH ~/tla-practice OR ~/Study WITHOUT A VERIFIED BACKUP FIRST. Neither
is a git repo and no repo-level search reaches them. A guessed delivery
manifest deleted 39 delivered files on 2026-10-02. Backups live in
~/tla-practice-backups/. Use the existing deliver scripts as the pattern for
how a manifest is derived rather than guessed.

Also file a follow-up rather than solving it here: nothing detects a stale
delivery, which is tla-mjvx, and this channel adds a fourth thing that can go
stale.

REGISTRATION. Add both suites to scripts/test with a measured budget, and
check the totals comment at the top still sums. harness/test-coverage-map.sh
was written and registered nowhere on 2026-10-15, so it ran nowhere until
somebody noticed.

HAZARDS. Never pipe into an early-exiting consumer under pipefail; use a
here-string. Run project scripts without a bash prefix. Do not edit
harness/verdict.sh or harness/Gate.tla, which are centrally owned: report
instead.

RED: INVARIANT: harness/recall-gate.sh exits nonzero when a canonical answer is corrupted, when a miss row is changed to a correct answer, and when a prompt is edited to contain its own answer notation; and bash scripts/test --list includes both new suites.

notes:
THREE THINGS FOUND BY THE WAVE-1 WORKERS, all landing in this bead.

1. recall/ IS IN NO GATE ROOT. scripts/lint has LINT_ROOTS=(scripts harness
   drill), and harness/test-spelling.sh and harness/test-pipefail.sh each
   carry their own root list. None includes recall/, so recall/recall.sh is
   linted by nothing and spell-checked by nothing. The tla-wekw worker linted
   and swept it by hand and both were clean, but a hand sweep has a shelf life
   and a root list does not. One word in each of three files.

2. THE BUDGET ROWS, both measured on an idle box:

     slow|15.8|recall runner|./harness/test-recall-runner.sh

   plus whatever this bead's own gate measures. Re-base the header comment as
   well as adding the row, because nothing checks the two against each other.
   Central corrected that comment at 01298ee after it drifted four suites and
   three percentage points.

3. DELIVERING THE SHEET IS A THREE-FILE PROBLEM, NOT A ONE-FILE ONE.
   harness/test-deliver-drill.sh:937-938 asserts that drill/INVENTORY.md and
   drill/COLD-LIST.md never land in the delivered tree. So all three
   drill-root reference files are undelivered by design today, and adding
   drill/SHEET.md means deciding about all three and inverting two assertions
   rather than adding a third. The shape to copy exists: drill/README.md is a
   file class the runner always overwrites, because the repo owns it.

   Related and separate: drill/README.md:71-76 has a "## The construct list"
   section pointing at COLD-LIST.md and never mentions the sheet. The cold
   list says what you do not know and the sheet gives the shape, so they are
   two halves of one answer.

ONE MORE THING, FROM THE tla-1sh7.2 WORKER, AND IT IS ABOUT THIS BEAD'S GATE.

The RED line I wrote for tla-1sh7.2 said "every row scores rc 0 when its
canonical answer is submitted through recall/recall.sh". That compares the
canonical against itself, so it can only ever prove the canonical parses and
evaluates. It cannot prove the row computes what its prompt describes. The
worker noticed and ran a second pass against values written independently of
each canonical: agreed=120, disagreed=0.

Do not copy my weak line into this bead's gate. Check 1 as written here has
the same defect. If the correctness property is to be gated rather than
checked once by hand, the table needs a predicted-value column written
independently of the canonical, and the gate compares the two. If that is
judged too expensive, say so in the gate's own comments and record that the
property was verified once at 552f09e rather than leaving a reader to assume
the gate covers it.

Also note harness/test-recall-runner.sh is still registered nowhere, so the
37-suite gate green at 420.3s never exercised recall.sh at all.

TWO MORE FROM tla-1sh7.3, both about how to write this bead's gate.

1. DO NOT MATCH EXPLANATIONS AGAINST EVERY DECLARED VERIFY-TREE NAME. The
   obvious check for "no explanation names a module or a variable from the
   verify tree" is a whole-word match against the 621 module basenames plus
   every declared VARIABLE name. The tla-1sh7.3 worker built that list and ran
   it: eight hits, all ordinary English words that happen to be declared
   somewhere.

     a, b     drill/core/08-altimeter-approx/verify/Altimeters.tla
     at       drill/functions-records/02-charging-bays/verify/BaysVanSide.tla
     holds    drill/functions-records/05-tool-crib/verify/ToolCribByWorker.tla
     level    drill/functions-records/03-ballast-tanks/verify/Ballast.tla
     occupied drill/modules/03-the-bank-that-vouched/verify/PostOffice.tla
     taken    drill/sequences/07-pneumatic-tube/verify/TubeDerived.tla
     where    drill/sets/02-two-pools/verify/PoolsWhere.tla

   No wording survives a matcher that includes "a", "at" and "where". Match
   module basenames and multi-character identifiers that are not English
   words. The names that actually matter came back with zero hits already:
   pos, out, unit, cover, board, line.

2. RC 10 HOLDS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND A GATE KEYED ON IT ACCEPTS BOTH. An
   evaluation failure inside the ASSUME surfaces as rc 10 ASSUMPTION_FAILED,
   not as a separate code. Measured on two live rows: a CASE with no OTHER arm
   gives rc 10 with "Attempted to evaluate a CASE with no conditions true",
   and an EXCEPT whose @ is applied as a function gives rc 10 with "A
   non-function (an integer) was applied as a function".

   So the band holds misconceptions that produce a WRONG VALUE and
   misconceptions that produce NO VALUE AT ALL. For this layer that is
   probably right, since both are a wrong answer from the learner's side. It
   is worth stating in the gate's comments rather than leaving the next
   reader to discover it, because rc 10 is also the code this channel uses
   for an ordinary wrong answer and the three cases are indistinguishable
   from the number alone.
