title: Recall: author the rep table for the 38 value constructs
description:
Author the rep table for the 38 value-producing constructs.

DEPENDS ON the runner bead, which fixes the scaffold contract. Do not start
before it lands.

WHAT IT IS. recall/REPS.tsv, tab-delimited with a literal first field REP so
prose in the file can never be read as data, matching drill/INVENTORY.md's
convention. Fields: marker, rep id, construct id (K001 to K105, resolving to a
drill/INVENTORY.md row), environment name, the prompt in English, the canonical
answer.

recall/env/<name>.tla holds each constant environment, so several reps over the
same domain share one. Keep the environments small and few: a set of three
strings and a range of four integers covers most of functions-records and
sets.

SCOPE. The 38 constructs in the value-producing families, by
drill/INVENTORY.md field 3: core 16, functions-records 11, sets 9, sequences 2.
Several phrasings per construct is wanted, not one, because the point is many
reps on the same fact. The other 67 constructs are a second slice and are NOT
in scope here.

THE PROMPT IS ENGLISH AND NAMES NO NOTATION. "the set of all functions from
Wagons to Tracks" is a rep. "write a function set" is not, because it hands
over the construct name and the answer is then a transcription.

HAZARDS.

- Never field-split a TSV with IFS=$'\t' read. Use cut, or awk -F'\t'.
- Write .tla content with the Write tool, not a shell heredoc: the isolation
  harness refuses a TLA+ conjunction and a set literal on a command line.
- Every canonical answer must score rc 0 through recall/recall.sh before it
  goes in the file. Watch it pass; a row nobody ran is not evidence.
- The Bash tool's grep is ugrep, not GNU. Any count that goes in a commit
  message or a report gets measured in a scratch script with a bash shebang,
  or through command grep, and both ways if it matters.

RED: INVARIANT: every row of recall/REPS.tsv scores rc 0 when its canonical answer is submitted through recall/recall.sh, and every construct id in the file resolves to a drill/INVENTORY.md row in one of the four value-producing families.

Files: recall/REPS.tsv, recall/env/
notes:
THE CONTRACT IS NOW FIXED. tla-wekw landed at 9cb8596 and these are measured,
not proposed. Do not re-derive them.

SIX TAB-DELIMITED FIELDS behind a literal REP marker:

  1 marker      the literal REP
  2 id          stable, never renumbered
  3 construct   K001 to K105, a drill/INVENTORY.md row
  4 environment resolves to recall/env/<name>.tla
  5 prompt      English, naming none of the notation it asks for
  6 canonical   the answer, as TLA+

recall/recall.sh reads it with awk -F'\t' and cut. Do the same. Never
IFS=$'\t' read.

recall/env/<name>.tla IS A FRAGMENT, NOT A MODULE. Bare definitions and
comments only. No module header, no EXTENDS, no trailing ====. The runner cats
it between a fixed EXTENDS line and Answer ==, so a file with its own header
will not parse. harness/fixtures/recall/env/shunting.tla is the shipped
example and it is three lines.

THREE RESERVED NAMES. An environment defining Answer, Canonical or Shown makes
every rep over it fail to parse with a multiple declaration. Gated.

THE EXTENDS LIST IS FIXED at Naturals, Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets, TLC
and a fragment cannot add to it, because TLA+ allows one EXTENDS and it must
come first. That list was measured to reach :> and @@ (which live in TLC, so
that module is load-bearing for the corpus and not only for PrintT), Len, and
record-field access. A rep needing more than those five modules is a one-line
change to EXTENDS_LIST in the runner, so report it rather than working round
it.

FOUR MEASURED CODES, so you know what a bad row looks like before you write
one. An unbalanced bracket is 150. An undefined name is also 150, caught by
SANY at semantic processing rather than 151 or 75, so a typo in your canonical
answer honestly reports "did not parse". A scalar answered against a set of
functions is 10, so a type mismatch reads as a wrong answer. A correct
alternate form is 0.

COST. 0.32 s a grading run on this box. A row that will not be exercised at
flow speed is a row in the wrong channel.

title: Recall: grading scaffold and runner
description:
Build the grading mechanism and the runner. This bead fixes the contract every
sibling depends on, so it lands first and alone.

WHAT IT DOES. recall/recall.sh takes a rep id and an answer, writes a scaffold
module into a mktemp -d, runs it through harness/verdict.sh, and reports. On
rc 0 it says so and stops. On rc 10 it prints the dual value block: the answer
evaluated, then the canonical answer evaluated, each with a cardinality line
where the value is a set.

THE SCAFFOLD, measured working 2026-10-16:

  ---- MODULE R ----
  EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, TLC
  <the rep's constant environment, verbatim>
  Answer == <what Frank typed>
  ASSUME Answer = <the canonical answer>
  ==================

An empty .cfg beside it. rc 0 is correct, rc 10 is ASSUMPTION_FAILED, which
harness/verdict.sh already names. Any correct form is accepted, because the
comparison is on values.

THE DUAL VALUE BLOCK uses a second scaffold with ASSUME PrintT(Answer) and
ASSUME PrintT of the cardinality. The cardinality assumption ERRORS on a
non-set value, and that error is part of the explanation rather than a
failure: print the value and skip the count. Measured output for the wrong
answer on the function-set rep is a three-field record whose fields are
ranges, followed by "Attempted to compute cardinality of the value".

HAZARDS THAT APPLY HERE.

- harness/verdict.sh is centrally owned. Call it, never edit it. If rc 10 does
  not come back where this bead expects it, report that rather than patching.
- Never pipe into an early-exiting consumer under pipefail. out=$(producer);
  grep -q PATTERN <<<"$out" is the form. Capturing first does NOT fix a live
  pipe.
- Write .tla content with the Write tool, not a shell heredoc. The isolation
  harness reads a TLA+ conjunction as a path leaving the worktree and a set
  literal as a brace group, and refuses both.
- Run project scripts without a bash prefix: harness/verdict.sh ... not
  bash harness/verdict.sh ...
- Clean up the mktemp dir on a trap, and leave nothing behind. drill/study/check
  at lines 724 to 764 is the pattern to copy: a scratch dir it cannot make is a
  hard error, never a fallback to the working directory.

FIXTURE. Ship harness/fixtures/recall/ with four rows covering the measured
cases above (canonical, a correct alternate, a literal-for-set error, a
reversed error) plus one rep whose value is not a set, so the cardinality
skip is exercised. The fixture is this bead's, not the corpus; the real rep
table is a sibling bead and must not be authored here.

RED: INVARIANT: for every row in harness/fixtures/recall/, recall/recall.sh reports correct exactly when the row says correct, and the rc it reports is the rc harness/verdict.sh returned, never a rc inferred from TLC's prose.

THE DESIGN-BEARING FINDING: the cardinality probe errors rc 10 on a non-set value, the same code a wrong answer scores, and IsFiniteSet returns TRUE rc 0 on that very value so there is no in-TLA+ guard. Central re-measured all three independently. The grading run and the value probes are therefore separate modules, one probe per value, and only the grading run's code leaves the script. My epic's single-scaffold sketch was wrong. Three more codes measured: unbalanced bracket 150, undefined name 150 at semantic processing rather than 151 or 75, scalar against a set of functions 10. title: Recall rung: notation drilled at flow speed
description:
The corpus has no rung that runs at flow speed. Every drill item that declares
a time declares 8 to 12 minutes, so the smallest unit on offer is eight
minutes of modeling. Frank spent an hour on functions-records/01-shunting-yard
on 2026-10-16 and the hint system laddered a question he had explicitly marked
as a mechanism question.

This epic adds the RECALL rung: a need stated in English, the notation typed,
graded exactly, in seconds. It is the only rep shape in the design that
generalizes, because the retrieved item is the same in every module. Three
earlier candidates were rejected as module-bound: predicting an exit code,
picking which of a pair reports a defect, and editing one module into another.
Frank's rejection: "None of those feel like I would become better at TLA+ in
general with them."

THE MECHANISM, measured 2026-10-16 on TLC2 2026.07.31.184830:

An answer is dropped into a scaffold module beside a fixed constant
environment, and correctness is asserted as value equality against the
canonical answer. A false ASSUME is rc 10, ASSUMPTION_FAILED, already in
harness/verdict.sh's table. Measured on "the set of all functions from Wagons
to Tracks":

  [Wagons -> Tracks]                 rc 0
  {f in [Wagons -> Tracks] : TRUE}   rc 0    correct alternate, accepted
  [w in Wagons |-> Tracks]           rc 10   literal where a set was asked
  [Tracks -> Wagons]                 rc 10   reversed

So grading is one exit code, no string matching, any correct form accepted,
0.29s per run. That last property is what makes it a drill rather than a quiz.

THE FEEDBACK, four layers, cheapest first:

1. Print both values. TLC explains the mistake itself. The wrong answer above
   prints [a |-> 1..3, b |-> 1..3, c |-> 1..3] and fails to be counted; the
   right one prints a set of 27 functions. No authored prose, no model.
2. The sheet entry for that construct. 105 already written across the twelve
   exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md files.
3. A named misconception, when what was typed matches a known wrong move.
   Source: 406 of the 498 drill/*/*/verify/*.tla modules carry a leading
   comment naming one mistake and its consequence, each with a measured rc.
4. One model call otherwise. Safe at this rung only: the answer is already on
   screen, so nothing is withheld, and no ladder or classifier applies.

SCOPE OF THE FIRST SLICE. The value-equality scaffold reaches the constructs
that produce a value. By drill/INVENTORY.md family that is core 16,
functions-records 11, sets 9, sequences 2, so 38 of the 105. The remaining 67
(pluscal 31, temporal 20, state-space 8, modules 8) are not values and need a
six-line spec scaffold keyed on a recorded rc or state count. That is a second
slice and not in this epic.

CONVENTIONS THIS CHANNEL FOLLOWS. It matches completion/: a top-level
directory, a README.md, a runner, scripts/deliver-recall.sh,
harness/recall-gate.sh plus its own test suite, registered in scripts/test.

Files: recall/, scripts/deliver-recall.sh, scripts/gen-sheet.sh, harness/recall-gate.sh, harness/test-recall-gate.sh, harness/test-recall-runner.sh, drill/drill.sh, drill/SHEET.md, drill/study/CLAUDE.md, drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md, scripts/test

title: Make the drill and reading channels a general-purpose tool, not a tool for one reader
description:
DEFERRED FROM tla-jaob BY FRANK, 2026-10-15: "For now, let's keep me as the
only audience, and file a P1 for later to shift this to being a more general
purpose tool for others."

So this is the published-course question, kept whole and given its own
priority rather than blocking work. tla-jaob carried it for twelve days as a
P0 and blocked tla-ahxl the whole time.

WHAT THE ORIGINAL BEAD ESTABLISHED, and it is worth keeping rather than
re-deriving. Frank, 2026-10-02, after being laid off the previous day:
skilling up specifically for CrossnoKaye is in the rearview, and the goal is
"creating an expanding and interesting artifact for other people studying
TLA+. The exercises that we have that match learntla are awesome, this should
be the post graduate course."

WHAT THE PUBLISHED SITE IS TODAY. mkdocs.yml's site_description reads "A
107-puzzle progressive curriculum for learning TLA+ and PlusCal by doing" and
docs/curriculum/ holds tier-0 through tier-7. That is puzzles/, the v1 set,
which drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_78e0afcd8f0f7bb925f61ef0 records as having
died of QG rule 2. So the public face of the project is the failed curriculum
and none of the v2 work is published. That was true when tla-jaob was filed
and nothing since has changed it.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY HAVE TO MOVE, as far as I can tell tonight:

  - PRACTICE-PLAN.md names Frank as the audience throughout, and a general
    tool needs a different document rather than a patched one.
  - The quality bars are Frank-calibrated. "Get fully in my head in 10
    minutes" and "moderately interesting so it's something I need to work
    out" are his reading speed and his boredom threshold.
  - The study loop assumes one person, one study root, one LAST-SERVED
    pointer, and a hardcoded ~/Study/tla-drills default.
  - drill/study/CLAUDE.md names an absolute path in Frank's home directory
    twice, in tilde and expanded form, and a structural gate asserts both.
  - tla-5zgr is the open epic for publishing, and tla-16je is open about
    redistributing corpus specs from five repositories that ship no licence,
    which a published artifact cannot ignore the way a private one can.

DO NOT START THIS WITHOUT FRANK REOPENING IT. The whole point of the ruling is
that the single-reader assumption buys speed right now, and a half-generalized
tool would cost that without buying an audience.

title: Nothing detects a stale delivery, so a merged fix can sit unreachable for hours
description:
Files: harness/test-deliver-drill.sh, scripts/cibuild

RED: INVARIANT: a check fails when a delivered artifact under ~/tla-practice/drill or the study root differs from its source in the repo, and names every path that drifted.

FOUND BY FRANK, 2026-10-15, by running the command and reading the error:

  ./drill --style
  drill: unknown option: --style

THE REPO HAD --style FOR SEVERAL HOURS AND HIS COPY DID NOT. I delivered once
after the tla-rzvk wave, then merged tla-iiow (the style pass), tla-9y5h (the
checker's temp copy) and tla-1s89 (eight prompt edits) without delivering
again. Measured at the time he reported it:

  drill/drill.sh            01:42, 44 mentions of style
  ~/tla-practice/.../drill  00:15,  0 mentions of style
  study root                CLAUDE.md and check only, no STYLE.md, no style
  prompts                   8 of 64 differed, exactly the telegraph fixes

So three separate waves of work were invisible to the only person who uses it,
including a fix to a defect he had reported himself.

THE GATE CANNOT SEE THIS BY CONSTRUCTION TODAY. cibuild and every suite run
inside the repo. ~/tla-practice is not a git repo and no repo-level search
reaches it, which CLAUDE.md already names as one of the two surfaces that get
missed. The delivery scripts are gated for what they WOULD write, and nothing
checks whether they have been RUN.

WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. A check that compares each delivered artifact
against its source and reports drift. It has to degrade gracefully: an absent
~/tla-practice is the ordinary case on any box but Frank's, and a CI runner has
no delivery to compare, so absence is a skip and never a failure.

The comparison is cheap and already half written. scripts/deliver-drill.sh
knows every source and destination pair, since it prints them, and
--refresh-prompts already computes the difference: run on a stale tree it
reported "8 replaced, 56 left alone", so the per-file comparison exists inside
the script. A --dry-run or --verify mode that exits nonzero on drift would be
most of the bead.

WIRE IT WHERE IT WILL FIRE. A suite in the fast tier is the obvious home, but
it only helps somebody who runs the gate. The better home may be a line in
cibuild phase 1 beside the toolchain assertion, or in the wrap-up ritual, since
the failure mode is forgetting a step at the end of a session rather than
breaking something in the middle of one.

RELATED AND NOT THE SAME: tla-hjb3 is open about two tlc on the PATH with no
gate observing which one a run used. Same family, which is an unobserved
difference between what the repo believes and what the box does.
notes:
2026-10-16: a fourth channel can now go stale. scripts/deliver-recall.sh landed at 5ecd591 and joins deliver-drill, deliver-completion and deliver-problems. Noted by the tla-1sh7.4 worker, which could not file it because a dispatched worker runs read-class bd only. Today also produced the concrete cost: three waves merged on 2026-10-15 without re-delivering and none reached Frank until somebody noticed, and the hint repair sat undelivered until it was run by hand. --refresh-prompts already computes the drift, so a --verify mode is most of the work.
2026-10-18, central. THE RECALL CHANNEL IS DONE AND THE BEAD STAYS OPEN. Landed at 693ee8f.

scripts/deliver-recall.sh --verify compares each manifest entry against its
source, names every drifted path, exits 3, and writes nothing.
harness/test-deliver-verify.sh is registered fast at 0.5 s with 20 assertions.

WHY --check COULD NOT BE WIRED STRAIGHT IN, which is the part of this bead I
had wrong going in. --check reports what a delivery WOULD do, so on a
byte-identical tree it prints '66 to overwrite' and exits 0. The bead says
'--refresh-prompts already computes the difference', and that is true of
deliver-drill.sh's prompt path and NOT of --check on any channel. So the
comparison existed in one place for one file class, not generally.

FOUR SHAPES, each distinguishable in the output:

  DRIFT, never delivered:        in the manifest, absent from the tree
  DRIFT, differs from <src>:     present and stale, which is Frank's case
  DRIFT, not executable:         the runner lost its 0755
  no delivered tree, Skipping:   exit 0, every box but Frank's and all of CI

The mode row earns its place: content compares equal whatever the mode is, so
nothing else would catch a runner delivered 0644, and that is a channel that
reports success and cannot be run.

WHAT IS LEFT, and the four are not equal work.

deliver-drill.sh is the channel that actually bit and it is the hard one. It
has two file classes and a learner owns one. REFERENCE_POLICIES=('always'
'once') at scripts/deliver-drill.sh:448, and install_reference_once() has no
copy path over an existing file at all. So a verify there has to read the
policy before calling a difference drift, or it will report every learner
edit as staleness. The study side is tractable today: study_srcs[] and
study_dests[] are parallel arrays and every entry goes through
install_study_file(), which always overwrites, so that half is the same loop
recall uses. The item side and COLD-LIST.md are the part that needs a
decision.

deliver-completion.sh, deliver-problems.sh and deliver-exercises.sh never
overwrite, so for them 'differs' means a learner edited it and 'absent' means
a delivery is owed. Those are two different findings and only the second is
drift. A verify that conflated them would be red on every completed sitting.

THE cibuild WIRING IS STILL OPEN AND I DID NOT TAKE IT. The bead offers three
homes and I took the fast-tier suite. cibuild runs where there is no
delivered tree, so the check skips there every time and buys nothing. The
wrap-up ritual is the home that would actually fire, and that is a change to
the session-close checklist rather than to a script, so it is Frank's call.

ONE THING THE SUITE DOES THAT IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE IT SURPRISES SOMEBODY.
Part 3 reads the real tree, so merging a recall change makes this row red
until somebody delivers, with no code change to explain it. That is the whole
purpose. The row note in scripts/test says to read the DRIFT lines, back up
~/tla-practice, and run the delivery, and never to fix it by editing the
suite.
2026-10-18, central, follow-up. tla-oa0m closed at 86faa11 and it ANSWERS THE DESIGN QUESTION THIS BEAD DEFERRED for the three never-overwrite channels.

The note above says 'for them differs means a learner edited it and absent
means a delivery is owed. Those are two different findings and only the second
is drift.' That was right and incomplete: there is a third finding, and
scripts/deliver-exercises.sh now carries the mechanism for it.

A digest recorded AT DELIVERY TIME tells an unedited copy from an edited one,
so 'differs' splits into 'stale and safe to update' and 'his work, report and
never touch'. Only a delivery writes an entry. The record is
.delivered.sha256 in the delivered directory and --adopt bootstraps a tree
delivered before records existed, by recording only files byte-identical to
their source.

SO THE REMAINING CHANNELS ARE NO LONGER A DESIGN PROBLEM, they are the same
pattern applied three more times:

  scripts/deliver-completion.sh   never overwrites, same shape as exercises
  scripts/deliver-problems.sh     never overwrites, same shape as exercises
  scripts/deliver-drill.sh        two file classes, see below

deliver-drill.sh is still the interesting one and the record does not settle
all of it. Its study side is already tractable: study_srcs[] and
study_dests[] are parallel arrays and every entry goes through
install_study_file(), which always overwrites, so that half is the recall
loop. REFERENCE_POLICIES=('always' 'once') at scripts/deliver-drill.sh:448 is
where the record earns its keep, since COLD-LIST.md is the 'once' entry and a
learner owns it.

The cibuild wiring is still open and still Frank's call, for the reason in the
note above: cibuild runs where no delivered tree exists, so the check skips
there every time.
FRANK RULED 2026-10-18: the stale-delivery check goes in the WRAP-UP RITUAL, not cibuild. So the session-close checklist in CLAUDE.md gains a verify step, and cibuild gets nothing, for the reason in the note above: cibuild runs where no delivered tree exists so the check would skip every time.
2026-10-18, central, Frank ruled and the ritual half is DONE at 0946a62. scripts/verify-delivery.sh is the single entry point: every channel with a verify mode, writes nothing, exits 3 on drift and 1 on an unknown scripts/deliver-*.sh. It NAMES THE UNCHECKED CHANNELS on every run, because a wrapper reporting all clean while skipping three would be this bead wearing the uniform of its own fix. CLAUDE.md gains a project-owned session-completion section outside the beads-managed block, which carries a content hash and would eat anything written inside it. harness/test-deliver-verify.sh goes 20 to 26 with a part 4 over the channel table, both directions watched.

TWO LYING COUNTS FIXED ON THE WAY, both from tla-oa0m the day before. deliver-exercises.sh --check exited 3 on stale OR conflicted, against its own usage line which has always said stale only. Conflicted is the learner work and is never actionable, so that put a permanent red on 10 of 12 chapters, every one red because he had done the exercises. And --adopt reported 0 left unrecorded on a chapter that left five unrecorded. Assertions for both, watched failing. Exercises suite 74 to 79.

THE RECORDS HAD NEVER BEEN BOOTSTRAPPED. find returned no .delivered.sha256 anywhere. --adopt run across all twelve chapters: 70 recorded, 93 left as his work.

A NEW FINDING FOR THE DRILL CHANNEL, which is the one still open. A plain scripts/deliver-drill.sh run reports "0 prompt(s) to land, 64 already there" and lands NONE of eight changed prompts. Only --refresh-prompts replaces them. So the drill channel reports success while delivering nothing, which is this bead exactly. Whatever verify lands for drill has to compare prompts rather than trusting a plain run.

STILL OPEN: deliver-drill.sh, deliver-completion.sh and deliver-problems.sh. The last two are the exercises pattern applied twice. drill has two file classes and COLD-LIST.md is the once entry a learner owns.
2026-10-18, central. TWO MORE CHANNELS DONE at the merge of 174ee05 and dfd8962. scripts/deliver-completion.sh and scripts/deliver-problems.sh carry the .delivered.sha256 record, --verify and --adopt. Suites: completion 131 to 182, problems 101 to 159, exercises 79 to 84, verify 26 to 34. Six mutations watched, including the stale-or-conflicted exit code this bead's own note warned about.

scripts/deliver-exercises.sh takes --verify as an alias for --check, so the wrapper calls one spelling everywhere. That closes a collision worth naming: --check meant a dry run on four scripts and a drift report on the fifth.

RECORDS BOOTSTRAPPED: completion 76 adopted and 5 left as his work, problems 55 adopted and 1 left. Backup verified at 1080 files first. scripts/verify-delivery.sh now reads four channels in sync and names drill as the only unchecked one.

DRILL IS ALL THAT REMAINS AND IT IS THE HARD ONE. Two file classes, REFERENCE_POLICIES=('always' 'once') at scripts/deliver-drill.sh:448, and COLD-LIST.md is the 'once' entry a learner owns. The study side is tractable: study_srcs[] and study_dests[] are parallel and every entry goes through install_study_file(), which always overwrites.

AND A FINDING THAT MAKES DRILL MORE URGENT THAN IT LOOKS. A plain deliver-drill.sh run reports '0 prompt(s) to land, 64 already there' and lands NONE of eight changed prompts. Only --refresh-prompts replaces them. So the drill channel reports success while delivering nothing, which is this bead's original failure living inside the channel that produced it. A verify for drill has to compare prompt CONTENT, not trust a plain run's summary line.

ONE UNWRITTEN DIFFERENCE BETWEEN CHANNELS, reported by the worker as a gap in my brief. On completion, problems and exercises an ABSENT delivered file is reported and never failed on. On recall it IS drift at exit 3, correctly, because recall always overwrites. That difference is recorded only in the script headers and belongs somewhere a reader of the ritual would find it.
2026-10-18, FRANK RULED ON THE DRILL CHANNEL, which was the last one open. He took central's read: the digest record, same mechanism scripts/deliver-exercises.sh already implements. A delivered file matching its record but differing from its source is stale and fails. One differing from its record is the learner's work and is counted, never failed on.

THE BOOTSTRAP IS CLEAN TODAY, measured by central 2026-10-18 before dispatch. All 64 delivered PROMPT.md files are byte-identical to their sources, and so are COLD-LIST.md, SHEET.md and README.md in the drill tree. So an adopt records all of them correctly rather than guessing which Frank had annotated. That window is the reason to do this now.

AND THE SECOND FINDING GOES IN THE SAME BEAD. A plain deliver-drill.sh run prints '0 prompt(s) to land, 64 already there' and lands none of eight changed prompts, because only --refresh-prompts can replace one. The summary now says how many delivered prompts DIFFER and names the flag. The default does not change: a plain run still does not overwrite a prompt, because that default protects work with no git behind it.

Dispatched 2026-10-18. The worker owns scripts/verify-delivery.sh and removes drill from NO_VERIFY_YET. It was told not to touch scripts/test, since both its suites are already registered, and to report a budget overrun rather than re-base it.
close_reason:
Landed at merge 1bef968, with the wrapper wiring and three fixture repairs at 816fb27. Frank ruled the digest record on 2026-10-18 and the channel that opened this bead is now the last one closed.

TWO VOCABULARIES, BECAUSE THE TWO FILE CLASSES HAVE DIFFERENT REMEDIES. DRIFT is a file he never edits, so a plain run lands it. STALE is a prompt or the cold list matching its recorded digest, so he has not touched it and only --refresh-prompts replaces it. CONFLICT is his edit and exits 0. Absent is a finding here where completion, problems and exercises report it and never fail, because those hand items over on a ramp while this one delivers the whole corpus every run.

THE BOOTSTRAP RAN AND THE WINDOW IS CLOSED. The worker could not do it, since --adopt writes into ~/tla-practice and its brief forbade that absolutely. Central backed the tree up first (tla-practice-20261018-155932.tar.gz, 1096 files verified) and ran it: 65 file(s) adopted, 0 left unrecorded, and 1 more for practice-root. The tree went 1096 to 1162 files, which is exactly 66 record files and nothing else. Every channel then read in sync.

That window was real. Until the adopt ran, every future source move on a prompt would have read as CONFLICT unrecorded rather than STALE, so the channel would have reported and not failed.

THE STUDY ROOT IS READ TOO, and no argument of the delivery script selects it. It resolves from DRILL_STUDY_ROOT or $HOME/Study/tla-drills, so the wrapper prints the root it read. That tree holds ./drill --style, the command that failed on 2026-10-15 and the reason this bead exists.

A VACUOUS CONTROL WAS FOUND IN THE SUITE BEING EXTENDED. The row asserting the wrapper reports a result for a channel grepped the whole output for a two-space-indented name, and a channel listed under NOT CHECKED is indented identically, so the row passed for drill while the wrapper had never called it. It now reads only the part above NOT CHECKED.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S OWN TEXT. The string '0 prompt(s) to land, 64 already there' is --check wording, not a plain run's. A plain run printed '<n> prompt(s) landed, <n> skipped'. The substance held: a plain run lands none of the changed prompts, because only --refresh-prompts can replace one. Both arms now carry the differing count and name the flag.

BUDGETS NOT RE-BASED AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Three runs each read drill delivery 7.5 s against a 2.3 budget and stale delivery 7.5 s against 1.9, but load sat at 3.2 with a java process at 34 percent belonging to another application. Re-basing on a contended reading is what produced a wrong conclusion on tla-evqq the day before. Both suites were already over budget on the worker's box before its change, so there is probably a real overrun under the load, and it needs a genuinely quiet box to separate the two.

title: Apply the eight clean telegraph fixes the audit ranked
description:
Files: drill/modules/05-two-ledgers-one-helper/PROMPT.md, drill/modules/08-the-shared-siding/PROMPT.md, drill/modules/04-the-two-yards/PROMPT.md, drill/modules/01-the-weighbridge/PROMPT.md, drill/control-state/04-the-interlock/PROMPT.md, drill/temporal/08-turnstile-clock/PROMPT.md, drill/functions-records/05-tool-crib/PROMPT.md, drill/functions-records/02-charging-bays/PROMPT.md

RED: INVARIANT: each edited PROMPT.md no longer carries the quoted sentence the audit named, the corpus gate still passes 64 items with every count claim matching, and no ANSWER.md, META.md or verify/ file is touched.

AUDIT-telegraph.md on main is the spec, 809 lines, one reader over all 64
items. Read its section for each item you edit, and the ruling on tla-0yis
before any of them.

THE AUDIT RANKED THESE EIGHT AS THE CLEAN ONES, because in each a foreclosing
row or verdict ALREADY exists, so cutting the hint costs the reader no
foothold. Its own wording, which you should check against the prompt rather
than apply blind:

  1. modules/05  FAIL-CLEAR. Reword "the two marks, on two different lines of
     the helper, that stop each one traveling" to "what stops each one
     traveling". Row two forecloses. The sentence is LOCAL with the keyword
     removed, and the item's own ANSWER.md:160 says so.
  2. modules/08  Already ruled on tla-0yis. Row three forecloses. Cut the
     second half of Q2.
  3. modules/04  Row six's count forecloses. Replace "the permutation set"
     with "row six's line".
  4. control-state/04  The verdict forecloses and the prompt anticipates it.
     Cut "and whether it belongs in the statement that the guard never stops
     for good".
  5. modules/01  Row six forecloses. Cut "and which variable of the pair it
     lives in".
  6. temporal/08  S2 and S5 foreclose. Cut the clause after the colon.
  7. functions-records/05  Keep the first half of the closing question. No
     count route exists, so the first half is the foothold.
  8. functions-records/02  Same shape, same remedy.

THE TEST, as ruled, so you can check each edit against it: does removing the
sentence leave the item underdetermined? Keep it if the prompt cannot pose its
problem or publish a reproducible count without it. Cut it if the reader could
have reached the answer from the rest and the sentence only shortens the
search.

DO NOT TOUCH ANY OTHER ITEM. Four are Frank's decision and recorded as such in
the audit: control-state/02, 03 and 07, and state-space/06. One needs a
measured neighbour first and is filed separately: sequences/01. One is low
confidence and deliberately held: modules/02.

PROSE UNDER FRANK'S NAME goes through the frank-writing skill. Load it before
you edit, not as a cleanup pass. Never an em dash, never a semicolon, American
spelling. These prompts are read by a person and the register is already set
by the 64 around them, so match the item you are editing rather than importing
a voice.

A CUT MUST LEAVE A SENTENCE THAT READS. Several of these are mid-sentence
clauses, so check the result aloud rather than only checking the token is gone.

GATE IT. The corpus gate reads every prompt: `harness/test-drill.sh` and its
static sweep. Counts are now guarded by tla-ywf4, which closed with 253 claims
parsing and all 251 compared ones matching, so a prose edit that accidentally
disturbs a count table will be caught. Run the drill gate and the spelling
gate, and report both.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-10-15. FIVE OF THE EIGHT PATHS IN THE Files: LINE ABOVE ARE
SLUGS I INVENTED. They exist nowhere in the repo.

  written                                  real
  modules/05-two-ledgers-one-helper        modules/05-the-helper-that-leaked
  modules/08-the-shared-siding             modules/08-doors-of-the-hall
  modules/04-the-two-yards                 modules/04-the-berth-and-the-phantom-ship
  modules/01-the-weighbridge               modules/01-two-tanks-one-hose
  control-state/04-the-interlock           control-state/04-night-patrol

The family and the index were right in all eight, which is what made them
plausible. The three that matched were the three I had read in this session.
The five I got wrong I wrote from recollection of what an item about a helper,
a siding or a weighbridge would be called.

This is exactly the shape CLAUDE.md's "A claim of absence or completeness
names its search" exists to stop, arriving as a claim about a path rather than
about a set. The worker searched for all five and reported rc 1 on every form
before editing the real items, which the audit names correctly.

A WRONG Files: LINE IS NOT COSMETIC. It is the input the fan-out detector uses
to decide which beads are wave-compatible, and two beads are compatible only
when their Files: sets are provably disjoint. A path that names nothing is
disjoint from everything, so a stale line reads as safe to parallelize when it
is not.

SECOND CORRECTION, AND THE AUDIT CONTRADICTS ITSELF. Item 8 above says of
functions-records/02 "Same shape, same remedy", copied from the audit's
summary at AUDIT-telegraph.md:744, which lumps 05 and 02 together as "keep the
first half of each closing question".

The audit's own per-item section at :506-508 says the opposite: the first half,
"which of the two rules you had to write down as a property", presupposes the
same thing, so cutting one half does not close it. The section is right. The
worker took the section over the summary and rewrote the question instead of
half-cutting it, which is the judgment the brief asked for rather than
compliance.
close_reason: Eight prompts edited at 888373b, with before and after quoted for every cut. Gates green: drill gate 185 assertions and 64 items with 0 findings, static sweep 5, spelling 16, and count claims reading 253 parsed 251 compared 2 waived, exactly the tla-ywf4 figures, so no count table moved. cibuild --skip-docs green at 36 suites in 410.5s with corpus 107 passed. The worker diverged on functions-records/02 and was right to: the audit's summary and its own per-item section disagree, and the section is correct that cutting half the question leaves the presupposition intact.

title: verdict.sh's rc 12 line says safety, and the discriminator measures as the declaring keyword
description:
Files: harness/verdict.sh (CENTRALLY OWNED, report not edit), .claude/rules/tla-practice.md

MEASURED 2026-10-15 by the tla-d6o0.3 author, which reported rather than
edited because harness/verdict.sh is centrally owned. Verified against the
file by central in the same session.

harness/verdict.sh:54-57 documents:

  12  SAFETY_VIOLATION   something refutable by a finite prefix -- an
                         INVARIANT, or a PROPERTY that is a safety
                         property. NOT "an INVARIANT was violated"

THE MEASURED CASE CONTRADICTS THE SECOND CLAUSE. A state predicate declared
under `PROPERTY` and refuted by the INITIAL STATE returns **rc 13**, printing
`Property RInit is violated by the initial state`.

An initial state is the shortest finite prefix there is, so by the documented
rule this is squarely rc 12. It is 13.

THE LIKELY DISCRIMINATOR, and it needs confirming before the file is edited:
rc 12 against rc 13 tracks the KEYWORD the formula was declared under rather
than the logical character of the formula. Anything under `PROPERTY` goes
through the liveness checker and exits 13 whether its counterexample is finite
or not. If that is right, the clause "or a PROPERTY that is a safety property"
describes a case this build never produces, and the honest line is that 12
means INVARIANT and 13 means PROPERTY.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE COMMENT. The whole v2 corpus takes verdicts from
exit codes rather than from TLC's prose, which V2-PLAN.md section 5.1 settles.
Several drill items and now several reading items publish an expected rc, and
an author reasoning from this comment would predict 12 for a safety-shaped
PROPERTY and be wrong. The tla-d6o0.3 author predicted exactly that and
measured 13.

BEFORE EDITING, MEASURE THE THREE CASES. A state predicate under INVARIANT
(expect 12). The same predicate under PROPERTY, refuted at the initial state
(measured 13). A box-action safety property under PROPERTY, refuted mid-trace
(unmeasured, and the one that decides whether the rule is about the keyword or
about the initial state specifically). Every empirical constant in V2-PLAN.md
section 5 was verified against two independent builds four months apart, which
is the standard this line should be held to rather than one observation.

Related, same wave, same author: the same property answers to TWO NAMES
depending on which conjunct broke. A refinement conjunct prints `Temporal
property Refines was violated`, the name the .cfg declared, while the box
action inside it prints by SOURCE SPAN, `Action property line 9, col 19 to
line 9, col 30 of module Cycle`. Both at rc 13. Worth a line wherever the
first fact lands.
notes:
2026-10-18, central. MEASURED, and this bead's proposed discriminator is REFUTED.

The bead proposed that 12 means INVARIANT and 13 means PROPERTY, on the
strength of one observation. A 24-cell grid plus two INVARIANT controls says
no. Three PROPERTY shapes exit 12 with no INVARIANT anywhere in the .cfg.

THE GRID, TLC 2026.07.31.184830, one system, one claim per run:

                    no conjunct   WF   SF   []<>   empty spec   []P conjunct
  INVARIANT P            12       12   12    12        12           255
  PROPERTY []P           12       12   12    12        12           255
  PROPERTY P             13       13   13    13        13           255
  PROPERTY ~<>P          12       13   13    13         0           255
  PROPERTY []<>FALSE     13       13   13    13         0           255

THE THREE CASES THE BEAD ASKED FOR, all measured:

1. A state predicate under INVARIANT: 12, and fairness does not move it.
2. The same predicate under PROPERTY, refuted at the initial state: 13, and
   fairness does not move that either. So this bead's case is not about
   fairness at all, which is what separates it from tla-vzu3.
3. A box-action safety property under PROPERTY refuted mid-trace: 13 in every
   column. The bead called this the one that decides between the keyword rule
   and the initial-state rule. It decides against both.

THE RULE THAT SURVIVES: 12 and 13 name the CHANNEL that reported, and there
are three channels. The invariant channel lifts a box over a state predicate
and is immune to everything below it. The safety channel holds a
finite-prefix-refutable formula that will not lift, and only while the spec
formula carries no liveness conjunct. The liveness channel takes the rest.

A BARE STATE PREDICATE UNDER PROPERTY IS THE SHARPEST CELL. TLC prints
'Property P is violated by the initial state' and exits 13. So 'rc 12 means a
finite counterexample' is not the rule either, and the bead was right that the
old comment predicted a code it does not deliver.

The second file this bead named, .claude/rules/tla-practice.md, took a
different finding than expected: the machine-closure paragraph in section 2
now carries the empty-spec route, because 'subactions of Next' turned out to
be the whole condition and breaking it costs more than machine closure.
close_reason: Settled at db5f869. A 24-cell grid plus two INVARIANT controls shows three channels rather than two, so both beads' proposed discriminators are refuted and the rule that survives is that 12 and 13 name the channel that reported. lj1n's three measured cases and vzu3's reproduction are in their notes. harness/verdict.sh carries the grid, harness/test-verdict.sh pins eleven cells and goes from 39 assertions to 50, and .claude/rules/tla-practice.md section 2 takes the empty-spec route into machine closure. title: test-coverage-map.sh hardcodes the corpus size, which is the staleness shape the rules file complains about
description:
Files: harness/test-coverage-map.sh

RED: INVARIANT: no assertion in harness/test-coverage-map.sh carries a literal corpus count, and the suite stays green when a reading item or a drill item is added.

REPORTED INDEPENDENTLY BY TWO WORKERS in the tla-d6o0 wave, 2026-10-15,
within minutes of each other.

harness/test-coverage-map.sh:271 reads `[ "${n_uses:-0}" -eq 25 ]` against a
mirror built from the live tree. The reading corpus went 25 to 33 in one wave,
so the suite reports:

  FAIL the mirror holds 64 META.md and 26 USES.md, expected 64 and 25
  FAIL --check reddens on the unmutated mirror, so every control below is
       meaningless

and the second line cascades into four more, so 6 of 31 fail and 18 of the 31
are controls that stop meaning anything.

THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE THE DISPATCH RULES FILE COMPLAINS ABOUT TWICE, now in
an assertion rather than in prose. That file carried "28 suites" and an
"18-suite fast tier" against a real 35 and 23, and its own paragraph records
going stale at 10 suites and then at 13 before that. I took those numbers out
tonight rather than correcting them a fourth time. An assertion is worse than
prose, because prose that is stale merely misleads while an assertion that is
stale turns 18 controls into noise and reddens a gate nobody broke.

THE FIX IS TO DERIVE THE COUNT, not to move 25 to 33. Count the live tree and
compare the mirror against it, so adding an item can never redden this suite.
If a count has to be pinned for a control, pin it inside a fixture the suite
builds rather than against the real corpus.

A SECOND THING, AND IT IS MINE. The suite was never registered in
scripts/test, so the gate it provides has been running nowhere since it
landed. `command grep -c test-coverage-map scripts/test` returned 0. I
registered it at `fast|1.3` in the same session this bead was filed, from the
author's measured worst-of-three of 1.2 s. That is the gate-don't-advise shape
arriving by omission rather than by decision: the author said central owned
the row, the brief said so too, and I registered the sibling suite and forgot
this one.

ALSO NEEDED ONCE, AND NOT PART OF THIS BEAD: `bash scripts/gen-coverage.sh`
has to run and be committed after the tla-d6o0 wave lands, because fields 8, 9
and 10 of drill/INVENTORY.md are generated from both corpora and eight new
reading items belong on a lot of rows. Per worker that would collide eight
ways on one file, which is why every worker correctly left it alone.
close_reason: Fixed inline at 9a69f11, the same session it was filed. harness/test-coverage-map.sh:271 asserted the mirror holds exactly 25 USES.md, which the eight-model wave broke, and the next assertion says a red mirror makes every control below meaningless, so one stale literal took 18 controls with it. It now counts the live tree and compares the mirror against that, so adding an item cannot redden it. 31 assertions pass. The suite was also registered nowhere in scripts/test, so the gate had been running nowhere since it landed, and it is now registered at fast|1.4.
