title: Build the eight reading models the plan ruled for
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: epic, children carry the work

THE PLAN IS THE SPEC. PLAN-reading-expansion.md on main, 727 lines, written by
a single planner that read all 25 landed models so no two insights collide.
Each child names its own section. Read the epic, then your section, then the
three landed models nearest yours.

WHY EIGHT AND NOT FORTY. The planner ruled against a wave and I agree. Reading
already reaches 100 of the 105 constructs at 25 models, measured by the gated
coverage map (drill/INVENTORY.md field 10). Volume is not short either: Frank
has read one model and 25 are unread, four sittings at his figure of six. What
survives is DEPTH and DIFFERENTIATION, which supports eight. Its own stated
limit: it cannot measure whether an insight lands in 10 minutes without Frank
reading some, so after these eight the channel waits for his reaction.

THE SHARED CONTRACT, from tla-fwkz.2, and every child obeys all of it.

CONSTRUCT EXPOSURE, NOT RECOGNITION PRACTICE. Settled by Frank 2026-10-13. NO
comprehension question and NO answer key. He reads a model and moves on.

HIS QUALITY BAR, verbatim 2026-10-11: "The models should do something
moderately interesting so it's something I need to work out, there should be
interesting PROPERTIES etc for them." Plus "get fully in my head in 10
minutes". The epic is blunt about the failure: "A twelve-line counter with a
type invariant satisfies every gate and is worthless to read."

THE INSIGHT FIELD IN YOUR SECTION IS THE DELIVERABLE. Everything else serves
it. Aim for the moment a reader says "wait, why does that hold" and then works
it out from the spec in front of them. reading/temporal/01-handover is the bar:
WF_vars(Grant) alone satisfies want ~> ~want, which looks too weak until you
notice Request's own guard disables it.

EVERY MODEL IS A DIRECTORY of three files: <Module>.tla, <Module>.cfg and
USES.md. USES.md carries a `Subject:` line, an `rc:` line, `## Constructs` and
`## Constructs from other families, also exercised` in drill/INVENTORY.md
field 4 spelling, and prose on what the properties rest on. Read three landed
USES.md files before writing yours.

TWO GATES ARE NEW SINCE THE LAST WAVE AND BOTH BIND YOU.

harness/reading-gate.sh check 7 refuses a reused slug. Check 8 refuses a
Subject that restates a landed one, firing at 4 shared distinctive words AND
40% of the shorter subject. Calibration, measured: the real corpus worst pair
is 3 words at 27%, a real historical duplicate was 5 at 50%. Run
`harness/reading-gate.sh --registry reading` and read the roster before you
write your Subject. Do not paste a copy of the roster into anything, generate
it.

The gate also prints, on every run, that a duplicated LEMMA inside a different
system is NOT gated. That one is on you to avoid by reading the landed models.

VERIFY YOUR OWN rc AND STATE COUNT, and put the real numbers in USES.md. Your
section predicts both. A prediction that turns out wrong is a finding worth
reporting, not a number to quietly replace.

tla-16je is open about five corpus repositories shipping no licence. Calibrate
against the Community Specifications at learning.tlapl.us and never copy a
spec from them.
notes:
HAZARD FOUND BY tla-d6o0.5, 2026-10-15, relayed to the two siblings exposed.

THE PLAN'S "Constructs" LISTS NAME OPERATORS, NOT IMPORTS, and they mix
keywords and module members without marking which is which. The .5 author's
first run came back PARSE_ERROR rc 150, "Could not find declaration or
definition of symbol '@@'", because `:>` and `@@` live in the TLC standard
module rather than in Naturals. `EXTENDS Naturals, TLC` fixed it, and
reading/functions-records/03-overlay already does exactly that.

Sections 1 and 4 name `Cardinality`, which is in FiniteSets, so both were
warned. Section 4 also names SUBSET, RECURSIVE and LET-IN, which are keywords
needing no import, which is the mixing.

Check each operator in your list for the module that defines it, and read what
the landed models in your family already EXTEND, before your first run.

TWO MEASUREMENTS FROM .5 WORTH CARRYING.

An action can contribute ZERO distinct states. Its `Forget` did: every state
Forget reached was already reachable by a shorter path through `Hit`, and TLC
said so on the per-action coverage line as `<Forget ...>: 0:144`. So do not
predict a state count from the number of actions, and read the coverage line
before reaching for a CONSTRAINT when a count comes in low.

`EXCEPT` on a key a function does not carry is a SILENT NO-OP and the `@`
inside it is never evaluated. The author expected rc 75 on an undefined
reference and got rc 12 naming a different invariant instead. It kept that as
a second probe because it reaches the same insight from the other side, which
is the right instinct.

IT ALSO SHIPPED THREE INVARIANTS AGAINST THE PLAN'S TWO, with a reason I
accept: typing the sparse range as `0..Max` rather than `1..Max` keeps
`TypeOK /\ Agree` from implying the third, so the headline probe names the
invariant the plan predicted instead of naming TypeOK. A deviation argued from
what the probe would otherwise report is the kind to make.
close_reason: All eight reading models landed, merged and gated. The corpus went 25 to 33 items, cibuild --skip-docs green at 36 suites in 410.8s with corpus 107 passed 0 failed, pushed through the bead export. Coverage regenerated: 77 both, 24 reading-only, 2 drill-only, 2 neither, with K091 moving off drill-only exactly as the Peterson author predicted. Every one of the eight refuted at least one plan prediction, which is the plan working rather than failing, since the predictions were specific enough to be wrong. Commits a24733a 6de323f 4e65e88 b692b25 eb1b32a 29d3f61 f2623e7 7bdb58d. Plan at PLAN-reading-expansion.md.

title: The Bash tool's grep is not GNU grep, and the word-boundary idiom silently disagrees
description:
Files: .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md

MEASURED 2026-10-15, found by the tla-iiow planner and verified independently.

`type grep` in the Bash tool's shell reports a SHELL FUNCTION from
~/.claude/shell-snapshots/snapshot-zsh-*.sh, not /run/current-system/sw/bin/grep.
It does not answer the same as GNU grep 3.12 on one common idiom:

  pattern                              shell  gnu
  CASE                                   1      1   same
  ^CASE                                  0      0   same
  CASE|VARIABLES                         1      1   same
  CASE([^A-Za-z_]|$)                     1      1   same
  [[:space:]]CASE                        1      1   same
  (^|x)CASE                              0      0   same
  (^|[^A-Za-z_])CASE                     0      1   DIFFER

All against reading/core/02-chameleons/Chameleons.tla with -cE.

SO THE BROKEN SHAPE IS THE WORD-BOUNDARY IDIOM, `(^|[^class])TOKEN`, which is
exactly what you reach for when counting a construct's occurrences without
matching it inside a longer identifier. It returns 0 where the answer is 1.
A leading-anchor alternation against a literal works, and a trailing one
works, so the divergence is narrow and therefore easy to walk into.

GATES ARE UNAFFECTED. Every suite and harness file here carries a
`#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang and gets GNU grep. The exposure is interactive
measurement, which means central and every dispatched worker, both of which
run their scans through the Bash tool.

I SUSPECT THIS CONTRIBUTED TO THE MEASUREMENT ERRORS. Five wrong counts in one
session, all plausible. At least three were my own pattern bugs and are
accounted for (a `\|` written inside -E, a character class that allowed
whitespace and ran past a declaration, an awk walk that stopped after one
continuation line). How many of the rest were this is not established, and
claiming it without evidence would be the same error in a new costume.

THE FIX IS ONE PARAGRAPH IN THE RULES FILE, beside the pipefail hazard: when a
count matters, run it through `command grep`, or put the scan in a scratch
script with a bash shebang. Both get GNU. Prefer the script, which the file
already recommends for other refusals.

Worth checking whether the same wrapper covers other tools a measurement
depends on. `sed`, `awk` and `find` are the ones to look at, and `type` answers
it in one call each.
close_reason: Characterized and recorded at 616e0cd. grep and find are both shell functions from the Claude Code snapshot, running the claude binary as ugrep 7.8.4 and as bfs, while ten other tools are real binaries. The lying shape is wider than I found: a negated bracket expression as a whole alternation branch or under a quantifier, plus (x|$) reading 1 against 13, -co counting matches rather than lines, and grep -r honoring .gitignore for a 1474 against 1481 file-set difference. The blast radius came back empty: 121 open and 396 closed beads, the drawers, tla-practice.md and the generated inventory carry no count measured in the lying shape, and seven re-measured load-bearing counts matched both ways.

title: Gate reading-model subject collisions, which wave 1 only caught by luck
description:
Files: harness/reading-gate.sh, harness/test-reading.sh

RED: Given two reading models whose USES.md Subject lines describe the same system, When the reading gate runs, Then it fails and names both paths; and Given 25 distinct subjects, Then it passes.

THE MEASURED FAILURE, from bead tla-fwkz.2.9. Wave 1 produced two near-misses
in nineteen models and the authors catching them was luck rather than process.
The tla-fwkz.2.1 author finished a chameleons model, found it duplicated
reading/core/02-chameleons written by a sibling in the same wave, replaced it,
finished a coprime model, found THAT duplicated 01-euclid's own divisor lemma
two items along in its own family, and replaced it again. 04-ring is the third
attempt. Both discards are in the reflog at fbd5ae2.

NO GATE SEES THIS CLASS. harness/reading-gate.sh checks shape, the phone
bound, the recorded rc, and that the .cfg declares an obligation. Two models
teaching the same thing both pass, and the cost lands on Frank, who reads them
back to back in one sitting of six.

A PARALLEL WAVE MAKES IT WORSE BY CONSTRUCTION, because no worker can see what
a sibling is writing. The one author who caught the core collision did so
because it read the landed six and then happened to re-read main. This bead is
the prerequisite for spending any volume on reading authoring, because at
forty models collisions stop being unlucky and become certain.

THE REGISTRY IS ALREADY MECHANICAL. Every USES.md carries a `Subject:` line
and there are 25 of them today:

  grep -h '^Subject:' reading/*/*/USES.md

A Subject is prose and wraps across lines, so read it flattened. A line-based
scan of this corpus has produced a plausible wrong count five times in one
session, twice in the hour before this bead was filed.

WHAT "THE SAME THING" MEANS IS THE HARD PART and you do not have to solve it
perfectly. A cheap exact-ish check that fires on the real cases is worth far
more than a clever one that is hard to trust. The two real collisions were a
duplicated SYSTEM (chameleons) and a duplicated LEMMA inside a different
system (coprime against euclid's divisor lemma). The second is harder and may
be out of reach of a mechanical check. If it is, gate the first, SAY the
second is not gated, and do not pretend otherwise. An advisory half of a gate
that claims to be whole is worse than a gate that states its limit.

Also emit the registry in a form a brief can paste, because every authoring
brief above this bead needs it and deriving it by hand in each one is how the
three copies of the smoke battery drifted before .claude/rules existed.

harness/Gate.tla and harness/verdict.sh are centrally owned. If you need
either changed, report it rather than editing it.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-10-15, found by the tla-ldvw worker.

This bead says "Both discards are in the reflog at fbd5ae2". ONLY THE
CHAMELEONS ONE IS. `git log --all --oneline -S'coprime'` returns one commit,
7a66975 "Refresh the bead export", which is this bead's own text rather than
the model. The coprime model was discarded BEFORE it was ever committed, so no
blob of it exists and no measurement of its Subject line is possible.

That matters for the gate's calibration rather than just the record: the
coprime-against-euclid case is the HARDER of the two collisions, a duplicated
lemma inside a different system, and there is no artifact to test a check
against. The worker recorded the absence in the gate's header rather than
guessing at the wording, which is the right call.

THE GATE AS BUILT, and its calibration is measured rather than chosen:

  real corpus worst pair      3 shared words at 27%   (handover/converge)
  the real chameleons discard 5 shared words at 50%
  the pair kept on purpose    1 shared word at 12%    (contend/contention)

The bound fires at 4 words AND 40% of the shorter subject. So three words of
margin above the corpus and one word below the duplicate.

THIS BEAD'S OWN OBJECTION IS ANSWERED. tla-fwkz.2.9 argued a subject check
would flag pluscal/03-contend against temporal/04-contention, which central
keeps deliberately. It does not: 1 word at 12%, nowhere near the bound.

The worker is honest that the bound sits in a gap one word wide on each side,
and that this is one real positive against 300 real negatives. The lemma case
stays ungated, the gate prints that on every run, and a suite row pins the
string so it cannot quietly stop saying so.
close_reason: harness/reading-gate.sh now refuses a reused slug and a Subject that restates a landed one, with a --registry roster for briefs. Commit afa3a98. Calibration measured rather than chosen: the real corpus worst pair is 3 shared words at 27%, the real historical duplicate was 5 at 50%, and the pair central keeps deliberately is 1 at 12%, against a bound of 4 words and 40%. It answers tla-fwkz.2.9's own objection, which argued the check would flag that kept pair. The duplicated-lemma case stays ungated and the gate prints that on every run.

title: Fill INVENTORY field 8, so both channels know which of the 105 constructs they reach
description:
Files: drill/INVENTORY.md, scripts/gen-coverage.sh, harness/test-coverage-map.sh

RED: INVARIANT: every one of the 105 ROW lines in drill/INVENTORY.md carries a non-empty field 8, the generator reproduces the file byte for byte from the two corpora, and the gate fails when a row's coverage disagrees with what the corpora actually contain.

THE HOLE. drill/INVENTORY.md's header documents field 8 as coverage and says
"empty today". Measured 2026-10-15: `grep '^ROW' drill/INVENTORY.md | cut -f8
| sort | uniq -c` gives 105 empty. So no one can answer "which constructs has
the reading channel reached" or "which has the drill corpus reached", and both
questions are the input to every authoring decision above this bead.

TWO CORPORA TO MEASURE AGAINST:
  - the drill corpus, 64 items, whose META.md files carry a constructs list
    under one of two headers (56 `## Constructs`, 8 `## Constructs exercised`,
    plus 32 with a second `## Constructs from other families, also
    exercised`). Bullets are spelled as INVENTORY field 4 spells them, which
    the META files say explicitly, so the join is by that spelling.
  - the reading corpus, 25 models under reading/*/NN-slug/ with a USES.md
    each. USES.md carries `Subject:` and prose and NO construct list, so
    reading coverage has to be derived from the .tla itself or the USES.md
    needs a field. Decide which, argue it in the generator's header, and say
    in your report which you chose and what it cost.

GENERATE, NEVER HAND-EDIT. 105 rows by two channels is exactly the shape that
goes stale silently. scripts/gen-coverage.sh regenerates the field and the
gate proves the file matches what the corpora say. Model it on
scripts/gen-curriculum-map.sh, and read its hazard first: that script used to
open with a hardcoded `cd /home/frank/repos/tla-puzzles`, so running it from a
worktree wrote into the MAIN checkout, which no footprint check can see.
Resolve the root from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`, never a literal path. Bead tla-1hf.

ROWS ARE TAB-DELIMITED with the literal first field `ROW`. Never field-split a
TSV with `IFS=$'\t' read`: bash strips leading and trailing empty fields and
collapses runs of the separator, so a TSV read that way loses data without
saying so. `cut -f` is the sanctioned form.

A LINE-BASED SCAN OF THESE CORPORA GIVES PLAUSIBLE WRONG ANSWERS. Measured
five times in one session. Two of mine in the hour before this bead was
filed: a `grep -E` pattern written with `\|`, which matches a literal pipe
rather than alternation and returned 0 items where the answer was 9; and a
character class that allowed whitespace, so the scan ran past a declaration
into the next keyword and reported 104 lowercase constants where the answer is
6. Flatten deliberately and check any surprising zero or round number twice.

The empty field is NEVER a coverage of zero. A construct no corpus reaches
gets an explicit marker, so "nothing reaches this" and "nobody measured this"
can never be confused. That distinction is the whole point of the bead.
close_reason: drill/INVENTORY.md now carries a generated coverage verdict per row, with scripts/gen-coverage.sh and harness/test-coverage-map.sh gating it. Commit b158d5a. The headline measurement killed the premise of a 40-model wave: reading reached 100 of 105 constructs at 25 models and drill 79, with only 2 unreached by either and one of those already retired as anti-idiomatic. Field 8 could not carry the marker because drill-gate.sh:815 seeds a count from it and any word would have dropped all 26 gap rows out of CONSTRUCT GAPS, so the verdict went in a new field 10 and the safety was proved by diffing COVERAGE lines byte for byte.

title: The style measuring script
description:
Files: drill/study/style, harness/test-drill-style.sh

RED: Given an attempt whose constants are snake_case, whose Next inlines its disjuncts and which declares no type invariant, When style runs, Then it reports one fact line per axis with the measured value and the survey count beside it, and exits 0.

A measuring script in the shape of drill/study/check: the script measures, the
model interprets. The model has no tools under `--tools ""` and cannot run a
count, which is why this exists at all.

STYLE HAS NO PASS AND NO FAIL, AND THE EXIT CODES SAY SO. 0 when it measured
anything, 3 when it could not run (no module, no prompt, nothing to read).
There is NO exit 1. A style pass that can fail becomes a gate on Frank's own
work, and the one thing worse than no reviewer is one that blocks.

THE AXES, each mapping to a register entry so the two files agree:
  - identifier case for every CONSTANT and VARIABLE name, classified
    CamelCase / snake_case / short-lowercase
  - is a type invariant declared, by name shape and by body shape
  - does a `vars` tuple exist, and does it cover every declared variable
  - is the behavior formula named `Spec`
  - is the box subscript the full tuple or a proper subset
  - are Next's disjuncts named actions or inline anonymous arms
  - how many obligations does the config name

REPORT FACTS, NOT JUDGMENTS. The script says what it measured and what the
survey counted. It never says "wrong" or "should". The model reads the facts
against drill/study/STYLE.md and writes the prose. Same split that keeps
`check` honest: `check` reports a count and refuses to judge intent.

A worked instance to assert against, measured 2026-10-15 on Frank's real
attempt at ~/Study/tla-drills/01-slip-on-the-spike/pickers.tla. It declares
`CONSTANTS picker_count, max_slips` (both snake_case), `vars == <<pickers,
slips>>` covering both declared variables, `Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars`,
`Next == \E p \in 1..picker_count: \/ ... \/ ...` with two anonymous inline
arms, no type invariant, and a config naming 2 invariants. Every axis has a
real value on that one file, so it makes a good fixture. COPY it into a
fixture rather than reading his tree, and do not write into his tree.

THE BORROWED-CONFIG AND SKIP RULES ALREADY SETTLED IN tla-rzvk.4 APPLY HERE
TOO. Skip `*_TTrace_*`, `states/` and `*.old`. A module with no config of its
own is still a module worth measuring for style, since style needs no config
at all, so do NOT inherit check's pairing requirement. Measuring style does
not run TLC.

DO NOT RUN TLC. This script reads text. tla-rzvk.5 is open because `check`
runs TLC in the work directory and litters it, and a style pass has no reason
to go near that.

Read drill/study/check first for the house style: the two environment
variables with documented defaults, resolution by slug glob with no mapping
data, and a header that argues its own decisions. Match it.
close_reason: drill/study/style landed at 7bc9022, 181 assertions, measuring seven axes per module with both tiers on every line and no judgment word anywhere. Improved on my instruction: rather than making C3 win when the tiers disagree, it prints both and lets the register rule, so an empty corpus-c1 field states that published practice never measured identifier case. Cross-checked the register's counts by its own method and matched five of six exactly, finding the sixth difference was an operator arity its first tokenizer dropped. A grep-per-line draft ran 10 to 34 s and parameter expansions took it to 1.53 s.

title: Deliver the style pair, and add ./drill --style
description:
Files: scripts/deliver-drill.sh, harness/test-deliver-drill.sh, drill/drill.sh, harness/test-drill-runner.sh

RED: Given a delivered study root, When deliver-drill.sh --study runs, Then drill/study/STYLE.md and drill/study/style land with the right modes and are named in the output with their own verbs; and Given LAST-SERVED names a drill, When ./drill --style runs, Then the stub claude receives MODE: style, the register, the style script's output and the attempt, on stdin, with --tools empty.

TWO HALVES, both small, and they are one bead because they share no file with
their siblings and both are plumbing for files those siblings write.

(1) DELIVERY. `drill/study/STYLE.md` and `drill/study/style` are new study
files. scripts/deliver-drill.sh already delivers four classes with their own
output verbs (`configuration delivered:`, `command delivered:`,
`checker delivered:`, and the README it always overwrites). Add these two the
same way, with `style register` and `style script` as their verbs, and the
script at mode 0755 like the checker. The existing refusal when the root does
not exist, and the `left alone (your work, never written here):` line, both
stay exactly as they are.

(2) THE FLAG. `./drill --style`, resolved from LAST-SERVED like `--check`,
with the same optional explicit drill argument. It runs
`$STUDY_ROOT/style`, cats the attempt, cats `$STUDY_ROOT/STYLE.md`, and pipes
`MODE: style` plus all of it to `claude -p --tools ""` on stdin. Everything
about the invocation is settled and measured in tla-rzvk: stdin not argv, cwd
is the slug directory so CLAUDE.md loads itself, no tool is ever added back.

THE REGISTER IS CAT INTO THE PROMPT, which is new. `--check` ships the prompt,
the checker output and the attempt. `--style` also ships STYLE.md, because
with no tools the model cannot read it off disk. That makes the style prompt
the biggest of the three, so report its byte size in your return.

IT FAILS SOFT LIKE EVERY OTHER DEPENDENCY. No `claude`, no
`$STUDY_ROOT/style`, no `$STUDY_ROOT/STYLE.md`, no attempt: one clear message
each and a nonzero exit, never a crash under `set -u` and never a half-run.
The serve path keeps working with none of them present.

THE HEADER INVARIANT. drill/drill.sh's header was narrowed once for the study
mkdir and again in tla-rzvk.2 for the three outside reads. This adds two more
reads under the same root, which the existing argument already covers. Check
whether it does before you widen it again, and if it covers them, say so
rather than adding a paragraph.

YOUR SIBLINGS WRITE THE TWO FILES AND MAY NOT HAVE LANDED YET. The filenames
are locked in the epic, so build and test against your own fixtures rather
than waiting. A suite that only passes once a sibling lands is not green.

Do not touch scripts/test. Central owns the budget rows. Report worst-of-three
wall time for both suites you touch.
close_reason: scripts/deliver-drill.sh ships the style pair and ./drill --style works, committed d44ca09. Measured the register at 87% of the style prompt, 9871 bytes against 1303 for a check over the same attempt, which is the price of the model having no tools. The header invariant did not need widening but its enumeration said the script reads three things outside itself where the code now reads five, and a row went red to force that count up. Found that two message assertions also passed vacuously, because the unknown-option path prints usage() and usage() contains the tokens they looked for.

title: The style register, distilled from the corpus survey
description:
Files: drill/study/STYLE.md

RED: INVARIANT: every claim in STYLE.md carries a tier marker (C1, C2 or C3), no claim is stated without one, the register names core/04-lift-types as excluded from the type-invariant axis, and it carries the survey's own descriptive-not-normative limit verbatim enough to bind a reader.

Write the register a study session reads to interpret what drill/study/style
measures. Source it from `.claude/rules/tla-practice.md` (474 lines, 2026-09-05,
27cd653). Read the WHOLE survey before writing a line of this.

IT IS A DISTILLATION, NOT A COPY. The survey is a research document with
methodology, thin-spot caveats and re-run instructions. The register is what a
coach needs at the moment it is reading an attempt. Keep the counts and the
page citations. Drop the methodology.

EVERY CLAIM CARRIES A TIER, and the epic defines all three. C1 is a count from
the survey. C2 is Lamport's stated reason with a page number, and it is the
only ground for saying a choice COSTS something. C3 is a count run now over a
named body on disk, and drill/study/style is what runs those.

THE AXES WORTH CARRYING, with the counts already verified 2026-10-15:
  - the state tuple: 181 of 375 plain-tuple definitions are named `vars`, 342
    of 375 end in vars or Vars (tla-practice.md:253)
  - the behavior formula: 170 of 205 definitions shaped `Init /\ [][Next]_v`
    are named `Spec` (:260)
  - the subscript: 405 of 421 resolvable box sites cover every variable,
    96.2% (:175)
  - type invariants: `TypeOK` is 117 of 713 invariant declarations and a
    `Type` prefix is 164 of 713, 23% (:269, :293)
  - Next's shape: 105 of 238 modules write it as a bulleted disjunction of
    NAMED actions, 69 as an existential over a NAMED parameterised action
    (:279). Action names are verbs from the system's vocabulary.
  - decomposition: median 2 named obligations, mean 2.79, and the C2 reason
    at Specifying Systems 14.5.3 p. 259.
  - identifier case: C3 only, because the survey never measured it. 126 of 132
    reference-spec constants are CamelCase or ALLCAPS, 0 snake_case, and the 6
    others are `a b l1 l2 w1 w4`. So the rule is CamelCase for a named concept
    and short lowercase for a mathematical placeholder.

SECTION 7 IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART TO CARRY. "A reviewer that fires on every
deviation is worse than no reviewer", then thirteen routine shapes. A register
that carries the conventions and not the exemptions produces a coach that
fires on a subscript naming one variable of several, which 12 of 16 corpus
sites do soundly, or on an obligation defined and never checked, which is 133
of 286. Carry all thirteen.

THE SURVEY'S SILENCE RULE BINDS THE COACH. "Silence in this document is a gap,
not permission." Where no tier has a number, the register says to say nothing
rather than to reason from first principles. That is the whole difference
between this and a model inventing conventions and sounding authoritative.

EXCLUSION, one item, by name. core/04-lift-types drills the `TypeOK` idiom
itself ("the `TypeOK` idiom, `Int` against `Nat`, and the config's missing
negative literal"), so the type-invariant axis is silent on it. The other 8
items naming a type invariant are all sequences/* where the construct is
`Seq(S)` and TypeOK is only where it sits, so they are NOT excluded.

KEEP THE EXISTING REGISTER. drill/study/CLAUDE.md reports behavior, never the
construct, and this file does not get to overrule that. A style remark is
about the TLA+ he DID write, never about what the drill wanted and he missed.
"126 of 132 constants in the reference specs are CamelCase and yours are not"
is a style remark. "You need a type invariant here" is the answer to some
other item and is not one.

DO NOT quote any item's ANSWER.md, META.md or verify/ contents into this file.
It is delivered to the study tree. The reference-spec counts are aggregates
and safe. A named spec from under verify/ is not.
close_reason: drill/study/STYLE.md landed at 3582bd9, 306 lines, 54 claims and every one tiered: 40 C1, 3 C2, 11 C3, zero untiered. It deleted the claims it could not source and named them as explicit silences instead, including operator spelling, comment density, definition order and indentation. Found my constant count wrong with the mechanism: 134 of 140 rather than 126 of 132, because my walk stopped after one continuation line, and it reproduced 113, 132 and 140 to prove it. Carried all thirteen routine shapes from section 7.

title: Style commentary on a drill attempt, grounded in three citation tiers
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: epic, children carry the work

Frank asked for style commentary beside the correctness check: "It's working
TLA+, is it good TLA+? Is it idiomatic TLA+, this will require careful research
so the checker knows what good and idiomatic are."

THE RESEARCH ALREADY EXISTS and has never been delivered.
`.claude/rules/tla-practice.md`, 474 lines, filed 2026-09-05 at 27cd653: 666
modules and 337 configs from 16 public repositories, every number from a script
run over the clones. It is in the repo, which the study session is forbidden to
read, so no session has ever seen it.

ITS OWN LIMIT IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT. It opens by calling itself "a record of
what people who publish TLA+ do, not advice about any particular project", and
closes with "Silence in this document is a gap, not permission." So it grounds
IDIOMATIC with counts and cannot ground GOOD at all.

THE THREE CITATION TIERS. Frank's contribution, and every style remark carries
exactly one and names it. A remark with no tier is not made.

  C1  MEASURED IN THE PUBLISHED CORPUS. A count from the survey. The strongest
      ground for "idiomatic". Reproducible: the survey's "Re-running the
      numbers" section carries all 16 repos with clone SHAs and the exact
      greps. THE CLONES ARE GONE from this box (searched ~/corpus,
      ~/tla-corpus, ~/clones, ~/src, /tmp, and for CommunityModules and
      kafka-tlaplus by name), so an axis the survey did not measure is
      re-clonable rather than unknowable. Bead tla-16je's licence caution is
      about REDISTRIBUTING specs, not measuring them, and the survey is the
      precedent for measuring.

  C2  LAMPORT'S STATED REASON, with a page number. The ONLY ground for saying
      a choice costs something rather than merely being unusual. The survey
      already carries several, e.g. Specifying Systems 14.5.3 p. 259, that
      separate names make TLC tell you which conjunct is false.

  C3  OBSERVED IN CODE TO DATE. A count run NOW over a named body on disk.
      Two bodies, and they answer different questions:
        - this repo's 498 reference specs under drill/*/verify/: what the
          answers to these drills look like.
        - Frank's own .tla files: whether something is a habit of his.

C3 WORKS, AND IT ANSWERED THE QUESTION THAT PROMPTED IT. Measured 2026-10-15:

  132 distinct CONSTANT names across the 498 reference specs. 126 CamelCase or
  ALLCAPS, 0 snake_case, 6 all-lowercase. The six are `a b l1 l2 w1 w4`, all
  mathematical placeholders rather than words, so the rule is "CamelCase for a
  named concept, short lowercase for a placeholder" and not "always CamelCase".

  Across Frank's own 10 .tla files: 18 CamelCase, 2 snake_case, 21
  all-lowercase. Both snake_case names are `picker_count` and `max_slips` in
  today's drill, and nothing older carries any. He called it "a Python habit
  that I let bleed over" and the evidence says it bled into one item.

Neither figure exists in the survey, which never measured identifier case. C1
was silent and C3 answered it.

THE COLLISION WITH THE DRILL, AND IT IS NARROW. Style commentary names
constructs, and drill/study/CLAUDE.md's third prohibition is "NEVER name the
construct that's missing". Measured over all 64 META.md files: 9 items name a
type invariant in a construct bullet, and of those, ONE genuinely drills the
idiom (core/04-lift-types, "the `TypeOK` idiom, `Int` against `Nat`"). The
other 8 are all sequences/* naming `Seq(S)` in TypeOK, where the lesson is
`Seq(S)` and TypeOK is only where it lands.

So one item of 64 needs an exclusion, by name, on one axis. That is cheap
enough to spend and it is why this is buildable at all.

THE ARCHITECTURE IS THE ONE ALREADY BUILT. The model has no tools, so it
cannot run a count. A SCRIPT measures and the model interprets, exactly as
`check` and the reading pass split. Locked filenames so the children can run
in parallel:

  drill/study/STYLE.md   the register, distilled from the survey
  drill/study/style      the measuring script
  ./drill --style        the flag

SEPARATE FLAG, NOT FOLDED INTO --check. Correctness and style are different
questions, Frank asked for style as an addition, and folding it in makes every
check pay for it. One line to change if he wants them together.

WHAT THE SCRIPT CAN MEASURE MECHANICALLY, each mapping to a survey axis:
identifier case for constants and variables; whether a type invariant is
declared; whether a `vars` tuple exists and covers every declared variable;
whether the behavior formula is named `Spec`; whether the box subscript is the
full tuple; whether `Next`'s disjuncts are named actions or inline; how many
obligations the config names.

SECTION 7 OF THE SURVEY IS NOT OPTIONAL READING. "A reviewer that fires on
every deviation is worse than no reviewer", then thirteen shapes that look
like defects and are routine, including a subscript naming one variable of
several and an obligation defined and never checked. A style pass that reports
those is worse than none.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-10-15 by the tla-iiow.1 worker, with the mechanism found.

MY CONSTANT COUNT WAS WRONG. The epic says "126 of 132 reference-spec
constants are CamelCase or ALLCAPS". The figure is 134 of 140.

My awk walked only ONE continuation line. The worker reproduced all three
numbers: no continuation walk reads 113, one continuation line reads exactly
132, a full walk reads 140. The eight names on a second continuation line are
all CamelCase.

THE CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED and is why this did not invalidate anything: 0
snake_case either way, and the six non-CamelCase names are `a b l1 l2 w1 w4`,
all mathematical placeholders. drill/study/STYLE.md carries 134 of 140.

THREE MORE DISCREPANCIES THE SAME WORKER REPORTED, all against my brief:

Section 7 of the survey tabulates TWELVE rows, not thirteen. The thirteenth
item is the survey's own non-ruling at :459, where it declines to say whether
SYMMETRY alongside a PROPERTY is sound for TLC's liveness checks. The register
carries all thirteen and words it as "twelve shapes it tabulates, and one it
refuses to rule on", because an unsettled question produces silence by the
same rule a missing number does.

TEN META files mention a type invariant, not nine, but the epic's claim holds
as written. The tenth is drill/core/02-vending-unchanged/META.md:46, which
mentions TypeOK in prose about the reference specs rather than in a construct
bullet. So "9 items name a type invariant in a construct bullet" is still
right, and the core/04-lift-types exclusion is confirmed.

C1 AND C3 CONFLICT ON OBLIGATION COUNT, and this one is a design finding
rather than a correction. The published corpus runs a median of 2 named
obligations and mean 2.79. The 540 reference configs run a median of 1, mean
1.55, with 327 naming exactly one. A coach holding a drill attempt to the
PUBLISHED median would fire on most correct answers, so the register writes a
general C3-wins rule and flags this axis as where it bites.

THE `Next` AXIS NEEDS THE RIGHT DISCRIMINATOR. The register states it as:
does the Next body contain a prime or an UNCHANGED, or does it only name
operators? Splitting the body on `\/` breaks the `\E ... :` structure and
misclassifies a delegating body as inline, measured at 60 false inline against
15 real. Relayed to tla-iiow.2 in flight.
close_reason: Style commentary ships, grounded in three citation tiers, and verified end to end on Frank's real attempt. Frank's own contribution was the third tier, observed code to date, after I offered cite-or-silent and he said he was mixed. That tier earned itself immediately: C1 was silent on identifier case and C3 answered it, finding 0 of 140 reference constants in snake_case and 2 of his own 41 declared names, both in one drill rather than across his practice. The collision with the drill measured as one item of 64, core/04-lift-types. Commits 3582bd9 7bc9022 d44ca09. Drawer drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0c6c0d3408545ba606dbbb0f.

title: check runs TLC in the work directory, so every violated run litters it
description:
Files: drill/study/check, harness/test-drill-check.sh

RED: Given a drill directory whose model violates an invariant, When check runs twice, Then the directory holds exactly the files it held before, and no *_TTrace_* pair and no states/ entry was added by either run.

MEASURED 2026-10-14 ON FRANK'S REAL DIRECTORY, by me, which is how it was
found. `drill/study/check:373` runs

  out="$(cd -- "$WORK" && tlc -config "${module}.cfg" "$module" 2>&1)"

so TLC executes IN the work directory. A violated run makes TLC write a trace
module beside the spec. One check of ~/Study/tla-drills/01-slip-on-the-spike
added:

  pickers_collision_TTrace_1792036425.tla
  pickers_collision_TTrace_1792036425.bin
  states/26-10-14-23-53-45.700/

I removed all three and `git status --short` in the study repo came back
empty, so his tree is as it was. His own committed trace file from 19:41 was
left alone.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE CHURN IT LOOKS LIKE. The name carries a timestamp, so
the files do not overwrite: every check of a violating model leaves a NEW
pair, and the violating model is the common case on the families that ask for
one. Twenty checks is twenty pairs, none of them cleaned up, in the tree that
holds the only copy of his work. `scripts/deliver-drill.sh` prints "left alone
(your work, never written here):" about this tree, and the checker is now the
thing writing in it.

It also feeds tla-rzvk.4's borrowing rule its own input. A trace leaving IS an
unpaired module, which is why the `*_TTrace_*` skip became load-bearing in
that bead. Left alone, check generates the exact shape it has to special-case.

THE FIX IS A TEMP COPY. Copy the directory's .tla and .cfg into a scratch
directory, run TLC there, read the log, and delete it. Every local module must
go across or an EXTENDS of a sibling stops resolving, so copy all of them
rather than only the one being run. The scratch directory goes somewhere the
tool owns, never under the study tree.

Then the `*_TTrace_*` skip guards only what TLC left there BEFORE, which is
what it was always meant to do.

A SEPARATE AND SMALLER THING, and it is Frank's call rather than a bead:
~/Study/tla-drills/.gitignore covers states/ and *.old but not *_TTrace_*, and
he has one trace module committed. Fixing the ignore after this bead lands is
cosmetic. Fixing it before would hide the evidence of this defect.
notes:
SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-10-15, same session, same directory, by me again.

I cleaned the first round at ~00:15, then ran check against
~/Study/tla-drills/01-slip-on-the-spike at 00:37 to verify the merged
tla-rzvk.4 and left a fresh pair: pickers_collision_TTrace_1792039041.tla and
.bin. Removed, and `git status --short` in the study repo is empty again.

TWICE IN ONE SESSION, BY THE PERSON WHO FILED THE BEAD, raises the priority
rather than merely confirming the diagnosis. Every run against a violating
model leaves a pair, the names carry timestamps so nothing overwrites, and the
one tree holding the only copy of Frank's work accumulates them silently. He
has not started using ./drill --check in earnest yet.

A CONTRAST THAT MAKES THE FIX CONCRETE. drill/study/style was run against the
same directory minutes later and wrote NOTHING, because it reads text and
never starts TLC. `git status --short` stayed empty across that run. So a
sibling script in the same tree already has the property this bead wants, and
the temp-copy fix is the only thing standing between check and the same
property.
close_reason: check now runs TLC in a mktemp copy of the work directory and deletes it on a trap, so a check never writes beside the work. Verified on Frank's real tree: the same verdict and violating state as before, and git status in the study repo stayed empty. Commit 7c79a1e. Found two things past the bead: a CLEAN run was also leaving a states/ directory so the defect covered every check rather than only violations, and a one-module copy breaks EXTENDS, which confirms copying all of them was necessary. Corrected its own overclaim about which assertion caught what.

title: check silently skips a module that has no config of its own
description:
Files: drill/study/check, harness/test-drill-check.sh

RED: Given a drill directory holding Foo.tla, Foo.cfg and Bar.tla with no Bar.cfg, When check runs, Then it names Bar as a module it did not run and why, and the skip list (*_TTrace_*, states/, *.old) is still skipped silently.

MEASURED ON FRANK'S REAL ATTEMPT, 2026-10-14, the first drill he worked.

~/Study/tla-drills/01-slip-on-the-spike holds pickers.tla, pickers.cfg and
pickers_collision.tla. There is no pickers_collision.cfg. check reports:

  module=pickers rc=0 distinct=4 claimed=- count=NONE run=CLEAN invariant=-
  UNCHECKED: 01-slip-on-the-spike publishes no distinct-state count...

pickers_collision is not mentioned anywhere. It is the model with the defect
in it. Pairing it with a copy of pickers.cfg gives:

  module=pickers_collision rc=12 distinct=5 claimed=- count=NONE run=VIOLATED invariant=NoDoublePicks
    State 3: <Next line 27, col 10 to line 30, col 27 of module pickers_collision>
    /\ pickers = <<1, 1>>
    /\ slips = 1

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The control-state family and several others
ask for TWO models: write it, run it, then change one thing and run it again.
A learner who keeps one config and renames modules gets a CLEAN verdict with
the broken model invisible. That is a false reassurance from the one tool in
this loop whose whole job is to be objective, and it is the exact shape
CLAUDE.md's "NEVER estimate a count" prohibition exists to stop, arriving
from the other direction: not a guessed number, a missing row.

THE FIX IS TO REPORT, NOT TO GUESS. Do NOT pair an unconfigured module with
some other module's config. Name it and say it was not run:

  module=pickers_collision NOT RUN: no pickers_collision.cfg beside it

THE SKIP LIST STAYS SILENT. *_TTrace_*, states/ and *.old are skipped on
purpose and naming them would be noise. Only a module that would otherwise
have been a candidate gets a line. Frank's directory has a
pickers_TTrace_1792021269.tla in it right now, so the suite has a real
instance of the quiet case to assert against.

EXIT CODES DO NOT MOVE. An unrun module is a report, not a failure: it does
not make a matching count mismatch and it does not turn exit 2 into 1. Same
reasoning as the epic's, which is that check reports and does not judge.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-10-14, same day, by Frank. THE REMEDY ABOVE IS WRONG.

Frank: "the logic to the other pickers not having its own config, because the
configs are consistent across both files. So I used the same config twice and
just did it with the --config on TLC."

One config serving two modules is the normal workflow, not an oversight. His
two modules declare the same constants, the same Spec and the same two
invariants, so pickers.cfg is valid for both and `tlc -config pickers.cfg
pickers_collision` is the right way to run the second. Verified: that pairing
gives rc=12, run=VIOLATED, invariant=NoDoublePicks. Reporting NOT RUN would
make him write a duplicate config he has no reason to keep.

THE RULE THAT REPLACES IT, still guessing at nothing:

1. A module with its own <name>.cfg runs with it. Unchanged.
2. A module without one runs with the directory's single .cfg when there is
   EXACTLY ONE, and the output names which config it used.
3. Zero or two-or-more configs: not run, reason and candidates named. This is
   the only case the original NOT RUN wording survives into.

The line carries the config so a borrowed one is never invisible:

  module=pickers_collision config=pickers.cfg rc=12 ... run=VIOLATED invariant=NoDoublePicks

THE CASE THAT WOULD OTHERWISE GO WRONG. A helper module another module EXTENDS
is also unpaired, and borrowing a config for it would run TLC over something
that is not a spec. So borrow only for a module that DEFINES what the config
names: grep for the operator its SPECIFICATION names, or the INIT/NEXT pair.
One grep, no guessing, and no special-casing of filenames.

The defect this bead reports is unchanged and still real: the skip was SILENT.
Only the remedy moved, from refusing to run to running it correctly and saying
which config it used.
close_reason: check now runs a module that has no config of its own against the directory's single config, and carries config= on every output line so a borrowed one is never invisible. Two or more configs, or a module that does not define what the config names, is reported by name with the reason and nothing is guessed. Frank corrected my original remedy mid-flight: one config serving two modules is his normal workflow, not an oversight, so refusing to run it would have made him keep a duplicate he has no reason to write. Verified on his real directory, which now reports both modules with pickers = <<1, 1>>, slips = 1 under the violated one. Suite 139 to 181 assertions, RED stub failed 25 of 180, and two assertions that passed by construction were earned by breaking the skips, at 8 and 11 failures. Found that TLC on this build writes a trace module with no config beside it, which makes the *_TTrace_* skip load-bearing. Commit 4dbfa75. Design in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0c3c870780855336bfa37043.

title: The study config: reach the checker, and compare a violation against the prompt's table
description:
Files: drill/study/CLAUDE.md, drill/study/.claude/commands/check.md, drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md, harness/test-deliver-drill.sh

RED: INVARIANT: drill/study/CLAUDE.md never tells the reader to run `./check` from a slug directory, carries the behavior-table comparison as a named step, and defines both MODE: check and MODE: hint.

THREE CHANGES, and the second is the one Frank asked for.

(1) THE PATH IS WRONG TODAY. CLAUDE.md's "How to run the check" says "Run
`./check` in the directory". The checker is delivered to the study ROOT, so
from a slug directory it is `../check`. Frank's session hit this, reported
"./check doesn't exist in this directory", and improvised correctly. Say how
to reach it from where the session actually stands. `./drill --check`
(tla-rzvk.2) also makes it moot from the shell, so name that too.

(2) A VIOLATION AT A STATE THE PROMPT BLESSES IS A REPORT ABOUT THE RULE, NOT
THE MODEL. This is the missing diagnosis and it generalises past one item.
8 prompts carry a table whose rows are marked possible:

  control-state/01-slip-on-the-spike, 02-pumps, 05-crane-and-riggers,
  06-three-reds, 07-donor-session, functions-records/02-charging-bays,
  05-tool-crib, 06-depot-cover

(15 carry something in that family on a wider net.) The table is a constraint
the model must satisfy and NOTHING verifies it. So add the step: when the
prompt carries states marked possible and the run violated, compare the
violating state against those rows. A violation landing on a row marked
possible means the invariant forbids something the prompt requires, which is
a defect in the RULE even when the verdict is the expected one.

Worked instance, 2026-10-14. Frank's control-state/01 reports a violation at
`pickers = <<1,1>>, slips = 1`: both pickers have seen the slip, neither has
reached the shelf. That is row 3, marked possible, and the item's META calls
it "one foreclosing row". He got the expected verdict from a state that is
legal, one step before any pick. His invariant is the obvious reading of the
stated rule, and nothing in the prompt asked him to check where it fires.
That gap is ours, not his.

Keep the existing register. Report the behavior, never the construct. Saying
"your rule forbids row 3, which the prompt marks possible" names no construct
and leaves him the whole fix.

(3) THE TWO MODES tla-rzvk.2 SHIPS. drill.sh writes `MODE: check` or
`MODE: hint`, plus a `QUESTION:` block carrying Frank's text verbatim on a
steered hint. This file owns what they mean. drill.sh owns neither.

A STEERED HINT NEEDS A BUDGET THE LADDER NEVER HAD. Two kinds of question
arrive under one flag and they are not rationed the same way:

  - A mechanism he has forgotten about TLA+ itself. His own example: "I have
    the named value in DontMakeDoubles, but don't remember what to put in the
    cfg file." That is the `.cfg` keyword. Answer it plainly and completely.
    It says nothing about what his invariant should assert.
  - A question about THIS item's content. "What am I missing in
    DontMakeDoubles." Ladder it, same as /hint does now.

The test is one question: would answering in full still leave him the item's
work? If yes, answer it flat, with no rung and no coyness. If no, ladder. A
one-shot prints everything before he can look away, so the classification
happens before the first word, not after.

DO NOT TOUCH scripts/test. Central owns the budget rows this wave.
close_reason: The study config now tells a session the checker is at ../check rather than ./check, which Frank's first session hit and had to work around. Adds the diagnosis that a violation at a state the prompt marks possible is a report about the rule rather than the model, covering the 8 prompts carrying a possible-table without editing any of them. Defines MODE: check, MODE: hint and QUESTION:, and gives a steered hint a budget: a forgotten TLA+ mechanism is answered flat, a question about the item's content is laddered. Suite 215 to 238 assertions, 21 of 23 new rows watched red, the other two proved by mutation. Found that the gate never counted the four prohibitions and that NEVER estimate a count had no header row at all. Commit 32fcb8d. Design in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0c3c870780855336bfa37043.

title: drill --check and drill --hint, one-shot with no tools
description:
Files: drill/drill.sh, harness/test-drill-runner.sh

RED: Given a study directory holding an attempt and a stub `claude` first on PATH that writes its stdin and argv to a file, When ./drill --check runs, Then the captured argv carries --tools with an empty value and -p, the prompt arrived on STDIN rather than argv, and that prompt carries the item's PROMPT.md text, every .tla and .cfg of the attempt, and the checker's output verbatim.

TWO NEW FLAGS:

  ./drill --check            run the checker, then a one-shot reading pass
  ./drill --hint             the best hint the one-shot can give
  ./drill --hint "<text>"    a hint steered by a question Frank types

WHICH DRILL. The directory Frank is standing in when its basename matches a
drill slug, and LAST-SERVED otherwise. Standing-in wins because it cannot
drift when two terminals are open, which is the same reason `done` and
`shaky` already take an explicit name. Say which one was used in the output,
because guessing silently is the failure that the pointer already warns about.

THE INVOCATION, and all three parts are measured (see tla-rzvk):

  cd <slug dir> && claude -p --tools "" <<'EOF' ... EOF

  - cwd is the slug directory, so drill/study/CLAUDE.md loads BY ITSELF from
    the study root above it. Do NOT restate the prohibitions in drill.sh.
    One source for the register rules, and it is not this file.
  - `--tools ""` is what makes the read prohibition structural. The model
    cannot reach ANSWER.md, META.md or verify/ because it cannot reach
    anything. Never add a tool back to make something convenient.
  - stdin, never argv. `--tools` is variadic and swallows a positional
    prompt, and a heredoc also sidesteps quoting in the free --hint text.

THE SEAM WITH tla-rzvk.3, which owns what the modes mean. drill.sh writes a
first line reading `MODE: check` or `MODE: hint`, and for a steered hint a
`QUESTION:` block carrying Frank's text verbatim. drill.sh decides nothing
about rungs or registers. It assembles and ships.

THE HEADER INVARIANT MOVES AGAIN AND THE COMMENT MUST SAY SO. drill.sh's
header currently argues it "sources nothing, resolves no repo root, and reads
nothing outside the directory it sits in", with ONE write-only exception for
the study mkdir. This adds three reads outside: exec `$STUDY_ROOT/check`, read
the attempt files under the study dir, and exec `claude` from PATH. Narrow the
invariant honestly and argue it, the way the mkdir exception is argued. Do not
delete the section. An invariant narrowed twice in one day without saying so
stops meaning anything.

EVERY NEW DEPENDENCY FAILS SOFT, like the mkdir does. No `claude` on PATH, no
`$STUDY_ROOT/check`, no attempt in the directory: each is one clear message
and a nonzero exit, never a crash under `set -u` and never a half-run. The
serve path must keep working with none of them present, because serving is
the job and coaching is the convenience.

DO NOT TOUCH scripts/test, and do not run a real `claude` in a suite. The
stub on PATH is the whole test surface. A suite that calls out to a model is
neither offline nor repeatable, and every gate here runs offline.
close_reason: ./drill --check and ./drill --hint [text] ship, resolved from LAST-SERVED after Frank overruled my cwd-detection rule. The invocation is claude -p --tools "" with the prompt on stdin and the slug directory as cwd, so the study CLAUDE.md loads by itself and the model has no tools at all. Verified end to end against the delivered runner with a stub model: ARGV reads -p --tools with an empty value, the prompt arrives on stdin, and it carries MODE/DRILL/DIRECTORY, the PROMPT.md, the checker output verbatim and one block per attempt file. Suite 105 to 267 assertions over two rounds, 48 then 15 rows watched red. Four judgment calls stand, including that --hint runs the checker too, since with no tools the model has no other objective input. Commits e569e98 and 8f6d14d. Design in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0c3c870780855336bfa37043.

title: check reports the run verdict beside the count
description:
Files: drill/study/check, harness/test-drill-check.sh

RED: INVARIANT: on a prompt that publishes no count, check still runs TLC, reports run=VIOLATED with the violating invariant's name and the violating state, and still exits 2.

THE DEFECT. check:326 decides the claim before anything else and skips TLC
entirely when the prompt publishes none: "a drill with nothing to compare
never asks for tlc or a model." So on the 21 prompts that publish no count
the session gets NO objective input. All 8 control-state items are in that 21
and every one of them asks for a verdict, which is as checkable as a count.
Frank's session on control-state/01 ran TLC on scratch copies by hand to get
one, and was right to.

check:373 already captures the whole TLC run into `out` and throws away
everything but the number. The verdict, the invariant name and the trace are
in hand already.

THE LOCKED LINE FORMAT, which tla-rzvk.2 is being built against in parallel:

  module=<name> rc=<n> distinct=<n|-> claimed=<csv|-> count=<MATCH|MISMATCH|NONE> run=<CLEAN|VIOLATED|NOCOUNT|ERROR> invariant=<name|->

one per module, then the violating state as an indented block when any module
violated. `-` is the absent marker everywhere. An absent count is never a
count of zero, which the header already argues.

EXIT CODES DO NOT MOVE: 0 matched, 1 mismatched, 2 no count claim, 3 could
not run. A violation is the RIGHT answer on some items, so check reports a
verdict and never judges one. Do not add an exit code for VIOLATED and do not
let a violation change the exit on a matching count. The existing header
already decides the sibling case ("A NONZERO RC AT A MATCHING COUNT IS STILL
A MATCH") and this is the same decision.

THE RC TABLE IN THE HEADER IS MEASURED AND STILL HOLDS. rc does not predict
whether a count printed, and rc 75 prints its count AFTER the error. Read the
verdict out of the log the same way, never from the rc.

WATCH IT FAIL FIRST. The suite is 78 assertions and three RED stubs were
needed to prove the last round: a silent stub, an adversarial one, and a
mismatch-everything one. The third was the only one that caught `grep -F
MATCH` matching MISMATCH as a substring, and the new `count=`/`run=` fields
have exactly that hazard again: CLEAN is not a substring of anything here but
NOCOUNT contains COUNT and MISMATCH contains MATCH. Assert on the whole field.

DO NOT TOUCH scripts/test. Central owns the budget rows this wave; three
workers editing it last time made a three-way conflict. Report the timing you
measure and central rebases.
close_reason: check now runs TLC even when the prompt publishes no count, and reports run=VIOLATED with the invariant's name and the violating state. Verified end to end against Frank's real attempt: 01-slip-on-the-spike prints 'module=pickers_collision rc=12 distinct=5 claimed=- count=NONE run=VIOLATED invariant=NoDoublePicks' with 'pickers = <<1, 1>>, slips = 1' beneath it, which is the blessed row 3 his session had to find by running TLC by hand. Suite 78 to 139 assertions, three RED stubs failing 49, 27 and 29 of 139. Exit codes did not move except a no-claim prompt with no tlc, now 3 rather than 2, which the worker decided and argued. Commit 23b690a. Design in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0c3c870780855336bfa37043.

title: A one-shot coach on ./drill: --check and --hint
description:
Frank asked for the slash commands to be reachable from the shell: `./drill --check`
runs the checker and a one-shot Claude from the right directory, and
`./drill --hint [text]` gives a hint, optionally steered by a question he types.

AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: epic, children carry the work

MEASURED ON 2026-10-14, claude 2.1.300, and these decide the design:

  F1  `claude -p` loads CLAUDE.md from the cwd AND from a subdirectory of it,
      and fires project slash commands. A probe dir with a marker CLAUDE.md
      and a .claude/commands/probe.md returned `ZZQUUX SLASHWORKS`.
  F2  `--tools ""` removes file access. Asked to read a file beside it, the
      model answered CANNOTREAD, and still carried the CLAUDE.md marker. So
      the read prohibition in drill/study/CLAUDE.md becomes a property of the
      invocation rather than advice. 6.7s wall on a trivial prompt.
  F3  The prompt must arrive on STDIN. `--tools` is variadic, so
      `--tools "" "prompt"` eats the prompt as a tool name and exits with
      "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument".
      A heredoc also sidesteps quoting in Frank's free-text --hint.

THE ARCHITECTURE F2 FORCES, and it is better than the interactive path:
drill does every fetch, the model does none. drill runs the checker, cats the
attempt and the prompt, pipes all of it on stdin, and the model runs with no
tools at all. It cannot reach ANSWER.md, META.md or verify/ because it cannot
reach anything. This makes tla-ytv2.4 unnecessary for the one-shot path: no
Read deny to verify, and no Bash `cat` escape around it.

The cwd is the slug directory, so drill/study/CLAUDE.md loads by itself (F1)
and stays the single source of the register rules. Do NOT restate the
prohibitions in drill.sh.

LOCKED OUTPUT CONTRACT for check, so .1 and .2 can be built in parallel:

  module=<name> rc=<n> distinct=<n|-> claimed=<csv|-> count=<MATCH|MISMATCH|NONE> run=<CLEAN|VIOLATED|NOCOUNT|ERROR> invariant=<name|->

one such line per module, then, when any module violated, the violating state
as an indented block under it.

EXIT CODES DO NOT MOVE. They stay about the count dimension only: 0 matched,
1 mismatched, 2 no count claim, 3 could not run. check reports a verdict and
never judges one, because a violation is the RIGHT answer on some items:
drill/control-state/01-slip-on-the-spike asks for model 1 to fail. check
knows counts. It does not know intent.

WHAT PROMPTED IT. Frank's /check session on control-state/01 found a real
error in his spec, and in doing so turned up two defects of ours:
  - drill/study/CLAUDE.md says "Run `./check` in the directory". The checker
    is delivered to the study ROOT, so from a slug directory it is `../check`.
    His session had to work that out for itself.
  - check skips TLC entirely when no count is published (check:326), so on
    the 21 prompts that publish none the session gets no objective input at
    all. All 8 control-state items are in that 21 and every one asks for a
    verdict. That is why his session ran TLC on scratch copies by hand.

The 43/21 split is CONFIRMED, twice, against both a flattened scan and the
checker's own parser. A line-based grep gets 36/28 and is wrong: the claim
wraps across lines in 7 prompts. prose_claims already flattens the file and
reads them correctly.
close_reason: ./drill --check and ./drill --hint ship, gated and delivered. All four children closed: the checker reports a run verdict on the 21 prompts that publish no count, the two flags resolve from LAST-SERVED, the study config says where the checker is and what a blessed violation means, and an unpaired module runs against the directory's single config. The architecture turned on one measurement, that --tools "" removes file access while CLAUDE.md still loads, so drill does every fetch and the model has no tools and cannot reach ANSWER.md, META.md or verify/ at all. cibuild --skip-docs green, 34 suites in 434.6s, corpus 107 passed 0 failed. Delivered behind a verified backup, 1370 entries both sides. Frank overruled me twice during the wave and was right both times, on drill resolution and on the config-borrowing remedy. Commits 23b690a 32fcb8d e569e98 8f6d14d 4dbfa75, merged through b187569. Design in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0c3c870780855336bfa37043.

title: A Claude configuration in the study root, written as a refusal contract
description:
Frank wants to spin up Claude in his study directory and ask it to check his work. This bead writes that configuration and delivers it.

WHAT TO WRITE.

drill/study/CLAUDE.md, delivered as $DRILL_STUDY_ROOT/CLAUDE.md. Its first and longest section is what the session must NOT do, because the default disposition of a coding agent asked to check work is to fix the work, and that is the exact failure this whole corpus is built to avoid.

  - NEVER read anything under ~/repos/tla-puzzles/drill/. ANSWER.md, META.md and verify/ are withheld from delivery on purpose and sit one absolute path away. The withholding in scripts/deliver-drill.sh is a delivery boundary, not an access boundary, so the config is the only thing standing in front of it. Name the paths so there is no ambiguity about what is off limits.
  - NEVER write TLA+ for him, in any quantity, including a single line and including a correction shown inline.
  - NEVER name the construct that is missing. Saying "you need an ASSUME" hands over the retrieval.
  - Report which obligation the model fails to make true, as a behaviour it admits or forbids. "Your Next admits a step where both tools are held at once" is the register. "Add a conjunct" is not.
  - The count comes from the checker, never from the session reading TLC output and estimating. Run drill/study/check and quote its numbers.

drill/study/commands/check.md, the /check command. Runs ./check for the objective half, then does the two things a script cannot: read the spec for a RIGHT COUNT REACHED BY A WRONG MODEL, and read his prose answers on the 20 prompts that end in a question instead of a count. The wrong-model case is real and the corpus contains the proof: drill/sequences/07-pneumatic-tube/verify/TubeCountOnly.tla is rc 0 at 57 distinct states on a rule that is true of a stack and a queue alike.

drill/study/commands/hint.md, the /hint command, GATED. It refuses to say anything until the session has seen an attempt in the directory, because the supported protocol is attempt, then failure, then immediate feedback, and feedback without a preceding attempt is the lookup this is meant to replace. Ladder it: first the obligation that fails, then which part of the state it concerns, then the shape of the fix, and never the text of it.

DELIVERY. scripts/deliver-drill.sh grows a mode that lands drill/study/ into $DRILL_STUDY_ROOT, default $HOME/Study/tla-drills. title: A gated objective checker: run the attempt, compare its distinct count against the prompt
description:
A standalone script, drill/study/check, delivered to the study root. It answers one question with no judgment in it: does the model Frank wrote reach the distinct-state count the prompt publishes?

INTERFACE, PINNED, because a sibling bead writes a slash command against it.

    check [<slug-or-dir>]        default: the current directory

    exit 0   every count claim in the prompt was matched
    exit 1   a claim was not matched, or TLC failed where the prompt says it should not
    exit 2   UNCHECKED: the prompt publishes no count, so there is nothing to compare
    exit 3   usage, no prompt found, no module found, or TLC not on the path

Stdout names the module run, the rc, the distinct count TLC printed and the count the prompt claimed, one line per module, then a single verdict line. Print the number TLC printed and never a number derived any other way.

RESOLUTION NEEDS NO MAPPING DATA. The slug is the basename of the directory. The prompt is the single hit of ~/tla-practice/drill/*/<slug>/PROMPT.md; all 64 slugs are distinct across the eight families, so more than one hit is a corpus bug and must be reported rather than guessed past. Honour DRILL_PROMPT_ROOT, default $HOME/tla-practice/drill, so the test can point it at a fixture.

THE COUNT CLAIM IN THE PROMPT. 44 of 64 prompts carry one and 20 do not. Shapes in the corpus include "A correct model finds 129 distinct states." Scan for a count claim rather than assuming one sentence form, and treat the absence of one as exit 2 and never as zero. By family, the prompts carrying a claim: modules 8, state-space 8, core 7, functions-records 7, sets 6, control-state 4, sequences 4, temporal 0.

FINDING THE LEARNER MODULE. Every .tla in the directory that has a .cfg of the same name, excluding TLC output: skip anything matching *_TTrace_*, skip the states/ directory, skip *.old. If several qualify, run each and report each; Frank keeps variants side by side, and 01-slip-on-the-spike already holds pickers.tla next to pickers_collision.tla.

IT RUNS WHEREVER FRANK IS, SO IT DEPENDS ON NOTHING IN THE REPO. No sourcing harness/verdict.sh, which does not exist in the study tree. Invoke tlc directly and read the count out of its output. Absent tlc is exit 3 with a message, never a silent pass.

AND GIVEN a module that reaches 8, THEN exit 1 and both numbers appear. AND GIVEN a prompt with no count claim, THEN exit 2 and the word UNCHECKED, with no number invented. AND GIVEN a directory holding foo.tla, foo.cfg and foo_TTrace_123.tla, THEN only foo is run.

title: A drill queue runner Frank can grind from, delivered to ~/tla-practice/drill
description:
Frank, 2026-10-14: "for drills, ideally I'd like a clear path to just pick up and
grind through them. The easiest would be: 1. a way to mark a drill as done, 2. a
script that can be run at ~/tla-practice/drills that will jump me to the next one
in the queue."

TWO DECISIONS RULED BY FRANK THE SAME DAY, both central's recommendation:

ORDER: interleaved by index. 01 of every family, then 02 of every family. The
number inside a family is authoring order rather than a difficulty ramp, which
deliver-drill.sh's own header says, so interleaving costs nothing and keeps
variety high. Family order within an index is alphabetical, for determinism.

MARKS: done and shaky, with shaky resurfacing. done retires an item. shaky
retires it from the current pass and returns it after every undone item, so a
drill half-got comes back instead of vanishing. Every entry carries a timestamp
whether or not anything reads it yet, so a real spacing schedule can be added
later without rewriting the log.

THE COMMAND, as agreed:
  ./drill            serve the next item: its path, then its PROMPT.md
  ./drill done       mark the served item done, then serve the next
  ./drill shaky      mark it shaky, then serve the next
  ./drill status     counts
  ./drill list       the queue

IT RUNS WHERE THERE IS NO REPO. ~/tla-practice is not a git repo, has no harness,
no bd and no TLC guarantee. The script is self-contained bash, depends on nothing
outside its own directory, and works on a first run with no state file.

STATE IS APPEND-ONLY, which is what makes it a practice record rather than just a
cursor:
  ~/tla-practice/drill/PROGRESS.tsv   <iso8601>\t<mark>\t<family>/<item>
A later mark supersedes an earlier one by recency. Never rewrite a line, never
delete one. A pointer file holds the last item served so done takes no argument.

THE QUEUE IS DERIVED FROM THE DELIVERED TREE, by globbing */NN-*/PROMPT.md and
sorting on (NN, family). Not from a checked-in list. The corpus grows, and a
hardcoded list is the staleness shape this project has hit repeatedly.

THIS RESOLVES tla-emzu, which is blocked on whether never-overwrite should be
per file class. Frank's request answers it, because the three classes want three
policies:
  PROMPT.md     never overwrite. It is the learner's page and may carry work.
  the runner    ALWAYS overwrite. It is tooling, and a fix has to reach him.
  PROGRESS.tsv  never written by the delivery script at all. It is his work.
deliver-drill.sh currently places PROMPT.md and nothing else, so the runner is
the first non-item file it writes. Its header is emphatic about naming files and
about failing safe, and that reasoning has to be extended rather than bypassed.

GATE IT. A new suite asserting the interleaved order, both marks, the
resurfacing, the append-only property, the no-state-file first run, and that
delivery places the runner while never touching PROGRESS.tsv. Register it in
scripts/test with a measured budget.

HAZARD: never field-split a TSV with IFS=$'\t' read. That is a recorded rule in
this project. Use cut -f or awk -F'\t'.

Files: drill/drill.sh, scripts/deliver-drill.sh, harness/test-drill-runner.sh, scripts/test

The resurfacing rule needed a fix central missed: in canonical order, once every drill is shaky the head stays the head forever, so the shaky tail is ordered by when it was last marked. Delivered to ~/tla-practice/drill/drill behind a verified backup, 64 untried, runner driven end to end in the real tree. Commits e18c4ed, 22f855d, 055feda, 89b2643.
