title: Both step-5 checks found the same failure: a statement satisfiable by a model that lacks the mechanism
description:
Two of two step-5 consistency checks run on 2026-10-08 returned NOT SUFFICIENT for the same structural reason. That is a pattern in how this project authors statements, not two coincidences, and it is worth a rule before the next authoring wave.

THE SHAPE. A statement's requirement set goes green over a model that does not contain the mechanism the problem is about. The learner finishes, every check passes, and they never meet the defect.

THE TWO INSTANCES, both measured rather than argued.

acme-challenge-retry-deadlock. All nine requirements hold at rc 0, 16 distinct states, depth 5, over a model whose retry loop provably never turns. A model where nobody ever sends word also satisfies all nine, because the statement's own rule removes every obligation and no requirement is a reachability claim.

progressive-sync-stale-status. All seven requirements hold at rc 0, 14 distinct states, depth 11, over a model with no board and no clerk at all. The statement's own extra check passes too. The stale board is the entire mechanism and it is unreachable from the requirement set.

WHY IT HAPPENS. Every requirement in both statements is a safety invariant or an action property. Neither set contains a REACHABILITY claim, and a safety-only requirement set is always satisfiable by doing less. The statements are faithful to their sources and the sources describe machines, not obligations to run them.

THE FIX BOTH REVIEWERS PROPOSED INDEPENDENTLY. A second deliverable: the learner hands in one formula they EXPECT TLC to refute, plus the run that refutes it. The acme reviewer's wording withholds the diagnosis while supplying the instrument. The progressive-sync reviewer called the same thing a required red run.

That is the general fix and it belongs in the pipeline rather than in two statements. It also teaches a technique the project wants taught: an invariant you expect to fail is a reachability claim, and nothing else in the curriculum reaches for one.

A COROLLARY WORTH ITS OWN LINE. The acme reviewer found the trace pairs CANNOT be authored as specified, because the allowed run needs a state the requirement set forbids. So any allowed run satisfying every requirement is a degenerate run, and the pairs would certify the defect rather than catch it. Settle the second deliverable BEFORE authoring any trace pair, on any problem.

Files: PRACTICE-PLAN.md

RED: INVARIANT: every delivered statement's requirement set is unsatisfiable by at least one named degenerate model that the statement's own Checking section identifies, OR the statement carries a second deliverable requiring a refuted formula. A requirement set consisting only of safety invariants and action properties, with no reachability claim and no refutation deliverable, is the defect.
notes:
THIRD INSTANCE, 2026-10-08. All THREE step-5 checks returned NOT SUFFICIENT, not two. The bead title and body say two because imap-move's report had not landed when it was filed.

imap-move-partial-failure. PROBLEM.md:96-97 says 'The clerk never marks an entry for striking at all.' No model the rules permit can reach a part entry, so requirement 1 at :177 is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION. The statement WARNS ABOUT THAT EXACT TRAP AT :44 AND THEN SETS IT.

THAT INSTANCE SHARPENS THE DIAGNOSIS AND NARROWS THE FIX.

On acme and progressive-sync the requirement set was satisfiable by a model that did less. Here the requirement is not merely satisfiable, it is UNFALSIFIABLE: the rules forbid the state that would refute it. So the pattern has two faces, and a reachability deliverable only catches the first one. A learner asked to hand in a formula they expect TLC to refute cannot produce one for imap requirement 1, because no permitted model reaches the refuting state. They would report 'I could not refute it' and be right.

THE RULE THAT CATCHES BOTH, from the imap reviewer and it generalises. RFC 9051 states its analogue as a prohibition on a REACHABLE ACTION, 'the \\Deleted flag MUST NOT be set for any message', not as a denial that the action exists. A statement that removes the action instead of forbidding the outcome has turned a requirement into a tautology.

So the check is: FOR EVERY REQUIREMENT, DOES THE RULE SET PERMIT A MODEL THAT VIOLATES IT? If not, either the requirement or the rules are wrong. That is mechanically checkable at step 5 and it subsumes the degenerate-model check, because a model that does less is just one way to make a requirement unfalsifiable.

AND IT GIVES THE TRACE PAIRS A JOB. The imap reviewer noted that writing traces/requirement-01.md is what FORCES the rule 3 fix, since the state the trace needs does not exist. The acme reviewer found the mirror image: there the pairs CANNOT be authored, because the allowed run needs a state the requirements forbid. Both reviewers reached the trace pairs as the instrument that exposes the defect, from opposite directions.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION. Author one violating trace per requirement BEFORE the freeze, following the laytime and custody convention of traces/README.md plus one trace per requirement. The authoring attempt is the gate. Earlier guidance on this bead said to settle the refutation deliverable before authoring any pair, and that ordering is now wrong: the pair attempt is cheaper than the deliverable design and it finds the defect faster.

Files: PRACTICE-PLAN.md
THE REFUTATION DELIVERABLE IS WEAKER THAN THIS BEAD CLAIMED, measured on acme 2026-10-08.

This bead said a refutation deliverable catches the first face of the pattern, a requirement satisfiable by doing less. It does not catch it either. It discloses it.

Measured after the acme edit landed: the collapse model satisfies the nine at rc 0 AND the new probe holds at rc 0. A collapse learner produces every artifact the statement asks for and nothing rejects them.

The reason is structural rather than a drafting miss. No model both satisfies the nine and refutes the probe, so a statement that DEMANDED a refutation would be demanding something unsolvable, and would announce the answer by demanding it. So the deliverable can only ask what the learner's model does, not require a particular answer.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS BEAD. A statement-level fix can make a wrong answer VISIBLE. It cannot make a wrong answer FAIL. Rejecting a degenerate model is a GRADER capability, and this bead should say so rather than implying the statement can carry it.

So the rule splits in two:

1. STATEMENT LEVEL, and this is checkable at step 5. For every requirement, does the rule set permit a model that violates it? A requirement no permitted model can violate is a tautology, which is the imap-move face and is a real defect in the statement.
2. GRADER LEVEL, and this is new work nobody has scoped. A submission whose model never reaches the mechanism should not grade as correct. The statement can require the learner to state what their model does; only the grader can act on the answer.

Face 1 stays a step 5 gate. Face 2 needs its own bead and probably belongs with harness/grade.sh. Central is not filing that tonight, because scoping it properly needs the grader's current contract read rather than recalled.
CORRECTION, same evening. This bead's previous note said face 2, rejecting a submission whose model never reaches the mechanism, 'needs its own bead and probably belongs with harness/grade.sh' and that central was not filing it because scoping needed the grader's contract read rather than recalled.

Central then read it, and THE CAPABILITY ALREADY EXISTS.

harness/grade.sh:4-13 grades by conjunct-wise two-sided implication plus non-vacuity. Obligation 2, PHI => psi_j for each submission conjunct, IS the over-constraint check, and grade.sh:45-52 reports over_constrained as its own boolean with a witness, because 23.6% of wrong models are over and under constrained at once.

A collapsed or boardless or no-mechanism model is OVER-CONSTRAINED. It forbids behaviour the reference permits. So obligation 2 should already fail it.

So face 2 is wiring and verification, not new capability, and it is filed as tla-8kgj at that smaller size: confirm each wave-1 reference carries a decomposition the grader can consume, then grade each degenerate model recorded in the step 5 reports and assert over_constrained = true. If one grades as acceptable, that is a defect in obligation 2 rather than in the statements.

THE LESSON IS THE SAME ONE AS EVERY OTHER CORRECTION TODAY. Central described a capability as missing from memory, having never opened the 1,299-line file that implements it. Four statements, two survey claims, five instruments and now one grader have all come back differently from how central described them, and in every single case the difference was found by reading the artifact.

title: The seeded-bug matrix cannot grade a temporal property, so gate 1 is blind to every liveness problem
description:
Found by the tla-pmm2.2 spike author on 2026-10-08 and confirmed by central reading the line.

THE LINE. harness/seeded-bugs.sh:546 builds every variant's config as:

    printf 'SPECIFICATION %s\n' "$SPEC"
    printf 'INVARIANT %s\n' "$PROPERTY"

INVARIANT, always, with no PROPERTY branch anywhere in the script. A temporal formula handed to it is written into the cfg under the wrong keyword.

WHY THIS IS P1 AND NOT A FEATURE REQUEST. The seeded-mutant pass is this project's FIRST-RANKED quality gate. The START HERE drawer for the 10-08 run says it is not optional and gives the cost of skipping it: 4 of 5 mutants uncaught on the holdout build, 5 of 11 on the pilot. So for any problem whose property is liveness, the gate everything else leans on is measuring a state-predicate surrogate rather than the thing the learner is asked to write, and it reports BUGS_CAUGHT either way.

The tla-pmm2.2 spike hit this on the first liveness problem the project has attempted. Its mutant result, 4 caught of 4 seeded, is a true statement about a surrogate invariant it wrote for the purpose, and it said so rather than banking the number. It also quantified the surrogate's weakness: the surrogate fires exactly one Begin step later than the oracle, every time.

HOW THIS COMPOUNDS WITH THE SAME BEAD'S OTHER FINDING. On that problem the stated liveness property does not isolate the defect. Three one-line fixes exist at three sites and they are not equivalent: one makes liveness green while NoExhaustedEpochHeld still exits 12. So a learner who states only the liveness requirement can fix the system wrongly and get a green run. A matrix that could grade the temporal property is exactly the instrument that would catch that, and it is the instrument we do not have.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT from tla-hl96. That bead is about instruments reporting a pass over work they SKIPPED. This one runs its work and the work is about the wrong formula. Fix them separately.

WHAT TO BUILD. A PROPERTY branch, chosen by the shape of the operator rather than by a flag the caller might forget, plus the fairness conjunct the spec needs for any liveness verdict to mean anything. Note that the rc table changes: a liveness violation is rc 13, not 12, and the matrix's oracle reads 12 today.

Files: harness/seeded-bugs.sh, harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/selftest.sh

RED: GIVEN a reference module whose obligation is a temporal formula and a variant that breaks it WHEN harness/seeded-bugs.sh grades the pair THEN the variant is caught, the cfg carries PROPERTY rather than INVARIANT, and the spec carries a fairness conjunct. A run that silently writes INVARIANT over a temporal formula is the defect, and the selftest fixture must contain one liveness pair so this cannot regress.
notes:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN FRAMING, from the fix that closed it.

I wrote that the matrix 'grades a state-predicate surrogate and reports BUGS_CAUGHT either way'. That is wrong about the mechanism and it made the bug sound like a silent lie.

MEASURED RED, driving a new liveness fixture against the pre-fix script:

  RelayGood     SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE  rc=76
  RelayVacuous  SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE  rc=76
  RelayWeak     SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE  rc=76
  RelayUnsound  SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE  rc=76

title: Three quality instruments report a pass over work they did not do
description:
Found across three independent dispatches on 2026-10-08. Filed as one bead because it is one defect shape, and fixing it one instrument at a time will miss the fourth.

THE SHAPE. An instrument whose check could not run reports success rather than indeterminate. The caller reads an exit code, sees a pass, and the thing the instrument exists to catch walks through.

THE THREE SITES.

1. harness/screen.sh returns CLEAR exit 0 with step 1 skipped. Step 1 is the GitHub code-search check that catches a proposed module name colliding with a published spec. The call returns 401 because the gh token has no code-search scope. Filed separately as tla-795s, which carries the measurement over four candidate names.

2. harness/vacuity.sh returns NON_VACUOUS rc 0 when its satisfiability and dead-action probes were SKIPPED. That happens on every model that violates its configured invariant, which is to say on every broken-variant run, which is to say on exactly the runs a spike author cares about. Its remediation text says the probes were skipped. Its token does not, and the token is what a script reads. Reported by both the tla-pmm2.1 and tla-pmm2.4 spike authors independently.

3. verdict.sh passes -deadlock unconditionally while TLC's deadlock checking is an AND across cfg and command line, so a learner's CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE yields no check and no notice. Filed separately as tla-ka3r.

WHY ONE BEAD. Each of the three was found by a different agent looking at something else, and none of the three would have been found by looking for it. That is what a shape rather than a bug looks like. The project already has the rule this violates, in .claude/rules/loom-conventions.md under 'Gate, don't advise': a correctness check must never depend on a human noticing. An instrument that reports PASS over a skipped step is worse than an advisory grep, because the advisory grep at least does not lie.

WHAT TO BUILD. A convention for indeterminate, applied to all three, plus a sweep for the fourth. Concretely: reserve an exit code that means 'the check did not run', make every instrument use it, and add a gate asserting that no instrument under harness/ can reach a success token on a path where a probe was skipped. The sweep matters more than the three fixes.

The verdict-channel suite is the natural home for the assertion, since V2-PLAN.md section 5.1 already forbids reading verdicts from stdout and this is the same principle one level up: an exit code that cannot distinguish 'passed' from 'did not run' is not a verdict channel.

Files: harness/screen.sh, harness/vacuity.sh, harness/verdict.sh, harness/test-verdict.sh

RED: INVARIANT: no instrument under harness/ returns a success exit code on a run where any of its probes or steps was skipped. For each of screen.sh, vacuity.sh and verdict.sh there is a fixture driving the skip path, and each returns the reserved indeterminate code rather than 0. The sweep fails if a new instrument reaches a success token past a skipped probe.
close_reason:
Fixed in 21eb31a, merged. RED 31 passed 27 failed on the new suite; GREEN 61 passed 0 failed. All three sites now return rc 99 CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN where they returned 0.

RESERVED CODE 99, and the number was chosen by measurement rather than taste. Clear of every documented band in the repo: screen 0-2/64, comment-gate 0-3, grade 0-5, vacuity 0-8, verdict's TLC rows, refinement 20-30, seeded-bugs 40-46. And BELOW 124 and 126 so it cannot be read as timeout(1) or a shell signal code. Part 1 of the suite asserts the non-collision by HARVESTING every header verdict-table row, so a future band that collides fails the gate.

THE SWEEP, AND ITS HONEST LIMIT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE. It takes a census of every harness/*.sh that is not test-*.sh, 10 instruments, strips comments, and matches a fixed skip-admission vocabulary. An admitter not driven by a registry row fails. Three controls over a planted tree: finds a planted admitter, does not flag a quiet one, excludes test-*.sh. Part 6 closes the obvious loophole by requiring every registered instrument to have at least one non-pass row.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO: IT CANNOT SEE A SILENT SKIP. verdict.sh printed NOTHING about the discarded keyword, so the census MISSES SITE 3 ENTIRELY and part 4 covers that site by enumeration instead. So A FOURTH SILENT SITE WILL NOT BE FOUND BY THIS GATE. The worker says that is the largest thing wrong with it and central agrees. Four other limits are stated in the file header: no path proof, a fixed English vocabulary, test suites out of scope, and scripts/ not covered.

TWO EXTRA FINDINGS AT SITE 1. The 403 hole is CLOSED, measured: gh api --jq writes GitHub's JSON body to stdout on failure and exits nonzero, no line is bare digits, so the ^[0-9]+$ guard rejects it and the verdict is now 99 rather than CLEAR. And a SECOND INSTANCE of the same defect was found and fixed in the mechanism code-search, which printed ERROR and left the verdict untouched. WAIVED is now separate from SKIPPED so --offline still exits 0.

Budget 7.375, 6.947 and 7.046s over three serial runs, registered slow|7.4 because it model-checks, which is the rule in scripts/test's header rather than a wall-clock judgment.

THE SCREEN QUERY FIX IS NOT IN THIS COMMIT, deliberately. It breaks harness/fixtures/screen/gh-stub, which strips a trailing ' language:tla' and looks the remainder up in a table, so it needs gh-stub, gh-stub-counts.txt and selftest.sh in the same commit and all three are outside this footprint. The measurement and the exact working query are recorded in screen.sh's header under STILL BROKEN, AND NOT FIXED HERE. tla-795s now carries those three files.

THE TEST LAYER HAS THE SAME DEFECT AND IS OUT OF SCOPE. harness/test-corpus-manifest.sh exits 0 having reported 10 skipped checks, and scripts/test prints only PASS. Filed separately.

title: Deadlock checking is an AND across cfg and command line, so a learner's CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE is silently ignored
description:
Measured by the tla-pmm2.3 spike author on 2026-10-08, five cells, and reported rather than fixed because it was outside that bead's footprint.

THE FINDING. TLC's deadlock checking is an AND across the .cfg keyword and the command line. Either side switches it off, and neither side says so.

harness/verdict.sh passes -deadlock by default. So a learner who writes CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE in their .cfg gets NO deadlock check and NO notice. The keyword they wrote is overridden by a flag they never see, and the run comes back green.

WHY THIS IS P1. It is the gate-dont-advise failure in its worst direction, and it points at a learner rather than at us. A learner who suspects a deadlock, writes the keyword that checks for it, and gets a clean run has been told their model is fine by an instrument that was not looking. 82 of 337 configs in the published corpus carry a CHECK_DEADLOCK line, per .claude/rules/tla-practice.md section 7, so this is ordinary practice and not an exotic path.

Our own references are unaffected in the sense that verdicts come from exit codes and the harness passes the flag deliberately. The exposure is the learner's cfg.

A SECOND, SMALLER FACT FROM THE SAME MEASUREMENT. With the flag on, the ACME spike's prose-faithful and wedged models both exit 11, because RFC 8555 section 7.1.6 gives a challenge two intended final states. So rc=11 does not discriminate between a correct and an incorrect model there. Worth knowing before anybody treats 11 as a signal.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is a design call rather than a patch. Either verdict.sh stops passing -deadlock unconditionally and lets the cfg speak, or it keeps the flag and the tooling tells a learner their keyword was overridden. The second is safer, because silently honouring a learner's cfg could turn every intended-terminal-state reference red.

Files: harness/verdict.sh

RED: GIVEN a .cfg carrying CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE WHEN the run goes through harness/verdict.sh THEN either the deadlock check actually runs, or the run reports in its output that the cfg keyword was overridden by a command-line flag. A keyword that is silently ignored is the defect.
close_reason:
Fixed in 21eb31a as part of the tla-hl96 sweep, merged.

REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY, ALL SIX CELLS, which is what this bead asked for since central had filed it on one agent's word and never re-run it.

  verdict.sh with CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE in the cfg   OK, rc 0
  raw TLC, same pair, no flag                      rc 11
  raw TLC, same pair, with -deadlock               rc 0
  no keyword and no flag                           rc 11
  CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE and no flag                 rc 0

And TLC PRINTS NOTHING about the override. The three grep hits that suggested otherwise were filename matches.

So the finding was correct: the check is an AND, verdict.sh passes -deadlock unconditionally, and a learner's TRUE was silently discarded.

THE DESIGN CHOSEN, and it is the safer of the two central named. KEEP THE FLAG, REFUSE ON DISAGREEMENT, returning rc 99. The measurement behind it: 334 repo .cfg files carry CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE and ALL 334 AGREE with the default flag and still run, while only 3 carry TRUE and all three are in sources/spikes/. So silently honouring every cfg would have been the riskier change and refusing on disagreement costs nothing today.

--deadlock-override is the declared escape hatch, and vacuity.sh's three probe call sites now use it. The cfg scan uses shell builtins only, so test-verdict.sh's structural ban on text matchers stays green. test-verdict went 35 to 39 assertions.

ONE DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE, FILED SEPARATELY AND IT IS NOT A REGRESSION TODAY. grade.sh, refinement.sh, seeded-bugs.sh and sequence.sh all call verdict.sh and none of their fixtures carries CHECK_DEADLOCK, so the gate is green. But a LEARNER submission carrying CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE would now hand grade.sh an rc 99 it has no arm for, giving HARNESS_ERROR 4. Each of the four callers has to decide whether to pass --deadlock-override or surface the 99.

And the three CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE cfgs in the acme and txn-epoch spikes now need --check-deadlock on their vacuity runs. That is the lesson rather than a regression.

title: spike-measure.sh counts comment words as variables, and its own suite does not catch it
description:
Found by the tla-pmm2.1 spike author on 2026-10-08, isolated with a purpose-built probe rather than asserted.

THE SYMPTOM. The spike's first measured row read 36 variables for a module declaring 5.

THE PROBE, which is why this is a measurement and not a guess. The author built probe-vars-comment/ with two modules declaring the same two variables, one with a commented VARIABLES block and one without:

  VarsCommented reads 8
  VarsPlain     reads 2

THE CAUSE. strip() removes \* line comments but leaves (* *) block comments. tally() then matches English words inside the block comment as variable names.

WHY THIS IS P1. Every difficulty measurement in the project runs through this script. The load vector's representation dimension, every spike report's measured row, and the 1-to-5 candidate estimates all read variable counts from it. A module that documents its state in a block comment above VARIABLES, which is good practice and which the shipped references do, reads high by however many English words the comment carries. The number is not noisy, it is wrong in one direction, and nothing flagged it for two months.

The mitigating fact, and it is worth keeping: variable count barely separates difficulty levels anyway. corpus/MANIFEST.md measured one level spanning 1 to 87 variables over 143 systems, and spike-measure.sh:6-12 says so in its own header. The author also re-ran its model in a 7-variable framing and got identical verdicts. So no verdict in the repo is known to be wrong because of this. What is wrong is every variable count a block-commented module ever produced.

THIS IS A SECOND HOLE, NOT THE FENCING ONE. The fencing spike found and fixed a different bug, VARIABLES alone on its line. That fix is in and this is beside it.

harness/test-spike-measure.sh does not catch it. That is the part to fix first: a suite that passes over a wrong answer is worth less than no suite, because it is why this survived.

Files: harness/spike-measure.sh, harness/test-spike-measure.sh

RED: GIVEN two modules declaring the same two variables, one with a (* *) block comment above or inside its VARIABLES block and one without WHEN harness/spike-measure.sh measures each THEN both report 2. The probe the tla-pmm2.1 author built is the fixture: use it rather than writing a new one.
close_reason:
Fixed in 7e3552a, merged. RED 32 passed 9 failed, GREEN 41 passed 0 failed. All 22 pre-existing assertions passed on the red run, so the fix broke nothing. The probe reads 2 and 2 where it read 8 and 2.

A THIRD HOLE WAS FOUND AND IT IS THE BIGGER ONE. The bead was about over-counting. The worse defect is UNDER-counting to zero.

The shipped line-comment strip BLANKED a comment-only line instead of removing it, and a blank line ends the VARIABLES declaration block, so a comment sitting between two declarations lost everything after it.

Swept over git ls-files '*.tla' with the old and new strips side by side: 13 of the 613 tracked modules that declare VARIABLES read ZERO VARIABLES under the old strip, against 1 that over-counted. All 13 use the Apalache per-declaration '\* @type:' form, for example puzzles/A01-hello-snowcat/solution/VendingMachine.tla:4-8.

That matters beyond this repo's v1 tree. .claude/rules/tla-practice.md records 63 modules in the published corpus carrying @type: annotations, so the one-annotation-per-declaration style is ordinary Apalache practice and any such module measured zero.

SIX COMMENT SHAPES TESTED, each with its wrong before-reading: nested (* a (* b *) c *) on a declaration line read 6, and nesting is depth-tracked with all six shape fixtures at rc 0 so it is legal on this build; two separate blocks with a declaration between them read 4, which is the greedy-strip discriminator; a block spanning three lines inside the list read 28; a line comment inside a block read 5; an open-block token inside a line comment read 1; and an open-block token inside a STRING LITERAL read 2, kept as a guard because without string handling the fix would delete the declaration and report 0.

NOT HANDLED, DELIBERATELY AND RECORDED IN THE CODE. An unterminated block comment bleeds into the next module in the EXTENDS closure instead of resetting at the module header. Such a module does not parse, TLC gives rc 150, and nobody reads that row's descriptive columns.

TWO THINGS FOR CENTRAL, both outside footprint. scripts/test:244 records 1.9s and the suite now measures 4.3s in-suite, 5.99 and 5.94 standalone. No nudge fires because it needs 3x AND +5s and this is +4.09. Rolled into tla-kqry. And the gate now reads its fixture from sources/spikes/progressive-sync-stale-status/probe-vars-comment, failing loudly by name if that moves, though a harness/fixtures/ home would be better.

sources/spikes/fencing/REPORT.md remains stale and was not re-measured.

title: Author imap-move-partial-failure through steps 3 to 8
description:
Off-ramp candidate. Yardstick shape: two-store. Source: RFC 9051 section 6.4.8 against RFC 6851 section 3.3.

THE PROPERTY AT STAKE, in the system's own vocabulary: However the command fails, every message ends up in at least one of the two mailboxes and preferably not in both.

NO TARGET POSITION AND NO TARGET DIFFICULTY. This problem is authored to be good, not to hit a vector band. Its VECTOR.md gets measured after the reference is frozen, and --search decides where it goes.

Steps 3 and 4 run as SEPARATE agents in SEPARATE worktrees and neither sees the other's output. Step 4's author writes the statement from the external source alone. A disagreement between spike and statement is a finding, not an accident: on tla-fr50 it caught statement rules 4 and 5 contradicting each other over two senses of the word cancels, and the published spec took rule 4's side.

Step 3 writes sources/spikes/imap-move-partial-failure/. Step 4 writes authoring/imap-move-partial-failure/statement/PROBLEM.md.

Files: sources/spikes/imap-move-partial-failure/, authoring/imap-move-partial-failure/
notes:
STEPS 3 AND 4 COMPLETE AND MERGED, 2026-10-08. Steps 5 to 9 remain. Both halves are on main.

  spike      sources/spikes/imap-move-partial-failure/REPORT.md
  statement  authoring/imap-move-partial-failure/statement/PROBLEM.md

Both authors ran their pre-flight green against tlc 2026.07.31.184830. Each statement author confirmed in writing that it read no .tla, no .cfg, and nothing under sources/. Each spike author confirmed it read nothing under its problem's statement/ directory. So the step 4 isolation held and a spike-against-statement disagreement is a finding rather than an accident.

NEXT STEP IS 5, the consistency check: one reader that sees source, spike and statement together. Per D4 it must NOT also write the vector, because that puts a number-producer in a position to reshape the artifact the number is about.

NO VECTOR.md EXISTS YET and that is correct. The vector is measured after the reference is frozen at step 6. When it is written it uses the new field from tla-5zgr.3:

  uses constructs from: <bare number in 2..13>, <constructs>, <path:line>

A bare number, not ch12. The retired reading-gate vocabulary is refused by name.
WHAT STEP 5 MUST SETTLE. The statement author predicted a disagreement and the two CONVERGED instead, which is the stronger result.

The statement author, blind, argued clause 1 at MUST makes clause 3 dead text UNLESS clause 1 means per-item atomicity rather than location, and encoded the per-item reading. The spike measured exactly that and found the escape hatch:

  State 2: <StoreOne(m1)>  inSource={m1}  inTarget={}  deleted={m1}

One mailbox, carrying \\Deleted. Clauses 2 and 3 hold, clause 1 fails. So unaffected carries the deleted flag, and that is what stops clause 1 collapsing into clause 2 AND clause 3, the redundancy shape tla-practice.md section 4 found in only 3 of 899 published configs.

The spike also measured the forward implication: a server satisfying RFC 9051's MUST cannot leave a duplicate. Under RFC 6851 clause 1 was SHOULD and the duplicate was permitted by every MUST, which is where Thunderbird 610131 sat. The spike reads 9051 as now in mild tension with itself and found no erratum saying whether that was intended.

THE PRICE OF THE THIRD NAME, measured. Dropping clause 1 and keeping the other two catches 4 of 5 mutants, missing stray-deleted-flag. The three-name reference catches 5 of 5. Clause 1 earns its separate name by exactly one mutant.

WHICH CLAUSE A NON-ATOMIC MOVE BREAKS. Copy-first breaks clauses 1 and 3 on the first COPY and never touches clause 2. Expunge-first breaks 1 and 2 and never touches 3. So the three are independently breakable, which is the condition for three names.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SURVEY, both measured by both authors independently.

1. The diff is TWO changed lines of nine, not one. SHOULD either be became MUST be either, the adverb moving with the modal. And separately, Because a MOVE applies to a set of messages, it became Unlike the COPY command, MOVE of a set of messages. Byte-identical holds from sentence 2 onward and overstates by one sentence.
2. RFC 9051 Appendix E does NOT record the strengthening. The item at rfc9051.txt:8039 is about target-mailbox creation and TRYCREATE, a neighbouring tightening. sources/rfcs.md section 11.8 quotes it truncated and reads it as corroboration, which it is not. A grep over Appendix E for move, partial, orphan and duplicate finds no item about the per-message clause.
STEP 5 COMPLETE. Verdict NOT SUFFICIENT, one required change to rule 3. Report at authoring/imap-move-partial-failure/reports/step5-consistency.md.

THE DEFECT, and the statement sets the trap it warns about. PROBLEM.md:96-97 says 'The clerk never marks an entry for striking at all.' No model the rules permit can then reach a part entry, so requirement 1 at PROBLEM.md:177 is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION. The statement warns about exactly that trap at :44 and then sets it.

RFC 9051 states the analogue as a prohibition on a REACHABLE action, 'the \\Deleted flag MUST NOT be set for any message' at rfc9051.txt:4683, not as a denial that the action exists. Rule 3 must match. This is also the one leak: with no diagnosis to withhold, a leak here looks like a sentence that resolves a check.

CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER NOTE AND TO WHAT CENTRAL TOLD FRANK. Both halves' argument about clause 1 is BACKWARDS. Per-item atomicity does not rescue clause 3 from redundancy, it RELOCATES the redundancy: clause 1 then strictly implies BOTH others. The spike measured ClauseOneImpliesNotLost at rc 0 right beside ClauseOneImpliesNotBoth and drew the conclusion only for clause 3.

So the three names are earned DIAGNOSTICALLY, by Specifying Systems p. 259 and by the seeded-bug signatures, and NOT logically. The earlier note's claim that the per-item reading is what stops clause 1 collapsing into clauses 2 and 3 is wrong.

Q1, and the per-item reading IS right, reached from the text alone. The clause is the only one of the three naming no mailbox while its neighbours do, rfc9051.txt:4687 against :4688 and :4690. Its own contrast is set-against-item. And 'moved' was already defined as a three-part compound at :4667.

BETTER PROVENANCE THAN AN ERRATUM. RFC 9051 has 9 errata, 0 Rejected, none naming 6.4.8; 7323 is 6.4.4.4, one digit away. RFC 6851 has none. But the DRAFT SERIES dates the edit exactly: revision 24 reads SHOULD, revision 25 reads MUST, and the same revision rewrote the lead-in. Posted 2021-01-20, the day Last Call closed. That is stronger evidence than the survey had and it explains why both changed lines moved together.

Q2. KEEP requirement 3 as an INVARIANT. The statement declares the narrowing honestly at :115-120, and under RFC 9051 the no-duplicates condition is a consequence of a MUST, so the promotion adds no constraint. BUT the reason given at :207 is wrong: it says two names preserve two strengths, and TLC has one strength. Replace it with the labelling reason.

Q3. THE SILENCE TURNS OUT NOT TO MATTER, which contradicts central's brief and the spike's third recommendation. The claim that the statement avoids making 'stop here' obvious is verified: no sentence says she stops or continues, and :60-62 actively removes the index a learner would reach for. But Observe carries no order, so NO formula over it can tell a prefix model from a set model. The prefix reading costs state count, not content.

Q4. Follow the laytime and custody convention: traces/README.md plus one violating trace per requirement. Writing requirement-01.md is what FORCES the rule 3 fix, since the state it needs does not exist. For Checking, do not quote 43, which is the three-message row while the statement checks at two, and do not quote 17 either without re-measuring, since flagged has no counterpart in a statement-faithful model. Measure on the frozen reference at step 6. Every spike anomaly is 2 states at depth 2.

BOTH SURVEY CORRECTIONS CONFIRMED, and the Appendix E one is worse than reported. diff -u over the nine-line blocks gives two changed lines and seven identical, at the cited line numbers. Appendix E item 8 at rfc9051.txt:8039 is target-mailbox creation and TRYCREATE, and sources/rfcs.md section 11.8 truncates at the word that changes the subject.

STRONGER THAN THE SPIKE PUT IT: Appendix E is 'Changes from RFC 3501', and RFC 3501 HAS NO MOVE COMMAND, so it was never the place to look. Downstream, sources/rfcs.md:1932 and :2152 both rest on that wrong reading, and :2152 GENERALISES THE METHOD from this wrong example. Fix the method claim, not just the citation.

TWO MORE. Rule 4's promise 1 at :111 and requirement 1 at :177 are different claims presented as one, which is the root of the verdict, and the history paragraph at :212 attaches the revision to the weaker. Against that, the statement's three requirements are MUTUALLY LOGICALLY INDEPENDENT where the RFC's three clauses are not, which is a real improvement on the source and worth keeping. The spike's view that the clause set must be derived rather than handed over is a format disagreement with this project's statement shape, not a defect, and the reviewer recommends not acting on it.
REQUIRED EDIT APPLIED AND IT WORKED, e98194e, merged.

Requirement 1 now reaches a part entry, measured: State 2 <Begin(m1)> with receiving = (m1 :> 'part' @@ m2 :> 'off'), Invariant Req1 violated, rc 12. Under the old rule 3 that step was not a model the rules permitted.

Rule 3 now forbids the OUTCOME. Before: 'The conditions those three steps would pass through never stand as moments of their own. The clerk never marks an entry for striking at all.' After: 'The clerk has the pen for each of those three steps and she can make a part entry with it. The orders forbid a part entry that stands.'

FIVE TRACES, each measured on a scratch model of the amended rules:

  allowed.md run 1       NoFullRun witness          rc 12, 4-state
  allowed.md run 2       NoPartwayRefusal witness   rc 12, 3-state
  requirement-01.md      begin-receiving vs Req1    rc 12, 2/2
  requirement-02.md      strike-first vs Req2       rc 12, 2/2
  requirement-03.md      copy-first vs Req3         rc 12, 2/2

Each broken model against its OTHER two requirements: rc 0, 18 distinct, depth 6. The correct model on all three: rc 0, 8 distinct, depth 4. So the three are independently breakable in the delivered artifact, not just in the spike.

FOUR PLACES THE STEP 5 REPORT WAS WRONG WHEN APPLIED. The worker found all four and fixed or declined each with a reason.

1. The report named only PROBLEM.md:96-97. The sentence BEFORE it, 'The conditions those three steps would pass through never stand as moments of their own', is the same denial and keeps requirement 1 unfalsifiable on its own. FIXING THE NAMED SENTENCE ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED.
2. The report's claim that once rule 3 is fixed, rule 4's promise 1 and requirement 1 become the same claim is false. Promise 1 is a per-member outcome over a run; requirement 1 is a single-state claim. Separated in the requirements preamble rather than merged.
3. The report says laytime's traces/ holds a README.md. It holds pair-1.md to pair-3.md only. Central passed that on unverified. The worker followed custody instead.
4. The worker DECLINED to put 'earned diagnostically, not logically' in the statement, correctly. That holds of the RFC's clauses, while the same report calls the statement's three requirements mutually logically independent. Putting it in would have confused the two. The replacement reason for requirement 3 is the labelling one only.

REPORTED NOT FIXED. Requirement 1's own gloss at :177-179, 'there's no third condition for it to be caught in', still reads as a denial of the shape rule 3 just stopped making. Not false, so left. Checking carries no state count.

title: Author txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry through steps 3 to 8
description:
Off-ramp candidate. Yardstick shape: workflow. Source: Apache Kafka KAFKA-20090.

THE PROPERTY AT STAKE, in the system's own vocabulary: A fenced transaction can never be reopened, and every transaction can eventually be committed or aborted.

NO TARGET POSITION AND NO TARGET DIFFICULTY. This problem is authored to be good, not to hit a vector band. Its VECTOR.md gets measured after the reference is frozen, and --search decides where it goes.

Steps 3 and 4 run as SEPARATE agents in SEPARATE worktrees and neither sees the other's output. Step 4's author writes the statement from the external source alone. A disagreement between spike and statement is a finding, not an accident: on tla-fr50 it caught statement rules 4 and 5 contradicting each other over two senses of the word cancels, and the published spec took rule 4's side.

Step 3 writes sources/spikes/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/. Step 4 writes authoring/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/statement/PROBLEM.md.

Files: sources/spikes/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/, authoring/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/
notes:
STEPS 3 AND 4 COMPLETE AND MERGED, 2026-10-08. Steps 5 to 9 remain. Both halves are on main.

  spike      sources/spikes/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/REPORT.md
  statement  authoring/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/statement/PROBLEM.md

Both authors ran their pre-flight green against tlc 2026.07.31.184830. Each statement author confirmed in writing that it read no .tla, no .cfg, and nothing under sources/. Each spike author confirmed it read nothing under its problem's statement/ directory. So the step 4 isolation held and a spike-against-statement disagreement is a finding rather than an accident.

NEXT STEP IS 5, the consistency check: one reader that sees source, spike and statement together. Per D4 it must NOT also write the vector, because that puts a number-producer in a position to reshape the artifact the number is about.

NO VECTOR.md EXISTS YET and that is correct. The vector is measured after the reference is frozen at step 6. When it is written it uses the new field from tla-5zgr.3:

  uses constructs from: <bare number in 2..13>, <constructs>, <path:line>

A bare number, not ch12. The retired reading-gate vocabulary is refused by name.
WHAT STEP 5 MUST SETTLE, and this problem has the hardest open question in the wave.

1. THE SOURCE CONTAINS A MAINTAINER DISAGREEMENT ABOUT WHETHER THIS IS A DEFECT. Justine Olshan: the key to fixing this issue is not treating an abort as a retry of a fenced producer, and we actually need to prevent this case regardless of max epoch. Artem Livshits, on a late aborter getting success and starting another transaction: this is also ok, because one of 2 things happen, confirmed in a later comment.

The statement took Justine's side, which is the side central's property-at-stake line took without knowing there was a side. The spike did not address the split directly. SO THIS IS STILL OPEN, and it is Frank's call rather than a reader's: a learner-facing problem whose correct answer two maintainers dispute is a defect unless the dispute is the exercise.

2. THE STATED LIVENESS PROPERTY DOES NOT ISOLATE THE DEFECT. Measured. TxnBeginChecks.tla adds one conjunct to Begin and gives rc 0 on TxnEventuallyEnds while NoExhaustedEpochHeld still exits 12. Three one-line fixes exist at three sites and they are NOT equivalent:

  TxnFenceRotates  both green, system stays open. The real fix.
  TxnRetryGuarded  both green, system closes.
  TxnBeginChecks   liveness only.

So a learner who states only the liveness requirement can fix the system wrongly and get a green run. The statement's requirement 2 is insufficient as the deliverable, and step 5 should decide whether a second requirement is handed over or left to be found.

3. GATE 1 CANNOT GRADE THIS PROBLEM. harness/seeded-bugs.sh:546 writes INVARIANT only, so the 4-of-4 mutant result is about a state-predicate surrogate the spike wrote for the purpose, not about the temporal property. The spike said so rather than banking the number, and quantified the surrogate: it fires exactly one Begin step later than the oracle, every time. Filed as tla-r2ih, P1. Do not treat this problem's mutant pass as a pass on its real obligation until that lands.

MEASURED. 4 variables, 21 distinct states, depth 12, 0.4s, rc 13. The counterexample reproduces the JIRA's four numbered steps in order. The tail is verified twice, by a CHECK_DEADLOCK run exiting 11 on an identical state and by a no-fairness run stopping with two actions still enabled. Scaling in the counter range is close to linear, 21/39/147 states at MaxEpoch 2/4/16.

Property and fairness, quoted:
  TxnEventuallyEnds == (txn = "Ongoing") ~> (txn # "Ongoing")
  FairSpec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Next)

THE CEILING. The spike made a bump at the ceiling unavailable, guarding every write with cEpoch < MaxEpoch, and confirmed central's brief that the source is silent: none of the 24 comments says what a bump from max does. It rejected saturate as contradicting cannot commit, and wrap-to-zero as epoch reuse already covered by the fencing spike. The off-by-one IS reachable here, rc 12 at 12 states depth 6, and exits 0 on the repaired spec.

WHAT THE SOURCE DOES SETTLE and it changed the model: the normal end path renews an exhausted epoch and the fencing path skips the rotation. Without that asymmetry the stuck state is reachable by a path that never touches EndRetry, so it is load-bearing for the defect being necessary.

TWO VACUITY REDS THAT ARE FINDINGS, not failures. ReInit never fires in the broken spec, because a client never told it was fenced never re-initialises. EndRetry never fires under the pre-KAFKA-19367 double bump, which is stronger than the JIRA thread's own prediction.

SCREEN GAP. harness/screen.sh returned CLEAR exit 0 with step 1 skipped on a 401. The proposed module name is therefore unverified against GitHub code search. Central re-ran it and got 401 too, so it is the token. Filed as tla-795s and tla-hl96. Re-run step 1 with an authenticated gh BEFORE the freeze.
CENTRAL'S RESOLUTION OF THE MAINTAINER DISPUTE, 2026-10-08 evening, stated to Frank and awaiting his confirmation.

THE FORK, restated precisely, because the first note left it vaguer than it needs to be.

Requirement 2, every permit is closed in the end, is the liveness property. NOBODY disputes it. A transaction that can neither commit nor time out is a bug by both maintainers' reckoning, Artem included.

Requirement 1, a withdrawal puts the gang out, is the safety property. This is the only disputed one. Artem Livshits says a late aborter getting success and starting another transaction is also ok.

THE BIND IS NOT THE DISPUTE. It is that requirement 2 alone does not isolate the defect, which the spike measured: TxnBeginChecks.tla gives rc 0 on requirement 2 while NoExhaustedEpochHeld still exits 12, and three one-line fixes at three sites are not equivalent. So handing a learner only the undisputed requirement lets them produce a wrong fix and get a green run. Fixing that means handing over requirement 1, the disputed one.

THE RESOLUTION. Ship both requirements. The statement is not set in Kafka, it is a dockyard fire office, and its requirements define THAT system's contract. Artem's position is about what Kafka should guarantee and says nothing about what the fire office guarantees. So the problem is free to require both, and TxnFenceRotates is then the fix that makes both green, which the spike already identified as the real fix.

WHAT THIS COSTS. The problem stops being a faithful model of the upstream dispute. Off-ramp authoring never asked for that, it asked for a good problem, so the cost is acceptable.

WHERE THE DISPUTE GOES INSTEAD. notes/CHOICES.md, which is one of the four techniques farmed from fencing and recorded on tla-jaob.2: a format that reads a published spec as a set of decisions somebody made. The disagreement is provenance, not a requirement, and that file is where provenance lives.

THE ALTERNATIVE FRANK MAY PREFER, and it is more interesting: make the dispute itself the exercise, handing the learner both readings and asking which the system actually needs. Much harder to grade, and the grader would need a notion of a defensible answer rather than a correct one. Not recommended at this budget.

STEP 5 IS HELD on this problem until Frank confirms, because its first question is exactly this. Step 5 on the other three is dispatched.
STEP 5 COMPLETE. NOT SUFFICIENT. Report at authoring/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/reports/step5-consistency.md.

THIS IS THE WAVE'S INTENDED SPIKE-VERSUS-STATEMENT FINDING, and the spike is right.

PROBLEM.md:84 says the desk does not read the gang's card at a raise. THAT DELETES THE FENCE. The spike's Begin carries pEpoch = cEpoch at TxnBroken.tla:92, and JIRA comment 7 proposes ADDING an exhaustion check to AddPartitionsToTxn, which presupposes the currency check is already there. The statement took the issue body's 'we don't check epochs on starting transactions' literally.

FIX: rule 4 must refuse a gang whose card does not say the leaf the desk holds, while still not counting the leaves left.

THE tla-n8oq TEST: IT FAILS, in its own idiom. At Leaves = 3, each requirement in its own cfg over Observe alone:

  statement as written                   Req1 12  Req2 13  Req3-8 0   22 distinct  depth 6
  rule 5 row 4 deleted outright          Req1 12  Req2 13  Req3-8 0   16 distinct  depth 5
  card read at raise, row 4 present      Req1 12  Req2 13  Req3-8 0   17 distinct  depth 6
  card read at raise, row 4 deleted      Req1  0  Req2  0  Req3-8 0   11 distinct  depth 4

IDENTICAL VERDICT VECTOR WITH THE RETRY MECHANISM DELETED. card reads 1 in every state of both counterexamples. It escapes the siblings' all-green shape only because two requirements are false, so the underlying test fails anyway: THE ANSWER IS UNCHANGED OVER A MODEL WITH NO MECHANISM. The all-green row is not idle, with raise, withdrawal, last leaf and book-taken-back each confirmed by a probe exiting 12.

LIVENESS DID NOT SAVE IT. No fairness at all also gives 12/13, because the trap is a genuine terminal state rather than a stutter. TLC's own stuttering warning, printed or not, is the only discriminator.

Q1 PARTLY UNDOES CENTRAL'S RULING, and Frank should see this. Requirement 1 is violated under ALL THREE fixes in BOTH readings, rc 12 every time, because rule 4 raises from 'abandoned' and rule 8 sets 'abandoned', so TWO ADJACENT SENTENCES OF THE STATEMENT REFUTE IT WITH NO MODEL NEEDED. That is a drafting defect independent of the Kafka dispute, so the dispute was never the real obstacle here.

The requirement that actually discriminates is Observe.card = Leaves => Observe.standing = 'spent', which reproduces the spike's three-fix table exactly: rotation 0, retry-guard 0, entry-check 12. No formula over the four fields isolates the rotation fix uniquely, because the fire office has no stays-open axis.

So central's ship-both ruling stands in spirit, a safety requirement is kept, but requirement 1 as written must be replaced rather than shipped.

Q2. The ceiling is REACHABLE but NOT SETTLEABLE, and both readings are faithful. Rules 1 and 6 winning gives Req2 rc 13; rule 10 winning gives rc 0 at 22 states. Step 6 must record both and key Req2's verdict to the declared ceiling choice. The general instruction rather than a callout was the right call.

Q3. Collision present and unflagged. !isEpochFence present as rule 7, rotation present as rule 7's threshold, Artem's invariant withheld, the two disagreeing predicates never juxtaposed. ONE LEAK: PROBLEM.md:84-85 is the only negative-capability sentence in 25 grep hits and it names the only gap the trap runs through. That is the same sentence the blocking fix removes.

Q4. SCREEN CLEAR with the repo exclusion. 'MODULE TxnBroken' gives 1 self-hit and 0 with -repo:. isEpochFence 0. MODULE FireOffice 0. Two side findings for tla-795s: screen.sh should carry -repo: at :178, and BURNED_AT=3 is applied to fork-inflated raw hits, where TxnEpoch gives 16 hits across only 3 distinct files.

PRIOR ART NOBODY HAD FOUND, and it is in our own surveyed corpus. Vanlightly/kafka-tlaplus models PrepareEpochFence, annotates four sites '(no exhaustion modeled)', and says at line 272 that bounding the epoch 'can actually result in failed liveness'. So this exact modelling choice was already considered and DECLINED by a published author. Weigh that before shipping: the survey's own rule says a problem whose answer is the top result for its own name is a poor problem.
BOTH EDITS APPLIED, f23c0e4, merged. THE DEGENERATE IDENTITY IS BROKEN.

Before: faithful 12/13/0, no-mechanism 12/13/0, IDENTICAL.
After:  faithful 12/13/0 at 16 distinct depth 5 and 17 depth 6; no-mechanism 0/0/0 at 11 distinct depth 4.

Two of eight verdicts flip, so the answer is no longer unchanged over a model with no mechanism. The worker REBUILT THE MODEL INDEPENDENTLY and reproduced every row of the step 5 report byte for byte, including the three-fix table on the NEW requirement 1: rotation 0, retry guard 0, entry check 12. So the reviewer's measurements are now independently corroborated.

RULE 4, before: 'The desk doesn't read the gang's card when it raises a permit, and it doesn't count the leaves the book has left.' After: 'The desk reads the gang's card and sets it against its own book. If the card doesn't say the leaf the desk holds, the desk refuses it as out of date and raises nothing. The desk doesn't count the leaves the book has left.'

REQUIREMENT 1, before: 'A withdrawal puts the gang out.' After: 'A card on the last leaf means a book taken back. At every moment, if the leaf on the gang's card is the last leaf, the standing is spent. The desk has taken the book back.' Keyword line unchanged.

TRACES: NONE.md RATHER THAN PAIRS, and the measurement is in the file. Requirement 1's state is only LEGALLY reachable through a withdrawal, since (leaf = Leaves AND standing # spent) => withdrawn gives rc 0 over 17 states, so the legal route is the office's own counterexample. The one break that reaches it without a withdrawal is 'a close on the last leaf does not fill the book', rc 12 at 3 trace states, and that signposts the rule 7 asymmetry step 5 certified as withheld. Breaking requirement 5 instead does not reach the state. And shipping seven of eight fires the screen's tiling and elimination probes at harness/PUZZLE-SCREEN.md:305. Nine clean breaks with rc are recorded for the step 6 reference. The refutation-coverage pin moved accordingly.

THE CEILING IS STILL NOT SETTLED, unchanged by these edits. Reading B still gives requirement 1 rc 12 and requirement 2 rc 0, so the ceiling flips only requirement 2.

TWO THINGS THESE EDITS MADE INCOMPLETE, reported rather than fixed, and both are real follow-up.

1. The fixed rule 4 ADDS A THIRD TERMINAL STATE: a gang stranded with a stale card. CHECK_DEADLOCK now reports THAT first, at 3 states, instead of the book-full stall. PROBLEM.md:288-289 names one stall and there are now two. Fix the prose or the instance before step 6.
2. THE LEAK IS HALVED, NOT REMOVED. The negative-capability sweep still returns 25 lines and PROBLEM.md:85 still names a gap.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO CENTRAL'S BRIEF. authoring/custody/statement/traces/ holds property-01.md through property-10.md plus README.md and full-window.md, NOT pair-N.md. Central asserted the wrong convention twice today, having already been corrected once on laytime. And the degenerate identity was between the statement as written and row 4 deleted under the OLD rule 4, not under the card-checked one.

title: Author acme-challenge-retry-deadlock through steps 3 to 8
description:
Off-ramp candidate. Yardstick shape: lifecycle. Source: RFC 8555 section 8.2 against section 8 and 7.1.6.

THE PROPERTY AT STAKE, in the system's own vocabulary: A challenge stays retriable while the authority is still trying, and becomes final only once the authority has given up.

NO TARGET POSITION AND NO TARGET DIFFICULTY. This problem is authored to be good, not to hit a vector band. Its VECTOR.md gets measured after the reference is frozen, and --search decides where it goes.

Steps 3 and 4 run as SEPARATE agents in SEPARATE worktrees and neither sees the other's output. Step 4's author writes the statement from the external source alone. A disagreement between spike and statement is a finding, not an accident: on tla-fr50 it caught statement rules 4 and 5 contradicting each other over two senses of the word cancels, and the published spec took rule 4's side.

Step 3 writes sources/spikes/acme-challenge-retry-deadlock/. Step 4 writes authoring/acme-challenge-retry-deadlock/statement/PROBLEM.md.

Files: sources/spikes/acme-challenge-retry-deadlock/, authoring/acme-challenge-retry-deadlock/
notes:
STEPS 3 AND 4 COMPLETE AND MERGED, 2026-10-08. Steps 5 to 9 remain. Both halves are on main.

  spike      sources/spikes/acme-challenge-retry-deadlock/REPORT.md
  statement  authoring/acme-challenge-retry-deadlock/statement/PROBLEM.md

Both authors ran their pre-flight green against tlc 2026.07.31.184830. Each statement author confirmed in writing that it read no .tla, no .cfg, and nothing under sources/. Each spike author confirmed it read nothing under its problem's statement/ directory. So the step 4 isolation held and a spike-against-statement disagreement is a finding rather than an accident.

NEXT STEP IS 5, the consistency check: one reader that sees source, spike and statement together. Per D4 it must NOT also write the vector, because that puts a number-producer in a position to reshape the artifact the number is about.

NO VECTOR.md EXISTS YET and that is correct. The vector is measured after the reference is frozen at step 6. When it is written it uses the new field from tla-5zgr.3:

  uses constructs from: <bare number in 2..13>, <constructs>, <path:line>

A bare number, not ch12. The retired reading-gate vocabulary is refused by name.
WHAT STEP 5 MUST SETTLE, and the two authors already converged on it independently.

BOTH halves say the contradiction is FOUR-way, not three. The step-2 table, sources/rfcs.md and central's brief all said three normative sentences cannot all hold. Both authors say that is wrong, from opposite sides of the isolation wall.

The three sentences ARE jointly satisfiable, by exactly one system: one that gives up on its first failed query. The fourth ingredient is RFC 8555 section 7.1.6, which draws no arrow out of invalid and whose retry self-loop the three sentences then forbid.

So a statement carrying only the three sentences is satisfiable by a model with NO retry loop, and all nine requirements go green over a system that no longer exists. Section 7.1.6's diagram is load-bearing here, which is the opposite of how central briefed it.

MEASURED. Contradiction reaches in 4 distinct states, depth 3, rc 12. Wedged.tla, which resolves it in section 8's favour, satisfies queries <= 1 at rc 0.

THREE THINGS FOR STEP 5.

1. Collapsing the give-up and the error write is WORSE than hiding the bug. Against the wedged model, section 8 as published holds at rc 0, the 7.1.6 diagram is refined at rc 0, and erratum 5732's own sentence holds at rc 0. Every safety check a learner writes comes back green over a spec whose retry mechanism is unreachable. Seeing it needs an invariant the learner EXPECTS to be refuted, which is a reachability claim and not a safety one. Check the statement supports reaching that.

2. ERRATUM 5732 IS VERIFIED AND NOT SUFFICIENT. MCErratum exits 12. A challenge reaches valid while still carrying the entry section 8.2 made it MUST write, and the erratum permits an error only beside processing or invalid. The spike searched sections 7.1.6, 7.5.1, 8 and 8.2 for a sentence emptying the error field on success and found none, and named the surface it did not search. Its read is that the RFC needs a third sentence nobody has written. FILE THIS UPSTREAM RATHER THAN BUILDING ON IT.

3. THE DIAGRAM'S LABEL IS WRONG AND THE COMMUNITY TREATS THE DIAGRAM AS ARBITER. Graphs agree, Refines at rc 0. Labels do not: the processing-to-invalid edge is labelled Failed validation, but section 8.2's failed validation query does not take it (rc 13). GiveUp does (rc 0), and 8.2 never calls a give-up a failed validation. The diagram has no give-up edge. So the BROKEN model matches the picture, and still-open errata 7826 settles ambiguities by appeal to this diagram. The disagreement is invisible to any check over states.

THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES HOW THIS IS SET. Erratum 5732's sentence alone, as the learner's deliverable, catches 1 of 5 seeded mutants. The seven-arm reference catches 5 of 5. If the problem asks for that one invariant the deliverable is thin.

TWO GAPS THE STATEMENT AUTHOR DECLARED. No distinct-state count under Checking, because computing one means resolving the contradiction. And traces/ is promised in the statement and not shipped. The trace pair matters here: a pair only catches a wrong property if its forbidden run reaches the state that property is about, so the allowed run must contain the retry loop, which is exactly what an over-constrained model drops.
STEP 5 COMPLETE, and its verdict is NOT SUFFICIENT. One edit required before freeze. Report at authoring/acme-challenge-retry-deadlock/reports/step5-consistency.md.

IT MEASURED THE THING EVERYONE ELSE REASONED ABOUT. Encoding the statement's nine requirements verbatim over Observe at the statement's own instance, two applicants and Patience 2:

  the collapse, one act writes the entry and gives up   ALL NINE HOLD, rc 0, 16 distinct, depth 5
  the faithful reading, give-up its own act             requirement 1 violated, rc 12, depth 3

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER NOTE ON THIS BEAD, AND TO WHAT CENTRAL TOLD FRANK. The spike's suggestion that the honest state count may be 'no model satisfies all nine' is FALSE. The collapse satisfies all nine. The true claim is that no model WHICH TURNS THE LOOP satisfies all nine. Do not write the spike's sentence into the Checking section.

WHY THE STATEMENT FAILS. All nine requirements go green on a model whose retry loop provably never turns. On the collapse, both 'never two entries' and 'never inspecting with an entry' hold at rc 0. A model where nobody ever sends word also satisfies all nine, because rule 9 removes every obligation and no requirement is a reachability claim. So a learner can get a clean run on a system that does not exist, which is the exact failure the four-way finding predicted and nobody had measured.

THE FIX IT PROPOSES, and central endorses it: a SECOND DELIVERABLE requiring a formula the learner expects TLC to REFUTE. Its wording, which withholds the diagnosis while supplying the instrument: deliver one formula you expect TLC to refute, and the run that refutes it, declared as an INVARIANT, reporting which way it came out.

THE TRACES CANNOT BE AUTHORED AS SPECIFIED, and this is the sharpest catch. The allowed run needs a row with an applicant at inspecting carrying an entry. Requirement 1 forbids exactly that row. So any allowed run authored to satisfy all nine is a COLLAPSED run, and the trace pairs would CERTIFY THE WEDGE. Shipping them does not fix the insufficiency, it blesses it. Settle the second deliverable before authoring any pair.

ON Q2. The statement's one vacuity lesson teaches the SUBSCRIPT hazard, which is a different bug. The collapse defeats all nine with every subscript watching all three fields. Requirement 3's givenUp-after conditioning is the right trapdoor and correctly left open, but an open choice with no instrument is a coin flip whose green side is wrong.

ON Q4. No leak, confirmed. Rule 5 licenses the separate give-up without requiring it. The Your task paragraph leaks the SYMPTOM, a loop that never turns with checks staying green, not the cause, and it should stay because it is the only instrument the statement currently has.

THE ERRATUM FILING IS CONFIRMED OVER THE WHOLE RFC. No sentence emptying the challenge error field on success exists anywhere in RFC 8555's 5323 lines. The field name occurs 3 times, at 3431, 3502 and 3504, and only 3426 and 3504 are normative about it. A sweep for clear, remov, empt, delet, reset, discard, unset and omit returns 28 lines, none of them emptying it. The nearest passage, section 7.5.1 at 3074-3076, runs the other way. FILE THIS UPSTREAM.

THREE NEW DISAGREEMENTS, none in the earlier notes.

1. Section 7.1.6 carries the fourth ingredient in PROSE, not only as a missing arrow. 1674-1676 asserts the loop and 1686-1688 moves an error to invalid, one paragraph apart. So the four-way contradiction is textual and does not depend on reading the diagram.
2. The RFC ITSELF calls the error field the retry state, at 3501-3502. So errata 7826 is QUOTING the RFC rather than interpreting it, which strengthens that reading considerably.
3. The three-field interface cannot express two of the spike's seven arms, and the error-without-query mutant SURVIVES all nine at rc 0. That puts the current deliverable near 2 of 5 mutants, not the 1 of 5 recorded earlier for the erratum sentence alone.

Diagram label defect re-confirmed independently at rfc8555.txt:1701-1702.
REQUIRED EDIT APPLIED, ba48baf, merged. AND THE HONEST RESULT IS THAT IT DOES NOT MAKE THE COLLAPSE FAIL.

MEASURED, Applicants = {a1, a2}, Patience = 2:

  collapse                      nine: rc 0, 16 distinct, depth 5   probe: rc 0, holds
  error-without-query mutant    nine: rc 0, 25 distinct            probe: rc 0, holds
  faithful reading              nine: rc 12, R1 violated           probe: rc 12, refuted

So a collapse learner still produces all three artifacts and nothing rejects them.

THE AGENT'S REASONING, AND CENTRAL ACCEPTS IT. No model both satisfies the nine and refutes the probe. So demanding a refutation would make the problem unsolvable and would say so out loud. What the edit actually buys is that the collapse learner's own submission now has to carry the sentence 'my office never goes back', which the nine could not produce. That converts a SILENT wrong answer into a STATED wrong answer, and that is as far as a non-leaking statement reaches.

CORRECTION TO CENTRAL'S EARLIER CLAIM, including what central told Frank. The second deliverable is not the fix. It is a disclosure requirement. The grader, not the statement, is what can reject a collapsed model, and that is now a step 6 or step 8 question rather than a solved one.

THE AGENT IMPROVED THE WORDING AND WAS RIGHT TO. It dropped 'a formula you expect TLC to refute', because that phrasing tells the learner rule 3's side wins and the spike leaves the resolution to them. The shipped wording asks for a formula that is false the moment the office goes back to a man it has already put an entry against, declared as an INVARIANT, run on its own, with a line on which way TLC called it. Either answer is a fact about the model.

ROUTE CHOSEN: NO TRACES, and route 2 was rejected with a reason. Marking the loop-turning run allowed says requirement 1 is the one to drop; marking the collapse forbidden says the collapse is wrong. Both halves leak. authoring/seedlib/statement/PROBLEM.md ships without traces so this is in convention. Removed the traces bullet, task step 5, the whole traces section, and 'The pairs in traces are the check'.

requirement-01.md CONFIRMED UNAUTHORABLE, measured rather than argued. The allowed run built from rules 2 to 5 and replayed one row per state violates requirement 1 at State 3, the row inspecting / 1 / FALSE, rc 12.

THE FINDING FOR STEP 6, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. The probe's PIN decides whether it works. Pinned to a second entry on the list, which was the reviewer's 'goes back twice' phrasing, the error-without-query mutant refutes it at rc 12 WHILE satisfying all nine at rc 0 with the loop never turning. So that pin would pass a wrong model. Pinned to the REVISIT instead, it holds on the collapse and on that mutant and is refuted only on the faithful reading. Do not reword the probe without re-running both.

1. THE ISSUE'S OWN PROPOSED FIX IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. The spike found this and the brief did not ask for it. With the revision comparison in place, RolloutNoRestart.tla still goes red in 8 states at depth 3 on a single commit, because an app whose step has already passed is stranded permanently. The missing half is whether a new commit restarts the rollout, which the source never says. The spike chose restart and thinks it is the only coherent reading.

2. THE STATEMENT AUTHOR FLAGGED ITSELF. Its rule 7 lets the clerk read which amendment is current among her own records. Faithful to the source, and the problem is unsolvable without it, but one step from the fix. Step 5 should judge whether that is leakage.

3. BOTH AUTHORS LEFT THE SAME FORK OPEN AND NEITHER CLOSED IT. Whether a status refresh can land mid-cohort or only between cohorts. The spike let it land mid-cohort, which is what makes the inversion reachable, with NoMidCohortRefresh as the witness. The statement left it to the reader with a warning that tightening the clerk's round shrinks the checked system. The statement author said that warning is the only thing stopping a reader closing the fork the degenerate way and asked for a reviewer's judgment on it. Give it one.

MEASURED. 5 variables, 37 distinct states, depth 11, 0.3s, rc 0 on the fixed model. Inversion at 9 states depth 4, divergence at 21 states depth 5, both with traces. 16 vacuity probes all refuted, plus four controls because sixteen rc 12s is also what a channel stuck at 12 looks like. The discriminating control is one constant apart and splits red on broken, green on fixed.

THE MUTANT RESULT THAT JUSTIFIES THE GATE. Three domain invariants caught 6 of 7. Adding TypeOK caught 7 of 7. The missed mutant still rolls in cohort order and leaves nobody behind, so only the type invariant notices target leaving its range. The spike author's own words: it would have cut TypeOK as boilerplate without that run.

A SECOND COMPLETION ROUTE NOBODY MODELLED. Apps confirmed unchanged. Every commit in the spike touches every cohort. The spike suspects that route is where PR 29418's SpecsEquivalent work went and that it is the harder half of the real fix. Worth a look before the freeze.

MEASUREMENT BUG FOUND HERE. spike-measure.sh read 36 variables for 5 declared, because strip removes line comments but leaves block comments and tally then matches English. Isolated with a two-module probe reading 8 against 2. Filed as tla-83lg, P1. This is a SECOND hole beside the fencing spike's over-count, which three agents independently confirm is fixed on this build.
STEP 5 COMPLETE. Verdict NOT SUFFICIENT, one blocking change. Report at authoring/progressive-sync-stale-status/reports/step5-consistency.md.

THE BLOCKING DEFECT, AND IT IS IN RULE 4 RATHER THAN RULE 7. PROBLEM.md:104 says a box pastes the amendment in and stops being under issue, 'a step of the box's, not of hers'. PROBLEM.md:130 then lets her read that set freely. So underIssue drops exactly when a box finishes, and the clerk's stale board is not needed to decide anything.

MEASURED. A model with NO BOARD AND NO CLERK, whose guard reads only underIssue and her issued set, goes green on all seven requirements at rc 0, 14 distinct states, depth 11. It also passes the statement's own 'head office never issues' check, EverIssues at rc 13. So a learner can finish this problem without ever meeting the stale board, which is the entire mechanism.

THE FIX: leaving underIssue must be HER act on board evidence, which is what PR 29418 actually guards.

CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER NOTE ON THIS BEAD, AND TO WHAT CENTRAL TOLD FRANK. The leak is rule 4, not rule 7. The statement author flagged rule 7 and asked for review, and the reviewer cleared it: rule 7 names an operand and not the comparison, and the open-choices section withholds the half the defect lives in.

THE SPIKE'S OWN CLAIM IS REFUTED BY ITS OWN TRACE. sources/spikes/progressive-sync-stale-status/REPORT.md:157 says the mid-cohort refresh choice is what makes the inversion reachable at all. MCBrokenInversion contains NO Refresh step. The stale verdict comes from Init. So that choice is not load-bearing for reachability, and the statement is safe for the same reason, rule 8's opening board.

Q1 REPRODUCED EXACTLY and strengthened. rc 12, 8 distinct, depth 3, NoStrandedApp, same trace. One correction: RolloutNoRestart.tla:41 claims one difference from the base but Init differs too, step = 1 against Rollout.tla:74's step = Idle. Under the faithful Idle init, no-restart is red at depth 2 with 2 states, so the conclusion holds a fortiori.

THE SOURCE DOES ANSWER THE RESTART QUESTION, in the PR rather than the issue. PR 29418 carries 'if revisionsChanged || specChanged', resetting each app to Waiting. The spike called this unanswerable from the source and it is answerable. Do not adopt a two-commit statement change: rule 6 already forces the amendment onto the board line, so the fix's shape is forced even at one amendment.

SECOND COMPLETION ROUTE: not needed before freeze. Requirement 1 plus rule 3 already close it. But SpecsEquivalent IS in PR 29418 and its tests show the unchanged route leaving apps permanently stuck in Waiting, which corroborates necessary-not-sufficient from the source itself.

TWO MORE DEFECTS FOUND. The statement's checking .cfg DOES NOT PARSE: a sequence of sets is rejected at rc 255, 'expecting = or <-' at line 5. Its own fallback works. This was one of the two claims the statement author hedged as unverified, and it is wrong. And NoStrandedApp's 'target < MaxRev' arm leaves it toothless below the top revision.

Q4. Checking should quote a counterexample-depth band of 3 to 6 steps for a wrong first attempt and an order of magnitude rather than a state count, add the missing completion probe, and require a red run. Requirement 7's new wording DOES fix the vacuity, verified: under lazy fairness Req7 is rc 13 violated while Req7Original is rc 0 no error.
REQUIRED EDIT APPLIED, 66c0e1b, merged. AND THE PROSE EDIT ALONE DOES NOT SHUT THE DOOR. Read this before trusting the fix.

Rule 4 now has a second paragraph: 'A box leaves under issue one way only. She reads that box's line on the board, takes the line as good enough, and closes the issue off. That's a step of hers, and the board is the whole of what she goes on. What makes a line good enough is yours to settle, along with what the line carries.'

THE CORRECTION, measured. The step 5 reviewer's exact boardless model, where underIssue drops on the paste step, is STILL rc 0, 14 distinct, depth 11 after the edit, BECAUSE NO REQUIREMENT MENTIONS THE BOARD. The prose changed and the requirement set did not, so the requirement set still cannot see the difference.

What DOES go red is the boardless model that OBEYS amended rule 4: Req1 rc 12 at depth 6, Req5 rc 13 at depth 6. The original paste-drops model is caught instead by the SATISFYING TRACE, rc 0 at row 5.

So both doors are shut, by two different instruments. A reader who obeys the amended rules is caught by the requirements. A reader who ignores them is caught by the traces. That is the tla-n8oq amendment holding up: the trace is the instrument, not the requirement.

NINE TRACES, each forbidden run replayed against the reference, rc 0 meaning refused:

  req1 0/4   req2 0/3   req3 0/4   req4 0/9   req5 0/2   req6 0/8
  req7 rc 12/10 BY DESIGN, since the forbidden thing is the infinite stall and every row is legal
  full-circulation.md replays rc 12, depth 17

Source mutants each named by their own requirement: rc 12/d6, 13/d4, 12/d5, 12/d10, 13/d3, 13/d8, 13/d17.

THE .cfg IS FIXED AND CENTRAL'S DIAGNOSIS WAS SLIGHTLY WRONG. The failure is SEQUENCES, not sets-of-sets: a sequence of naturals fails identically with rc 255 ConfigFileException 'expecting = or <-'. New shape uses two set constants with Districts in the module. Reference run rc 0, 24 distinct, depth 17. EverIssues rc 13, completion probe rc 12.

FOUR THINGS REPORTED NOT FIXED, all outside footprint or judgment calls for Frank:
1. Rule 7's 'the one thing in the region left to you' is now TWO guards after this edit, so that phrase is stale.
2. Rule 9 and the fairness section still say 'a box under issue has to paste', while rule 3 enables pasting off issued.
3. Requirement 4 cannot catch a cap applied to every district on this instance.
4. Trace provenance wants an author-notes/ file, outside footprint. NoStrandedApp's target < MaxRev arm left alone.
