title: Stage 1 §4 — author the refinement chapter
description:
Goal: a chapter teaching refinement in TLA+, pitched as a direct continuation of learntla.com's
core section — same register, same assumed background, same voice. learntla's own
topics/refinement is a STUB (its topics index says outright "Most of the topics haven't been
written yet"), so this fills a hole the upstream site advertises.

THESIS (§4.1 — Frank's, and it is well supported): refinement is the technique that makes
modeling large and complex systems tractable, not a formalism to be admired. Supporting
evidence to use:
  - Lamport & Merz, Prophecy Made Simple §5: rather than adding prophecy variables to Afek's
    snapshot algorithm they INVENT AN INTERMEDIATE SPEC, so one link needs only history
    variables and the other needs prophecy on a simple spec. Their justification: "the
    specification of what an algorithm is supposed to do is generally much simpler than the
    algorithm."
  - ewd998/EWD998ChanID.cfg chains three instance hops (EWD998Chan!EWD998!TD!Live) —
    transitivity as practiced.
  - Properties proved of the abstract transfer to the concrete for free.
HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT, must be included: Lamport (SS §10.9) says that when writing from scratch a
monolithic spec is usually easier to understand. The chapter says refinement earns its keep when
the system exceeds what you can hold in one spec — NOT that it is always better.

DO NOT RE-TEACH (§4.2). Core ch.13 already teaches INSTANCE, INSTANCE..WITH, constant and
variable substitution, EXTENDS vs INSTANCE, partial parameterization. Core ch.12 teaches vars,
Init, Next, actions, primed variables, UNCHANGED, Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars, stuttering via
[A]_v, ENABLED, and formal WF/SF — but to READING depth, as a bridge from PlusCal. The gap is
narrow: the IDEA that a concrete spec implements an abstract one, refinement mappings, and the
Spec => Abstract!Spec check.

CUT LIST §4.3 — dense notation, easy idea:
  \EE / ∃∃ (Lamport calls it the stone in the soup; neither TLC nor TLAPS handles it — present
  once for meaning, never for use) · the LM!Inner(omem, octl, obuf)!ISpec chains from SS §5.8 ·
  the overbar F̄ (it means "substitute"; say "substitute") · parametrized instantiation
  Inner(q) == INSTANCE InnerFIFO (Lamport himself: "If this seems confusing, don't worry about
  it") · Prophecy.tla's general machinery (ProphAction, ProphCondition, DomInj, PredDom) — use
  PMS §4.2's three-line recipe instead · Abadi & Lamport's Σ,F,N,L tuples and structured proofs.

SLOW-DOWN LIST §4.4 — genuinely hard, all nine:
  1. Stuttering as CONSTITUTIVE, not permissive. A spec describes part of a world; that alone
     forces [...]_vars. Refinement then gets stuttering for free.
  2. THE VACUITY HOLE — make this the CENTREPIECE of the stuttering section, not a footnote.
     [][ANext]_(mapped) unfolds to ANext \/ UNCHANGED(mapped), so a frozen mapping makes the
     right disjunct true at every step and ANext is never evaluated once. Verified: a concrete
     spec with three interleaving actions and 27 distinct states passes at rc=0. Stuttering is
     both the load-bearing beam and the trapdoor.
  3. The vars-substitution consequence — the abstract's stuttering subscript is itself rewritten
     by the mapping, determining which concrete steps are invisible. Almost never stated.
  4. Why refinement mappings can FAIL TO EXIST — Abadi & Lamport's three counterexamples.
  5. Prophecy variables. Unlock: PMS §4.3 — "a specification is not a rule for generating
     behaviors. It's a predicate on behaviors." Get that sentence in EARLY.
  6. The non-constraining obligation — an equivalence, not an implication. History variables get
     it free (syntactic); prophecy variables must earn it.
  7. ENABLED not distributing over substitution — what makes liveness refinement hard.
  8. Machine closure, and prophecy's interaction with it.
  9. "Refinement is a claim about THREE things, not two." From Hiding §5: for ANY two specs,
     adding suitable auxiliary variables makes a mapping exist, so "X refines Y" is a fact about
     X, Y, AND THE MAPPING. PUT THIS NEAR THE BEGINNING, not the last page.

OPEN DETAIL TO SETTLE FIRST (§2.3): total length, and whether this ships as one document or as
chapter + separate worked example. Everything else in §2.3 is approved.

Brief: V2-PLAN.md §9.1 — copy-paste it.

Files: chapter/refinement.md, chapter/snippets/

Steps:
  1. Settle the §2.3 length/format detail with Frank.
  2. Dispatch the §9.1 author brief to an isolated agent.
  3. Every TLA+ snippet lands in chapter/snippets/ as a runnable .tla + .cfg pair — execution is
     verified by the sibling bead, but this bead must make them runnable in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: chapter/refinement.md exists; covers all 9 §4.4 slow-down items and none of the §4.3 cut list; every snippet has a runnable pair in chapter/snippets/.
close_reason: chapter/refinement.md (5477 words) + chapter/worked-example.md + 26 runnable snippet pairs, merged to main; plan corrections in commit 8f6da6a. All 26 snippets execute green on TLC 2026.03.04.183147 via chapter/snippets/run-all.sh. All nine section 4.4 slow-down items placed, with the two mandated positions honored: 'a claim about three things' is section 3, and the vacuity hole is the spine of both documents. Every quotation traced to a clone or a local pdftotext extraction, none from WebFetch. title: Stage 1 §4.5 — verify the refinement chapter: execute every snippet, trace every quotation
description:
Goal: adversarial verification pass over chapter/refinement.md.

§4.5 makes this NON-NEGOTIABLE: every TLA+ snippet must be EXECUTED before it ships. A

title: [epic] v2 implementation: refinement chapter, harness, pilot, tutor directory, batched production
description:
Implementation epic for the v2 rebuild. Spawned from V2-PLAN.md (bead tla-qpm) on 2026-08-06.

V2-PLAN.md is the execution plan and the source of truth for every child here; each child cites
its section. READ V2-PLAN.md §1 AND §3 BEFORE WORKING ANY CHILD — §3 is a list of decisions that
are CLOSED, and reopening one wastes a session and usually re-derives a worse answer, because
most were settled against measured evidence rather than intuition.

Six stages, ordered by dependency:

  Stage 1  §4   refinement chapter        no deps — start now
  Stage 2  §5   harness, 8 components     no deps — start now, parallel with Stage 1
  Stage 3  §6   pilot problem end-to-end  needs Stage 2
  Stage 4  §6b  tutor directory           needs Stage 2 + Stage 3
  Stage 5  §7   batched production        needs Stage 3 + Stage 4
  Stage 6  §8   assembly                  needs Stage 5

Copy-pasteable subagent briefs for every unit are in V2-PLAN.md §9.

WHY SUBAGENTS SPECIFICALLY — isolation is load-bearing, not just parallelism (§0):
  - a BLIND SOLVER is only a valid instrument if it genuinely has not seen the reference; a
    fresh agent with a minimal brief guarantees that and a same-context continuation cannot
  - the COMMENT PASS must not be able to reshape the spec it is annotating
  - the LEAKAGE CHECK must be adversarial against a statement its author is attached to
Treat "spawn a fresh agent" as the enforcement mechanism for these gates. Never shortcut one by
doing the work inline.

LAYOUT settled 2026-08-06: harness/ and chapter/ are NEW top-level dirs in this repo. v1's
puzzles/ and scripts/ are untouched. tla-practice/ and tla-answers/ (§6b.2) split off as
SEPARATE repos at Stage 4 — that separation is a leak defense, not a preference.

Stages 5 and 6 are filed COARSE on purpose. Batch 1's learner telemetry is expected to reshape
them (§7.1), so they get decomposed when the pilot lands, not now.

title: v2 rebuild: consolidate design, author refinement chapter, build harness, then spawn implementation epic
description:
v1's programmed-text microlesson curriculum failed: test questions were trivial or near-copies of the lesson example; lessons were sometimes vacuous or wrong. Post-mortem concluded the failure was STRUCTURAL, not execution — the "exactly one new concept" + minimal-novelty quality gate mechanically produces near-copies. See drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_78e0afcd8f0f7bb925f61ef0.

v2 replaces the content (not the infrastructure): learntla.com core assumed as read, ~40-60 original modeling problems at 20-40 min each, ~25 of 60 in pure TLA+ back-loaded.

DESIGN IS CAPTURED IN THREE DRAWERS (tla_puzzles/decisions):
  78e0afcd8f0f7bb925f61ef0 — v1 post-mortem
  d6fc1f6386188c44b58278b8 — problem-set contract, production pipeline, exclusion regime
  be8cc4b03efbea276e444a12 — mechanical grading architecture + TLC harness constraints

Design is informed by a four-sweep research pass (2026-08-05): existing TLA+ exercise sets, Lamport refinement extraction, formal-methods pedagogy, and empirically-verified TLC/Apalache tooling capability.

NOT YET DONE — this bead tracks the remaining design-to-build transition:
  - assemble the three drawers into one consolidated design document for human review
  - decide the final problem count and the modeling-situation taxonomy
  - author the refinement chapter (learntla's topics/refinement is a stub; Specifying Systems ch.10-11 rewritten in learntla's register). Cut/slow-down outline is in the refinement research notes.
  - build the harness (vacuity probes, conjunct-wise grading, blind-solve loop, comment-pass gate)
  - THEN spawn the implementation epic via create-beads

KEY CONSTRAINTS not to relitigate:
  - coverage is an end-of-run AUDIT, never the problem-list generator
  - statement fixes the SYSTEM, leaves the REPRESENTATION open, names an observation operator
  - interleave by idiom; never consecutive problems of one kind (d=0.83)
  - reference-comparison grading is invalid (oracle is #1 for only 33% of exercises)
  - mechanical layer decides pass/fail; LLM judge explains only, never overrides
  - comments added in a SEPARATE post-freeze pass, enforced by strip-and-diff
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated v2 design document exists and is human-reviewed; the refinement chapter is drafted; the verification harness runs end-to-end on one pilot problem; an implementation epic is filed.
notes:
NEW SCREEN ADDED 2026-08-06: §5.7b, the puzzle-versus-system screen. It is INDEPENDENT of the §5.7 mechanism-collision screen — §5.7 asks 'has someone already solved this?', §5.7b asks 'is it even the right kind of thing?' A candidate can pass §5.7 cleanly and still be useless.

THE SCREEN: if you hand the learner the legal moves, is there anything left to model? If no, it is a puzzle — cut it, or add agents and failure until it isn't.

WHY IT MATTERS: every puzzle in tlaplus/Examples (Die Hard, Hanoi, N-Queens, missionaries, sliding block) is flagged Beginner — not because they are small but because the modeling was pre-done by whoever wrote the rules. 'Puzzles where the state space is handed to you and the work is search' is the first of the four categories the corpus survey found the entire public corpus consists of, and it is the category this project is defined against.

IMPORTANT NUANCE: local representation choices do NOT rescue a puzzle. Change-ringing genuinely offers some (bells->positions vs positions->bells; explicit visited-row history vs exploiting TLC's own dedup, since a repeated row IS a repeated state). Those are real and interesting, but they are local — about transcribing a given action set tidily, not about deciding what the actions are. Good taste, not modeling judgment.

RESCUE PATTERN: add agents and fallibility, which converts search into specification. Change-ringing as a puzzle is 'find a Hamiltonian path through the Cayley graph of S_n'. As a system it is 'model a band of fallible ringers; does their behaviour refine the method they are attempting?' — which lands in column F.

THE SCREEN HAS TEETH BEYOND CHANGE-RINGING: restaurant seating FAILS as 'seat this party optimally' (bin-packing) and PASSES as 'model the host stand with walk-ins and reservations arriving concurrently'. Same domain, different statement. So the screen is applied at STATEMENT time (§6 step 4, brief §9.6) as well as at domain-selection time — passing once does not immunize a domain.
EPIC FILED 2026-08-06: tla-kl5 (22 children) is the implementation epic this bead's fourth acceptance criterion called for. Stage 1 = tla-kl5.1/.2 (chapter); Stage 2 = tla-kl5.3-.10 (harness); Stage 3 = tla-kl5.11 (pilot); Stage 4 = tla-kl5.12-.15 (tutor directory); Stage 5 = tla-kl5.16/.17 (batch 1 + holdout); Stage 6 = tla-kl5.18-.21 (assembly); tla-kl5.22 = the §11 research gaps. Layout settled at filing time: harness/ and chapter/ are NEW top-level dirs in this repo; tla-practice/ and tla-answers/ split off as separate repos at Stage 4. tla-syn (verify-puzzle.sh rc rewire) now depends on tla-kl5.4, which owns the canonical rc table. Stages 5-6 are deliberately coarse — batch 1 telemetry is expected to reshape them per §7.1.
close_reason: Retired 2026-09-05 by PRACTICE-PLAN.md, unfixed. It describes machinery the project dropped: the grader, the vacuity and seeded-bug harnesses, the screens, the observation interface, the load vector and ramp rule, the shape taxonomy, the blind panel, or a defect in the seven delivered problems which stand unreworked by Frank's decision. Not wrong, just no longer load-bearing. V2-PLAN.md keeps the reasoning.

Gate 3 sharpened text:
Strip the new concept from the puzzle's task. What remains must contain at least one non-trivial prior concept the learner must compose — not just 'assign a variable' or 'increment a counter'. If the residual task is trivial, the puzzle is demo-with-renames: revise it by composing the new concept with one or more prior concepts as scaffolding.

Gate 7 extension:
Add 'demo bareness' clause — the worked demo must teach only the new concept with the minimum state vars/processes/labels. Demo carries no scaffolding from prior concepts. Asymmetry is deliberate: bare demo, composed puzzle.

title: SUBSET binds tighter than .. and no reference page says so
description:
Found 2026-10-22 when Frank hit it mid-drill on sets/01-any-healthy-upstream
and neither he nor the hint system could place it. Recorded as bd memory
subset-binds-tighter-than-dotdot-so-parenthesize.

THE FACT, reproduced on a six-line fixture on TLC 2026.07.31.184830:

  {s \in SUBSET 1..3 : Cardinality(s) < 2}     Cannot cast
                                               tlc2.value.impl.SubsetValue to
                                               tlc2.value.impl.IntValue
  {s \in SUBSET (1..3) : Cardinality(s) < 2}   {{}, {1}, {2}, {3}}

SUBSET binds tighter than .. , so the bare form is (SUBSET 1) .. N. TLC takes
the powerset of 1, which TLA+ permits because every value is a set, and hands
that to an operator wanting an integer.

WHY IT IS WORTH A SECTION RATHER THAN A ROW. The error names a Java method and
a cast, so it reads like a tool bug. Nothing in it says the word precedence, and
the span that is wrong appears only as the LAST entry of the nested-expression
list, which is the deepest position and the one a reader scrolls past. Frank had
the full message in front of him and it did not land, which is the test of
whether a trap needs prose.

THE COVERAGE GAP, measured. core-language-docs/sets.md owns SUBSET and contains
zero matches for 'precedence' or 'binds tighter'. Across all eight reference
pages only core.md mentions precedence at all. The sets page's CASES manifest
has one SUBSET row, which is the powerset-as-a-state-space case rather than this.

AND THIS IS THE SECOND PRECEDENCE TRAP THIS PROJECT HAS BEEN BITTEN BY. The
first is in bd memory tlc-breaks-its-own-naturals-div-contract: -17 \div 5
parses as -(17 \div 5), and that memory cost three days of the repo believing
TLC broke the Naturals contract when the parser was the whole story. Its rule
was 'parenthesize every negative literal you hand to an infix operator'.

THE GENERAL RULE IS WIDER THAN EITHER INSTANCE: a PREFIX operator binds tighter
than an infix one, so parenthesize the infix expression you hand to a prefix
operator. SUBSET, UNION and DOMAIN are all prefix. I measured only SUBSET with
.. , so the wider rule is INFERRED from two instances plus the shape, and
whoever writes the section should measure the others rather than assert them.

NOT EXTRACTED: the precedence ranks. The \div finding pulled them out of
tla2sany/parser/Operators by disassembling, and a plain string scan of that
class does not yield them. Worth doing, because a section that states the ranks
is stronger than one that quotes two measurements.

Files: core-language-docs/sets.md, core-language-docs/snippets/sets/
Acceptance: the sets page carries a named section on prefix-versus-infix
precedence with both forms as real CASES rows, one failing and one passing, and
the UNION and DOMAIN cases are either measured or explicitly named as
unmeasured. If the ranks come out of the jar, the section states them.
notes:
THE RANKS ARE NOW EXTRACTED, 2026-10-22, so the 'NOT EXTRACTED' note above is
answered. Method: unzip tla2sany/parser/Operators.class out of the pinned jar,
'javap -p -c' it, and read each Operator(String,int,int,int,int) construction
out of the disassembly. 89 operators recovered. The jar's values are 10x the
book's, so the jar's 100 is the book's 10.

THE TWO ROWS THAT DECIDE THIS BEAD:

  ..        90-90     book  9-9
  SUBSET   100-130    book 10-13
  UNION    100-130
  DOMAIN   100-130

Higher binds tighter, so SUBSET beats .. and 'SUBSET 1..N' is '(SUBSET 1) .. N'.
The table and the reproduction agree, so the mechanism is settled rather than
inferred.

AND THE WIDER RULE IN THE BEAD ABOVE IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED for
UNION and DOMAIN: all three sit at 100-130, identically, so all three bind
tighter than .. and the section can state that without hedging.

THE CHART CORROBORATES THE PROJECT'S OWN \div MEMORY from a surface I
re-derived independently. tlc-breaks-its-own-naturals-div-contract records
prefix minus at 12-12, \div at 13-13 and % at 10-11. The extraction reads
'-.' at 120-120, '\div' at 130-130 and '%' at 100-110. All three match.

A SECOND MEASURED FACT THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and it explains why Frank's
bug was SILENT. Precedence here is a PARTIAL order: a row is a RANGE, not a
rank, and two operators whose ranges OVERLAP have no defined relative order.
SANY refuses those outright:

  Amb == SUBSET {1, 2} \div 2
  ***Parse Error***
    Precedence conflict between ops SUBSET in block line 13, col 8 to line 13,
    col 13 of module Amb and \div.

SUBSET is 100-130 and \div is 130-130, so they overlap at 130 and the parse is
refused. SUBSET and .. do NOT overlap, 100-130 against 90-90, so that pairing
is decided and the parser applies it without a word. So the two cases split:
overlap gives a loud parse error, disjoint gives a silent reparse. The silent
one is the trap and it is the one worth a section.

The extractor is about 45 lines of python and lives only in this session's
transcript. Whether it belongs in scripts/ is a judgment I did not make
unasked, and the project has now needed this chart twice.

PUBLISHED SOURCES, for the page's citation: Lamport's 'Summary of TLA+' is the
canonical chart and prints ranges with '(a)' marking left-associative
operators. Specifying Systems p. 271 carries the same table. Lamport's parsing
tutorial states the partial-order framing and the rule of thumb that
numeric-valued operators bind tighter than set-valued, which bind tighter than
Boolean-valued.

title: refute.sh is unregistered with the indeterminate gate, so its four refusal paths are undriven
description:
Found 2026-10-22 by the full registry pass. harness/test-indeterminate.sh
exits 1 with:

  FAIL  UNREGISTERED instrument(s) can admit a skip - drive them from this
        suite, or fix them:
  harness/refute.sh

THE INSTRUMENT IS FROM EARLIER THE SAME DAY. harness/refute.sh runs a learner's
obligations against the wrong machines an item ships in verify/ and prints one
TLC exit code per pair. Its reach is 48 of 64 items. It has FOUR refusal

WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PAPERWORK. test-indeterminate.sh exists
because an instrument that exits 0 without saying what it did not verify is the
defect, and one that admits a skip silently is the same defect one step quieter.
The tla-gxsv author hit exactly this path tonight and read it correctly:
refute.sh exits 3 on drill/modules/01 because all three wrong neighbors refuse
before any state, so there is nothing for an obligation to run against. That is
a true report about a real item, and nothing asserts it stays true.

WHAT TO DO: drive all four refusal reasons from test-indeterminate.sh so each
one is observed rather than assumed, then add refute.sh to that suite's
registered list. The other instruments in that list are the model for the shape.

The three names in the same FAIL block are NOT findings. comment-gate.sh and
completion-gate.sh appear with their line numbers as context for what a
registered instrument looks like, and both are already registered.

AND ASK THE QUESTION THE SUITE IS ASKING. Which OTHER instrument added since
that list was last reviewed can admit a skip? refute.sh was added today and
went unregistered on the same day, which suggests the registration is not part
of whatever checklist an instrument author follows. If adding an instrument has
a written procedure, this belongs in it.

title: The 75/76 split is about which channel failed, not about timing, and three documents say otherwise
description:
Found 2026-10-22 by the tla-9y4s.6 author, which FALSIFIES a published page, a
manifest comment, and a claim a sibling page shipped the same night. Two
independent accounts were in circulation by the end of the run and both are
wrong.

THE TWO WRONG ACCOUNTS.

Account A, the one already published. core-language-docs/snippets/core/CASES:26-27
glosses 75 as the failure reached 'before TLC had a behavior to show' and 76 as
the one where 'TLC had a behavior to show', and core-language-docs/core.md:256-258
publishes that reason to the site.

Account B, shipped the same night by the tla-9y4s.5 author, is that the split
tracks TIMING: its eight 75s all failed while TLC worked on the initial state
and its four 76s all failed on a state reached by a step. It built a measured
pair on each side of that line and correctly marked TLC's rule as unsourced.
Over its own cases the generalization held.

BOTH ARE FALSIFIED BY TWO CASES IN core-language-docs/snippets/temporal/:

  Mainspring.cfg    rc 75 WITH a behavior, two states deep
                    (an incomplete next-state relation)
  MetronomeInv.cfg  rc 76 with NO behavior and NO state count
                    (an invariant rejected for its SHAPE before the first state)

So 75 can carry a behavior and 76 can carry none, which is the exact opposite
of account A in both directions, and account B's timing rule is wrong in both
directions too.

THE ACCOUNT THAT FITS ALL FOUR POINTS is cause, and harness/verdict.sh already
names it: 75 is the SPEC channel, 76 is the INVARIANT channel. verdict.sh:66-67
reads SPEC_EVAL_FAILURE and SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE, which is right and was right
all along. The two documents invented a timing story on top of a correct
cause-based table.

Nobody has sourced TLC's actual rule, and this bead should not invent a third
account. The cause reading is consistent with every measurement in hand and
with verdict.sh's own naming, which is enough to correct two documents and not
enough to call settled.

THIS COMPOSES WITH tla-x90i, which found 76's second meaning from the
state-space page: an action formula in the INVARIANT slot gets 76 as a static
rejection with no behavior. That is the same MetronomeInv shape found
independently, so two authors reached it from different families. x90i should
probably be worked with this bead rather than separately.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. A learner reading core.md is told the exit code
tells them whether a counterexample exists. It does not. What it tells them is
WHICH FORMULA failed to evaluate, and whether there is a behavior to look at is
a separate question answered by reading the log. Those are different debugging
moves.

Files: core-language-docs/core.md, core-language-docs/snippets/core/CASES, core-language-docs/snippets/sequences/CASES
Acceptance: all three documents state the cause-based reading, each citing the
Mainspring and MetronomeInv cases that refute the timing one. The sequences
manifest's timing comment is corrected rather than deleted, since its own four
cases are real and are now evidence for the cause account instead. None of the
three claims TLC's rule is sourced.

title: Three wrong claims in drill/INVENTORY.md about pc, the pure-TLA+ five, and two survey bases
description:
All three found 2026-10-22 by the tla-9y4s.8 author while building the PlusCal
reference page, each measured against a real pcal run. This is drill-channel
work: INVENTORY.md is the construct frame the whole drill corpus is aimed at.

DEFECT 1, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT WOULD MISLEAD SOMEBODY.
drill/INVENTORY.md:139 reads 'All three PlusCal references are single-label
uniprocess algorithms, so the translator elides pc entirely.'

The label count is not the cause. Measured with 'pcal Flume.tla' and
'pcal Trestle.tla', generated output now committed at

title: Exit 76 also means a static rejection, with no behavior to show
description:
Found 2026-10-22 by the tla-9y4s.7 author while building the state-space
reference page. Same shape as tla-ry2y's 151 finding, one code over.

THE DOCUMENTED MEANING. harness/verdict.sh:66 records

  76  SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE  the INVARIANT could not be evaluated

and core-language-docs/snippets/core/CASES:27 sharpens it to '76 evaluating an
invariant failed, AND TLC HAD A BEHAVIOR TO SHOW'. That second clause is what
distinguishes 76 from 75 in this project's own account, and the sequences page
independently measured the same split: its eight 75s all fail while TLC works
on the initial state and its four 76s all fail on a state reached by a step.

THE SECOND MEANING. An ACTION FORMULA in the INVARIANT slot also exits 76, with
no behavior and no state count:

  Error: The invariant NeverSkips is not a state predicate (one with no primes
  or temporal operators).

Reproduced at core-language-docs/snippets/state-space/ with
Semaphore.tla + SemaphoreSlot.cfg, which carries the 76 row and an empty state
field. That is a STATIC rejection before the first state is generated, so the
'had a behavior to show' clause is false for it and the 75/76 timing split does
not describe it either.

WHY THIS MATTERS THE SAME WAY 151 DID. A caller reading SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE
concludes the invariant blew up mid-evaluation and that nothing is known about
the spec. Here the spec is fine and the OBLIGATION IS MALFORMED, which is a
different thing to tell a learner and a different thing for a gate to act on.
A learner who wrote a temporal formula where a state predicate belongs needs to
hear that, not 'your invariant could not be evaluated'.

THE DECISION IS THE SAME ONE tla-ry2y SETTLED and the precedent is in the file.
verdict.sh now reads TLC's output for exactly one code, 151, under a scoped
exception documented at THE ONE STDOUT EXCEPTION in its header. The rule
recorded there is that a future row wanting the same treatment needs what 151
has: a measurement showing one code means two different things. This bead
supplies that measurement for 76. The structural gate in test-verdict.sh
counts matcher sites and requires each to be a permitted needle, so adding one
means widening that pair deliberately rather than by accident.

ALSO FIX THE TWO PROSE CLAIMS, since both are now false:
  harness/verdict.sh:66                         'the INVARIANT could not be evaluated'
  core-language-docs/snippets/core/CASES:27     'and TLC had a behavior to show'

AND ASK THE QUESTION OF THE WHOLE TABLE AGAIN. That is now 151, 76, plus 11, 75
and 76 having been absent from run-all.sh's comment block, which is five
findings against one exit-code table in two days. Every row was built from the
codes this project happened to run, so each is a claim about the corpus rather
than about TLC. Related: tla-v8ev, where harness/grade.sh and recall/recall.sh
carry their own copies of the same table.

title: The ch02 cheat-sheet correction cannot reach the practice tree, and 9 delivered copies are conflicts
description:
Found 2026-10-22 delivering tla-t1ka's two corrections. The ch10 one landed.
The ch02 one cannot, and the reason is structural rather than a bug.

WHAT HAPPENED. tla-t1ka corrected two cheat sheets. exercises/ch10/CHEATSHEET.md
delivers to exactly one place, ch11/cheatsheets/ch10.md, which had a recorded
digest, read STALE, and updated cleanly. Verified: the delivered card now
carries 'line takes an arity' and no longer carries 'do not combine'.

exercises/ch02/CHEATSHEET.md delivers to NINE places, ch03 through ch11, because
scripts/deliver-exercises.sh hands every earlier chapter's sheet to each chapter
as a lookup card. Every one of those nine differs from source with no recorded
delivery, so the script classifies them:

  CONFLICT, differs from source and has no record, so it may be your work

That classification is CORRECT behavior and must not be overridden. CLAUDE.md:
'A delivered file that differs from its recorded digest is Frank's own work, and
the only correct action is to leave it alone.' The 93 own-work files
verify-delivery reports under exercises/ include these nine.

SO THE REPO IS RIGHT AND FRANK'S COPIES STILL SAY THE FALSE THING. Measured:
/home/fkberthold/tla-practice/exercises/ch03/cheatsheets/ch02.md and
ch11/cheatsheets/ch02.md both still carry 'are the only operators that work
across types', and none of the nine carries the corrected text.

--adopt DOES NOT REACH THEM EITHER. Its own usage says it records a digest for
every delivered file 'that is byte-identical to its source'. These are not
byte-identical, which is exactly why they are conflicts, so --adopt skips them.

THIS IS FRANK'S CALL AND THAT IS WHY IT IS A BEAD RATHER THAN A FIX. Three
routes and the choice depends on something only he knows, namely whether those
nine files carry his own margin notes or are just old generated cards:

  1. If they are untouched old cards, a one-time --adopt widened to accept a
     delivered file matching ANY committed version of its source would let the
     delivery reach them, and that is a real improvement to the channel.
  2. If any carries his notes, the right move is to leave it and tell him which
     line is wrong, which this bead does.
  3. Diff each of the nine against every committed version of
     exercises/ch02/CHEATSHEET.md and split them into the two classes above.
     That is mechanical and is the recommendation, since it answers 1 against 2
     with evidence instead of asking him to remember.

WIDER SCOPE, not measured: verify-delivery calls deliver-exercises.sh for ONE
chapter, and the run printed only '--- exercises ch11'. Whether chapters 2
through 10 are also owed deliveries is unknown and worth one pass of
'scripts/deliver-exercises.sh --check N' for each.

Files: scripts/deliver-exercises.sh, scripts/verify-delivery.sh

untouched old card or Frank's own work, with the diff that decided it. Untouched

title: Nothing gates a claim in a cheat sheet, and three have now been found false by hand
description:
Scoped out of tla-t1ka deliberately, which fixed two lines and said this was
the bigger job underneath them.

THE GAP. 12 cheat sheets under exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md carry 105
'- Construct:' entries plus a Major themes section of prose claims about how
TLA+ and TLC behave. harness/test-spelling.sh reads these files for spelling
and scripts/lint reads their shell, and NOTHING checks a claim in any of them
against a run.

THREE FOUND FALSE BY HAND SO FAR, all within one week and all by somebody
looking at something else:

  exercises/ch10/CHEATSHEET.md:45  recursion and higher-order 'do not combine'
                                   (they do, RecHigher.cfg is rc 0 / 4 states)
  exercises/ch02/CHEATSHEET.md:99  '= and # are the only operators that work
                                   across types' (TLC aborts at rc 75)
  exercises/ch12  two accuracy gaps, filed separately as tla-8art

The first two were found by the tla-9y4s.2 author while sourcing a reference
page's Shape column from them. Nobody was auditing. That is the tell: a
surface with no gate gets corrected only when another piece of work happens to
cross it.

THE SHAPE THAT WORKS IS ALREADY IN THE REPO. core-language-docs pages have the
opposite property BY CONSTRUCTION: every tagged block is a real module under
core-language-docs/snippets/<family>/ with a CASES row asserting its exit code
and distinct-state count, and core-language-docs/snippets/run-all.sh discovers
the manifests rather than carrying a list. tla-t1ka's two fixes cite those
modules by name, so the measurements are gated. The CITATION is not.

SO THE QUESTION TO ASK OF THE CHAPTER CORPUS is CLAUDE.md's completeness rule
turned on the sheets: which claim in a cheat sheet would I expect a run to
contradict? Three for three says the answer is not none.

TWO THINGS TO DECIDE RATHER THAN ASSUME. Whether every claim needs a module,
which is 105 constructs plus prose and probably too much, or whether only
claims naming an exit code, a count or an impossibility do. And whether the
sheets should cite the reference pages instead of re-stating behavior, which
would move the gating problem to a link check and is much cheaper. The second
is the recommendation, since the reference tree exists now and did not when
the sheets were written.

NOTE THE DELIVERY CONSTRAINT. exercises/ is a delivered channel and
scripts/deliver-exercises.sh:123-125 renames each sheet to chNN.md under a
cheatsheets/ directory, delivering every earlier chapter's sheet as a lookup
card while holding back the current chapter's. 93 files under exercises/ are
Frank's own work that the delivery correctly leaves alone. Check which class a
sheet is in before any bulk edit, and never close a gap by editing the source
to match a delivered copy.

an impossibility is either backed by a gated module or rewritten to cite a
reference page, and a suite fails when the backing goes away. The decision
between those two routes is recorded before the work starts.

title: Two more copies of the exit-code table map 151 to CONFIG_ERROR alone
description:
Found 2026-10-22 while fixing tla-ry2y, which corrected harness/verdict.sh only.

THE EXIT-CODE TABLE EXISTS THREE TIMES IN THIS REPO and tla-ry2y fixed one of them:

  harness/verdict.sh:637   FIXED by tla-ry2y, now splits 151 three ways
  harness/grade.sh:632     151) echo CONFIG_ERROR
  recall/recall.sh:1814    151) printf 'CONFIG_ERROR\n'

So after tla-ry2y the canonical table disagrees with two live copies, which is
worse than the uniform bug it replaced. A reader checking either of the other
two now gets an answer the harness no longer gives.

WHAT 151 ACTUALLY MEANS, measured on TLC 2026.07.31.184830 against
harness/fixtures/verdict/InvariantFalse.tla, all three reproduced directly:

  INVARIANT NoSuchOperator  151  'The invariant NoSuchOperator specified in the configuration file'
  INVARIANT DiffSet         151  'The invariant of DiffSet is equal to FALSE'
  PROPERTY  DiffSet         151  'The property of DiffSet is equal to FALSE'

DiffSet is {1, 2} = {1, 2, 3}. An obligation mentioning no variable is folded
to a constant before any state is walked, so a FALSE one exits 151 with no
state and no trace.

WHY grade.sh IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. tla-ry2y's harm statement names a grader
deciding 'the configuration is broken, so this run established nothing' and
discarding a real refutation. grade.sh IS that grader. Whether its path can
actually receive a variable-free obligation is NOT yet measured, and measuring
it is most of this bead.

EXPOSURE, measured with a transitive scan over 1,425 cfg files resolving 2,693
obligations: variable-free bodies exist in the swipe corpus and the
reference-page snippets, some seeded FALSE on purpose. The first scan said 582
and was wrong, because it did not close the body's identifier set over the
module's own definitions, so an obligation reaching state through a defined
operator read as variable-free. Closed transitively the answer is far smaller.
Do not re-derive this with a flat grep.

AND ASK THE QUESTION OF THE WHOLE TABLE, not of this row. Every row was built
from the codes this project happened to run, so each is a claim about the
corpus rather than about TLC. Four findings landed against it in one day:
151's second and third meanings, plus 11, 75 and 76 turning up absent from

and .4 authors.

title: Two cheat sheets state what TLC contradicts, both measured twice
description:
Two shipped cheat sheets state things TLC contradicts. Found 2026-10-22 by the
tla-9y4s.2 author while sourcing the core reference page's Shape column from
them, and both re-verified independently in the main tree before the page
merged.

DEFECT 1. exercises/ch10/CHEATSHEET.md:45 reads:

  "Higher-order operators take another operator as a parameter, written Op(_),
  and LAMBDA builds a quick anonymous one instead of naming it separately. The
  two features do not combine, an operator cannot be both recursive and
  higher-order."

The last clause is false. Measured on TLC 2026.07.31.184830, module
core-language-docs/snippets/core/RecHigher.tla:

  RECURSIVE Walk(_, _)
  Walk(Op(_), k) == IF k = 0 THEN 0 ELSE Op(k) + Walk(Op, k - 1)

reads rc 0 with a state-dependent invariant holding over 4 distinct states.
Re-run in the main tree at 00:07 on 2026-10-22, rc 0, 4 distinct states.

What DOES fail is the higher-order marker inside the RECURSIVE declaration,
RECURSIVE Walk(_(_), _), which reads rc 150 with "Was expecting comma or )".
So the true statement is narrower than the sheet's: the declaration takes an
arity, not a shape, and the operator parameter is declared in the definition
rather than in the RECURSIVE line.

WORTH KEEPING ABOUT HOW THIS WAS MEASURED. The author's first run used a
constant-level invariant and read rc 0 having never evaluated Walk at all,
which would have been the same green for the wrong reason. It re-ran
state-dependent before believing it. That is the vacuity trap the core page
itself documents, met while documenting it.

DEFECT 2. exercises/ch02/CHEATSHEET.md:99 reads:

  "TLA+ is untyped, but the checker still recognizes primitive types like
  integers, strings, and booleans. = and # are the only operators that work
  across types, and most other operators need an EXTENDS line first."

TLC does not evaluate a cross-type equality at all. It aborts: 0 = "0" reads
rc 75 with "Attempted to check equality of integer 0 with non-integer".

CORROBORATED FROM A SURFACE THE AUTHOR NEVER READ. bd memory
tlc-2026-07-31-184830-cross-type-comparison already records that cross-type
comparison aborts rather than returning FALSE. So this is two independent
findings of one behavior, which is why it is worth acting on rather than
re-measuring.

The author also probed three type-invariant forms before writing it up, since
membership might have behaved differently from equality. box \in Int, box \in
0..3 and box \in {0, 1, 2, 3} all fail to evaluate at rc 76, and the
set-literal message names equality rather than membership. So \in inherits
what = cannot do.

The sheet's claim is about the LANGUAGE and the measurement is about TLC.
Specifying Systems does define = over all values, so the sheet may be right
about TLA+ and wrong about what the checker will run. Whoever fixes this
should decide which claim the sheet is making, since a learner meets the
checker rather than the semantics. Do not simply delete the line.

THE DEEPER FINDING, AND IT IS THE DAY'S PATTERN AGAIN. No gate reads a cheat
sheet. harness/test-spelling.sh covers exercises/ for spelling and
scripts/lint covers its shell, and nothing checks a claim in either sheet
against a run. The reference pages under tla-9y4s have the opposite property
by construction: every tagged block is a real module with a CASES row
asserting its exit code, which is exactly why this page's author found these
two and nobody had before.

So the question to ask of the chapter corpus is CLAUDE.md's completeness rule
turned on the sheets: which claim in a cheat sheet would I expect a run to
contradict? That is a bigger job than fixing two lines and is not this bead.

DELIVERY CONSEQUENCE. exercises/ is a delivered channel, and 93 files under it
are Frank's own work that the delivery correctly leaves alone. Check which
class CHEATSHEET.md is in before editing, and run scripts/verify-delivery.sh
afterwards. Never close a gap by editing the source to match a delivered copy.

Files: exercises/ch10/CHEATSHEET.md, exercises/ch02/CHEATSHEET.md
Acceptance: both lines say what the measurement says, each naming the exit
code and the module that produced it. The ch02 line states whether it is a
claim about TLA+ or about TLC. verify-delivery.sh is run afterwards and its
finding for exercises/ is either cleared or recorded as deliberate.

title: Derive the snippet runner's case list per page, so the seven reference pages can be authored in parallel
description:
Blocks parallel authoring of tla-9y4s.2 through .8. Found 2026-10-21 while
deciding whether those seven pages could be dispatched as one wave.

THE PROBLEM. core-language-docs/snippets/run-all.sh:35-46 holds a single
hardcoded CASES array, and every page under this epic adds its snippets to it.
Seven page authors would all edit the same twelve lines, so the wave is not
possible and the pages have to land one at a time.

Per loom's splitting heuristic two beads are wave-compatible only when their
Files: sets are disjoint. These seven are disjoint in everything except this
one file, which is what makes it worth fixing before they start rather than
after.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE. scripts/build-docs.sh:697 already
carries the lesson in its own comment: "THE PAGE LIST IS DERIVED, NEVER
WRITTEN ... a hand-kept list is right until somebody adds a chapter, and then
it is silently wrong with every gate still green." tla-llf5 is filed against
chapter/snippets/check-blocks.py for the same defect, where DOCS is a
two-element tuple. This is the same thing a third time, and here it costs
parallelism rather than correctness.

THE SHAPE TO BUILD. One directory per page under snippets/, each holding that
page's modules, its cfgs, and a CASES manifest in the five-field format the
array already uses:

  core-language-docs/snippets/<family>/CASES
  core-language-docs/snippets/<family>/<Module>.tla
  core-language-docs/snippets/<family>/<Module>.cfg

run-all.sh discovers */CASES rather than carrying any list, runs each case with
its own directory as cwd, and reports per family and in total. A page author
then owns one new directory and touches no shared file.

tla-9y4s.1's 21 files move to snippets/modules/ and its ten cases become
snippets/modules/CASES. The registry row in scripts/test keeps its path, since
run-all.sh does not move.

THE FLOOR MATTERS HERE. A glob that matches nothing must redden rather than
report zero cases and exit 0, which is the hole tla-d64i closed in
scripts/lint on the same day. Assert at least one CASES file and at least one
case inside each one.

KEEP THE FIFTH FIELD AND ITS COMMENT. The state-count field is not decoration:
two of the modules page's findings ARE counts, 16 states against 4, and both
runs exit 0, so an rc-only suite would stay green while the page went wrong.
That argument moves with the code.

core-language-docs/snippets/modules/ (21 files moved from snippets/)

and watch the full gate go red, as tla-d64i did for the flat version.

  pass 2, the possible? table     can do work on  8 of 64

temporal 8 of 8, sequences 5 of 8. So for 16 items, two of the four passes are
guaranteed empty before the model reads anything.

asks for exactly the honest summary: "say which of the four passes actually had
something to check", and it names the empty case outright, "a green run over an
item whose prompt publishes no count, carries no table and asks no question is
a run that checked one thing". Pass 4 also already knows the temporal family
ends in a question by design. The sheet is not wrong.

WHAT GOES WRONG ANYWAY. Applicability is discovered rather than given. The
model works pass 1, finds exit 2 and reports it. Works pass 2, finds no table
and reports that. Both arrive in the report as findings, and over nine runs
they arrive nine times, which is a third of the report spent on two facts about
the prompt that were true before the run started.

prompt to build the one-shot. Have it compute the two facts and state them in
the prompt header: whether the prompt publishes a count, and whether it carries
a possible? column. Then a pass with nothing to check is declared inapplicable
rather than worked and reported.

The checker's exit 2 already carries the first fact, and CLAUDE.md calls exit 2
"a common case rather than a failure". That is the same information arriving
after the pass instead of before it.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING AT ALL, given the sheet is already honest. The report is
what Frank reads, and a report whose first two items are "no count published"
and "no table" on an item that has neither reads as a run that found two
problems. Over nine runs that is the loudest thing in the output.

title: The drift threshold's own derivation is stale: the two test tiers now overlap
description:
Found 2026-10-21 while adding a registry row under bead tla-d64i, and not
fixed there because adjusting a drift detector's threshold is a different
decision from registering a suite.

THE CLAIM. scripts/test, in the margin paragraph above the registry, derives
the overrun threshold like this:

  Trip when BOTH hold:  elapsed >= 3.0x budget  AND  elapsed - budget >= 5 s

  The multiple is tied to the tier boundary itself. The fast tier tops out
  at 2.4 s and the slow tier floors at 10.2 s, so any suite that crosses
  from fast to slow does so by at least 4.2x comfortably above 3.0x. A
  3x threshold therefore catches every possible tier crossing by
  construction

THE MEASUREMENT. Read over the registry on 2026-10-21, taking the budget field
of every row:

  fast tier, highest budget:  12.0   harness/test-swipe-stemblind.sh
  slow tier, lowest budget:    8.9   harness/test-drill-check.sh

So the tiers overlap by 3.1 s rather than leaving a 4.2x gap. The derivation no
longer holds, and "catches every possible tier crossing by construction" is
false: a 9.0 s slow suite crossing to 12.0 s is 1.33x and trips nothing.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG. The 3.0x figure may still be the right threshold. It sits
above the 8% measured jitter and above the roughly 2x a contended box costs,
and both of those reasons are independent of the tier boundary. The 5 s
absolute floor is also untouched by this. What is broken is only the claim that
3.0x follows from the boundary, which is the paragraph's own argument for the
number.

WHY IT DRIFTED. Nothing gates it. The two figures are prose, the rows they
describe move every time a bead re-bases a budget, and the paragraph was
written when they were true. tla-7xql.7 re-based the swipe stem-blind gate to
12.0 in the fast tier and tla-9y5h re-based the drill study check to 8.9 in the
slow tier, and neither had any reason to read a comment thirteen hundred lines
up.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE IT, and I would take the first.

Re-derive the number from something that is measured rather than from the tier
boundary, say so in the paragraph, and leave 3.0x in place if the jitter and
contention figures still support it. Cheapest, and it makes the paragraph
honest about what the number rests on.

Or keep the boundary argument and gate it: assert at run time that the fast
tier's top budget times 3.0 is at most the slow tier's floor, and redden when a
re-based budget breaks it. That keeps a stronger invariant and it means the next
budget change has to decide about the tier gap rather than discover it later.

The tier assignment itself is not in question. tla-d64i's row went to slow at
3.2 s on the grounds that it starts a JVM, which is the distinction that
matters for whether --fast needs a toolchain, and that reasoning does not
depend on the boundary numbers either.

Files: scripts/test
Acceptance: the margin paragraph's numbers either match the registry or are no
longer load-bearing. If the gated route is taken, break a budget and watch the
new assertion fail before trusting it.
notes:
A CONCRETE ROW FOR THIS BEAD, measured 2026-10-22 on a verified-quiet box
across two full registry passes:

  drill corpus static sweep   6.4 s then 6.2 s   budget 3.0 s

That is 2.1x over and NOTHING COMPLAINS, because scripts/test's drift
threshold is 3.0x, which is the threshold this bead says was derived from a
tier gap the registry no longer has. So the row sits at twice its budget
indefinitely and the instrument designed to notice stays quiet.

WORTH KEEPING: THE 6.4 CAME FIRST. I added three assertions to that suite
tonight (tla-w8yu's part 0) and was about to attribute the overrun to myself.
The before-and-after readings say my change cost nothing measurable, 6.4 then
6.2, which is inside noise and if anything faster. The row was already 2x over
before I touched it. Checking the prior run rather than assuming is what caught
that, and it is the same discipline this project records for contaminated
timings.

Eight rows read over budget in that pass. Seven are sub-second to 1.4x and read
as noise at that scale, which scripts/test's own header already says a multiple
cannot resolve. This one is the outlier and the only one worth a number.

Full readings are in the session's fullgate output and the three rows tla-6ont
re-based are at a85aa32.

title: Generalize check-blocks.py: it traces two hardcoded chapters and no other tree
description:
The third gate that reads none of core-language-docs/, and the only one of the
three that needs more than a root-list line. tla-d64i closed the other two.

WHAT IT DOES TODAY. chapter/snippets/check-blocks.py, 317 lines, enforces three
things over the refinement and worked-example chapters:

  1. every tla-fenced block in the page traces to a module in the snippets dir,
  2. every module and cfg pair the page shows a transcript for is asserted in
     run-all.sh at the exit code the transcript prints,
  3. every cfg's own "Expected: rc=" header agrees with what run-all.sh
     asserts for it.

That is the right set of three. It is what makes a tagged fence an assertion
rather than a decoration, and it is why the chapter's code has not rotted.

TWO PROBLEMS, and the second one is not about the new tree at all.

PROBLEM 1. core-language-docs/modules.md ships 6 full modules as tagged blocks
and 21 files under core-language-docs/snippets/, and nothing re-checks that the
blocks still match the files. A one-off python check confirmed all 6
byte-identical on 2026-10-21, which is exactly the advisory state
gate-don't-advise rules out. Seven more pages land under tla-9y4s, each with
its own snippets.

PROBLEM 2, ON THE CHAPTER SIDE. The page list is hardcoded:

  DOCS = ("refinement.md", "worked-example.md")

So a third chapter goes untraced and this gate stays green. That is the same
hand-kept-list failure scripts/build-docs.sh was fixed for under bead tla-i3zu,
which now derives its chapter list from the tree and says so in a comment at
build-docs.sh:697: "THE PAGE LIST IS DERIVED, NEVER WRITTEN ... a hand-kept
list is right until somebody adds a chapter, and then it is silently wrong with
every gate still green." The build learned that lesson and the gate beside it
did not.

GENERALIZE, DO NOT COPY. Two copies of a 317-line tracer drift from the day the
second one is written, which is what three hand-copied smoke batteries did to
this project in 2026-08. Take the page directory and the snippets directory as
arguments, derive the page list from a glob of that directory rather than from a
tuple, and call it twice from scripts/test.

HERE forms CHAPTER from its own location today, so the snippets dir and the page
dir are assumed to be parent and child. Keep that as the default and let each be
given, since nothing says the next tree has to nest the same way.

RED, in two parts, and both should fail before either is fixed.

  1. Add a throwaway page under chapter/ carrying a tagged block that traces to
     no module. The current script passes. It must fail.
  2. Point the generalized script at core-language-docs/ and edit one line of
     one module out from under its block. It must fail.

title: The reference nav ships a Concept Index that 404s, and no gate reads a nav target
description:
Found 2026-10-21 while surveying what the site publishes as reference, for
tla-9y4s. Not reported by a reader, which is the point: nothing catches it.

THE SYMPTOM. The reference nav carries a "Concept Index" entry and its page is
not on the live site. https://fkberthold.github.io/tla-puzzles/reference/concepts/
returns HTTP 404. In the rendered sidebar the entry's link href is the raw
../../concepts.md rather than a resolved page URL, which is what mkdocs emits
when a nav entry names a file that does not exist.

THE CAUSE, scripts/build-docs.sh:71-74:

  # ---- concept index (built by separate Python script) ----
  if command -v python3 >/dev/null && [ -f /tmp/puzzle_concepts.json ]; then
    python3 scripts/build-concept-index.py >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi

Three things stack up. The page is built only when a cache file in /tmp happens
to exist, which CI never has. Output is sent to /dev/null. Failure is swallowed
with || true. Meanwhile the reference .pages at build-docs.sh:77-85 names
concepts.md in the nav unconditionally, so the nav entry ships whether the page
was built or not.

WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT. No suite asserts that a .pages nav target resolves.
harness/test-build-docs-chapter.sh, harness/test-build-docs-exercises.sh and
harness/test-build-docs-reading.sh all read .pages files and none of them checks
that the files named there exist. Measured: grep -rn 'nav:' harness/*.sh returns
nothing.

ONE MORE THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE FIXING IT. The page is v1 material. Its
builder reads bead labels from /tmp/puzzle_concepts.json and its own docstring
says it indexes "every concept tag with the puzzles that introduce or use it".
puzzles/ is v1 and out of scope for v2, so restoring the page may be the wrong
fix. Decide between restoring it with a real source and dropping the nav entry
before writing code.

THE FIX, in two parts, and the second is the durable one.

1. Rule on the page. Either give the builder a source that exists at build time
   and let the step fail loudly, or drop the nav entry and the script. A silent
   conditional build behind a /tmp cache is not a third option.
2. Gate the nav. Assert that every file named in every generated .pages exists
   in the built tree, derived from the .pages files rather than hardcoded. Watch
   it fail by removing one page before believing it. That assertion catches this
   class rather than this instance, and the class is "the nav promises a page
   the build did not make".

Files: scripts/build-docs.sh, scripts/build-concept-index.py, harness/test-build-docs-chapter.sh

"PlusCal-only syntax is 26 of 105 inventory constructs, and none is rated
high-frequency. Of the 31, five are pure TLA+ filed there deliberately. The 31

.claude/rules/tla-practice.md section 6 measures the consequence: 49 of the 59
translated modules have pc in their vars tuple, so every subscript covers it and
a partial subscript has to decide about it explicitly. Termination becomes
expressible over pc, and 29 of the 59 define Termination against 41 in the whole
corpus, so 71% of the corpus's Termination definitions sit in the 9% of modules
that are PlusCal.

Second named section: only 5 of 59 use a fair algorithm declaration, and all 59
commit the translated TLA+ rather than generating it at check time. Both are
facts about how to work with the tool, and neither is in any cheat sheet.

Third, and it is a boundary rather than a trap: the five pure-TLA+ constructs
filed under pluscal deliberately. Name them and say where their real home is, or
a reader looking for them on another page will not find them.

is indexed from ONE and DOMAIN over it gives an integer interval. Everything
about functions applies, including EXCEPT, and the functions-records page
carries that end of it. Readers coming from a zero-indexed language get this
wrong first.

Second named section: Seq(S) is the set of ALL finite sequences over S and is
infinite, so it is not a thing TLC can enumerate in a type invariant. That is a
real stopping failure rather than a style note, and the page should say what to
write instead.

THE BEAD WAS WRONG ABOUT Seq(S) AND THE PAGE SAYS SO RATHER THAN ADAPTING.
It claimed Seq(S) 'is not something TLC can enumerate in a type invariant'.
INVARIANT TypeOK where TypeOK == wire \in Seq(Colors) exits 0 over 7 distinct
states, because membership is a TEST and not a draw. What fails is a quantifier
over it (rc 75) or a draw from it in Init (rc 75, 0 states). Filed separately,
because module-docs/Sequences.md carries the same confusion.

FOUR FINDINGS BEYOND THE BEAD. A string is half a sequence: Len, Tail, SubSeq
and \o accept one and hand one back, while Head, Append, SelectSeq, indexing
and DOMAIN all stop the run, so a Len bound does not establish that a value is
a sequence. SubSeq checks its bounds only when the slice is non-empty, which
makes SubSeq(s, 1, Len(s) - 1) safe unguarded. Seq(S) is an opaque value rather
than a set. And the 75/76 split tracks TIMING rather than cause, built as a
measured pair on each side of the line rather than inferred, with the page

title: Settle the page format, and author the modules page as the exemplar
description:
Part of tla-9y4s, and it goes first because every other page inherits what it
settles. Read the epic for the shape ruling, the sources, and the two rules that
bind every page: never publish INVENTORY fields 8 or 9, and never author under
docs/ because it is generated and gitignored.

TWO DELIVERABLES. The page format, and the modules page as the exemplar.

THE FORMAT, modeled on module-docs/Integers.md, which already has the right
bones.

  1. H1 is the family as a reader would say it, not the inventory's slug.
  2. One or two lines on what the family is for.
  3. A table, one row per construct: construct, syntax shape, what it means,
     how common it is in published specs. The first two columns come from
     exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md, the fourth from INVENTORY field 6 and from
     .claude/rules/tla-practice.md where that file has a real count.
  4. Then one NAMED section per trap, in the style of Integers.md's "Negative
     operands". Prose, with a reproducible claim, not a bullet list.

The named trap sections are the whole value. A table of syntax shapes is what
the cheat sheets already are, and the cheat sheets did not save Frank an evening
on 2026-10-20.

ROWS THE MODULES PAGE OWNS, eight of them:

  K004 EXTENDS (module import)                               high
  K099 LOCAL (definition modifier)                           low
  K100 INSTANCE                                              medium
  K101 LOCAL INSTANCE                                        low
  K102 named instance                                        medium
  K103 ! (namespace lookup)                                  medium
  K104 INSTANCE ... WITH (<- constant substitution)          low
  K105 partial parameterization                              low

THE TRAP THIS PAGE MUST CARRY, and the reason the epic exists. Substituting a
VARIABLE through the same keyword has no inventory row, and it is the harder
half. Three measured facts to write up, all reproduced on TLC
2026.07.31.184830 on 2026-10-20:

  1. Every constant AND every variable the module declares must be substituted,
     explicitly or by a same-named one in the instantiating module. Missing one
     is a semantic error before any state is computed: "Substitution missing
     for symbol tank declared at ... and instantiated in module TwoTanks."
     Frank hit this and spent an evening on it.
  2. There is no way to name a parameter from outside. A module's VARIABLE is a
     formal parameter, so T1!tank does not exist and the eight "Unknown
     operator: tank" errors are downstream of the two missing substitutions.
  3. Substitution is on the parse tree, not on the text. With
     takings <- a + b, the operator takings' = takings + 1 becomes
     a' + b' = a + b + 1 and NOT a + b' = a + b + 1. Checked both ways as
     PROPERTY [][T!Ring <=> ByHand]_vars: the first is clean, the second
     reports "Action property is violated". A text macro would give the second.

Two further things worth a line each, both measured the same day. Pointing two
instances at the same variable gives two names for one state rather than two
objects, which is 4 distinct states and a violated cap where the pair gives 12.
And INSTANCE with no WITH, where the instantiating module has a superset of the
instantiated module's variables, is "my spec with the extra variables ignored".

CROSS-REFERENCE, not duplicate. chapter/refinement.md:223, "Substituting for
variables", already carries the rule and the error text. This page states the
rule and links there for the refinement treatment. tla-w8yu covers the routing
in the other direction.

present; the three measured facts each written as prose with the command and its
output recorded in this bead's close reason.

PROPERTY Text, rc 13, counterexample at the first step, a=1 b=0 after BumpA. Both outputs quoted verbatim on the page.

title: A TLA+ language reference on the site, one page per authoring family
description:
Frank asked for this on 2026-10-21, after fighting drill/modules/01: "it would
be really useful to have reference docs for each of the components of TLA+".
Shape ruled the same day: one page per authoring family, not one page per
construct.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, and none of it is this. docs/reference/ serves six
standard-library pages built from module-docs/ (Integers, Naturals, Sequences,
FiniteSets, TLC, Apalache) plus four curriculum-management documents. No page
covers a language construct. Nothing for EXCEPT, INSTANCE, CHOOSE, UNCHANGED,
ENABLED, the fairness operators, or any cfg keyword.

Searched before filing: module-docs/, the reference nav at
scripts/build-docs.sh:77-85, the tracker on "reference", "language reference",
"operator reference" and "module-docs", and the tla_puzzles decision wing.

WHAT IS ADJACENT AND IS NOT THIS.

  tla-9h1.5 "Operator to meaning card" is a mnemonic: three columns of glyph,
  English meaning and stock-image cue, feeding the method-of-loci protocol.
  Blocked behind tla-9h1.1 and lands under docs/appendix/pangram/.

  exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md gives a syntax shape and a learntla anchor per
  construct. That is a pointer rather than an explanation, and learntla is
  where the gap recorded on tla-w8yu came from.

  chapter/refinement.md is 816 lines of real reference covering one topic.

THE PRIOR RULING THIS DOES NOT CROSS. Exploration drawer
drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_781911016d78a8fc67d62269 records "Original gamble
rejected: one dense atypical artifact held as a passive look-up reference", and
the tla-9h1 design doc puts passive-reference memorization out of scope. That
ruling is about the MASTERY METHOD, on evidence that passive review does not
build production fluency. A reference consulted when stuck is a different job.
The case for it is tla-w8yu: Frank needed one page saying that INSTANCE ... WITH
substitutes variables, and no page in this project says it.

SHAPE, ruled by Frank 2026-10-21. One page per authoring family. Eight
families, 105 constructs, measured with
grep '^ROW' drill/INVENTORY.md | cut -f3 | sort | uniq -c :

  pluscal 31, temporal 20, core 16, functions-records 11, sets 9,
  state-space 8, modules 8, sequences 2

WHY NOT ONE PAGE PER CONSTRUCT. The family partition already exists in the
inventory and in the drill, so a reader lands on the page for the family they
are working in. Several constructs only mean anything together, and the two
fairness operators plus machine closure cannot be three pages. Ten pages is one
authoring wave where 105 is a program. The alternative was named and declined:
per-construct pages win if drill and reading items are to link individual
constructs, since an anchor into a long page is a worse link target than a page
of its own.

SOURCES, mostly written and mostly gated already.

  drill/INVENTORY.md             105 rows: id, family, construct, weight
  exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md    syntax shape and the learntla anchor
  .claude/rules/tla-practice.md  497 lines, 11 sections, how published specs
                                 actually use each family, measured over 666
                                 modules, with Specifying Systems page cites
  module-docs/*.md               the house format
  harness/ suites                measured TLC behavior and exit codes

The third is the one worth knowing about. scripts/build-docs.sh contains zero
references to .claude, so those 497 lines are invisible to every reader of the
site. Its section 5 already carries the cfg-keyword table: what VIEW, ALIAS,
SYMMETRY, CONSTRAINT and POSTCONDITION each do, with the column saying which of
them states a property, where the answer is none of them.

TWO HOLES IN THE SKELETON, so treat the inventory as the frame and not as the
authority on completeness.

  1. tla-aj8c records five constructs with no inventory row at all: CONSTRAINT,
     ACTION_CONSTRAINT, VIEW, ALIAS and TypeOK. The first four are what the
     state-space family is about. That bead now also carries a sixth case,
     K104's row name covering constant substitution only.
  2. sequences reads 2 rows, and the tla-9h1 exploration drawer says why:
     "Sequences appears NOWHERE in the authoring tree, so its weight of 2 is a
     fact about Frank's output rather than about TLA+." A sequences page sourced
     from the inventory alone inherits that error.

NEVER PUBLISH FIELDS 8 AND 9. drill/INVENTORY.md field 8 holds the drill item
slugs per construct and field 9 the reading item slugs, both generated. Publish
those and the site becomes a reverse index from construct into both corpora,
which is the leak the collapsed cheat-sheet block and scripts/deliver-
exercises.sh both exist to manage. Publish fields 2, 3, 4 and 6 plus authored
prose, nothing else.

WHERE IT LANDS. A new tracked source directory, language-docs/, mirroring
module-docs/, copied to docs/reference/language/ by scripts/build-docs.sh with
its own .pages. docs/ is gitignored and generated, so nothing is authored there.

GATE IT. language-docs/ is a new tree, and this project is three for three on
gates that report green having never read a new tree, recorded in
.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md under the gate-that-never-read-the-tree
hazard. So the last child adds language-docs/ to the roots of
harness/test-spelling.sh and scripts/lint with a per-root floor, and asserts
that every family named in INVENTORY.md field 3 has a page.

Files: language-docs/, scripts/build-docs.sh, harness/test-spelling.sh, scripts/lint
notes:
FORMAT SETTLED by tla-9y4s.1, landed a754f84. Every page .2 through .8 inherits this. Read language-docs/modules.md as the exemplar.

STRUCTURE. H1 naming the family as a reader says it. Two or three lines on what the family is for and what pays for using it. A line saying the page's modules are real files under language-docs/snippets/ with the TLC build and date. Then the construct table. Then one named section per trap. Then a Where this is taught section.

THE TABLE HAS FOUR COLUMNS: Construct, Shape, What it means, In published specs. Shape comes from exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md. The fourth column reports a figure from the 666-module survey where one exists and the literal words not counted where it does not. On the modules page that is 6 of 8 rows, and the line under the table says so rather than hiding it.

DO NOT PUBLISH THE INVENTORY WEIGHT. Field 6 is how often a construct should appear in the drill corpus, per INVENTORY.md:87. That is an authoring quantity and it answers a question no reader asked. It is also adjacent to the fields 8 and 9 ban. Use it to decide which traps are worth a section, never as a column.

CITE THE SURVEY BY WHAT IT READ, never by its path. .claude/rules/tla-practice.md is not published, so a path is a dead reference for a site reader. Write it as a survey of 666 modules and 337 configuration files from 16 public repositories, read 2026-09-05.

EVERY TLA BLOCK IS A REAL FILE. One per module, under language-docs/snippets/, with a cfg per claimed outcome, registered in language-docs/snippets/run-all.sh. The runner takes module, cfg, expected rc, expected distinct-state count, and a label. Leave the count field empty when the page quotes no count. The count field is not decoration: two of the modules page's findings are state counts where both runs exit 0, so an rc-only suite would stay green while the page went wrong.

CHECK MODULE NAMES AGAINST chapter/snippets/ FIRST. 15 modules already live there. The first draft of the modules page defined a third Till, and chapter/snippets/Till.tla and TwoTills.tla were already using the same a + b mapping for a refinement claim. Link the existing pair rather than competing with it. Taken names on 2026-10-21: Almanac EnabledInner EnabledSubst Late LateProph LateProphMC Ledger Localize MissingSub Observatory Oracle Running RunningH Till TwoTills, plus the 10 this epic has now added.

THE NAMED SECTIONS ARE THE VALUE and six is a workable number. Each one states the trap in its heading as a claim, shows the module, shows the real TLC output, then says in prose why it happens. Quote output verbatim. The first draft of the modules page compressed a violation trace into something that read like TLC output and was not, and that was caught by re-running it.

ONE PAGE MAY FIND TRAPS THE BEAD DID NOT NAME. The modules bead named three and the page carries six. Three came out of writing it: EXTENDS Sequences not supplying arithmetic, one EXTENDS line per module, and the bare INSTANCE superset case. Expect the same on the other families and do not treat the bead's list as the ceiling.
FIELD 6 CORRECTION, 2026-10-22. This epic contradicted itself and the
contradiction survived into a child bead.

The epic's DESCRIPTION reads 'Publish fields 2, 3, 4 and 6 plus authored
prose.' tla-9y4s.9's description repeats it as 'Fields 2, 3, 4 and 6 are
publishable.' The epic's NOTES read the opposite: 'DO NOT PUBLISH THE INVENTORY
WEIGHT. Field 6 is how often a construct should appear in the drill corpus, per
INVENTORY.md:87. That is an authoring quantity and it answers a question no
reader asked.'

So two descriptions against one note. THE NOTE IS RIGHT and is what the authors
followed. Every one of the eight pages publishes fields 2, 3 and 4 only, and
the index page's suite asserts the exclusion against the real field 8 and 9
slugs rather than against a column header.

Reasoning, for whoever reads the descriptions later: field 6 is an authoring
quantity. It says how often a construct SHOULD appear in the drill corpus,
which is a fact about the corpus's design rather than about TLA+. A reader
consulting a language reference has no use for it, and it sits adjacent to the
fields 8 and 9 ban. The PlusCal page is the case that proves the note's own
carve-out: it uses field 6 to STATE that no row in that family is weighted high
and that this is measured rather than an oversight, which is a statement about
the weights and not a weight column.

EPIC COMPLETE. .1 through .8 authored, .9 wired. 180 snippet cases over 8 family
manifests, all green. Both descriptions want editing to match the note.

title: drill/modules/01 asks for three breakages where the other seven ask for one
description:
Reported by Frank on 2026-10-20 mid-attempt, as "the table and questions feel
like they're being too clever, I'm having trouble following what they're talking
about". Measured against the other seven items in the family before filing, and
the measurement overturned half of central's first read. See MEASURED below.

THE PROMPT. drill/modules/01-two-tanks-one-hose/PROMPT.md carries a six-row
table. Three rows are working models and three are deliberate breakages, each
named by its symptom only. The closing line reads "Write it, reproduce the 12,
then break it all three ways."

MEASURED over all eight PROMPT.md in drill/modules, 2026-10-21:

  item  rows  breakages  questions  closing ask
  01     6       3          4       break it all three ways
  02     5       3          5       break the reading             (1)
  03     5       1          4       reproduce the 2 and refuse    (1)
  04     6       2          3       make the phantom ship         (1)
  05     4       1          4       take the marks off            (1)
  06     3       2          4       write the rule as an expr     (1)
  07     4       2          3       take that line off            (1)
  08     4       2          3       move the instance to the top  (1)

01 is the ONLY item that asks the reader to reproduce every breakage its table
shows. Seven of eight show one to three and ask for exactly one. 01 also ties 04
for the largest table and ties 02 for the most breakages, so it sits at the top
of both distributions while being the only one asking for all of them.

WHAT CENTRAL GOT WRONG FIRST, recorded so the next reader does not redo it.
Central told Frank the analysis-to-production ratio was the defect: three
analysis questions against one write question. The measurement says that ratio
is the family's house style. Seven of eight items have exactly one write
question followed by two to four analysis questions. The ratio is not the
anomaly. The closing ask is.

THE FIX, two parts, the second optional.

1. The closing line asks for ONE breakage, and row six is the one to keep. It is
   the failure a reader meets by accident, being what you get when you
   substitute the constants and forget the variable, which is exactly what Frank
   hit. Rows four and five stay in the table as published outcomes, which is the
   telegraph ruling's bin 3 at AUDIT-telegraph.md:21, and questions 2 and 3 are
   then answerable from the table rather than by reproduction.

2. The table gains a column saying what changed from row two, so each breakage
   reads as one delta rather than a full restatement. Rows four and five
   currently differ by one clause buried mid-sentence, "the pair writing its own
   behavior formula" against "the pair writing nothing of its own", and that
   clause carries the entire distinction between them. Additive, and it leaks
   nothing, because a delta names the configuration and not the cause.

WHY NOT SPLIT THE ITEM. Central's first proposal to Frank was to move rows four
to six and questions 2 and 3 to the reading rung. Dropped on the measurement
above: the analysis questions are the house style, the family has eight slots,
and a split would leave 01 shaped unlike its seven siblings for no reason the
measurement supports.

BUDGET EVIDENCE. META says 10 min thinking. Frank's working copy under
~/Study/tla-drills is stamped 19:13 to 22:18 on 2026-10-20 for a 25-line answer.
drill/README.md asks for a REACTIONS.md line past forty minutes, and that line
is written as of 2026-10-21.

CHECK BEFORE EDITING. harness/drill-gate.sh reads PROMPT.md and maps prose
phrases to the TLA+ tokens they stand for, around drill-gate.sh:1060, and bans
ALL-CAPS keywords in prompt prose at 307, 342 and 964. Any rewording has to stay
inside that, which is also why the table reads obliquely in the first place.
