title: A div tripwire that can never fire, and two headers that still say TLC is broken
description:
Follows tla-mv4b, which found that TLC does NOT break the Naturals.tla
contract on a negative dividend. The -3 everybody measured was operator
precedence: prefix minus is 12-12, \div is 13-13, % is 10-11, so -17 \div 5
parses as -(17 \div 5) while -17 % 5 parses as (-17) % 5. Parenthesized, the
identity holds and \div floors.

THREE SITES STILL CARRY THE FALSE ACCOUNT, and one of them is a dead gate.

1 harness/test-swipe-level0.sh:480 asserts

    ASSUME 5 * (-17 \div 5) + (-17 % 5) # -17

  in the UNPARENTHESIZED form, so it evaluates -12 # -17, which is true, so
  the suite passes. It was written as a tripwire that would redden the day
  TLC fixed \div. There is nothing to fix, so IT CAN NEVER FIRE. Its comment
  at 467-474 states the false account as the reason it exists. A gate that is
  green for a false reason is the shape this project keeps finding, and this
  one is worse than most because its whole purpose was to catch a change.

  What to put in its place is a decision rather than an edit. The honest
  tripwire for the REAL divergence is the negative DIVISOR, which is upstream
  tlaplus#721 and open since 2022: 5 % (-2) raises and 5 \div (-2) answers
  -3 where the module's own witness interval is empty. A tripwire on that
  would fire the day upstream closes 721. Or drop the tripwire and keep only
  the inventory. Say which and why.

2 swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv:95-119 carries the same account in its header,
  including the sentence that TLC is the authority the bake reads so an item
  on -17 \div 5 would ship TLC's answer as the truth and teach a falsehood.
  That reasoning was right for the wrong reason: an item written without
  parentheses teaches the reader a precedence trap while claiming to be about
  division. The constraint "NO ITEM MAY DEPEND ON \div WITH A NEGATIVE
  DIVIDEND" can relax to "parenthesize every negative literal", which is a
  better rule and covers ^ as well.

  Three authored items were replaced rather than re-labeled on the old
  reading. They do not need restoring, but whoever edits this header should
  say that the replacement was done on a premise that did not hold.

3 harness/test-div-contract.sh:108-110 names module-docs/ 2 and quotes
  Integers.md:16 as reading "truncates toward zero". Both are stale after
  tla-mv4b. It cannot redden on this, because module-docs is not in
  SCAN_ROOTS at line 78, which is worth noting in its own right.

  The 76-row inventory in harness/div-sites.tsv is still worth keeping. A
  \div site nobody has reviewed is still worth forcing somebody to read. Only
  its stated reason changes.

The bd memory tlc-breaks-its-own-naturals-div-contract is corrected already.

Files: harness/test-swipe-level0.sh, swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv,
harness/test-div-contract.sh
close_reason: Merged on main 2026-10-20, worker commit ea71799. The old tripwire asserted the identity in the unparenthesized form, evaluated -12 # -17, passed, and could never fire. It sits on the real divergence now, the negative DIVISOR, upstream tlaplus#721 open since 2022, so it fires the day upstream closes it. THE SHAPE OF THE % HALF IS THE FINDING AND THE BRIEF ONLY GUESSED AT IT: a raise and a plainly false assumption reach the channel as the SAME exit code, measured through harness/verdict.sh where ASSUME 5 % (-2) = 0 reads rc 10 and so does ASSUME 1 = 2. An equation form would have sat at rc 10 whatever upstream did, which is the dead tripwire rebuilt on a new operand. It is written as ASSUME 5 % (-2) \in Int, 10 today because the raise aborts it and 0 the day % answers any integer. Two modules rather than one, because the halves want opposite codes and one module's first evaluation error hides every assumption after it. Both watched failing with expectations set to 99 and each named the real rc. MODULE-DOCS STAYS OUT OF SCAN_ROOTS and the deciding reason is not the one the brief expected: read_inventory checks a reason is non-empty and never that it is true, so a row reading 'prose documenting the operator' is true and sits happily beside a page that had the arithmetic backwards, and widening the scan would buy a green run on a wrong page. Every uncovered root was censused by hand first, 58 occurrences across six roots each named with its count. THE BRIEF SAID THREE SITES AND THERE ARE NINE: five are outside the footprint and filed as tla-ei4c, including scripts/test's registry note which still describes the tripwire as asserting the identity is broken. Counts with no gate behind them rotted in two days: four of six NOT-A-ROOT counts had moved and the inventory census read 76 rows and 83 occurrences while the gate computed 80 and 87, re-measured at 89 and 96 with a paragraph naming which figures the gate computes and which are hand-counted. swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv heads its block PARENTHESIZE EVERY NEGATIVE LITERAL and says the three replaced items were replaced on a premise that did not hold; git diff -U0 matches zero non-comment lines so fields 6, 7 and 8 are untouched. title: Nothing gates a reporter running inside a subshell, and it has happened twice
description:
Recommended by the tla-yxjn worker on 2026-10-20, after it swept 151 tracked
shell files and found the shape live nowhere.

THE SHAPE. A suite's reporter function, the thing that calls nope or ok and
increments the tally, must not run inside a subshell. Two ways it gets there:

  M7=$(mutate ...)        a command substitution, which also turns the
                          FAIL text into the variable the caller wanted
  producer | reporter     a pipeline, where there is no variable at all and
                          the increment just vanishes

The first is loud eventually, because the caller uses the bad value and
something downstream dies on it. The second is silent: the assertion reports,
the tally does not move, and the suite exits 0.

IT HAS HAPPENED TWICE. harness/test-drill-runner.sh under tla-vo5l on
2026-10-16, and harness/test-recall-runner.sh under tla-w91v. The second was
worse, because its call sites read M1=$(mutate ...) || M1="", which cleared
the FAIL text along with the path.

WHY A GATE RATHER THAN THE COMMENT THAT IS THERE NOW. Both suites carry a
line saying "Keep them that way. A capture puts nope back in a subshell and
the guard goes quiet again." That is an advisory, and an advisory is exactly
what let the shape sit in a second file until a worker happened to be editing
it. The project's gate-don't-advise convention says a correctness invariant
that must simply be true gets a gate.

THE PRECEDENT IS harness/test-pipefail.sh, which is a tree-scanning gate for
a shell hazard of the same family, selects files BY SHEBANG rather than by
extension, and so covers files that do not exist yet. Build this one the same
way and read its header first.

WHAT THE SWEEP ALREADY WORKED OUT, so the gate does not have to rediscover
it. The reporter list is derivable from the tree rather than spelled:
assert_rc, assert_source, assert_verdict, control_absence_bites,
control_bytes_bite, generate, nope, note_error, run_gate, run_mutant,
structural_defects. 152 non-reporter functions call one of those, which is
the set a gate has to follow.

THE KNOWN LIMIT, worth writing into the gate rather than hiding. The sweep is
one hop deep. A reporter reached through three or more hops slips past it,
and a gate that claims to cover the shape while reading one hop is the kind
of green this project has been bitten by. Say the depth in the header.

Files: a new harness/test-*.sh, plus a scripts/test registry row, since
harness/test-toolchain-pin.sh asserts every suite registers itself.

title: The learner install snippet hand-copies the tlc wrapper, and it has already drifted
description:

and left uncovered on purpose.

scripts/build-docs.sh hand-copies a wrapper body into the learner install
instructions for getting-started.md. It still names pcal.trans and tlc2.TLC
and has no tlc2.REPL, so the published docs now tell a reader to install a
wrapper the generator has moved past.

  git show main:scripts/build-docs.sh | grep -n 'pcal.trans\|tlc2\.'
  1533, 1535

THE FIX IS TO DELETE THE COPY, NOT TO SYNC IT. This is the shape bead tla-urv
already removed from these same two files for the jar URL, and
scripts/build-docs.sh:14-29 states the doctrine against it: "READ FROM
scripts/setup rather than written again. There is no fourth copy to drift."

So this wants an extraction. The generator owns the body, build-docs reads it
out of the generator the way it already reads the jar URL, and the published
snippet cannot drift again.

WHY A COPY-EQUALITY GATE IS THE WRONG FIX, and the worker's reason is worth
keeping: such a gate would have to be deleted as step one of the extraction.
And hand-copying -repl into the snippet without the usage text would give a
hand-installing learner the dispatch and not the warning, which is the half
measure most worth avoiding here, since the warning is the whole point of the
REPL bead.

harness/test-tlc-wrapper.sh prints a NOTE naming this hole on every run, so
the gap is stated rather than silent. Delete that NOTE as part of closing
this.

title: The step hint goes and an icon carries the gesture table
description:
Files: swipe/reader/swipe.js, swipe/reader/swipe.css, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh, swipe/README.md

RED: INVARIANT: chromeAt() answers for the help panel, render() draws it, a swipe is declined while it is open, and leaving it returns the reader to the depth they were at.

## Where this came from

tla-7xql.19 left the step hint reading "tap to come back" on all 24 models,
while 22 of 24 overflow sideways and so decline a tap over the model body.
About three quarters of the step view will not take the tap that sentence
promises.

Frank's answer, 2026-10-19: "Would it be sensible, instead, just to have an
`i` icon in the upper corner that can be clicked for any such hints, you could
even make it translucent to give readable space if that's useful."

Central's reading, put to him and not contradicted, splits it three ways
because the two hints do different jobs.

## D1 The step hint goes, and nothing replaces it

`renderStep()` writes "up for X, tap to come back" or "tap to come back" at
`swipe.js:1207` and `:1209`. Both go.

The head already reads "THE MODEL, 2 OF 3", which carries the there-is-more
signal, and the back button says "back" in words. The hint restated both and
added a promise the screen cannot keep. Roughly 20 pixels back and no icon
needed to earn them.

## D2 The card hint stays exactly as it is

`cardHint()` is the only thing that tells a reader the premise exists at all.
The resting view has room now that the menu is one control, so this costs
nothing it is short of. Hiding it would be paying discoverability for space
that is not scarce. DO NOT TOUCH IT.

## D3 The icon carries the gesture table

Five gestures and nothing on screen ever says what down means. That is the
hint a reader cannot reconstruct from what is in front of them, and it is a
different thing from either per-view hint.

Place it in the step head beside the back button, and at rest in the counts
row, so it is the same corner in both. It must say what all five gestures do,
including that tap steps back and that down is "not a claim".

## A PANEL, NOT AN OVERLAY, and this is the load-bearing part

`gesture()` already returns early on `v.panel !== null`. That guard is the
thing standing between an open help screen and an accidental verdict, and it
is the failure Frank reported on 2026-10-19: "I've now accidentally sent
multiple responses."

An overlay would leave the step rendered underneath and would need a second,
new guard written from scratch. A panel inherits the guard that already works.
So: a fourth `v.panel` value beside "stats", "message" and "menu".

Two things follow and the gate must pin both.

  1. `chromeAt(depth, panel, flash)` has to answer for it, and `render()`'s
     dispatch needs its own branch. Without one it falls through to
     `chrome.card`, which is false at depth, and draws the STEP instead.
  2. LEAVING IT MUST RETURN THE READER TO THE DEPTH THEY WERE AT. `v.depth`
     is not touched by opening a panel today, so this is about not breaking
     it rather than adding it, and it is exactly the kind of thing that works
     until somebody resets depth in the back handler.

## On translucency

Frank offered it. Use it for the ICON, which can sit over content and cost no
layout. Do NOT use it for the panel. A translucent panel over a model is
monospace over monospace, and a reader comparing a step against a claim is who
can least afford it. The panel is opaque and covers the model, because you are
reading one or the other and never both.

## Do not change

`scrollerDeclining()`. `answersLive()`. The gesture table itself. The card
hint. `harness/Gate.tla` and `harness/verdict.sh` are centrally owned. `docs/`
is generated from `module-docs/`. `puzzles/` is v1. No payload field changes.

## The gate

`harness/test-swipe-reader.sh`, split `--static` (3.0 s) and full (22.0 s).
Both budgets stay.

The chrome predicate is already driven over every combination of depth, panel
and flash in part 6. Widen that table rather than adding a second one, so the
new panel value is answered everywhere the others are. Add the depth-survives
check and a check that a swipe is declined while it is open.

Assert the step hint is gone and the card hint is still there. Those two
assertions next to each other are the record that this was decided as a pair.

Watch every new assertion FAIL first.
close_reason: Merged at 50bb006, worker commit 344c563. Step hint removed, card hint kept, an i control in the step head and the counts row opening a help panel that names all five gestures. A panel and not an overlay, so it inherits the swipe-declined-while-a-panel-is-open guard rather than needing a second one. Two findings worth more than the feature: chromeAt() needed NO change because it reads open = Boolean(panel) and never asks which, so six new table rows were green against untouched code and the worker said so rather than implying work; and the gate's depth check matched v\.depth, which does not match view.depth because the character before the dot is a w, so a mutation resetting depth through the outer name passed. Both spellings now redden. Verified: 249/0 in 14.4s against 22.0, 247/1 in 1.38s against 3.0, the previous gate against the new reader passed 225, spelling 20, lint clean over 146, swipe.js parses, footprint exactly the four declared files. Registry 49/49 in 1161.6s with zero failures.

title: Expose the TLC REPL through the tlc wrapper
description:
Files: scripts/setup

Frank asked for this on 2026-10-19. The REPL is already in the pinned jar and
the wrapper does not expose it.

## What is there

`tlc2/REPL.class` and `tlc2/REPLSpecWriter.class` are in
`~/lib/tla2tools.jar`, the pinned v1.8.0 build (manifest X-Git-Tag
`2026.07.18.145032;v1.8.0`, 2221 entries). `~/bin/tlc` dispatches only
`tlc2.TLC` and, under `-pcal`, `pcal.trans`. The wrapper is GENERATED by
`scripts/setup` at the `install_wrapper` call around line 206 and carries
"Do not hand-edit", so the change belongs there.

## Verified behavior, run against the pinned jar on 2026-10-19

    1 + 1                            -> 2
    Cardinality({1,2,3})             -> 3
    [x \in 1..3 |-> x * x]           -> <<1, 4, 9>>
    CHOOSE n \in 1..10 : n * n = 49  -> 7
    LET f == 2 IN f + 1              -> 3

The standard modules are already extended, so `Cardinality` resolves with no
ceremony. It writes nothing into the working directory: a probe directory held
only the two files put there before the run.

## L1, the limit that matters for this curriculum

CONSTANT LEVEL ONLY. `x` comes back "Unknown operator". No variables, no
primes. That is rung 0 of the swipe corpus exactly and nothing above it, since
level 1 is state and level 2 is action.

Worse than a refusal: `ENABLED (1 = 1)` returns TRUE, because a constant
expression is trivially enabled. The REPL accepts the syntax and answers
vacuously. That is a trap for the exact reader this project teaches, so the
wrapper's usage text has to say constant level out loud rather than leaving it
to be discovered through a false TRUE.

## L2

It cannot see a local module. It generates a module named `tlarepl` with a
fixed EXTENDS list and no hook to add to it. A `Toy.tla` in the working
directory defining `Double(n) == n * 2` gave "Unknown operator: `Double'".
`tlc2.REPL` takes no arguments at all: `-h` was parsed as negating an operator
named `h`.

`LET Double(n) == n * 2 IN Double(21)` works, which covers a one-liner and
nothing larger.

## The work

Add a `-repl` branch to the generated `~/bin/tlc` beside the existing `-pcal`
one, dispatching `tlc2.REPL`. Give the wrapper usage text that names the
constant-level limit.

NOTE THAT THE CHANGE ONLY REACHES A MACHINE WHEN `scripts/setup` IS RE-RUN.
Say so when closing.

## Gate

No suite covers the wrapper's dispatch table today. `harness/reading-gate.sh`
and `harness/comment-gate.sh` reference `bin/tlc` but do not check what it
dispatches. Decide whether this is worth a gate or whether `scripts/setup`'s
own verification step at the bottom of the file is the right place, and say
which you chose and why.

## Out of scope

A REPL that can see a module is different work: it means generating a scratch
module that EXTENDS the target and running `tlc2.TLC` on it, which brings the
state and action levels with it. That is the micro-models idea from the
exploration argument and wants its own bead.
close_reason: Merged on main 2026-10-20, worker commit c6a33d0. Frank asked for this on 2026-10-19. A -repl branch in the generated ~/bin/tlc dispatches tlc2.REPL, written into scripts/setup because the wrapper carries 'Do not hand-edit'. THE USAGE TEXT IS THE POINT OF THE BEAD. A level 0 prompt has three behaviors and only two are loud: a bare or primed variable reports Unknown operator, a temporal operator is a parse error, and ENABLED (1 = 1) returns TRUE, as does UNCHANGED 1, because a constant expression is trivially enabled and trivially unchanged. The third is silent and wrong for the reader this project teaches, so the text says so and a short form prints to stderr before the prompt opens. Written in frank-writing strict mode, which also dodges an apostrophe that the single-quoted bash body cannot carry. THE BEAD'S OWN MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER CORRECTED IT: tlc2.REPL takes exactly one argument and evaluates it non-interactively, so tlc -repl '1 + 1' prints 2 and exits, and -h had been read as an expression because an argument IS an expression. Two or more arguments fall back to the prompt and are silently ignored, so the wrapper refuses a multi-word unquoted expression with rc 2. A one-shot error still exits 0, so nothing can gate on that code. GATE DECISION: a new suite harness/test-tlc-wrapper.sh rather than a line in setup, because the two catch different things. It extracts the wrapper body out of the tracked generator and runs it against a java shim that prints its arguments, so it reads the class the wrapper chose rather than the string it contains, which caught that -h and -help both reach TLC's own option list and must only be intercepted after -repl. And bash -n over the body is a check nothing else can do, because the body is a single-quoted string shellcheck never parses, so 65 lines inside a file scripts/lint reads clean were never parsed by anything. 20 assertions, 12 invariants and 6 controls, 0.1s against a 0.3s budget, fast tier. Two of six controls failed on their first run and both were defects in the checks: a case-insensitive ENABLED grep passed over a text with every ENABLED line cut because a lowercase 'trivially enabled' sits below, and an apostrophe control mutated nothing because the mutant copied the body's apostrophe-free style. scripts/test is a declared deviation and it is forced, since test-toolchain-pin.sh asserts every suite registers itself. Filed tla-5lqr for the second hand-copied wrapper body in scripts/build-docs.sh, which already drifted. THIS REACHES FRANK'S MACHINE ONLY WHEN scripts/setup IS RE-RUN, and 'bash scripts/setup --no-docs' is enough since the jar is at the pin. Verified: new suite 20, pipefail 25, spelling 20 with a planted British word watched failing, lint clean over 147 with three new findings fixed rather than quieted, generator run end to end against a sandbox HOME inside the worktree with Frank's own ~/bin/tlc untouched.

title: Level 2 pins sit behind the dock, and nothing says to scroll
description:
Measured 2026-10-19 in Chrome at a true 390x844 viewport, against the
published site at ba1c0c7. This is the reading tla-7xql.14 could not take.

THE DOCK ITSELF IS FINE and this bead is not about it. It is fully visible at
scroll 0 and everywhere the premise is in view, 298px at level 1, 269px at
level 2, 384px at the worst claim. The sticky design held.

WHAT IS WRONG IS WHAT THE DOCK COVERS. At level 2 the premise is the model
screen at 296px plus the pin at 327px, which is 623px against the 575px above
the dock. So 198px of pin is behind the dock when the item is drawn. Measured
on a Handover item: pin top 446, pin bottom 773, dock top 575.

The reader lands on a `steps to` label with its content covered and no cue
that anything is under there. A level 2 item asks whether a formula holds
across a step, so the post-state is not optional context, it is half the
question. Answering without it is answering a different item.

Hiding the model clears it, since the screen collapses to its 44px head and
the whole pin then fits. That is a lever the reader has to know to pull, and
the hide state is remembered per bucket, so it is a reasonable answer once
somebody knows. It is not a fix.

Level 1 does not have this: screen 296 plus pin 112 is 408px against 546px of
room, so the whole premise is visible when the item is drawn.

Options, and I have not ruled between them:
  1. collapse the model screen by default at level 2 only, so the drawn state
     shows the whole pin and the screen is one tap away.
  2. cap the pin the way the screen is capped, with its own scroll.
  3. shrink the dock at level 2, which costs the thing the dock is for.
  4. a cue on the dock that there is premise underneath it.

Option 1 is the cheapest and it fits the rung: a level 2 item is about the
step, and the model matters less once you have read it for the bucket. It
also composes with the per-bucket hide memory that already exists.

Files: swipe/reader/swipe.js, swipe/reader/swipe.css, harness/test-swipe-reader.sh, swipe/README.md
notes:
=== FRANK'S DESIGN, 2026-10-19, and it supersedes the four options above ===

He ruled against fitting everything into one scrolling room. Instead the
resting card carries the QUESTION ONLY, and swipe up walks a stack:

  up 1   the state, where there is one
  up 2   the model
  up 3   a detailed explanation of the last wrong answer

This removes the occlusion by construction rather than by tuning heights,
which is why it beats every option listed above. Nothing can sit behind the
dock if nothing but the question is drawn.

HE ALSO ASKED FOR AN ENGLISH TAG on each item, saying the level number is
fine but words would be better. Recommended: TLA+'s own level names, which
are constant, state and action. They are the English for what is pinned,
the corpus is already organized around them, and they are the vocabulary
the project exists to make automatic. "level 1" teaches nothing.

THREE AMENDMENTS CENTRAL RAISED, not yet ruled on by Frank.

M1. The dock stays while the stack is open, so the stack fills the room
ABOVE it rather than taking the screen. Otherwise the reader reads the
state, swipes back, and answers from memory, which is a working memory test
rather than the recognition drill this rung measures. The measured room is
575px, the state is 327px and the model 296px, so either fits alone and the
two together do not. One at a time is what makes them fit.

M2. Up 3 changes subject. State and model are about the item on screen and
the last wrong answer is a different item. Keep it on the up axis, since it
is rare and up is free, but land it as a visibly different mode with its own
dismiss rather than a third drawer.

R1. Vertical swipe fights native scroll. A tall panel has to scroll inside
itself, and a drag there must scroll rather than move the stack. swipe.js
already declines a touch starting in .swipe-screen-body for the model's
sideways scroll, so the technique exists and now carries more weight.

AND DOWN MUST NOT ANSWER WHILE THE STACK IS OPEN. Down is "not a claim", so
a reader collapsing the stack would file a vacuity verdict. Down means back
while open and answers only at rest. The three answers are buttons as well
as gestures, so nothing is locked out.

WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE DRILL, worth saying before it is built: 192 of
432 items stop being answerable without at least one swipe. That is a change
to the task and not only to the layout.

CURRENT MECHANICS THIS HAS TO FIT, read out of swipe.js on 2026-10-19:
gesture() ignores every swipe while a panel is open, treats any swipe as
dismiss while a flash is up, maps up to the review panel, and otherwise
answers. answer() sets v.flash on EVERY answer, hit or miss, so the
explanation already auto-shows once and the review panel is the second look.
Putting the rare path at up 3 is right.
RULED BY FRANK 2026-10-19, in conversation. Two rulings, and M1 answers itself.

TAP IS THE FIFTH GESTURE AND IT MEANS STEP BACK. Frank raised it, central
measured it, Frank agreed. Every gesture now keeps ONE meaning in EVERY state:

  right / left / down   true / false / not a claim
  up                    one step deeper
  tap                   one step back

That retires the "down must not answer while the stack is open" clause above.
Down keeps its single meaning everywhere and tap owns the way out, so the
reader never has to track which mode they are in to know what down does.

WHAT WAS MEASURED ABOUT TAP, read out of swipe.js on 2026-10-19:

  F1. Tap is ALREADY bound, in exactly one state and for this meaning.
      renderFlash() attaches a click handler and prints the hint "Tap anywhere
      here for the next one" (swipe.js:795). The reader learns tap means "no
      opinion, move me along" on their first wrong answer.
  F2. On a plain card a tap reaches nothing. touchend returns before gesture()
      when both deltas are under SWIPE_THRESHOLD, which is 55px.
  F3. With a panel open every swipe is declined: gesture() returns early on
      v.panel !== null. The only way out today is a tap on a per-panel back
      button, so tap already carries "back out" through one small target.
  F4. THE ONE COST. touchstart declines any touch starting inside
      .swipe-screen-body, because a sideways scroll of a 73-character line and
      a left swipe are the same gesture on the same pixel. At level 2 that body
      is 296px of the 575px above the dock, so a tap-anywhere surface has a
      hole in it where the reader's thumb just was. The per-panel back button
      stays as the guarantee and tap-anywhere is the convenience on top.

M1 IS RESOLVED AS WRITTEN, and not by a coin toss. The dock is the CLAIM plus
the three answer buttons, not chrome: swipe.js:949 says the answer buttons live
in the dock with the claim so they cannot be scrolled away from the question
they answer. Hiding the claim to show the model means holding the claim in
memory while reading the premise, which is what the dock was built to prevent.
Each step fits above it alone (pin 327px, screen 296px, room 575px), so keeping
it costs nothing in fit.

M2 IS RESOLVED BY THE SAME READING. Steps 1 and 2 are the SAME item, so the
answers stay live there. Step 3 is a different item, so the dock goes dead.
That is the visible mode change M2 was reaching for, and it falls out of what
the dock holds rather than being bolted on.

SO swipe.js:1015 CHANGES. b.disabled = !view.current || view.panel !== null
is right for stats and review, which change the subject, and wrong for stack
steps 1 and 2, which do not.

THE STACK IS LEVEL-DEPENDENT, which is Frank's "if appropriate":

  level 0   depth 1 = the explanation. No state and no model exist.
            renderScreen() already returns null for level 0.
  level 1   depth 1 = the pinned state, 2 = the model, 3 = the explanation.
  level 2   depth 1 = from/steps to/where, 2 = the model, 3 = the explanation.

Build the step list from what the item actually has rather than from its level,
so an item with no screen skips that step instead of showing an empty one.

THE PIN AND THE SCREEN LEAVE THE RESTING VIEW. That is the fix for the 198px
of pin behind the dock: at rest the reader sees the tag, the ask, the claim and
the three answers, and the premise is one swipe up. The resting view then fits
at every level by construction rather than by arithmetic.

THE TAGS ARE constant / state / action, which is TLA+'s own level calculus, so
the tag teaches the vocabulary instead of inventing a second one. Level 3 is
temporal and this corpus has no rung for it.

THE CARD HINT HAS TO CHANGE. It reads "up for the last one you got wrong",
which stops being true at level 1 and 2 the moment up 1 is the state. Per
level: level 0 keeps it, level 1 says the pinned state is up, level 2 says the
step is up. The hint is how the reader learns the premise is there at all.

KEYBOARD PARITY. bindKeys maps the four arrows and nothing else, so tap has no
key. Escape is the one to add.
D1 AND D2 RULED BY FRANK 2026-10-19, in the same conversation. The tags are
constant / state / action, and the card hint changes per level. Both were
central's calls when the build was dispatched and both are now Frank's, so a
later reader should not reopen them as open questions.

title: The practice README has no source and no gate, and one read found three stale claims
description:
Successor to tla-bxcd, which Frank closed on 2026-10-18 after ruling on the
numbering. That bead's own warning line read "~/tla-practice/README.md has no
source in this repo. Nothing here generates it and no script writes it, so it
is hand-maintained in a tree that is not under version control."

THAT IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED. One read on 2026-10-18 found
three stale claims in it:

1. Steps 2 to 4 said an attempt goes in attempts/<name>/. The real shape is
attempts/<batch>/<NN_name>/, and the live batch has used it since 2026-10-02.

2. The problems section read "problems/ stays empty until the ramp's first
rungs land". Seven problems had landed in it.

3. It carried an em dash, which this project does not use in prose.

All three were fixed by hand the same day. Nothing stops a fourth.

WHY THE NEW GATE DOES NOT COVER IT. harness/test-number-problems.sh now
checks the delivered trees against the ORDER beside each one, which catches a
directory name going out of step. It cannot see prose. The README is the file
that tells a learner what the directory names MEAN, and it is the one part of
the delivered tree with no source and no check.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, and I lean to the first.

Give it a source under drill/ or a new practice/ directory in this repo, and
deliver it the way every other artifact is delivered. It then gets the
spelling gate, the delivery verify from tla-mjvx, and a diff anybody can read.
The cost is that a file Frank may want to annotate becomes one a delivery
overwrites, which is exactly the problem scripts/deliver-exercises.sh solved
with a digest record, so the mechanism already exists.

The alternative is to leave it hand-maintained and add a check that reads it
for the claims a script can verify, such as the directory names it mentions.
That is cheaper and it only catches the subset a script can parse. It would
have caught claims 1 and 2 above and not claim 3.

Files: scripts/deliver-drill.sh, harness/test-deliver-drill.sh

RED: INVARIANT: every claim ~/tla-practice/README.md makes about a directory name resolves against the delivered tree, and the file has a source in this repo that the spelling gate reads.
notes:
2026-10-18, FRANK RULED: OPTION 1, give it a source in the repo and deliver it. He took central's read over the cheaper parse-only check, which would have caught two of the three stale claims and not the third.

WHAT CENTRAL MEASURED BEFORE DISPATCH, and it changes the shape. All five scripts/deliver-*.sh deliver into a SUBDIRECTORY of ~/tla-practice: drill, recall, exercises, completion, problems. Nothing delivers to the tree ROOT, which is where this README lives. So this is a new channel rather than an extension of an existing one, and the bead's own Files line naming scripts/deliver-drill.sh was wrong. The worker builds scripts/deliver-practice-root.sh with --check, --verify and --adopt, modeled on deliver-recall.sh for the verify and deliver-exercises.sh for the digest record.

The source is seeded from the CURRENT live file read-only, so the three hand-fixes of 2026-10-18 are preserved rather than re-authored.

It owns scripts/test and does NOT touch scripts/verify-delivery.sh, which a sibling worker owns in this wave. That file fails on any deliver-*.sh it does not know about, so the KNOWN_CHANNELS line is reported and central adds it at merge.
close_reason:
Landed at merge b24495d, wired into the wrapper at 816fb27.

Frank ruled on 2026-10-18 to source it and deliver it. practice/README.md is byte for byte the live file, digest 302d78fa...52fe checked on both by central rather than read off the report, so the three hand-fixes survived and nothing was re-authored.

IT IS A NEW CHANNEL BECAUSE NOTHING DELIVERED TO THE ROOT. All five existing deliver scripts write into a subdirectory of ~/tla-practice, so the bead's own Files line naming deliver-drill.sh was wrong. scripts/deliver-practice-root.sh carries --check, --verify and --adopt with a record at the destination root, and the adopt has run: 1 file adopted, 0 left unrecorded.

THE PATH ASSERTION CATCHES NONE OF THE THREE CLAIMS THAT PROMPTED THE BEAD, which the worker measured and said plainly. This bead's description predicted it would catch two of them, and so did central when putting the options to Frank. Claim 1 wrote attempts/<name>/ and attempts/ resolves either way. Claim 2's contradiction was prose while the path it named resolved. Claim 3 was an em dash. What pays here is the source plus the spelling gate plus a readable diff, which is the half Frank picked. What the assertion catches is a path that STOPS resolving, and attempts/2026-10-02-fresh-start/ is a dated literal that rolls over when batch 2 opens.

AND WIRING IT REDDENED THREE ROWS OF harness/test-deliver-verify.sh, which is recorded because central's first fix was wrong. Those rows assert on the wrapper's aggregate exit code to say something about drill while provisioning only drill. Five of seven channels skip there because their trees are absent. practice-root does not: its tree IS the root, so it compares the moment the root exists and correctly reports the README owed. Central first changed the skip test in the script to ask whether this channel had ever been delivered, which went green everywhere and would have been silent on a real practice tree holding drill and no README. That is the tree this channel exists to catch. Reverted, and the fixtures were provisioned instead.

Follow-up filed: tla-azwl, the README names three of the seven delivered directories.

title: rc 150 is not a row in the level 0 channel, and a parse failure met it six times
description:
Found 2026-10-18 by the tla-7xql.7 author, which met this six times in 160 new items. A generator will meet it far more often than a human author does.

THE CHANNEL HAS THREE ROWS and a parse failure is in none of them:

  ASSUME (e)   ASSUME ((e) \/ ~(e))   verdict              swipe
  0            0                      holds                right
  10           0                      false                left
  10           10                     does not evaluate    down

A claim that does not PARSE comes back rc 150 from SANY before TLC evaluates
anything. The author replaced all six with claims that parse, which was the
safe call inside that bead, and every one of the six was the same shape: two
operators from a precedence band SANY will not associate, so \div beside *,
\/ beside /\, % beside +.

THE QUESTION. Is a parse failure a down-swipe item, a different item kind, or
not an item at all?

The case FOR a down swipe: D3 already merges vacuous and ill-formed onto that
gesture, and the epic says so for a stated reason, which is that without the
merge a vacuous item has no correct swipe at all. A reader seeing a claim
whose operators cannot associate is being asked the same sort of question as a
reader seeing one that does not denote.

The case AGAINST: 'does not evaluate' and 'does not parse' are different
lessons, and the corpus already distinguishes them in field 5 as illformed
against what a parse failure would need. Also the existing (10,10) pair is a
MEASURED fact about a well-formed boolean failing to denote, where a 150 never
reaches the pair at all, so the two would share a swipe while arriving through
different machinery.

MY READ, and it is a read rather than a decision. I would make it a down-swipe
item with its own value in field 5, so the swipe stays a clean partition while
the data keeps the distinction, which is exactly what D3 and D5 already do for
vacuous against illformed. That costs one field value and no new gesture.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE LATER. The operator-precedence family, T2, is built on
claims where the real parse differs from the expected one. A precedence trap
that goes one step further stops parsing altogether, so this is the family
most likely to produce them, and a generator working that family will produce
them constantly.

Frank's call, since it touches D3 and D5.

Files: swipe/README.md, swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv, swipe/level0/bake.sh, harness/test-swipe-level0.sh

RED: INVARIANT: every exit code the bake can observe maps to a declared verdict
and a declared swipe, and rc 150 is among them.
notes: FRANK RULED 2026-10-18: down-swipe with its own field-5 value. Agreed with the read in the description. So rc 150 becomes a fourth row in the channel, mapping to the down swipe, and field 5 gains a value distinct from illformed. The gesture stays a three-way partition while the data keeps the distinction, same as vacuous against illformed under D3 and D5. Unblocked, ready to build.
close_reason: Merged at 2299418 (worker 6f30c1f), follow-ups at 4d44d66. Frank ruled 2026-10-18: down-swipe with its own field 5 value, per my read. Field 5 value is unparsed, rc pair (150,150) measured through verdict.sh rather than assumed. bake.sh learns the row in swipe_for, rc_pair_for, check(), write_table() and --stats, probing unparsed items one at a time since a parse failure cannot batch. The safety property held unchanged: --check already enforced declared kind against observed rc, so a typo in an item declared true still reddens. What improved is the diagnostic, which used to invite a relabel where the fix is a pair of parentheses. Five induced breaks watched and restored, including controls in both directions. Corpus untouched, so no gate number moved. Worker found two defects outside its footprint, both fixed at 4d44d66: scripts/lint had never read swipe/ (89 files to 134), and ITEMS.tsv listed four kinds. Whether the shipped corpus should carry unparsed items is tla-7xql.11.

title: The no-perfect-correlation invariant is stricter than the stem-blind gate and is wired to nothing
description:
Found 2026-10-18 by the tla-7xql.7 author, which is the reason that bead's corpus is clean.

tla-7xql.8's RED line reads: no token appearing in three or more claims of one
template is perfectly correlated with that template's label.

THE PROBE NEVER FLAGGED ANY OF IT. harness/swipe/stemblind.sh probe was clear
on all five templates through every draft. What found the violations was the
author checking the RED line BY HAND. It found four:

  T5  the token 17, 4 items, all true     the bead named this one
  T2  the token 5, 3 items, all right     ON THE SHIPPED 80, UNWRITTEN
  T2  the universal quantifier, 3 claims, all vacuous   first draft
  T3  the empty set, 3 claims, all vacuous              first draft

Two of those were already in the corpus that shipped, and the T2 one had never
been recorded anywhere. The T3 one is the vacuity-sentinel problem wearing
different clothes: the empty set had quietly become that template's down
marker, which is the one thing matched-group authoring does not prevent.

WHY THE PROBE MISSES THEM. It scores a decision stump by leave-one-out against
a permutation threshold, so a rule covering 3 of 48 items is worth almost
nothing to it even when the correlation is perfect. That is correct for its
own job, which is asking whether a judge could score above the base rate. It
is the wrong instrument for 'this template has a tell', and the two questions
are not the same.

So the invariant and the gate disagree at n=48, THE INVARIANT IS STRICTER, and
only the gate runs. That makes the corpus's cleanliness a property of one
author having been careful rather than of anything that will fire next time.

WHAT I WOULD BUILD. An assertion in harness/test-swipe-stemblind.sh that reads
ITEMS.tsv directly and fails on any token in three or more claims of one
template that is perfectly correlated with the label. The author already ran
exactly this by hand and reported RESULT holds perfect=0 with the worst at
0.75 on a 4-item token, so the measurement exists and the threshold is known.

Tokenization should reuse stemblind.sh's own bag so the two instruments agree
on what a token is, and the suite should print the worst offender per template
whether or not it fires, the way the probe already prints its best feature.

Files: harness/test-swipe-stemblind.sh

RED: INVARIANT: no token appearing in three or more claims of one template is
perfectly correlated with that template's label, asserted rather than checked
by hand.
close_reason: Merged at 17cc4d0 (worker 35086cd). harness/test-swipe-stemblind.sh part 7, 10 assertions, 46 to 56. Correlates on field 6, the swipe, which is both what a judge predicts and the stricter column, since swipe is a function of kind so merging vacuous and illformed into down can only raise a token's purity. Shipped reading reproduces the tla-7xql.7 hand check: perfect=0 across five templates, worst 0.7500 on a 4-item token in T3, printed every run and not asserted. Watched failing both directions, with the min=2 half proving the plant is visible rather than the scan being blind. Worker also found part 4's comment was false on the grown corpus (five T2 claims carry TRUE or a slash) and caught its own sort-on-count-instead-of-purity bug in the summary line.

title: Three swipe authoring habits leave a signature in the claim's surface
description:
Found 2026-10-18 by the tla-7xql.1 author. None of these fails the stem-blind gate today and all three are the mechanism it hunts, so they are worth fixing before the corpus grows and bakes them in.

1. T5 SCORES 0.6250 ON THE TOKEN 17, which is 25 points over its 0.3750
floor. Four T5 claims carry 17 and all four are true. The author suspects it
is real rather than noise because it has a cause: the family's declared trap
is a negative operand, so a minus sign got reached for when writing false
items while 17 is the running example the true items share. A hand survey
found two more T5 skews the stump scores lower, has:- on 5 items with 4 false
and has:% on 5 items with 4 true, plus has:Cardinality on 2 items both false.

That is Gururangan's finding reproduced in miniature in our own corpus, by the
same route: the writer's habit rather than the item's content.

2. TWO TOKENS ARE PERFECTLY CORRELATED WITH THE DOWN SWIPE. The sentinel 99
on 5 items and the universal quantifier on 5 items, every one of them
vacuous. One per template, so leave-one-out neutralizes them in the gate's own
scoring, EXCEPT T1 carries two of the 99 items, which makes has:99 a real
two-item rule at 0.5000, tied at the top of T1's list.

A reader who learns 'a 99 in it means swipe down' never evaluates another
vacuous item. Vary the sentinel when items are next authored, and say so in
swipe/README.md so the next author does not reach for 99 again.

3. THE GATE CAN SEE ALL OF THIS AND CANNOT CALL ANY OF IT, because at 16 items
per template nothing under 69.0 percent predictability is reportable. Bead on
corpus size covers that half. This bead is the content half, and the two
should probably land together: growing T5 with the same habits would make the
skew significant rather than remove it.

WHAT I WOULD DO. Re-author the skewed T5 items so the minus sign and the 17
appear on both sides of the label, and vary the vacuity sentinel across
templates. Then re-run harness/swipe/stemblind.sh probe and record what the
per-template best feature becomes.

THE ALTERNATIVE worth naming: leave the items and declare the skew acceptable
because it sits under the detection floor. I would not take that. The floor is
a property of the sample size rather than of the corpus, so it moves the
moment the corpus grows, and then this becomes a real finding on items that
have shipped.

Files: swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv, swipe/README.md

RED: INVARIANT: no token appearing in three or more claims of one template is
perfectly correlated with that template's label, and no vacuity sentinel is
shared across every template.
close_reason: Merged at 76ae1ed, gates repaired at 9b70733. 240 items, 48 per template against 16, so the stem-blind tolerance goes 25 points to 14.6 and detection 0.6900 to 0.5705, which puts Gururangan's 0.67 clear of the floor rather than at the edge. Mix holds at 18/18/6/6 so the 0.3750 base rate does not move. THE PROBE IS NOT WHAT CAUGHT THE AUTHOR'S OWN HABITS, which is the finding: it was clear through every draft, and tla-7xql.8's RED line read directly found four violations, two on the corpus that had already shipped including a 3-item perfect correlation in T2 nobody had written down. So that invariant is stricter than the gate at n=48 and is wired to nothing, filed as tla-7xql.9. The vacuity sentinel was REMOVED rather than varied, which is better than the brief asked for, since five varied sentinels is five rules. Planted signature re-measured at both sizes: a token must be about half as widespread at 48 before the probe can call it. Nine of 160 items contradicted the author's field-5 prediction, six of them parse failures at rc 150 which is not a row in the level 0 channel, filed as tla-7xql.10. Every T5 dividend is non-negative so no item needed a div caveat.

title: The recall corpus gate costs 258 s against a budget set at 196.6, and 53 of the 61 seconds are unattributed
description:
Found 2026-10-18 by central while re-basing after two merges. Re-based 197.0 to 270.0 at the same time, so the row is not red, but most of the move has no cause named and that is worth more than the budget.

THE READINGS. Three back-to-back standalone runs on the merged tree, all 245
assertions passing: 258.166 / 275.156 / 302.086 s.

THAT IS NOT A BAND. whisper-cli came up on the box partway through at 395
percent CPU and 2.3 GB RSS, and the three readings rise with it. Run 1
finished before it started, so 258.2 is the only clean reading. 270.0 clears
it by 4.6 percent and deliberately does NOT cover the contended 302, because
budgeting to 302 would hide a real regression behind a transcription job.

WHAT IS ATTRIBUTED: 8 of the 61 seconds.

  tla-1sh7.7   +7.9 s   a field-7 pattern on 24 reps, so check 4 validates
                        24 patterns it did not before. That author measured
                        it as a paired 246.4 -> 254.3 s on its own box.
  tla-z4f3     +0.3 s   part 8, measured, and it starts no JVM.

WHAT IS NOT: about 53 s, and it predates both.

The row was set at 196.6 on 2026-10-17 over three readings spanning 194.010
to 196.595 s, a 1.3 percent spread, which is a tight and trustworthy band.
The same tree now reads 258 clean. So something grew between 3d05932 and
2026-10-18 and nothing in either bead accounts for it.

WHERE I WOULD LOOK, in order. git log over harness/recall-gate.sh and
recall/ between 3d05932 and today, since a per-row TLC run added anywhere in
the corpus multiplies by 160. Then the scaffold batteries: a SPEC row is one
TLC run per scaffold in its battery and 20 of the 40 name more than one, so
a scaffold added to a battery costs more than a row does. Then check whether
anything made check 2 grade more than its 90 recorded wrong answers.

THE CHEAP CONTROL FIRST, before any of that. Run the two recall rows together
with a filtered pass and read them against each other:

  bash scripts/test recall

If both are over by the same proportion, the box is the cause and this bead
is about measurement rather than about the suite. The recall runner row at
105.0 was set on 2026-10-17 the same way, so it is the sibling control.

AND READ ps RATHER THAN pgrep java. The command that found the contention,
which a stray-JVM scan misses completely:

  ps -eo pid,etime,pcpu,rss,args --sort=-pcpu | head -6

The etime column says whether it overlapped your reading. Load average will
not: it read 1.69 eleven minutes before the same box read 6.8.

RELATED. bd memory a-sibling-row-is-the-cheapest-control-for carries the
whisper-cli finding and names it as the first candidate for the unexplained
152-to-203 s window on the recall runner from 2026-10-17, which that session
recorded as having no cause after ruling out stray JVMs with ps.

Files: scripts/test, harness/recall-gate.sh (CENTRALLY OWNED, report not edit)

RED: INVARIANT: every second of the recall corpus gate's cost above its
2026-10-17 reading of 196.6 s is either attributed to a named bead in the row
note or shown to be contention by a sibling row moving with it.
notes:
2026-10-18, central. THE SIBLING CONTROL THIS BEAD ASKS FOR HAS NOW RUN, as a full registry pass under the same whisper-cli contention. 41 of 42 rows over budget at once, which settles that the box was the cause of the SPREAD even if not of the baseline.

Ratios of elapsed to budget on that pass:

  pipefail idiom ban          14.2 /   4.6   3.09x
  drill delivery               5.1 /   2.3   2.22x
  drill corpus gate          119.4 /  54.4   2.20x
  drill runner                 5.6 /   2.9   1.93x
  seeded-bug matrix           84.1 /  57.8   1.46x
  vacuity gate                82.1 /  60.0   1.37x
  indeterminate gate          65.7 /  50.2   1.31x
  grader                     120.5 /  99.0   1.22x
  recall runner              125.9 / 105.0   1.20x
  level 0 swipe corpus        33.8 /  31.0   1.09x
  recall corpus gate         284.1 / 270.0   1.05x
  TLA+ definition levels       8.9 /  10.0   0.89x

TWO THINGS THAT FALL OUT, and the second one is the useful one.

1. THE 270.0 RE-BASE LOOKS RIGHT RATHER THAN GENEROUS. The corpus gate is the
SECOND LEAST over-budget row on the pass, at 1.05x, while its siblings run
1.2x to 2.2x. A budget padded past the real cost would sit further down that
list than its neighbours, and this one sits at the bottom. So 258 clean is a
believable baseline.

2. THE RECALL RUNNER DID NOT BLOW UP, which answers the question its row note
left open. At 1.20x it sits in the middle of the sibling band, right beside
the grader at 1.22x. tla-1sh7.7 added 12 assertions and about 18 TLC runs to
it, and if that had cost what the corpus gate's 53 unattributed seconds cost,
this row would be at the top of the list rather than the middle. So 105.0 is
probably still about right and the runner is NOT showing the same unexplained
growth. That makes the corpus gate's 53 s a fact about THAT suite rather than
about the recall corpus or the box.

So the next step narrows: it is not 'the corpus grew', because the runner
grades the same corpus and did not move the same way. Look at
harness/recall-gate.sh itself, and at the scaffold batteries, which the
corpus gate walks and the runner does not.

WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT SETTLE. Every number above is contended, so none of
them is a budget signal and none was used as one. The baseline 258.166 s from
the clean run is still the only number this bead rests on.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING. The BUDGET DRIFT nudge fired on exactly one
row, pipefail idiom ban at 3.09x, and its own text says to ignore it if the
box was loaded. The box was loaded. Not filed.
2026-10-18, central, AND THE 258.2 s FIGURE THIS BEAD WAS FILED ON WAS CONTAMINATED. Re-based 270.0 to 245.0.

A power loss rebooted the box, which handed me the first genuinely quiet
window of the session. Three back-to-back runs, each with a 15-second load
sample running alongside for its whole duration:

  233.205 s   no outside consumer at any sample, 251 assertions
  229.925 s   none until the last 15 s, 251 assertions
  274.014 s   whisper-cli at 74 percent throughout, DISCARDED

So the clean band is 229.9 to 233.2, a 1.4 percent spread, and whisper costs
this row about 18 percent. The third reading is kept as the measurement of
that cost rather than averaged into a band it does not belong to.

WHAT THAT DOES TO THIS BEAD. The 258.166 s I called 'the only clean reading'
had whisper already ramping during it. It was the LEAST contended reading, not
a clean one, and the difference is 25 s. So:

  196.6   the 2026-10-17 baseline, over a 1.3 percent band
  + 7.9   tla-1sh7.7, field 7 on 24 reps, paired 246.4 -> 254.3 by that author
  + 0.3   tla-z4f3 part 8, and it starts no JVM
  + ~0    tla-2s12's six rows, static mutants, no JVM
  = 204.8 expected
    233.2 actual clean
  = ~28 s unattributed, not ~53

Half the mystery was measurement. The remaining 28 s is still real and still
predates all three beads.

AND ONE ARGUMENT I MADE FOR THE 270.0 WAS CIRCULAR, which is worth writing
down because it is easy to make again. I defended it by noting this row sat at
1.05x over budget on a contended full pass while its siblings ran 1.2x to
2.2x, and read that as the budget being right rather than padded. A
GENEROUSLY SET BUDGET IS EXACTLY WHAT LOOKS LEAST-OVER ON A CONTENDED PASS.
The sibling ratios were evidence about the box and none at all about this
number. The part of that pass that does still hold is the other half: the
recall RUNNER sat mid-band at 1.20x, so whatever the 28 s is, it is a fact
about recall-gate.sh rather than about the corpus both rows read.

245.0 will read over budget whenever Frank is dictating, and that is
intended. A budget here is informational: an over-budget row still prints PASS
and only the 3x drift nudge warns. So a tight budget costs one honest line and
a loose one hides a regression.

THE PROCEDURE THAT MADE THIS POSSIBLE, since the 2026-10-17 window had no
cause named for exactly the opposite reason: START THE LOAD SAMPLER BEFORE THE
RUN. One 15-second ps loop filtered to exclude the suite's own TLC, kept for
the whole window. It is what told me run 3 was contended and runs 1 and 2 were
not, and without it all three numbers would have looked like one 17 percent
band again.

NEXT STEP IS UNCHANGED and now narrower: git log over harness/recall-gate.sh
between 3d05932 and today for a per-row TLC run added anywhere, then the
scaffold batteries, since a SPEC row is one run per scaffold and 20 of the 40
name more than one.
2026-10-18, central, a READ rather than a run, because the box had a worker on it. EVERY STRUCTURAL HYPOTHESIS THIS BEAD NAMED IS NEGATIVE, so nothing in the repo accounts for the 53 seconds.

What was searched, named rather than implied, per the CLAUDE.md rule. All comparisons are 3d05932 against HEAD at b074c76, which is the span the bead asks about.

1. CORPUS GROWTH. recall/REPS.tsv 120 rows then and now. recall/MISSES.tsv 90 then and now. Not row count.

2. A PER-ROW TLC RUN ADDED ANYWHERE. harness/recall-gate.sh carries 12 verdict.sh or tlc invocation sites then and now. Not a new call site.

3. SCAFFOLD BATTERIES. Field 6 of REPS.tsv holds 156 scaffold entries then and now, so no SPEC row gained a scaffold. This was the bead's second-ranked hypothesis and it is the one that would have multiplied hardest.

4. THE SHARED ENTRY POINT, which the bead did not name and which multiplies across every call. harness/verdict.sh took 86 insertions over two commits and its CODE line count is unchanged at 203. Every one of those insertions was comment, the AMENDED grid from tla-lj1n and tla-vzu3. harness/Gate.tla untouched.

5. A PER-CALL FORK INSIDE A PER-ROW LOOP, which is this project's recurring performance defect and has produced itself twice in drill-gate.sh. harness/recall-gate.sh grew 131 lines, of which 43 are code. Its two forks, an awk over the INVENTORY and a printf for a tab, are both hoisted OUT of the loop into variables. No fork was added inside one.

SO THE PREMISE IS PROBABLY WRONG. The bead says something grew and nothing accounts for it. Nothing grew. The 196.6 readings of 2026-10-17 and the 258.2 reading of 2026-10-18 are of a suite that did not change in any way that costs time, so the difference is the box rather than the suite.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the bead's own cheap control, unrun because it needs a quiet box and about 350 s: bash scripts/test recall, reading the corpus gate row against the recall runner row at 105.0. If both are over by the same proportion the box is the cause and this bead is about measurement. title: TLC breaks its own Naturals.tla div contract on a negative dividend
description:
Found 2026-10-18 by the tla-7xql.2 author while baking level 0 swipe items. No prior record anywhere in this repo: git grep over main found nothing.

THE CONTRACT IS IN THE JAR. tla2tools v1.8.0's bundled Naturals.tla states

  a = b * (a \\div b) + (a % b)   for any integers with b > 0

MEASURED through PrintT on TLC 2026.07.31.184830:

  <<"-17 div 5", -3>>   <<"-17 mod 5", 3>>   <<"identity -17 5", -12>>
  <<"-9 div 4", -2>>    <<"-9 mod 4", 3>>    <<"identity -9 4", -5>>

5 * -3 + 3 is -12, not -17. 4 * -2 + 3 is -5, not -9.

THE REMAINDER IS THE HALF THAT OBEYS. -17 % 5 returns 3, which sits in 0..4
as the contract requires. So the quotient is the wrong one: it TRUNCATES
TOWARD ZERO where the contract forces rounding down. -17 \\div 5 should be -4,
and -4 * 5 + 3 is -17.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA. The whole v2 corpus takes
verdicts from TLC's exit codes, so an author writing an arithmetic item over
a negative dividend gets a baked verdict that is TLC's bug rather than the
truth. It caught three of 80 level 0 items. Those three were REPLACED rather
than relabeled, since baking them would have shipped the bug as the answer.

THE TRIPWIRE IS ALREADY IN. harness/test-swipe-level0.sh asserts the identity
is still broken, so a TLC that fixes \\div turns that suite red ON PURPOSE.
The row note in scripts/test says to read this bead before touching anything
if that happens.

WHAT TO SETTLE, and none of it is urgent.

1. Is this upstream's known behavior or a real divergence from the bundled
module's own comment? Read the Java (tlc2.module.Naturals or Integers) rather
than reasoning from the comment, and check the tlaplus issue tracker.
2. Should .claude/rules/tla-practice.md carry it? That file surveys published
specs rather than the toolchain, so probably not, and a bd memory may be the
right home. One is filed.
3. Does any shipped drill, reading, recall or completion item use \\div over a
possibly-negative dividend? Not scanned. That scan is the part with real risk
in it, because such an item would carry a wrong answer today.

Point 3 is the one worth doing first.

Files: (none yet, this is a scan plus a decision)

RED: INVARIANT: no shipped item in drill, reading, recall, completion or swipe
depends on a \\div whose dividend can be negative, or it carries a comment
saying it depends on TLC's truncation rather than on the module's contract.
notes:
2026-10-18, central. THE SCAN THIS BEAD CALLED ITS FIRST ACTION IS DONE AND NOTHING SHIPPED IS EXPOSED.

Point 3 of the description was the half with real risk in it: whether any
shipped item already depends on a \div with a possibly-negative dividend,
because such an item would carry a wrong answer today. It does not.

WHAT WAS SEARCHED, named rather than implied, per the CLAUDE.md rule that a
claim of absence names its search. GNU tools from a scratch script with a bash
shebang, because the Bash tool's grep is ugrep and lies on some shapes.

  22 \div lines   drill/ reading/ recall/ completion/ exercises/ chapter/,
                  every tracked .tla .cfg .tsv .md, via git ls-files
   6 \div lines   harness/fixtures/refinement/*/Concrete.tla
   4 \div lines   ~/tla-practice/, all copies of exercises/ch10

EVERY ONE HAS A PROVABLY NON-NEGATIVE DIVIDEND. The three that were not
obvious, and what settled each:

  Ex2GaugePanel  Chained(LAMBDA a: a \div 2, LAMBDA b: b - 12, 28) is
                 F(G(28)), so 16 \div 2. Gauges is {12, 28, 41, 55} and only
                 28 is passed.
  Josephus       USES.md's Pow2Below((k - 1) \div 2) is PROSE describing a
                 mutation rather than shipped code, and the else branch it
                 sits in has k >= 2, so k - 1 >= 1 either way.
  recall R014    Capacity \div 2, and recall/env/shunting.tla:16 reads
                 Capacity == 4.

The two surfaces I would have expected to miss, checked because the rule says
to ask which one you did not check:

  harness/fixtures  six refinement fixtures map level <- (ticks \div 3), and
                    ticks \in 0..6 is pinned by that module's own TypeOK with
                    Init at 0 and Tick guarded by ticks < 6. A negative
                    dividend there would have moved a gate's expected rc.
  the delivered tree  exercises/ has been frozen since 2026-08-12, so it could
                    carry a site the repo has since changed. It carries four
                    and all four are the same ch10 files. Ex3SettlingTank
                    looked like the risk, since Level counts down from 480,
                    and its own \ominus is saturating: IF x <= y THEN 0 ELSE
                    x - y, so Level never goes below 0.

NOT SEARCHED: swipe/, because a worker owns it right now and tla-7xql.2
already replaced the three items this bug caught. puzzles/, which is v1 and
out of scope.

AND THE % HALF NEEDS NO AUDIT AT ALL. The original measurement showed the
REMAINDER obeys the contract: -17 % 5 returns 3, inside 0..4 as Naturals.tla
requires. Only the quotient truncates. So every % site in the corpus is safe
by the same measurement that found the bug.

SO THE INVARIANT IN THIS BEAD'S RED LINE HOLDS TODAY, AND IT IS NOT GATED.
Nothing stops the next author adding a negative-dividend \div, and
gate-don't-advise says an invariant verified once by hand comes back. What
remains on this bead is the gate, and the cheap honest shape is z4f3's: pin
the 28 sites as a reviewed set and fire when a new \div site appears that is
not on it. 'Can be negative' is not statically decidable in general, but 'a
\div site nobody has reviewed' is, and that is enough to force a human to
read the dividend.

The other open question, whether this is upstream's known behavior or a real
divergence from the bundled module's comment, is unanswered and worth less
than the gate.
2026-10-18, central. CORRECTION TO MY OWN SCAN IN THE NOTE ABOVE. I reported 28 sites. The real figure over the same eight roots is 70 lines in 31 files. My pattern read .tla, .cfg, .tsv and .md, so it never looked at a shell file, and nine sites live in exercises/ch10/reports/mutants.sh, completion/verify-item.sh, recall/recall.sh, harness/fixtures/refinement/selftest.sh and swipe/level0/bake.sh. The rest of the gap is swipe/, which I excluded on purpose. One line is still unattributed, 23 against my 22 over the same extensions, and the worker marked it INFERRED rather than guessing. My note named three sites it settled and never enumerated all 22, so there is nothing to check it against. That is a defect in how I wrote the claim of completeness, which is the exact rule CLAUDE.md states.

A site not in the inventory fails the gate, which is the enforcement without deciding semantics. Watched red in four directions, and the worker reported that my two suggested experiments were the same direction and added a third. THE GATE CAUGHT THREE REAL SITES ON ITS FIRST DAY, the 12 \div 2 * 3 parse-failure example that landed in tla-7xql.10 an hour earlier. title: spike-measure.sh labels rc 12 'invariant violated' and the grid says it is not
description:
Found 2026-10-18 while measuring the 12/13 split for tla-lj1n and tla-vzu3.

harness/spike-measure.sh:247-248 maps the two codes to human-facing prose in
the spike report:

  12)  verdict="invariant violated"
  13)  verdict="property violated"

THE GRID SAYS BOTH LABELS ARE WRONG ON THREE CELLS. harness/verdict.sh now
carries it and harness/test-verdict.sh pins eleven of its cells.

  PROPERTY ~<>P on a spec with no liveness conjunct    rc 12, no invariant
                                                       anywhere in the .cfg
  PROPERTY []P over a state predicate                  rc 12, and TLC does
                                                       lift it, so the label
                                                       is defensible here
  PROPERTY P, bare, refuted by the initial state       rc 13, and it needs no
                                                       infinite behavior

So a spike report can read 'invariant violated' for a .cfg that declares no
INVARIANT, and 'property violated' is the only correct one of the pair.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A WORDING NIT. spike-measure.sh produces the
difficulty measurement a problem's VECTOR.md and spike report are built from,
and a human reads that column to decide what the spike showed. A reader who
takes 'invariant violated' at face value will go looking for the invariant.

WHAT I WOULD DO. Name the channel rather than the keyword, which is what the
codes actually report: 'safety or invariant channel reported' for 12 and
'liveness or implied-action channel reported' for 13. It is longer and it is
true. The short form that is also true is 'refuted' for both, with the code
printed beside it, since the report already carries rc in its own column.

THE ALTERNATIVE. Leave 12 and 13 as they are and add a note to the report
header. I would not take that, because the label travels into VECTOR.md and
the header does not.

title: Does the swipe rung move the recall rung
description:
This is the question the whole epic exists to answer, and it is the one the
literature could not.

SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND. No study trains truth-judgment over a formal model and
measures transfer to WRITING specifications. The search named: OpenAlex title
and full text, the 151-work citation set of Little 2012, targeted passes across
mathematics education, logic, proof, programming, formal methods, music
notation and chemistry notation, and the SIGCSE / ICER / ITiCSE grey
literature. Not reached, and most likely to hold it: PsycINFO systematically,
and the JRME back catalogue.

WHAT THE ADJACENT EVIDENCE SAYS, and it is not encouraging. Siu, Leahy and
Mann 2023, 62 participants judging whether sets of signal temporal logic
constraints would keep an agent safe, which is this task almost exactly:
validation accuracy 45 percent plus or minus 20, an affirmation bias
(significantly better on valid specs, worse on invalid), confidence
uncorrelated with correctness, and the overconfidence WORSE among those
familiar with formal methods. The peer-reviewed follow-up at NeurIPS 2024,
about 47 analysed: 62 to 67 percent across three conditions, none differing
from the others, and feedback did not help.

THE ONE POSITIVE EXISTENCE PROOF is Kellman's algebra perceptual learning
module, where students classified whether a transformation was legal and never
practiced solving, with large speed gains in equation solving. Its own
follow-up states the limit: robust for participants initially LESS proficient,
negligible for those initially proficient.

WHY FRANK CAN ANSWER THIS AND THE LITERATURE CANNOT. He already has a
production rung graded by exit code, recall/, 160 reps over 57 constructs. So
the measurement is available: build the swipe rung, keep drilling recall, and
watch whether recall accuracy on the overlapping constructs moves.

INSTRUMENTATION WARNINGS, both measured.

Do not tune on in-session swipe accuracy. Every finding in the spacing
literature says the schedule that looks worse in session is the one that pays
at delay, and Kornell 2009 found spacing more effective for 90 percent of
participants while 72 percent believed massing had worked better.

Confidence in this task carries no information, in three independent sources.
Koriat and Bjork explain the mechanism: a judgment made while the answer is
visible overstates readiness for a test where it is not, and a recognition
item is exactly that configuration. Their established remedy is test
experience rather than instruction, which is an argument for interleaving the
two rungs rather than running them apart.

Level 0 is the cheapest place to run this, because it is the same content
recall/REPS.tsv already drills in production.

Files: (measurement, no code footprint yet)

title: Read the TLA+ level per definition, so a generator dispatches instead of excluding
description:
Infrastructure for the level 1, 2 and 3 item kinds. Not needed for level 0.

MEASURED AND ALREADY PROTOTYPED by the research round, so this is adoption
rather than discovery. tla2tools.jar exposes the level on the semantic tree,
so it is read directly rather than scraped from an error message:

    SpecObj -> SANY.frontEndMain -> root.getOpDefs() -> OpDefNode.getLevel()

filtered by getOriginallyDefinedInModuleNode() == root, so EXTENDS-imported
definitions are dropped. It handles the modules/ family's inner modules and
surfaces instance-prefixed names like Below!Count with their levels.

COST: one SANY parse per module, NO TLC. 424 definitions across all 33 reading
models in 460 ms, against about 0.35 s for a single TLC run.

What it reads on reading/core/01-nim:

    vars 1 | TypeOK 1 | NimSum 1 | Init 1 | Take 2 | Next 2 | Spec 3
    NoEscape 3 | \oplus 0

Those match the levels SANY reported in its own ASSUME error messages exactly,
which is how the prototype was validated.

THE COUNTS, and they are the reason this bead exists. 49 level 0, 185 level 1,
113 level 2 (76 arity-0, 28 arity-1, 7 arity-2, 2 arity-3), 77 level 3. The
117 declared obligations were never the interesting set: 101 of the 185
level-1 definitions and 44 of the 77 level-3 ones are NOT declared
obligations, and those are precisely the ones that are not true-everywhere by
construction.

A Java driver is new ground for this repo. Decide deliberately whether it
lives here or whether the same thing is reachable through an existing channel,
and say which in the close reason.

Files: harness/levels/ (new), harness/test-levels.sh, scripts/test

RED: INVARIANT: every definition in every reading/ model gets a level in
{0,1,2,3}, EXTENDS-imported definitions are excluded, and the levels for
reading/core/01-nim match the table above exactly.
notes:
2026-10-18, central, merged at 59b47a3 (worker commit d4d364c). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD, both settled by a mutant that reproduces the old number.

1. THE 01-nim TABLE NAMES NINE DEFINITIONS AND THE MODULE DECLARES TEN. The
tenth is ZeroIsOneMoveAway at Nim.tla:38, level 1, and Nim.cfg:6 declares it
an INVARIANT. The suite pins the bead's nine verbatim, the tenth separately
with the omission in its label, and the count as exactly 10.

2. THE LEVEL-1 FREE COUNT IS 103, NOT 101. The bead's number came from
joining obligations to definitions by NAME ALONE. Five definitions share a
name with another model's obligation: Stamps!Gap, Brackets!Closes and
Chips!Held at level 0, Shelves!Held and Tickets!Waiting at level 1. Neither
level-1 one is declared in its own model, so the name-only join drops two
generable items. Mutant B joins by name and reproduces 84 declared and 101
free exactly, which is what settles it. Level 3's 33 and 44 matched because
its names happen not to collide. Also worth knowing: 2 of the 49 level 0
definitions ARE declared obligations, ClockFace!OrderIsSize and
ClockFace!Divides.

EVERYTHING ELSE REPRODUCES. 424 definitions, 49 / 185 / 113 / 77 by level,
level 2 arity 76 / 28 / 7 / 2, 117 declared obligations, 33 modules at SANY
rc 0, nothing outside 0..3, nothing past the EXTENDS filter. Fences!Below!Count
reads 1 and BitCounter!Abs!MFSpec reads 3, while Below!Span (LOCAL,
Fences.tla:7) is correctly not surfaced.

THE ROUTE DECISION THE BEAD ASKED FOR, measured rather than argued.

SANY's command line carries no level at all. -dls is rejected. -d mt prints
every top-level definition with no level beside any of them. -d dot writes a
.dot with zero occurrences of the word level. There is no flag.

The ASSUME refusal DOES carry a level and it is the wrong one. The level in
that message belongs to the APPLICATION, not the definition. \oplus
(Nim.tla:8) is one level 0 operator of arity 2, and the channel gives two
answers: ASSUME (a (+) b) = 0 reports level 1, while ASSUME (Heap (+) Heap) =
1 raises no level error at all. 37 of the 113 level 2 definitions take
arguments, so that channel answers wrongly IN SILENCE for every one of them.
Cost was the secondary objection: 247 ms per probe, so 105 s for the corpus
plus 424 generated modules.

So the semantic tree it is, and ONE COSMETIC CORRECTION to the bead's route:
both frontEndMain overloads are deprecated on this build, so the worker used
SANY.parse(..., SanySettings.defaultSettings()).
getOriginallyDefinedInModuleNode() is on OpDefOrDeclNode, which is why javap
OpDefNode does not list it.

NO BUILD STEP, which answers the 'new ground for this repo' question in the
bead. Java's single-file source launcher compiles in memory: 371 ms once per
invocation, 900 ms against 529 ms precompiled with byte-identical output. No
.class, no .jar, no .gitignore entry, and nothing for scripts/setup,
scripts/cibuild or the workflow to learn. CI already runs setup-java temurin
21, which is a JDK.

COST: 0.93 s wall for the whole corpus, 4.07 s user, 0.21 s system, so no
fork pressure. One JVM per module instead is 17.77 s. The one-JVM output was
diffed against 33 separate JVMs and came back IDENTICAL at 424 rows each.

ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND BY WATCHING A TEST FAIL. getLevel() throws
WrongInvocationException: getLevel called before levelCheck when semantic
analysis failed, and the throw escaped per-module handling, so ONE
UNPARSEABLE MODULE ENDED THE PROCESS and every module after it went
unreported, at rc 1 with plausible partial output. Fixed at
Levels.java:143-156, and the suite now asserts that a module after a broken
one is still reported in full.

THE INTERFACE THE NEXT BEAD CONSUMES:

  harness/levels/levels.sh [--corpus] [--all] [--defs-only] [--tally] <module.tla>...

  MOD  <path>  <module-name>  <sany-rc>  <definition-count>
  DEF  <module>  <name>  <level>  <arity>  <origin>  <local|exported>  <obligation|free|no-cfg>

The generable set is field 4 for the level and field 8 == 'free'.

TWO SMALL THINGS THE WORKER REPORTED AND DID NOT WIDEN INTO, both worth a
bead if anybody cares. scripts/bootstrap:62 says 'Java 17+' and checks java
rather than javac, which a JRE satisfies, and a JRE-only box hits levels.sh's
99 path with a clear reason. And harness/test-indeterminate.sh's 99-collision
scan walks harness/*.sh non-recursively, so harness/levels/levels.sh sits
outside it. That suite is green and nothing breaks, but the glob may want
widening.

Registered slow at 10.0 s from nine readings over two boxes and two load
conditions, 6.1 to 9.1 s. 61 assertions, four mutants, 0 failed.

No build step: Java's single-file source launcher compiles in memory, so nothing changes in scripts/setup, cibuild or the workflow, and CI already installs a JDK. The route was measured against both alternatives and the notes say why neither works, the sharp one being that the ASSUME refusal reports the APPLICATION's level rather than the definition's and so answers wrongly in silence for the 37 level-2 definitions that take arguments. Two corrections to the bead, each settled by a mutant that reproduces the old number: 01-nim declares ten definitions and the table named nine, and the level-1 free count is 103 rather than 101 because the bead joined obligations by name alone. title: Level 0 items: the corpus that needs no model screen
description:
Frank's first pick, and the exploration found a reason neither of us had going
in: a level 0 item needs NO MODEL SCREEN AT ALL.

A level 0 expression has no variables, no primes and no temporal operators.
`Cardinality(SUBSET {1,2,3}) = 8`. It is the only one of the four levels that
can run at flow speed on a phone, and it is the only one that is purely
authored, so the reading corpus bounds it not at all.

MEASURED. `ASSUME PrintT(e)` is already level 0, so none of the pinning
machinery is needed. Batched, one module, N assumes:

    N=1     377 ms   N=100   411 ms   N=1000  540 ms   N=4000  1117 ms
    per item: 377 ms / 4.11 ms / 0.54 ms / 0.279 ms

That is half the cost of a pinned-state item, because there is no INSTANCE.

ONE HAZARD, found by the research agent's own generator bug. An evaluation
error inside a batched ASSUME aborts the WHOLE BATCH at rc 10
ASSUMPTION_FAILED, not 75, and only the items before it print. So batch the
well-formed and run suspected-ill-formed ones singly. The bug that found it is
worth keeping as an item: `Cardinality({1,2} \X 1..7)` parses as
`({1,2} \X 1) .. 7`, because `\X` binds tighter than `..`.

WHY THIS ONE FIRST, beyond the cost. Level 0 is exactly the content
recall/REPS.tsv already drills in PRODUCTION. Running the same content in
recognition gives the comparison the literature could not supply, which is the
whole open question on the epic.

The 49 level 0 definitions already in reading/ are a starting point, not the
corpus. The corpus is authored.

Depends on the stem-blind gate for shipping, not for building.

Files: swipe/ (new), harness/test-swipe-level0.sh, scripts/test

RED: INVARIANT: every shipped level 0 item has a TLC-computed verdict, a
declared kind tag, and no reference to any variable or primed expression.

Registered slow at 31.0 s from 30599 / 30301 / 30606 ms at load 1.69, so the author's reading was never contended. THE BRIEF'S EXIT-CODE TABLE WAS WRONG AT LEVEL 0 and the worker caught it: a refuted constant INVARIANT lands on rc 151, which the brief put in the ill-formed set, so following it would have sent every false item down instead of left. The channel is a pair of ASSUME runs needing no spec. Most-common-label base rate 37.5% per template, computed from the corpus, which is the chance floor tla-7xql.1 needs. Found a TLC bug with no prior record in the repo, filed as tla-7n7e, and the suite carries a tripwire that reddens if TLC is fixed.
