title: Does a post-run question that states the lesson count as a telegraph?
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: needs Frank's ruling, not a default.

TWO WORKERS RAISED THIS INDEPENDENTLY on 2026-10-14, from two different drill
families, while doing the telegraph self-ranking no 2026-10-12 author had
completed. Neither was looking for it.

THE SHAPE. A drill prompt describes a system in prose and shows no TLA+. The
gate's check 1 passes it, and in these families that clean result is unwaived:
no prompt in sequences or functions-records contains a single operator token or
even a backtick. But several prompts close with a question that states the
item's lesson in English, such as "say how you stopped the treated list growing
without bound" or "what the step that raises one autoclave's pressure has to
say about the other two".

THE FUNCTIONS-RECORDS WORKER'S COUNT. Five of its eight items close with such a
question, and each ANSWER.md already flags its own as the honest caveat, so the
authors saw it and kept it. Its words: "whether a post-run question counts as a
telegraph at all is a corpus-level decision I don't think is settled, and it is
worth settling once rather than eight times."

THE DISTINCTION IT USED, which is the candidate ruling: an unavoidable domain
description is not a telegraph, a gratuitous methodological instruction is. On
that reading, 06-depot-cover is the worst in its family, because the prompt
BODY states the full semantics of the merge including which operand wins, so a
reader who knows the operator writes it straight off the page. It is also the
most defensible, because without saying which side wins the roster is not
defined.

WHERE IT IS NOT DEFENSIBLE. The sequences worker ranked 07-pneumatic-tube worst
in its family and the case is cleaner: the prompt says "you'll find the tube on
its own doesn't hold enough to say it, and you'll have to add what it needs".
The auxiliary history variable IS that item's entire lesson, and unlike
06-depot-cover nothing about the scenario required saying it. Its author calls
the caveat "a large one" and "half the discovery", and kept it so a reader is
not left with nothing to check.

Also named: sequences 03-returns-desk, whose closing question hands over the
whole discovery that the prose is silent about order, mitigated because all
three encodings are right. Then sequences 04 and 08, and functions-records 05,
both moderate.

WHAT A RULING WOULD CHANGE. Nothing mechanical: the gate already passes these
and nobody is proposing it should fail an English sentence. What it changes is
whether an author may buy a reader a foothold at the cost of the discovery, and
whether a post-run question is the right place to do it. The post-run position
is the authors' own defence, since the reader has already committed to a shape
before reading it.

TWO THINGS NOT TO CONFLATE WITH IT. A published expected state count is a
foreclosing row rather than a telegraph: it tells a reader their answer is
wrong without telling them why. And a waiver is for a SHOWN OPERATOR that could
not be avoided, which is a different mechanism with its own syntax in META.md.

Files: drill/sequences/, drill/functions-records/
notes:
A THIRD FAMILY, and it sharpens the question rather than just adding a count.

The modules worker judged all eight of its items and found the same shape: "All
eight state the mechanism in English, none shows a token, and four leave the
reader little beyond the spelling." Its ranking, worst first:

  07  "one declaration before its definition that an ordinary definition
      doesn't", "why does a definition need it to name itself" -- RECURSIVE
      defined in full with the word removed
  03  "which of the two ways of bringing a module in would have kept it" --
      gives that there are two and that one keeps the guard
  08  "what does the instance have to become so it can be filled later" --
      the construct's English name plus the fix's shape
  06  "neither rule gets a definition of its own"

That family is the hardest case for a ruling, because INSTANCE, WITH and ! are
difficult to describe without naming them. A ruling that forbids stating the
mechanism in English may be unsatisfiable for the modules family specifically.

A SECOND MECHANISM, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION, and it needs its own line
in the ruling. Item 06's prompt table quotes SANY's own error text, "refused:
something of arity 1 was expected". The worker recommends dropping it and left
it for central. Central left it too, so that it is decided once here.

The argument for keeping it: a drill prompt already publishes the expected
distinct-state count, which tells a reader their answer is wrong without
telling them why. Quoting the exact error the wrong answer produces is the same
category of foreclosing row. The argument for dropping it: the error text names
the mechanism more precisely than any English paraphrase in the eight prompts
above, and it is the only instance in the corpus of a prompt quoting a tool.

So the ruling wants three lines, not one:
  1. Does a post-run question that states the lesson count as a telegraph?
  2. If yes, does the modules family get an exemption, since its constructs
     resist description?
  3. May a prompt quote the error text the wrong answer produces?

NO WAIVERS WERE ADDED by any of the three workers, and the modules worker gave
the reason: a waiver suppresses a flagged token, nothing was flagged, so a
waiver would plant a permanent WAIVER line against no finding. Neither of the
two things it would change is reachable by waiver anyway, since "arity 1" has
no inventory row and lowercase "instance" is below the gate's case-sensitive
match by design. That is the right reading of the mechanism.

RULED 2026-10-14 by Frank. All three questions answered, central's recommendation taken.

Q1. NOT a category ban. A post-run question that states the lesson in English is
not a telegraph as such. The telegraph mechanism exists to stop a prompt showing
the reader the TLA+ it is asking them to produce, and an English sentence does
not do that.

THE TEST IS PER ITEM, and it is one question: does removing the sentence leave
the item underdetermined? If the prompt cannot pose its problem or publish a
reproducible count without it, keep it. If the reader could have reached the
answer from the rest of the prompt and the sentence only shortens the search,
cut it.

Q2. NO family exemption for modules. The per-item test is already per item, so a
family-level carve-out is a worse instrument than the test. INSTANCE, WITH and !
being hard to describe is exactly what the test measures: where the English is
needed to pose the problem it survives, and where it is not it does not. One
modules item still fails the test under this reading, so the exemption would
have protected the wrong item.

Q3. KEEP the error text. A prompt may quote the error the wrong answer produces.
It is the same category as the published distinct-state count: it tells a reader
their answer is wrong without telling them what is right. The objection that it
names the mechanism more precisely than the surrounding prose is true and does
not change the category. modules/06 keeps "refused: something of arity 1 was
expected".

WHAT MOVES TODAY. Two items fail the test clearly and both are being fixed.

sequences/07-pneumatic-tube. The sentence "You'll find the tube on its own
doesn't hold enough to say it, and you'll have to add what it needs" is cut. The
item is not underdetermined without it: "State the rule in the last sentence so
that TLC can check it" poses the problem in full, and the reader discovers the
tube is insufficient by trying. The author kept it so a reader would not be left
with nothing to check, and the right answer to that is a foreclosing row rather
than a hint. The prompt gains a stated model and a published count instead.

Central measured both halves of that trade today:
  harness/verdict.sh -c .../TubeRef.cfg       -> rc 0, 129 distinct states
  harness/verdict.sh -c .../TubeCountOnly.cfg -> rc 0,  57 distinct states
TubeCountOnly is tube plus two integer counters, which is the trap most readers
walk into, and it passes clean. 57 against a published 129 forecloses it. The
counter version can also express "stop once four have gone in" (SentBound ==
sentCount <= 4), so stating that bound in the prompt does not telegraph the
history lists.

modules/07-the-hoist-and-the-crates. Question 1's first sentence, "The sum over
a set needs one declaration before its definition that an ordinary definition
doesn't", is RECURSIVE defined in full with only the keyword removed. It is also
redundant with the table, whose third row already reads "the sum written without
its one-line declaration" and carries the SANY error. Cut the sentence, keep the
question, and reword the row label so it says what was done rather than naming
the construct class.

WHAT DOES NOT MOVE TODAY, with the reading recorded so the audit does not
re-derive it:

functions-records/06-depot-cover  PASSES. Without saying which operand wins the
roster is not defined, so the item is underdetermined without it.
modules/06  PASSES. "neither rule gets a definition of its own" is a constraint
on the answer, which is part of posing the task.
modules/03  PASSES, marginally. "which of the two ways of bringing a module in"
names the category without naming either construct, and rows two and four supply
the evidence. Re-read it in the audit.
modules/08  FAILS, mildly. "what does the instance have to become so it can be
filled later" hands over that the fix is a transformation of the instance, and
the first half of the same question poses the problem on its own.
sequences/03-returns-desk  FAILS the letter of the test and forecloses nothing,
since all three encodings are accepted. Audit it.
sequences/04, sequences/08, functions-records/05  moderate, unexamined by
central. Audit.

The remaining sweep across all 64 items is filed separately. This bead closes on
the ruling plus the two clear fixes.
close_reason: Frank ruled all three questions: not a category ban, the test is per item (does removing the sentence leave the item underdetermined), no modules exemption, and a prompt may quote the error the wrong answer produces. Two items moved. sequences/07-pneumatic-tube traded its hint for a published 129, measured against TubeCountOnly's clean 57, commit c3d6342. modules/07 lost question 1's definitional sentence, its row label and then question 3's leak, commits 60215ed and b748d21. The corpus-wide sweep is tla-3hwj. Drawer drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_1129be84450b30408259bfb1, section D1.

title: Five family helper scripts under two names do one job
description:
Landing the four pending drill families gives FOUR scripts under TWO names
doing the same job at four line counts, and completion/verify-item.sh is a
fifth cousin:

  drill/control-state/verify-all.sh       77 lines  on main
  drill/temporal/verify-item.sh           42 lines  on main
  drill/functions-records/verify-all.sh   59 lines  arrives with tla-pmm2.7
  drill/sets/verify-item.sh               34 lines  arrives with tla-pmm2.7
  completion/verify-item.sh                         a different channel, same shape

THE TWO DESIGNS ARE NOT EQUIVALENT, and one of them is right.

drill/temporal/verify-item.sh is GENERIC. It takes an item directory, walks
every .cfg in its verify/ tree, drives harness/verdict.sh, and prints stem, rc,
verdict token and distinct states. It handles a cfg with no same-stem module by
reading verify/MODULE or a '\* MODULE:' line in the cfg, and it passes -d when
the cfg carries CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE, which is exactly what the gate does.

drill/control-state/verify-all.sh is a HARDCODED TABLE of 29 rows naming every
module and its expected rc, and it calls tlc directly rather than through
verdict.sh. It exits 1 on any mismatch, which is useful, but the table goes
stale the moment an item changes and it bypasses the one place the exit-code
table lives.

So the consolidation is: one generic driver, taking an item or a family, driving
harness/verdict.sh, with the mismatch exit code the control-state one has. Then
delete the other three and fix the ANSWER.md prose that cites them by name.

WHY THIS IS NOT PART OF tla-pmm2.7. Four parallel workers cannot share one
refactor, and two of the four scripts are already on main outside any worker's
footprint. Each tla-pmm2.7 worker was told to leave its family's script alone.
Run this after that wave merges.

WATCH FOR: several ANSWER.md files cite their family helper by name, e.g.
drill/functions-records/02-charging-bays/ANSWER.md says "Each row is a line of
bash drill/functions-records/verify-all.sh 02". Deleting the script without
fixing the prose leaves an answer pointing at a missing file.

Both surviving names are mode 644, so they are invoked with a bash prefix,
which the isolation harness sometimes refuses. Consider the exec bit as part of
this bead.

Files: drill/control-state/verify-all.sh, drill/temporal/verify-item.sh, drill/functions-records/verify-all.sh, drill/sets/verify-item.sh

title: Nothing gates that build-docs.sh still publishes the reading probe block
description:
Found by the tla-fwkz.2.8 worker, 2026-10-13, and it is that bead's own bug
class pointed at the publisher instead of the source.

tla-fwkz.2.8 normalized all 25 USES.md files to one section, '## What the
properties rest on', and taught scripts/build-docs.sh to publish it in its own
collapsed block. harness/reading-gate.sh check 6 now gates the SOURCE shape: an
item whose USES.md lacks the section is a finding.

Nothing gates the other half. A refactor of the publisher's reading section
would keep check 6 green and silently stop publishing the block, which is
exactly the failure that bead existed to fix: the prose was in 16 source files
and reached the page from none of them.

The verification that found it was a hand-run grep, which is the advisory shape
gate-don't-advise rules out.

WHAT TO BUILD. harness/test-build-docs-reading.sh, the third sibling of
test-build-docs-chapter.sh and test-build-docs-exercises.sh. The reading
section of the publisher has no suite at all today, which is about 200 lines of
generator with nothing on it, so this is wider than the one block.

Assert at minimum: every family directory under reading/ gets a page; every
item gets a section on its family page; the spec is copied from the .tla rather
than re-typed; the three collapsed blocks all appear and in the order config,
properties-rest-on, constructs; and the probe prose of an item whose USES.md
carries it reaches the page. The last one is the regression: grep a sentence
that was dropped before 2026-10-13, such as 'Swapping it for' in
docs/reading/temporal.md, which returned 0 then and 1 now.

Follow test-build-docs-exercises.sh's shape rather than inventing one. Its
header explains why the expected set is DERIVED from the tree by an independent
glob rather than imported from the generator: a narrowed glob otherwise leaves
the real-tree assertion passing because the expected set shrinks to match.
Pattern to copy for the link half is test-build-docs-chapter.sh:100-113.

Files: harness/test-build-docs-reading.sh, scripts/test

RED: GIVEN scripts/build-docs.sh with the properties-rest-on block removed from
its reading section WHEN the suite runs THEN it fails and names the block.
notes:
BUILT AND MERGED 2026-10-14 as 864fcbb. harness/test-build-docs-reading.sh,
1213 lines, 258 assertions, registered as "fast|2.2|docs reading section".

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS DESCRIPTION, both from the author.

THE LINE POINTER WAS WRONG. This bead says "Pattern to copy for the link half
is test-build-docs-chapter.sh:100-113". Those lines are the mk_minirepo header
comment. The link half is check_links() at
harness/test-build-docs-chapter.sh:249-283, which is what the author copied,
along with its negative control.

THE BEAD'S OWN RED LINE IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and the author
measured why. The RED asks for the block REMOVED. It also ran the block
RETITLED, from "What the properties rest on" to "Why the properties hold", and
under that mutation the named sentinel 'Swapping it for' is STILL ON THE PAGE.
So the hand-run grep this bead was built on would have called a retitled block
a pass. Only the block-membership comparison catches it, and that is the
argument for keeping both halves rather than just the sentinel.

Measured failure counts per mutation: family glob narrowed 23, item glob
narrowed 19, spec reflowed 27, blocks reordered 27 and nothing else in the suite
moved, block retitled 53, block emission deleted 55.

TWO THINGS THE AUTHOR FOUND THAT ARE NOT ABOUT THIS SUITE.

harness/test-pipefail.sh read a logical-or as a pipe. All three of its patterns

title: Gate the completion corpus, because three draft defects were caught by reading
description:
Part of tla-rmuf. Nine completion items landed on 2026-10-13 and nothing checks
the corpus. Per-item verification is completion/verify-item.sh against that
item's own EXPECT, which answers "is this item solvable" and nothing else.

Three defects appeared in drafts during the authoring wave and all three were
caught by a person reading. Read tla-rmuf's notes for the measurements. Design
drawers: drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_83cde54858d6c07eac038766 for the item
contract, drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_5ea72b7f39dcd04cee6decb5 for the wave.

WHAT THE GATE MUST CHECK.

1. ONE MACHINE PER HOLE. For an item with N holes, each broken machine must be
caught by exactly one hole. This is the check that matters most, because the
reference item shipped a draft where a correct second claim caught the first
mutant unaided and the first hole was unchecked. The gate can measure it: fill
each hole with TRUE in turn and require the signature to differ from the
reference row in exactly the position EXPECT associates with that hole.

2. A HOLE MUST BE FALSIFIABLE. The both-TRUE signature must differ from the
reference signature. An item where they match has at least one hole nothing
checks.

3. NO TELEGRAPH, PER OPERATOR, OVER EVERY SHOWN FILE. Each item declares which
operator each hole needs, and that operator must not appear in any file the
learner sees, machines included. Two authors fixed a leak in a MACHINE rather
than in Claims.tla. Per OPERATOR and not per drill/INVENTORY.md row: K013
covers \cup as well as \subseteq, and a row-granularity check flags the
reference item wrongly.

4. NO STRAY FILE UNDER work/. pcal writes a <Module>.old backup beside every
module it rewrites, and scripts/deliver-completion.sh delivers work/
recursively by design. One author's first --check listed three .old files as
about to land. Refuse a work/ tree holding a file no EXPECT stem accounts for,
other than Claims.tla.

5. EVERY EXPECT STEM RESOLVES to a .tla and a .cfg under work/.

ONE EXEMPTION IS REQUIRED, not optional. A PlusCal terminal-state hole cannot
pass check 3, structurally: pcal writes Terminating == pc = "Done" /\ UNCHANGED
vars into every translation that can finish, so the guard is shown by
construction. completion/pluscal/01-squares names this in its META.md. Build a
per-item exemption that carries a reason in the item, not a blanket pass for
the family.

COST. Checks 1 and 2 run TLC, so this is a slow-tier suite. Checks 3, 4 and 5
are static. Give the script a --static-only flag the way harness/drill-gate.sh
does, so the fast tier can carry the static half.

Files: harness/completion-gate.sh, harness/test-completion-gate.sh, scripts/test

RED: GIVEN an item whose second hole is filled with TRUE in its committed
Claims.tla WHEN harness/completion-gate.sh runs THEN it reports a finding
naming that hole. AND GIVEN an item with a stray .old file under work/ THEN it
reports a finding naming the file.

WORK-STRAY-FILE naming the file. That first finding code exists BECAUSE the RED

names the item and not the hole.

even though its machine shows seen \cup {pos'} and K013 covers both operators.
Part 2b reproduces it as a one-change pair, \subseteq against \cup in the

NO GATE SEES THIS CLASS. harness/reading-gate.sh checks shape, the phone bound, the recorded rc and that the .cfg declares an obligation. Two models teaching the same thing both pass. The cost lands on Frank, who reads them back to back.

A PARALLEL WAVE MAKES IT WORSE BY CONSTRUCTION, because no worker can see what a sibling is writing. The pluscal author only caught the core collision because it read the landed six and then happened to re-read main.

THE CHEAP FIX. Every USES.md carries a 'Subject:' line. Derive the list mechanically and paste it into each brief:

  grep -h -A2 '^# USES' reading/*/*/USES.md

The brief then says: here are the 20 subjects that exist, do not write a 21st that restates one. That costs central one command per wave.

THE OTHER HALF IS HARDER AND MAY NOT BE WORTH IT. Two models can share a subject line and teach different things, and two can have different subjects and teach the same fact. Central kept exactly that case on purpose: reading/pluscal/03-contend and reading/temporal/04-contention both teach weak against strong fairness, and they stay because one shows why it is needed and the other shows the syntax for asking. So a mechanical subject check would have flagged a pair central wants. I would not gate this, which makes it the rare case where the nudge is right and gate-don't-advise does not apply: a human is supposed to weigh in.

title: A dispatched worker cannot write its report outside the worktree, so the crash-survival instruction does not work
description:
Found by the tla-fwkz.2.5 worker, 2026-10-13, and it will hit every report-only dispatch from here on.

bd memory a-report-only-dispatch-loses-everything-if-the says to tell every worker to write its report to a file as well as returning it, because a report-only dispatch is lost if the dispatching session dies before the notification arrives. Two red-teams were nearly lost that way on 2026-08-07 and a screen.sh lane WAS lost.

Central's briefs therefore name an absolute path outside the worktree. ~/.claude/hooks/edit-write-pwd-guard.sh BLOCKS that Write. Its only documented bypass is an environment variable, which no agent can set from inside its own session.

THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE edit-after-failure-guard GAP already recorded in .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md: a hook whose remedy is unreachable from where the hook fires.

THE SECOND HALF IS THE WORSE HALF. The worker got the file out by writing it inside the worktree and then running a Bash cp. So a Bash cp walks straight through a guard that stops the Write tool. A guard that blocks the audited tool and not the shell is not a boundary, it is a speed bump on the honest path.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is two separate questions.

1. Where should a worker report land? Options are a path the guard admits, a worktree-internal path central harvests before pruning, or nothing outside the return value with the memory amended to say so. The worktree-internal route is the cheapest and it already works: central reads the file from .claude/worktrees/agent-<id>/ before pruning, and the brief then carries no absolute path at all. That is the recommendation.

2. Should the guard cover Bash writes? That is loom's call, not this project's, since the hook is loom's. Report it rather than patching a copy.

Until this is settled, every brief in this repo should tell the worker to write its report inside its own worktree, and central should harvest it from there.

title: Normalize the reading corpus's USES.md construct lists, after the wave lands
description:
Measured 2026-10-13 on main at 53c63c6: all 8 reading modules carry an EXTENDS line, and only 2 USES.md files declare 'EXTENDS (module import)'. The two are reading/sets/01-clockface and 02-antichain, authored by the tla-fwkz.2.5 worker, which reported the divergence itself rather than quietly matching the six.

So either the first six under-declare or the sets pair over-declares, and the same question applies to every other skeleton construct that appears in all 8 modules.

WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED IN PLACE RIGHT NOW. Seven sibling workers own reading/<family>/ each while this is filed, so editing a landed USES.md would collide. reading/sequences/ is the one family with no worker, which is why it is not simply done.

WHAT TO DECIDE. A construct a reader meets in the module text is exercised, and EXTENDS is in the text of every module. That argues for declaring it everywhere. The counter is that a construct claimed by all 19 models tells Frank nothing about any one of them, and USES.md's second heading already reads 'Constructs from other families, also exercised' rather than 'constructs this item drills'.

Recommendation is declare it, because the file's own heading says exercised. Resolve it once over the whole corpus rather than per item.

WHAT TO BUILD. Pick the rule, apply it to every USES.md, and then GATE it: harness/reading-gate.sh should check that a module's declared construct list is consistent with what its text actually contains, for at least the mechanically checkable constructs (EXTENDS, CONSTANT, ASSUME, VARIABLE, UNCHANGED, the fairness operators). Gate-don't-advise. An ungated convention drifts on the next wave, which is exactly what this bead is reporting.

Files: reading/, harness/reading-gate.sh, harness/test-reading.sh

RED: GIVEN a module whose text carries EXTENDS and whose USES.md omits it WHEN harness/reading-gate.sh runs THEN it reports a finding and names the construct.
notes:
A SECOND GATE GAP FOR THE SAME FILE, found in wave 1 and worth fixing in the same pass.

Check 1's shape test reads the item directory off the FILESYSTEM, so an untracked file reddens it. A bare tlc run that finds an error leaves <Name>_TTrace_<n>.tla and .bin beside the module, and those are already gitignored at .gitignore:2-3, so they can never reach a commit and the finding is pure noise. The tla-fwkz.2.6 author hit it on both items and deleted four artifacts by hand.

Two ways to fix it. Skip paths git ignores, which is exact but puts a git call inside the gate. Or name the _TTrace_ pattern specifically, which is narrower and cheaper. I would take the second, because the gate otherwise has no git dependency and the artifact class is stable.

ALSO WORTH ONE LINE OF TEXT. SHAPE-EXTRA-ENTRY's message today names only scripts/build-docs.sh as the reason for the three-entry rule. The tla-fwkz.2.7 author measured a two-.tla item and got SHAPE-STEM-MISMATCH naming the LIBRARY as the item's module, because sort puts Lib.tla before Main.tla. The message pointed at the wrong file. If the one-module rule is meant to stand, the finding text should say so and should name the nested-submodule route that works.
A THIRD GAP IN THE SAME FILE, and this one loses content rather than
drifting. USES.md has two incompatible shapes for the probe prose, the
paragraph that says what to change to make the run go red. Measured
2026-10-13 on main at fcd020c.

Shape A puts it between the 'rc:' line and the first '## ' heading.
reading/core/01-nim, reading/temporal/04-contention and
reading/sets/02-antichain do this.

Shape B puts it in a '## What the measurements say' section.
reading/modules/03-fences does this.

scripts/build-docs.sh publishes neither region on purpose and both by
accident. reading_subject() takes 'Subject:' through the next blank line.
reading_constructs() takes the first '## ' to the end. So Shape B's prose
publishes, demoted, INSIDE the block titled 'Constructs, and the recorded
exit code', where it is not constructs. Shape A's prose is dropped
entirely: grep -c 'Swapping it for' docs/reading/temporal.md returns 0
while reading/temporal/04-contention/USES.md carries that sentence.

15 of 25 USES.md files carry at least one rc mention outside the 'rc:'
line, so this is most of the corpus rather than a corner.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE EXTENDS QUESTION. Every one of the 25 items
checks clean at rc 0, verified by reading the rc line out of all 25 files.
So the probe sentence is the only thing in an item that says which
construct is carrying the property. Without it the page shows a module
that passes and gives no way to tell what would stop it passing.

WHAT TO ADD. Pick one shape, convert the corpus to it, publish that region
in its own collapsed block, and gate the shape in harness/reading-gate.sh
alongside the construct-declaration check. Name the block for what it holds
rather than for the word 'measurements', which reads as a lab report.

Files: add scripts/build-docs.sh to the line above.
close_reason:
Landed in e18e5fe, merged as 2c9481c.

28 files, +710/-111: 25 USES.md, harness/reading-gate.sh, harness/test-reading.sh,
scripts/build-docs.sh. No deviation from the Files line.

VERIFIED BY CENTRAL IN THE MERGED TREE, independently of the gate that passed.
A script of my own compared module text against declared bullets for all seven
gated constructs over all 25 items: EXTENDS 23 in text and 23 declared,
CONSTANT 19/19, ASSUME 14/14, VARIABLE 25/25, UNCHANGED 15/15, WF_ 9/9, SF_
2/2, zero mismatches anywhere. That turns '100 of 105 rows claimed' into
'7 constructs checked against the text' for the first time.

reading-gate.sh over the real tree: 25 items, 0 findings, 0 unchecked, VERDICT
OK. test-reading.sh 80 passed, 0 failed, up from 53. lint clean over 56 files,
comment gate 25 passed.

PIECE 1 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. All 25 USES.md carry one section, '## What the
properties rest on', and it publishes in its own collapsed block between the
config block and the construct list. Measured on the rebuilt tree: 25 blocks
across the 8 pages, 25 of 25 source files carrying the section, and
grep -c 'Swapping it for' docs/reading/temporal.md returns 1 where it returned
0 before. The fences prose is now at its own block rather than inside the one
titled Constructs.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG TWICE AND THE WORKER MEASURED BOTH TIMES.

I said two incompatible shapes. It was five placements under six heading names,
16 files with between-region prose rather than three, and a fourth placement I
did not know about: prose inside a Constructs section, seven files, all
declaration notes, correctly placed and left alone.

I said the gate's directory check should read tracked files. It cannot.
git -C <mktemp dir> ls-files exits 128 because a fixture is not a git
repository, so every fixture would have reported an empty corpus. Naming TLC's
artifacts is also better on merits, since a stray .bak should fire.

THE CHECK STOPS AT SEVEN CONSTRUCTS FOR A MEASURED REASON. Those seven are
one-to-one with one drill/INVENTORY.md row each. K013 covers \cup, \cap and
\subseteq together, so a per-row scan there reports something true of the row
and false of the module, which is the K013 finding from the completion wave
appearing again from the other side.

FOURTEEN LANDED ITEMS WERE UNDER-DECLARING, thirteen missing EXTENDS and one
missing WF_, with zero over-declarations. All fixed. The only prose deleted
corpus-wide was nim's note saying EXTENDS was deliberately not claimed, which
the decision falsified.

Five items carried no probe prose at all and the worker authored sections from
its own probes. Three results worth knowing: Brackets' guard reports TypeOK
rather than PrefixSound, so two named invariants sit one behind the other on
one guard; Quorums' probe still gives rc 0 because a strict majority of four
cannot be mustered twice; Matching's guard is redundant given Involution.

Its first construct fixture tested nothing and it caught that itself with a
before-and-after count: the fixture used an item whose text has no UNCHANGED,
so the sed deleted a bullet that was never there.

TWO THINGS LEFT OPEN RATHER THAN DONE. Filed as tla-n7dv: nothing gates that
the publisher still publishes the block, which is this bead's own bug class
aimed at the other half. And the reading suite's budget is stale, 4.1s measured
at 6 items against a 25-item corpus now reading 16.4s. The worker declined to
re-base it on a box reading load average 3.10 and said so, which is the right
call and is what the header's own text asks for. Untouched main already
measured 13.4s, so the nudge was firing before this bead.

title: Two more sites report a declined cache as a skipped check
description:
tla-dnwi fixed ONE of three sites that make the same mistake. Its worker
found the other two, left them alone because they were outside the bead's
evidence and had no control behind them, and reported them. That was the
right call and this is the follow-up.

THE MISTAKE. Declining to cache is not failing to check. A run that verified
every job and recorded none of them has given a complete answer, and
reporting UNCHECKED turns it into rc 99, CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN, which is false.

  harness/drill-gate.sh:1325   unchecked when the jar or verdict.sh cannot
                               be hashed
  harness/drill-gate.sh:1874   unchecked when the state file cannot be
                               written

The second is the clearer one. Its own message says the run verified N jobs
and recorded none of them, which is a complete answer dressed as a
non-answer.

THE FIX IS THE ONE tla-dnwi ALREADY LANDED. Both become declared, with the
epilogue block saying what was not cached and why. Read :1316-1318 and
:1999-2002 for the shape, and declared()'s comment at :427-436 for the
category test: what claim went unanswered, and the answer is none, because no
check named verify-cache exists whose failure leaves the corpus unverified.

CONTROLS. The write-failure one is cheap: point --state into a directory that
does not exist, and the run should verify every job, say it recorded nothing,
and exit 0. The hash-failure arm is harder to reach, since it needs a file
that resolves and then fails sha256sum. An unreadable file with the read bit
cleared is one route. If you cannot reach it honestly, say so and leave the
arm uncontrolled rather than writing an assertion that passes for the wrong
reason.

Watch each one fail before believing it.

Files: harness/drill-gate.sh, harness/test-drill.sh

RED: GIVEN --changed-only and a --state path inside a directory that does not
exist WHEN the gate runs over a clean corpus THEN it exits 0, verifies every
job, and says it recorded nothing. A cache that reports CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN
because it could not write is the defect; one that silently swallows a write
failure is the worse fix.

title: Decide whether the budget-drift nudge's AND is right, because it swallowed nine rows for five days
description:
NEEDS FRANK. This is a judgment about how loud a gate should be, and nobody
else gets to make it.

scripts/test's budget-drift nudge fires only when elapsed exceeds BOTH
thresholds: at least 3.0x the budget AND at least 5s over it in absolute
terms. The AND is what keeps it quiet on small suites, where a 0.5s row
tripping 3x costs nobody anything.

THE AND HAS NOW SWALLOWED TWO REAL EVENTS.

Nine of twenty-one budgets sat over on 2026-10-08 and the gate stayed green,
because every one failed the 5s absolute half. That was tla-kqry, and it sat
at P3 for five days for exactly that reason.

The drill row read 96.6s against a 10.3s budget, 9.4x and plus 86s, which
trips both halves. That one was caught. It is also the only one that has
been.

AND THE JUSTIFICATION FOR 3.0x IS GONE. scripts/test's header justified the
factor by the tier gap: "the cut is at the 4.2x gap between 2.4s and 10.2s",
so "a 3x threshold therefore catches every possible tier crossing by
construction". Measured 2026-10-13 after the re-measure in ce776fa and the
reading row in 3a9ce5a, that gap has INVERTED. The slow tier's cheapest row
is the reading corpus gate at 4.1s and the fast tier's dearest is spike
measurement at 4.8s. There is no gap left for the factor to rest on.

The tier RULE is still sound, because the boundary is whether a suite runs
TLC's model checker rather than its wall clock. It is the NUMBER that lost
its reason.

THREE WAYS TO GO, and the first is my recommendation.

  Keep the AND and drop the absolute floor to about 2s. Nine rows would have
  nudged on 2026-10-08. That is noisier than today and it is the direction
  that would have surfaced tla-kqry when it happened.

  Keep both numbers and accept that the nudge only reports catastrophes. It
  caught the one that mattered this month.

  Replace the factor with a per-row tolerance, since the header already says
  wall clock is a property of the box rather than of the tree. More faithful
  and more work, and I would not start here.

I would take the first. A nudge nobody sees is advice, not a gate, and the
project's own rule says a correctness check must not depend on human memory.
The counter-argument is real though: scripts/test's header argues at length
that a flaky gate gets --no-verify'd or deleted, and a noisier nudge is a
step toward that.

Files: scripts/test

RED: none. This is a decision, not a defect, and it gets a RED once Frank has
picked a direction.
notes:
THIRD EVENT, 2026-10-17, and it runs the OTHER WAY from the first two.

Full registry after merging tla-1sh7.12 and tla-1sh7.13 at 169d53a, on a quiet box (load 2.4), 39 suites green in 719.4s:

  indeterminate gate     46.6s vs 10.7s   4.3x, +35.9s   NUDGED
  recall runner          88.0s vs 43.7s   2.01x, +44.3s  silent
  recall corpus gate    194.7s vs 86.7s   2.25x, +108.0s silent

All three are stale by the same night's merges and all three were re-measured. The two that were swallowed are the two LARGEST absolute misses in the registry's history as far as this bead records, and they passed the 5s floor by a factor of nine and twenty-one. It was the 3.0x FACTOR that swallowed them.

So every option in this bead that works on the absolute floor leaves tonight's two silent. Dropping the floor to 2s changes nothing here. What would have caught them is a lower factor, or an OR with an absolute ceiling of roughly 30s, or a rule keyed on the slow tier where every row is already tens of seconds.

The recall corpus gate is now the registry's single most expensive row at 194.7s, ahead of the grader at 87.7s, and it was 108s over a budget nobody was told about. That is the shape worth weighing: the nudge is quietest exactly where the wall clock hurts most.

Not acted on. The judgment is still yours.

title: A test suite can land with no scripts/test row, and nothing catches it
description:
harness/test-reading.sh shipped in 95264ad and had no scripts/test registry
row until 3a9ce5a. Between those two commits the reading corpus was gated by
scripts/cibuild and by nothing a developer runs, while scripts/test --list
read as the authority on what is gated.

A SUITE PRESENT IN THE TREE AND ABSENT FROM THE REGISTRY IS WORSE THAN A
MISSING SUITE. A missing suite is a visible hole. An unregistered one looks
like coverage: the file exists, its assertions pass when somebody runs it by
hand, and --list reports a clean set that does not include it.

NOTHING CURRENTLY GATES THAT PAIRING. The registry is a hand-maintained array
in scripts/test and the suites are files under harness/. No check compares
them, so the next suite to land has the same gap by default.

WHAT TO BUILD. A check that every harness/test-*.sh and every
*/selftest.sh reachable from the tree appears in scripts/test's registry, and
that every registry row names a command that exists. Both directions, because
a row pointing at a deleted suite fails the same way from the other side.

Two things to settle rather than assume.

  WHERE IT LIVES. harness/test-pipefail.sh already scans the tree by shebang
  rather than by extension and is the closest precedent. A new suite is
  cheaper to read but adds a registry row, which is the thing being counted.

  THE EXEMPTION PATH. A suite deliberately left out needs somewhere to say
  so, and that somewhere has to be checkable. An allowlist with a reason per
  entry is the shape test-pipefail.sh already uses for its own bans.

Files: harness/test-registry.sh, scripts/test

RED: GIVEN a new harness/test-*.sh with no registry row WHEN the registry
check runs THEN it fails and names the file. GIVEN a registry row whose
command does not exist THEN it fails and names the row. A suite nobody runs
is the defect; an allowlist that hides one without a reason is the worse fix.

title: Author the completion channel, the third of three and the one with no artifact or bead
description:
The third channel of the 2026-10-11 fluency design, filed so it stops living
only in the exploration drawer. Reading is tla-fwkz. Blank-page landed on
2026-10-12 as 32 items in four families. Completion has nothing.

WHAT IT IS. A completion problem gives a partially-worked spec and asks for
the missing piece. The learning-science ground for it is the completion-problem
effect, and the reason it is a SEPARATE channel rather than a cheaper
blank-page item is Frank's own line from 2026-10-11: "while exercises that
require modifying code are _really_ useful, what they're useless for is the
'blank page' problem". So completion does not substitute for blank-page and
blank-page does not substitute for completion.

TWO CONSTRAINTS ALREADY SETTLED, carried here so they are not re-litigated.

  - NOT PROGRESSIVE. Frank, 2026-10-11: "A key improvement I think we should
    make over the past is _not_ to make them progressive, where they're
    'mini'." Items are drawn, not climbed.
  - NOT ROTE. Frank, 2026-10-11: "The major problem we had with the mini
    puzzle attempts of the past were they were too rote. It was hard to make
    puzzles that didn't just have the answer built in." This is the same
    failure the blank-page gate's check 1 catches as a telegraph, and it is
    harder here, because a completion item must show surrounding code without
    the surrounding code implying the hole.

ONE REFUTED APPROACH, do not re-propose it. Single-line cloze extraction was
proposed and refuted on 2026-10-11: multi-line Parsons problems correlate
highly with code writing, single-line micro-Parsons shows NO correlation and
lower discrimination than writing one line from scratch. Retracted as F9 in
the exploration drawer.

Files: drill/completion/, harness/drill-gate.sh

RED: GIVEN a completion item WHEN the gate reads it THEN the item's shown code
does not contain the construct the hole exercises, and the completed module
reproduces a recorded rc. An item whose surrounding code implies the hole is
the defect.
notes:
FIRST ITEM BUILT 2026-10-13, and five things came out of it that the bead
could not have known. completion/sets/01-clockface, landed as the worked
reference for the rest.

1. THE CHANNEL DOES NOT FIT UNDER drill/. The bead's Files line says
drill/completion/, and building it there raised 5 gate findings:
harness/drill-gate.sh reads drill/<family>/<NN>-<slug>, so drill/completion/
sets reads as an ITEM named 'sets' and fails ITEM-BAD-NAME plus four
ITEM-MISSING-FILE checks. Moved to a top-level completion/ tree, sibling to
drill/ and reading/, and the fast tier went back to 17 of 17. The three
channels are now symmetric, which is what the gates already assumed.

2. THE VERIFICATION CONTRACT IS THREE MACHINES, not one. The learner writes
each claim once into work/Claims.tla, which declares the state and the given
helpers. Three root modules EXTEND it: the correct machine and two broken
ones. Measured with harness/verdict.sh at Face = 12.

    case            ClockFace  Stray  Skip
    reference            0       12    12
    both TRUE            0        0     0
    claim 1 only         0       12     0
    claim 2 only         0        0    12
    unfilled           150      150   150

Four distinct signatures, so three exit codes say WHICH claim is weak rather
than only that one is.

3. ONE BROKEN MACHINE IS NOT ENOUGH, and this is the part worth carrying to
every future item. The first draft used a mutant whose step size drifted. A
correct claim 2 caught it on its own, so 'claim 1 = TRUE' produced the
reference signature exactly. The fix is a mutant that makes the OTHER claim
vacuous: Stray halts before the hand returns to hour 0, which is claim 2's
antecedent, leaving claim 1 as the only thing that can fire. So an item with
N holes needs N machines each of which only one hole catches, and that has to
be measured per item rather than argued.

4. A HOLE MUST BE FALSIFIABLE BY A MACHINE. The source reading model carries
four properties and only two could be used. OrderIsSize and Divides are true
for every step and Face, so no broken machine refutes them and TLC cannot
tell a correct body from TRUE. State-independent arithmetic facts are good
reading and unusable as completion holes.

5. THE NO-TELEGRAPH RULE NEEDS OPERATOR GRANULARITY. The first draft gave
TypeOK as 'seen \subseteq Hour', which hands claim 1 its shape by pattern
match. It now reads 'seen \in SUBSET Hour', same typing, different operator.
At drill/INVENTORY.md row granularity the rule still reads as violated,
because K013 covers \cup as well as \subseteq and ClockFace.tla shows
'seen \cup {pos'}'. So the gate check has to be per operator, not per row.

STILL MISSING, and it is what stops a learner using this. deliver-drill.sh
cannot deliver a completion item: wrong depth, and the manifest differs. A
completion item delivers PROMPT.md, work/ and EXPECT, and withholds ANSWER.md
and META.md. That is scripts/deliver-completion.sh plus its test, and it is
the next thing to build.

Files: completion/, scripts/deliver-completion.sh, harness/completion-gate.sh
WAVE FINDINGS, 2026-10-13. Four items landed from two of the four authoring
workers so far. Three findings, the first a defect in completion/verify-item.sh
which is central-owned.

A. A COMPLETION ITEM CANNOT ASK FOR DEADLOCK CHECKING. completion/verify-item.sh
calls harness/verdict.sh with no deadlock flag, so a cfg carrying
CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE is refused at 99 CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN rather than run.
Measured by the tla-gz6m author on a copy of its own Canvass.cfg with that line
appended. CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE is agreement and runs fine. This matters because
both reading/state-space/02-tickets and 03-chips carry CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE and
discuss what it covers, so an author varying either one reaches for it.
drill/temporal/verify-item.sh already solves this: it reads the cfg and passes
-d when the keyword says TRUE. Port that. Held back during the wave because two
workers were still invoking the script.

B. A CFG-SIDE HOLE IS POSSIBLE AND NOT YET WORTH TAKING. A .cfg CONSTRAINT line
does resolve against an operator defined in Claims.tla, measured: the run would
exit 151 CONFIG_ERROR otherwise and it exits 0. So a hole in a constraint BODY
is an ordinary TLA+ hole. What Claims.tla cannot hold is a hole in the keyword
itself, since that lives only in the cfg and the cfg is a machine file. The
tla-gz6m author declined a constraint hole and the reason is R3 rather than
taste: a wrong constraint body is caught by every machine failing to terminate
rather than by one machine failing, so the signature is three timeouts at the
180 second budget. That satisfies the distinct-rows rule and breaks the
one-machine-per-hole rule, at nine minutes a run. A constraint hole wants a
contract amendment naming the correct machine as its own checker and capping
the timeout.

C. TWO CARRIED SETS IS THE CHEAPER WAY TO SEPARATE TWO HOLES. The reference item
needed a mutant engineered to make its second claim vacuous, because a correct
second claim caught the first mutant unaided. completion/sets/02-twohands gives
each claim its own carried set, so a mutant that corrupts one set leaves the
other claim alone and the one-hole-per-mutant rule falls out of the design
rather than being added to it. Reach for that first.

STILL THE REAL GAP: harness/completion-gate.sh does not exist. Per-item
verification is completion/verify-item.sh against the item's own EXPECT, and
nothing checks the corpus. Not the one-machine-per-hole rule, not the
no-telegraph rule, not whether a hole is falsifiable at all. All three of those
failed in a draft during this wave and all three were caught by a person
reading, which is what gate-don't-advise exists to stop.
WAVE COMPLETE 2026-10-13. Nine items, eight of them variations. Two grader
defects found and fixed in 1c4dbc4, and three more findings that belong to the
gate that does not exist yet.

FIXED. Finding A above is closed: the grader now passes the deadlock flag when
a cfg asks for it, measured 99 without and 0 with. And exit code 150 no longer
reports a parse failure as unstarted work: it checks for a surviving marker,
says which case it is, and prints SANY's own sentence. The marker check strips
comments first, because Claims.tla's own header says 'Replace each FILL_IN
marker' and the first version matched the instruction.

FOR harness/completion-gate.sh, the three things this wave found that a person
caught by reading.

D. A STRAY FILE UNDER work/ IS DELIVERED. pcal writes a <Module>.old backup
beside every module it rewrites, and scripts/deliver-completion.sh delivers
work/ recursively by design, 'including one added tomorrow'. The tla-w33x
author's first --check listed three .old files as about to land. It deleted
them, so nothing shipped, and nothing would have caught it if it had not looked.
The gate should refuse a work/ tree holding a file no EXPECT stem accounts for.

E. THE no-telegraph CHECK MUST READ EVERY SHOWN FILE, NOT JUST Claims.tla. Two
authors fixed a leak in a MACHINE rather than in Claims. The tla-vzch author's
loop catch read naturally as {i, (i % 5) + 1} and is now an IF, because % is
what a hole needed. The tla-w33x author's Tile!Cells was (At..Far) \cap (1..Wall)
and is now a set filter, because \cap is what its hole needed.

F. A PLUSCAL TERMINAL-STATE HOLE CANNOT PASS E, STRUCTURALLY. pcal writes
Terminating == pc = 'Done' /\ UNCHANGED vars into every translation that can
finish, so the guard a terminal-state claim needs is in the shown code by
construction. completion/pluscal/01-squares names it rather than hiding it and
records an escape hatch that states the same thing without pc. The gate needs a
per-item exemption with a reason, not a blanket pass for the family.

ALSO MEASURED, not acted on. Claims.tla can be EXTENDed by a PlusCal module
despite both declaring the variables: four SANY 'Multiple declarations'
warnings and a correct run, with coverage resolving every variable to Claims.
The author took INSTANCE instead because duplicate-declaration resolution is
unspecified and this build happens to pick Claims, so a later SANY picking the
local one would check the claims over unconstrained variables. That is a false
pass on a correctness gate, which is the right reason to pay four lines per
machine. And verdict.sh's -nowarning does not cover SANY semantic warnings.

SHAPE DEBT. Three of the nine items bound a cardinality against a tally:
functions-records/01-cloakroom, state-space/01-canvass and, in a different
form, core/01-shutters. Different families, mechanisms and quantities, so
nothing needs changing. A later wave picking claim shapes should know.

title: The rc 12 against 13 split holds only for specs without fairness
description:
Measured by the tla-pmm2 temporal drill author on 2026-10-12. This corrects a claim central has repeated several times today and wrote into four briefs.

THE CLAIM AS CENTRAL STATED IT. harness/verdict.sh:81-91 splits rc 12 from rc 13 on the SHAPE of the formula rather than on the cfg keyword, so [](P => []P) and ~<>P are safety written with temporal operators and exit 12, while []<>P, <>[]P, P ~> Q and [][A]_vars exit 13.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. The split holds only for specs WITHOUT a fairness conjunct. Same obligation, same module, two specs:

  AnswerR4NofairRun   rc 12
  AnswerR4Run         rc 13

So adding fairness to the spec moves the code for an obligation whose shape did not change. The author marked the mechanism INFERRED, having measured the effect without establishing the cause.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA. The tla-r2ih fix, which landed today, made harness/seeded-bugs.sh accept 12 OR 13 for a PROPERTY precisely because the shape decides and the keyword does not. That reasoning was right and the implementation is unaffected, since accepting both is the conservative choice either way. But any instrument that tries to PREDICT which of 12 or 13 it will get, from the formula alone, will be wrong on a fair spec.

And one is being built: the drill gate records a per-module rc and verifies it reproduces. It works today because each item measured its own rc rather than predicting it. The hazard is for the next author who reasons from the shape instead of running the model.

WHAT TO SETTLE. Whether verdict.sh's table and its comment at :81-91 should say 'for a spec with no fairness conjunct', or whether the behaviour is TLC's and the comment should name that. Read TLC's source or probe it; do not reason from the table.

RED: GIVEN one obligation and two specs differing only in a fairness conjunct WHEN each runs through verdict.sh THEN either both return the same code, or verdict.sh's documented table says which conjunct changes it. A table that predicts a code it does not deliver is the defect.
notes:
2026-10-17, central. Reproduced independently during the tla-7xql exploration,
on a module written for the purpose, with the fairness conjunct as the only
difference:

  claim                      with WF_V(Nxt)   without
  ~<>(i = 2)                 13 LIVENESS      12 SAFETY
  [](i = 0 => [](i = 0))     13               12
  [](i # 2)                  12               12

So the 12/13 split holds only for specs WITHOUT a fairness conjunct, which is
what this bead says.

NEW CONSUMER, and it raises the stakes. Every pinned-behavior item in epic
tla-7xql is a fair spec by construction, since the fairness conjunct on the
player's own advance action is what forecloses the stuttering-tail artifact.
So that whole item family reads 13 where a reader might expect 12.

The epic's contract already says read {0} = holds and {12, 13} = refuted, and
never predict which. harness/seeded-bugs.sh and harness/refinement.sh already
do it that way, taking REFINEMENT_VIOLATED from "run A's rc=12 OR its rc=13".
2026-10-18, central. REPRODUCED a third time, and the cause generalizes past fairness.

The bead's effect holds. One obligation, one system, and the code moves when
the spec formula gains a conjunct the obligation never mentions:

  PROPERTY ~<>P   Init /\ [][Next]_vars                      rc 12
  PROPERTY ~<>P   Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Move)      rc 13

FAIRNESS IS NOT WHAT DOES IT. Three conjuncts move the same formula the same
way, and only one of them is a fairness operator:

  WF_vars(Move)        13
  SF_vars(Move)        13
  []<>(s = 1)          13

So the bead's title understates its own finding. Any liveness conjunct in the
spec formula takes the claim out of the safety channel. The author marked the
mechanism INFERRED, having measured the effect without the cause, and that is
still where this sits: my hunch is that a liveness conjunct forces the tableau
and the tableau owns the exit code from then on. Nobody has read TLC's source.

THE BEAD'S RED IS MET BY THE SECOND BRANCH. The two specs do not return the
same code, so verdict.sh's table now says which conjunct changes it, carries
the full 24-cell grid, and harness/test-verdict.sh pins eleven cells including
this pair. Stripping the WF conjunct out of the fixture reddens one row and
only the row that rests on it.

WF over an action that [][Next]_vars forbids leaves no behavior, and the spec
then exits 0 on every temporal property including []<>FALSE. vacuity.sh's
VECTOR 4 already probes exactly that and reads the same two codes, so the
harness was built for it. The new part is the asymmetry: the same empty spec
still exits 12 on a lifted invariant, so a corpus checked only through lifted
invariants looks healthy while every liveness obligation on it is vacuous.

NOT AFFECTED. The epic's contract already says read {0} = holds and {12, 13} =
refuted and never predict which, so every pinned-behavior item is correct as

title: Four state-space keywords have no inventory row, and TypeOK has none either
description:
Found by the state-space and core drill authors independently on 2026-10-12, both of whom worked around it rather than editing drill/INVENTORY.md outside their footprint.

THE GAP. These have no ROW in drill/INVENTORY.md:

  CONSTRAINT
  ACTION_CONSTRAINT
  VIEW
  ALIAS
  TypeOK

The first four are the keywords the entire state-space family is ABOUT. The fifth is the single most common invariant name in the published corpus, at 117 of 713 invariant declarations with 164 of 713 starting with Type (.claude/rules/tla-practice.md section 3).

WHY IT BIT. harness/drill-gate.sh exits 99 on a META.md bullet under '## Constructs' naming something with no inventory row (drill-gate.sh:948-951), which is correct behaviour. So the state-space author put the four keywords under a separate '## Keywords with no inventory row' heading in each of its eight METAs, and said so. The core author hit the same wall and recorded it. Both were right to work around rather than edit.

THE COST. Those five constructs read as covered-by-nobody in the coverage report, because the report can only count rows that exist. So the instrument that is supposed to aim the next authoring wave is blind to the family that most needed aiming.

A SECOND, RELATED MISMATCH from the core author. Central's brief listed VARIABLE, Init, Next, Spec, the primed variable, UNCHANGED and vars as the 'core' family. The inventory files all of those under temporal as K079 to K086, and '..' under sets as K015. So central's family partition and the inventory's disagree, and the authors reconciled it per-item by using a second constructs heading. Pick one and make the other follow.

WHY THE INVENTORY MISSED THEM, and this is not a criticism of its author. It was built strictly from the 105 '- Construct:' entries in the twelve exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md files, which is the right source and is curated. The cheat sheets simply have no entry for a cfg keyword, because the exercise sets never reached one: state space never left zero across all seven delivered problems. So the inventory faithfully reflects a corpus that never used these.

WHAT TO DO. Add rows for the five, sourced from .claude/rules/tla-practice.md section 5's keyword table rather than from the cheat sheets, and mark their source so a reader can tell inventory rows that came from the curated sheets from rows added later. Then reconcile the family partition with central's. Then re-run the coverage report, which will for the first time be able to say something about the state-space family.

Files: drill/INVENTORY.md, drill/COLD-LIST.md

RED: INVARIANT: every construct named under a '## Constructs' heading in any drill item's META.md resolves to a ROW in drill/INVENTORY.md. An item forced to invent a second heading to describe what it exercises is the defect.
notes:
A THIRD AUTHOR'S LIST, harvested 2026-10-14 from the sequences family's eight
META.md files under "Operators with no inventory row". The sequences worker was
asked to harvest rather than re-derive, and it did, then checked the union
against INVENTORY.md's 105 ROW lines.

CONSTRAINT APPEARS AGAIN, from a third independent author. This bead already
names it. That is now three families reporting the same missing keyword.

NO ROW AT ANY GRANULARITY, the Sequences module nearly entire:

  Len, Append, Head, Tail
  SubSeq (1-based and inclusive, and past-the-end as a TLC error at rc 255)
  \o concatenation, including with an empty slice
  SelectSeq with a LAMBDA test

  s[i] with its 1-based origin, and the index-0 failure at rc 75
  s[Len(s)] as the last element
  the empty, one-element and pair literals
  tuple against sequence (a pair indexed like a list)

HAS A GENERAL ROW BUT NO SEQUENCE-SPECIFIC ONE:

  DOMAIN of a sequence as 1..Len(s)            general row K046
  a function literal over 1..Len(s) as a list  general row K047
  [1..N -> 1..N] enumerated as arrangements    general row K050

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, and it is the reason the list is this long. The
sequences family has exactly TWO rows in the whole inventory: K010 "sequences
Sequences" and K011 "sequences Sequence module operators". K011 covers every
operator in the module at once, so an eight-item family exercising fourteen
distinct operators reads as covering one row. The coverage report cannot aim a
wave at a family whose constructs are collapsed into a single row, which is the
same cost this bead already states for the state-space keywords.

Surfaces the worker searched: INVENTORY.md field 4 by operator name, the cfg
keywords, and the tuple and function rows. It noted that CONSTRAINT is absent
while PROPERTY (K064), Invariant (K034), deadlock (K059) and symmetry set

A SIXTH CASE, 2026-10-21, and this one is a row that EXISTS with the wrong name
rather than a missing row. Found while Frank worked drill/modules/01.

drill/INVENTORY.md:316 reads:

  ROW  K104  modules  INSTANCE ... WITH (<- constant substitution)
       exercises/ch13/CHEATSHEET.md:31  low  A1/12;B43of666@368

The name covers constants only. Substituting a VARIABLE through the same

Both METAs already carry a hand-written paragraph correcting the row's name,
which is the tell. modules/01: "The K104 row is named for constant
substitution. The same keyword substitutes the tank's variable here, and that

symbol is the abstract module's variable, which is the refinement mapping. Same

Two item authors independently wrote around the row name rather than editing

WITH examples substitute constants, and whose modules.rst:137 is a .. todo::

BLOCKED 2026-10-22 ON AN ARCHITECTURAL DECISION THIS BEAD PREDATES. Not

'- Construct:' entries in exercises/ch*/CHEATSHEET.md. scripts/gen-sheet.sh

  COUNT 106 inventory row(s) against 105 construct entr(ies)

harness/test-sheet.sh, harness/test-coverage-map.sh, scripts/gen-coverage.sh and
drill/SHEET.md. That is a decision about an architectural invariant across five
files, which is Frank's rather than a worker's.

A PLEASING NOTE FROM THE WORKER: the per-row source mark this bead already asks
for is exactly the thing that would partition the rows the bijection covers from

THE COST IS NOW MEASURED. The coverage report is IDENTICAL before and after the

THE RED INVARIANT IS MEASURED AT 55 BULLETS ACROSS 16 META.md FILES, in

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT. It says three families reported
