title: The test layer has the pass-over-skipped-work defect too, and scripts/test prints only PASS
description:
Found by the tla-hl96 worker, which declared test suites out of scope for its sweep and reported this rather than widening silently.

TWO MEASUREMENTS.

harness/test-corpus-manifest.sh exits 0 having reported 10 SKIPPED checks. So a suite announces that ten of its checks did not run and still reports success.

scripts/test prints only PASS or FAIL per suite. A suite that skipped most of its work is indistinguishable from one that did all of it.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT AS tla-hl96 AND WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY. The shape is identical: work that did not happen reported as success. But the fix is different, because a test suite legitimately skips on a missing optional dependency, where an instrument's probe skipping is always a loss of information. So the answer here is probably not rc 99. It is more likely a SKIPPED count surfaced in scripts/test's own output, so a reader sees '18 suites passed, 1 passed with 10 skipped' rather than a flat 22.

tla-hl96's new gate deliberately excludes test-*.sh, and its header says so, so this will not be caught by it.

WHAT TO SETTLE FIRST, before any code. Whether a skipped check in a test suite is ever acceptable in this project. The corpus-manifest suite's 10 skips may all be legitimate, in which case the fix is purely reporting. If any of the 10 is a check that should run on this box and silently does not, that is a second bug hiding inside this one. Read the ten before deciding.

Files: scripts/test, harness/test-corpus-manifest.sh

RED: GIVEN a suite that skips checks WHEN scripts/test reports it THEN the skipped count appears in the output. A suite reporting PASS while announcing skipped checks, with scripts/test showing a bare PASS, is the defect.

title: Four instruments call verdict.sh and none has an arm for rc 99
description:
Created by the tla-eafx fix on 2026-10-08 and reported by the worker that made it. NOT a regression today, and the reason is measured.

verdict.sh now returns rc 99 CHECK_DID_NOT_RUN when a cfg's CHECK_DEADLOCK disagrees with the command-line flag. Four instruments call it: grade.sh, refinement.sh, seeded-bugs.sh and sequence.sh.

WHY NOTHING IS BROKEN RIGHT NOW. None of those four's fixtures carries a CHECK_DEADLOCK line, grepped, and no cfg under chapter/ or puzzles/ sets it TRUE. The whole gate is green at 22 suites.

THE EXPOSURE IS A LEARNER, WHICH IS THE SAME DIRECTION tla-eafx POINTED. A submission carrying CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE now hands grade.sh an rc 99 it has no arm for, which falls through to HARNESS_ERROR 4. So a learner who writes an ordinary and reasonable cfg keyword gets a harness error rather than a grade. 82 of 337 configs in the published corpus carry that keyword, so this will happen.

EACH OF THE FOUR HAS THE SAME TWO CHOICES and they may not all pick the same one.

Pass --deadlock-override, which says this instrument owns the deadlock decision and the cfg does not get a vote. Right for the internal probe paths, which is why vacuity.sh's three call sites already do it.

Or surface the 99, which says the caller reports that the check did not run. Probably right for grade.sh specifically, because a learner needs to be told their keyword was discarded rather than seeing a harness error. That is a verdict-object question, and the leak gate at grade.sh's bottom constrains what the message may say.

DO NOT PICK ONE ANSWER FOR ALL FOUR WITHOUT READING EACH. The point of rc 99 is that an instrument says when it could not check, and papering over it in four callers with the same flag would reinstate the defect one level up.

Files: harness/grade.sh, harness/refinement.sh, harness/seeded-bugs.sh, harness/sequence.sh

RED: GIVEN a submission or fixture cfg carrying CHECK_DEADLOCK TRUE WHEN each of the four instruments runs it through verdict.sh THEN the instrument either declared it owns the decision, or reports that the deadlock check did not run. A fall-through to a generic harness error is the defect.

title: txn-epoch's fixed rule 4 adds a third terminal state, and the statement names one stall
description:
Created by the tla-pmm2.2 blocking edit on 2026-10-08 and reported by the worker that made it, rather than papered over.

WHAT THE EDIT DID. Rule 4 now refuses a gang whose card does not say the leaf the desk holds. That restored the fence, which was the point, and it introduced a THIRD terminal state: a gang stranded holding a stale card, which can neither raise nor bring back.

THE CONSEQUENCE. CHECK_DEADLOCK now reports the STRANDED state FIRST, at 3 states, instead of the book-full stall it used to report. PROBLEM.md:288-289 names ONE stall and there are now two.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. A learner who sets CHECK_DEADLOCK and reads the first terminal state TLC prints now meets a state the statement never mentions, three steps in, while the stall the problem is actually about sits further out. That is a reader sent to the wrong place by a true report.

THREE WAYS OUT, and this bead should pick one rather than describing all three.

A. Name both stalls in the statement. Cheapest, and it tells the reader the stranded state is expected rather than their bug.
B. Make the stranded state non-terminal, by giving a stranded gang some legal move. Changes the machine, so it needs a reason from the source rather than from convenience.
C. Change the checking instance so the stranded state is unreachable at that size. Fragile, and it hides a reachable state rather than accounting for it.

A looks right. The stranded gang IS what a fence does, so naming it is faithful.

SECOND, SMALLER ITEM FROM THE SAME EDIT. The leak is HALVED, not removed. Step 5 found PROBLEM.md:84-85 was the only negative-capability sentence in 25 grep hits and named the only gap the trap runs through. The edit rewrote :84. The sweep still returns 25 lines and :85 still names a gap. Decide whether :85 survives.

Files: authoring/txn-epoch-fence-vs-retry/statement/PROBLEM.md

RED: GIVEN the amended rules at the statement's own checking instance WHEN a learner runs with CHECK_DEADLOCK THEN every terminal state TLC can report first is one the statement names. A terminal state reachable in fewer steps than the one the problem is about, and unnamed, is the defect.

title: Nothing in this repo runs mkdocs build --strict, so a broken internal link ships green
description:
Found by the tla-jaob.5 worker on 2026-10-08 and confirmed by central reading both call sites.

  .github/workflows/pages.yml:42   mkdocs build
  scripts/cibuild:199              mkdocs build

Both plain. --strict is run nowhere.

WHAT --strict BUYS. It turns mkdocs's warnings into errors, and the warning that matters here is an unresolved internal link. Without it, a page that links a file which does not exist in the built tree publishes successfully and 404s for a reader.

WHY THIS IS NOW WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN BEFORE. Until today docs/ published two source trees, exercises/ and module-docs/, both flat. tla-jaob.5 just added chapter/, whose index links 44 snippet files individually plus two chapter pages, and the chapters cross-link each other. That is the first densely cross-linked part of the site, so it is the first place a stale link can hide.

The tla-jaob.5 worker ran --strict BY HAND in a scratchpad venv and it was clean, so the tree is good today. Nothing keeps it good.

A RELATED LOCAL PROBLEM, and it is why the worker needed a venv at all. The box's own mkdocs shim points at /usr/bin/python3, which does not exist on this NixOS box, so mkdocs is unrunnable locally. scripts/server and scripts/deploy both end in mkdocs, so neither works on this machine as it stands. That half may want its own bead once somebody decides whether the fix is a devbox entry, a nix shell, or a documented venv.

ONE CAUTION BEFORE FLIPPING THE FLAG. --strict will fail on warnings the current tree may already carry in the v1 curriculum/ subtree, which is 107 puzzles of generated pages nobody has link-checked. Measure first: run --strict over the whole built tree and count what it reports. If v1 is dirty, the honest move is to flip --strict in CI and fix or exclude v1 deliberately, rather than leaving the flag off because v1 is noisy.

Files: .github/workflows/pages.yml, scripts/cibuild

RED: GIVEN a docs page linking a file that does not exist in the built tree WHEN CI builds the site THEN the build FAILS. A broken internal link that publishes green is the defect.

title: Upstream: TLC 1.8.0's dumpTrace json writer skips ALIAS on the liveness path
description:
A clean minimal repro of an upstream defect, measured under bead tla-0igq on 2026-10-08. NOT YET FILED. Frank authorizes any outward-facing filing.

THE DEFECT. On TLC2 Version 2026.07.31.184830 (tla2tools v1.8.0, the Clarke release), -dumpTrace json honours a cfg's ALIAS for a SAFETY counterexample and ignores it for a LIVENESS counterexample.

THE REPRO, and it is already reduced to one variable. One module, one model, one ALIAS line, two cfgs differing ONLY in the obligation line:

  INVARIANT NeverTwo   rc=12   {"position":0}   vars:["position"]
  PROPERTY  Live       rc=13   {"stage":0}      vars:["stage"]

where the module declares VARIABLE stage, Alias == [ position |-> stage ], NeverTwo == stage # 2, and Live == []<>(stage = 2).

WHY IT IS NOT A CONFIGURATION ERROR ON OUR SIDE, which is the first thing a maintainer will ask. The alias IS evaluated on the liveness path: TLC's own console error trace prints 'position = 0' and 'position = 1' for the same rc=13 run whose JSON dump says 'stage'. So the cfg reached TLC, TLC applied the alias for console output, and only the JSON writer fell back to the raw variable.

LINEAGE. ALIAS arrived in TLC 1.8.0 via tlaplus/tlaplus issue 485, documented as running 'when printing an error-trace'. The JSON dump is a second error-trace channel and the feature did not reach it.

OUR FIXTURE IS THE REPRO. harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/relay/ plus the two cfgs. A filing should carry a self-contained module rather than a path into this repo.

WHAT TO DO. Use the upstream-a-bead recipe, lane --issue-only unless a maintainer asks for a patch. Redact nothing sensitive, there is none, but strip the tla-puzzles paths and inline the module.

ONE THING THE FILING MUST SAY. We are not blocked. Our consumer reads only action names and state-list length, both of which ARE present on liveness traces. So this is a report of a documented guarantee not holding on one path, not a request for an urgent fix. Saying so makes it a better report and costs nothing.

AND ONE THING TO CHECK BEFORE FILING. Whether a later tla2tools already fixed it. tla-0igq's pins are written to turn RED if a future TLC honours the alias, so our own suite will tell us, but a maintainer will reasonably ask whether this reproduces on master.

Files: (none in this repo; the deliverable is an upstream issue)

RED: GIVEN the two-cfg repro WHEN run against tla2tools master THEN the liveness dump carries the aliased field. Until it does, the issue stands.

title: ALIAS does not reach the dumpTrace output for a liveness counterexample on v1.8.0
description:
Found by the tla-r2ih worker while building the liveness fixture, outside its footprint, and reported rather than worked around.

MEASURED. With ALIAS Alias in the generated cfg and Alias == [ position |-> stage ] in the module, a LIVENESS counterexample's -dumpTrace output carries the raw variable rather than the aliased field:

  {"counterexample":{"action":[[[1,{"stage":0}],...

The same assertion in the opposite direction passes for a SAFETY violation. harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/selftest.sh's crossing rows assert that a dumped safety trace carries no raw variable name, and they still pass. So the two channels differ and only the safety one honours ALIAS.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS P2 RATHER THAN P1. harness/seeded-bugs.sh's header claims a normalisation guarantee over the trace channel. On the liveness path that guarantee does not hold. Nothing in tla-r2ih depends on it: the signature comparator reads only action names and the state-list length, and both are present and readable on liveness traces, measured as '2 steps: Advance -> Recycle' and '1 steps: UnnamedAction', so phase 3 never reaches PROBE_INCONCLUSIVE. The worker deliberately did not write the new liveness rows to assert the guarantee, which is why the suite is green and the gap is still open.

The exposure is any future consumer that reads a liveness trace expecting aliased fields. It will get raw variable names and no warning.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE. Whether this is a TLC 2026.07.31.184830 behaviour or a cfg-generation gap on our side, which the bead should establish before proposing a fix. And whether the header's claim gets narrowed to safety or the liveness path gets fixed to match it. Narrowing the claim is honest and cheap; fixing the path may not be ours to do.

Files: harness/seeded-bugs.sh, harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/selftest.sh

RED: GIVEN a module declaring an ALIAS and an obligation whose violation is a liveness counterexample WHEN seeded-bugs.sh dumps the trace THEN either the trace carries the aliased fields, or the script's header no longer claims normalisation over liveness traces and a selftest row pins that narrower claim. A documented guarantee that holds on one path and not the other is the defect.
close_reason:
Fixed in 332ce78, merged, by NARROWING THE CLAIM rather than the path, because the defect is upstream.

THE FINDING REPRODUCED. 4 of 4 dumped liveness traces carry the raw variable, 0 carry the aliased field.

QUESTION 1 ANSWERED, AND IT IS TLC's BEHAVIOUR ON 2026.07.31.184830, NOT OUR CFG GAP. Two measurements separate them:

1. The generated cfg DOES carry the line. ALIAS Alias appears in 6 of 6 run.cfg files on the liveness path, byte-identical to the safety path's.
2. TLC RECEIVED AND EVALUATED IT. The tlc.log for the same rc=13 run prints 'position = 0' and 'position = 1' in the console error trace while the JSON dump says 'stage'.

So the alias is evaluated and only the -dumpTrace json writer skips it on the liveness path.

THE MINIMAL REPRO, one module, one model, one ALIAS line, two cfgs differing only in the obligation line:

  INVARIANT NeverTwo   rc=12   {"position":0}   vars:["position"]
  PROPERTY  Live       rc=13   {"stage":0}      vars:["stage"]

That is a clean upstream bug report and it is filed as its own bead.

ROUTE: NARROWED THE CLAIM. Fixing is not ours. Post-processing the dump was rejected for a reason worth keeping: it contradicts the same paragraph's 'no second chance afterwards' and buys nothing, because the signature comparator never opens a state record. harness/seeded-bugs.sh:255-288 now carries the narrowing, the two-row measurement table, and why the path was not fixed. No grading logic touched.

THE PINS ASSERT THE GAP, NOT THE GUARANTEE, which is the right way round. selftest.sh:600-660 adds five rows, counted rather than sampled: every dumped liveness trace carries the raw name 4 of 4; no dumped liveness trace carries the aliased field, whose failure text tells the next reader to narrow the header back out; a liveness trace still carries action names, which is the reason this was P2; and two assert_file_present rows over the header so the prose cannot drift back.

So A LATER TLC THAT HONOURS THE ALIAS TURNS THIS SUITE RED rather than leaving the header quietly wrong. Selftest 68 to 70 assertions.

title: screen.sh step 1 cannot run: the gh token has no code-search scope, and the script reports CLEAR anyway
description:
Found by the tla-pmm2.2 statement author on 2026-10-08 and confirmed by central on the same box.

WHAT HAPPENS. harness/screen.sh step 1 checks a proposed module name against GitHub code search, so a domain that collides with a published spec is caught before the freeze. The call is:

  gh api 'search/code?q=<Name>+language:tla'

It returns HTTP 401 Requires authentication. Central re-ran it against four candidate names (FireOffice, Bureau, LandOffice, SignalBox) and got 401 on all four, so this is the token's scope and not the agent's environment. search/code needs a scope the current token does not carry.

WHY IT IS A BUG AND NOT A MISSING FEATURE. screen.sh returned CLEAR exit 0 with step 1 skipped. A skipped step that reports CLEAR is the gate-dont-advise failure in its worst direction: the caller reads a pass, and the thing the step exists to catch walks through. The worker caught it only because it read the output rather than the exit code, and it said so in its own return rather than banking the CLEAR.

The weaker fallback the worker used, a plain web search for FireOffice.tla, found nothing. That is evidence and it is not the same evidence. Code search reaches module names inside repositories that no web index surfaces.

TWO THINGS TO FIX, and the second is the real one.

1. The token. Re-authenticate gh with a scope that permits search/code. This is Frank's to do, since it needs an interactive login.
2. screen.sh must not report CLEAR over a step it could not run. A step that 401s is UNKNOWN, not PASS, and the exit code has to carry that. Pick an exit code for indeterminate and make the caller handle it.

Fix 2 stands on its own merit even after the token is fixed, because the next unavailable API does the same thing.

Files: harness/screen.sh

RED: GIVEN a gh token with no code-search scope WHEN harness/screen.sh runs step 1 THEN it does not exit 0 CLEAR, and its output names step 1 as indeterminate rather than silently absent. A step that could not run never counts as a step that passed.
notes:
TOKEN FIXED 2026-10-08 by Frank. search/code now works. Central ran the screen and found TWO more things, one of which is new damage this morning's push created.

1. THE SCREEN NOW SELF-MATCHES. Searching for an exact module name returns our own repo:

  gh api -X GET search/code -f q='"MODULE TxnBroken" language:tla' --jq '.items[].repository.full_name'
  -> fkberthold/tla-puzzles

MODULE Challenge, MODULE TxnBroken and MODULE Wedged each return total_count 1, and the 1 is us. The spikes went public this morning, so from now on step 1 reports a collision on every module the project ships. That is the opposite failure from the one this bead was filed about, and it is worse, because a screen that cries collision on its own work gets ignored.

FIX: the query needs -repo:fkberthold/tla-puzzles, or step 1 has to filter the owning repo out of the result rather than counting rows.

2. THE QUERY SHAPE MATTERS AND THE OLD ONE WAS USELESS. A bare name search counts substring hits anywhere in a .tla file, not module declarations:

  Challenge 389, Minimal 544, Props 211, Rollout 68, Wedged 68, Diagram 41, MoveBase 16, TxnBroken 13

Those numbers answer nothing. The quoted form '"MODULE <Name>" language:tla' is the one that answers the question. Check which form screen.sh actually sends before trusting any historical CLEAR it produced.

3. RATE LIMIT. search/code allows about 10 requests a minute and returns 403 past that, with a message rather than an error shape. Central hit it on the fifth consecutive query. A screen checking several names needs to pace itself, and must not read a 403 as a zero.

So the token half of this bead is closed and the script half is now bigger than when it was filed. The indeterminate-exit-code work stays in tla-hl96.
FOOTPRINT WIDENED, 2026-10-08. The tla-hl96 worker fixed the 403 hole and the SKIPPED-reports-CLEAR hole but DELIBERATELY DID NOT LAND THE QUERY CHANGE, because it breaks a fixture outside its footprint.

harness/fixtures/screen/gh-stub strips a trailing ' language:tla' and looks the remainder up in a table. The working query is the quoted MODULE form plus a repo exclusion, which that stub cannot parse, so the change needs the stub, its counts file and the selftest in the same commit.

Files: harness/screen.sh, harness/fixtures/screen/gh-stub, harness/fixtures/screen/gh-stub-counts.txt, harness/fixtures/screen/selftest.sh

THE MEASUREMENTS ARE ALREADY IN screen.sh's HEADER under 'STILL BROKEN, AND NOT FIXED HERE', taken against live GitHub:

  '"MODULE TxnBroken" language:tla'                            total_count 1, repo fkberthold/tla-puzzles
  '"MODULE Wedged" language:tla'                               1 distinct repo
  same, with -repo:fkberthold/tla-puzzles                      0
  'Challenge language:tla', which is what screen.sh:178 SENDS   390

So the shipped query is the bare-name form and it counts substring hits. Both halves need fixing in one commit: the quoted MODULE form AND the repo exclusion.

WHAT IS ALREADY FIXED AND NOT PART OF THIS ANY MORE. The 403 hole is closed: gh api --jq writes GitHub's JSON body to stdout on failure and exits nonzero, no line is bare digits, so the numeric guard rejects it and the verdict is 99 rather than CLEAR. A second instance in the mechanism code-search was found and fixed the same way. The token itself was fixed by Frank earlier today.

Also still open from this bead's earlier note: BURNED_AT=3 is applied to fork-inflated raw hits, where TxnEpoch gives 16 hits across only 3 distinct files. The fix is to count distinct repositories rather than rows, which the quoted-query work should do in the same pass.

title: A dispatched agent cannot write to an out-of-tree report path, and every brief asks it to
description:
Found independently by two step-4 authors in the 2026-10-08 authoring wave, both of whom worked around it and said so.

THE INSTRUCTION. Every brief central writes carries 'write your report to /tmp/claude-1000/<session>/scratchpad/reports/<name>.md as well as returning it'. That instruction exists for a good reason: a report-only dispatch is lost if the session dies before the notification lands, and two red-teams on 2026-08-07 were nearly lost that way.

WHY IT DOES NOT WORK. The path is outside the worker's worktree, and two separate guards stop it.

1. ~/.claude/hooks/edit-write-pwd-guard blocks the Write tool for any path outside the current worktree.
2. The isolation command scanner refuses a Bash heredoc whose body mentions a glob or a parent-directory path, which an out-of-tree absolute path does.

So the mandated step silently costs every worker a detour. The workaround both found on their own: write the file in-tree, copy it out with cp, then remove the in-tree copy before the footprint check. That works, and it is three extra steps plus a footprint hazard if the agent forgets the removal.

WHY IT IS P2 AND NOT P1. Nothing is lost today. Both workers delivered their report at the mandated path and both returned it inline as well. The cost is per-dispatch friction and a real chance that a worker which does not think of the copy trick drops the file-write half and keeps only the return, which is the exact failure the instruction exists to prevent.

THREE WAYS OUT, and this bead should pick one rather than documenting the detour.

A. Put the report path INSIDE the worktree, at a gitignored location, and have central read it from the worktree after the agent returns. The worktree survives until central removes it, and central already knows its path from the dispatch result.
B. Teach edit-write-pwd-guard to allow the session scratchpad directory specifically. It is session-scoped and outside the repo, so it is not the leak the guard exists to stop.
C. Document the cp detour in .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md so it costs a worker nothing to rediscover.

A looks best: it needs no hook change and no agent-side ritual. C is the fallback and is worth doing anyway.

Files: .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md

RED: GIVEN a dispatched worker in an isolation worktree WHEN its brief tells it to write a report to the session scratchpad THEN it can do so in one step with no path detour and no risk of leaving an untracked file in its footprint.
notes:
WIDER THAN FILED, 2026-10-08. A third agent reported that TWO guards block a worker's Write, not one.

1. loom's path-leak guard refuses Write outside the worktree, which is the scratchpad report path. That is what this bead was filed about.
2. The generic subagent guard refuses Write on a .md report file AT ALL, including sources/spikes/<name>/REPORT.md, which is INSIDE the worktree and is the bead's declared deliverable.

So a dispatched spike author can write neither its scratchpad return nor its own REPORT.md through the Write tool. Both have to go through Bash, which collides with the heredoc refusal on TLA+ content. One worker built an emit-report.sh to solve both at once.

That changes the fix. Option A in the original note, moving the report path inside the worktree, does NOT work on its own, because guard 2 fires on the in-tree path too. The fix has to address the .md-report refusal as well, or every spike author keeps paying for a script it should not need to write.

Three of eight workers in this wave hit one or both and all three worked around it silently enough that only their reports show it.

title: A dispatched worker has nowhere safe to put a scratch file
description:
Found by the tla-6mrz worker 2026-10-02. Two instructions a dispatched worker gets are in direct conflict and neither can be satisfied.

The environment prompt names a session scratchpad directory and says to always use it for temporary files, intermediate results, scripts and outputs that do not belong in the project, rather than /tmp.

The edit-write-pwd-guard hook refuses a write to that directory from inside a worktree, because the scratchpad sits outside the worktree and the guard exists to stop a worker leaking writes into paths it should not touch.

So the permitted location and the safe location do not overlap. The worker needed a throwaway probe script, which it could not put in the scratchpad, so it wrote it inside the worktree and deleted it before its footprint check. That worked and it is fragile: a worker that forgets the delete ships a scratch file, and a worker that crashes between the two leaves one on the branch.

The same shape has bitten before in the other direction. .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md records the isolation harness refusing --alias, and the workaround there is also "put it in a small scratch script and run the script", which lands in the same bind.

WHY THIS IS P2 RATHER THAN P1. There is a working route, and three workers in two days found it unaided. But the route is "write where you are told not to, then clean up", which is the kind of instruction that erodes.

THE FIX IS NOT IN THIS REPO. edit-write-pwd-guard is a loom hook under ~/.claude/hooks/. The honest options are for the guard to allow the session scratchpad path explicitly, or for the environment prompt to name a worktree-local scratch convention for dispatched workers, something like a gitignored .scratch/ per worktree. The second needs a .gitignore entry here and is the half this repo could do alone.

PRECEDENT for filing a loom hook gap here: .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md already does it for the edit-after-failure-guard, which blocks Edit and Write after a red run and whose idea of a test file does not match harness/test-*.sh. That section ends "The gap is filed as a bead in this repo, and the fix is one pattern in loom hook." Same handling.

Files: .gitignore, .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md

title: The twelve exercise H1s use two different shapes, now visible on one screen
description:
Found by the tla-jaob.1 worker 2026-10-02, outside its Files: line so reported rather than fixed.

The twelve EXERCISES.md files do not agree on a title shape. Four read "Chapter NN exercises: Topic" and eight read "Exercises: learntla core ch.N, Topic". For example exercises/ch11/EXERCISES.md:1 reads "# Exercises: learntla core ch.11, Action Properties".

This did not matter while the sets were delivered one chapter at a time into a local tree. It matters now that all twelve are published as sibling pages at docs/exercises/, because each page keeps its source H1 so the site matches the repo, and a reader scrolling the section sees both forms disagree on the same screen.

The nav is unaffected. scripts/build-docs.sh derives a consistent "Chapter NN: Topic" for .pages titles regardless of the H1 shape, so the sidebar already reads uniformly. The inconsistency is only in the page bodies.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN LIVING WITH. The audience changed on 2026-10-02 from Frank alone to anyone who finished learntla, and this is the first content a stranger sees. Two title conventions in a twelve-page section reads as unfinished, which is a bad first impression for the part of the project that is actually the most tested, 221 assertions over twelve chapters.

WHAT TO DECIDE. Pick one shape and rewrite eight H1s or four. "Chapter NN exercises: Topic" sorts and scans better in a web section. "Exercises: learntla core ch.N, Topic" says out loud that the set tracks learntla, which is the whole pitch now, so it carries more information and reads worse. I would take the first and put the learntla pointer in the section index at docs/exercises/index.md, where it belongs once rather than twelve times.

The generator needs no change either way, since it copies the source H1 verbatim.

Files: exercises/ch02/EXERCISES.md through exercises/ch13/EXERCISES.md

title: Plan the ramp above position 07, and settle what the reading gate is for
description:
Frank, 2026-10-02: get rid of fencing, farm it for ideas, then plan how to continue or modify the ramp. He also said what stalled him was using TLA+ on real projects and having no time for exercises, not anything about the problems.

MEASURED STATE OF THE RAMP, from the seven VECTOR.md files and their references at 2026-10-02.

  pos              repr kind count sources space form  gate
  floor ch11          0    2     1       0     0    0  ch11
  01 bonded-store     1    2     1       0     0    0  ch11
  02 laytime          2    2     1       0     0    0  ch11
  03 river-call       2    2     1       1     0    0  ch11
  04 assay-office     1    3     1       1     0    0  ch11
  05 floor-malting    2    3     2       1     0    0  ch11
  06 herbarium-sheet  2    3     2       1     0    1  ch11
  07 estate-notice    2    3     2       2     0    1  ch11

K=1 holds across every step. Each one raises exactly one dimension by one.

Construct counts over the seven references, grep per file:
  EXCEPT   4, 0, 5, 4, 5, 7, 4
  WF_      0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 4
  ~>       0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 2, 0
  SF_, []<>, INSTANCE: zero in all seven.

So property kind 3 IS liveness, and 04 through 07 already have it. The ramp sums to 10 of a possible 18 at position 07, so it is roughly half built.

H1. STATE SPACE HAS NEVER LEFT 0. Not one problem has made a reader deal with a model that does not fit. No CONSTRAINT, no VIEW, no SYMMETRY anywhere in the seven. For a course that calls itself post-graduate this is the biggest hole, and it is the one that connects to what Frank just said about his stall: he was using TLA+ on real projects, and real models blow up. The ramp never teaches that.

H2. REPRESENTATION CAPS AT 2, SO PLUSCAL NEVER APPEARS. Representation 2 means no program counter. Frank own fencing model is PlusCal with a pc. Nothing on the ramp is.

H3. PROPERTY KIND IS TOPPED OUT AT 3. Four of the six dimensions have one or two levels of headroom. Kind has none, so it cannot be the dimension that sets a new high again.

H4. NO REFINEMENT. INSTANCE is zero everywhere, so chapter 13 is untouched by the problem set even though exercises/ch13 exists.

THE READING GATE NEEDS SETTLING BEFORE ANY OF THIS, AND IT IS A LOCKED DECISION. D4 clause (c) of drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_4cd7acae35ef634cf4ebbabb says a problem gated ch13 sits after a ch13 checkpoint, with values ch11 | ch13 | refinement. That gate exists because PRACTICE-PLAN.md:117 says "I am at learntla section 11" and problems had to sit after the chapter they needed. The audience changed on 2026-10-02 to people who have FINISHED learntla.

If the reader has ch12 and ch13, the gate stops being an ordering constraint. And tla-h1ki, six of seven references needing EXCEPT while declaring ch11, dissolves rather than needing a fix: the reader has EXCEPT. ch12 was never even a legal gate value, which is the symptom of a vocabulary built for one reader progress rather than for a prerequisite.

RECOMMENDATION, and it reopens a locked decision so it is Frank call. Keep the field, stop using it to order. Re-read it as "what this problem assumes you have read", which is useful to a reader deciding whether they are ready, and drop clause (c) from the sequence invariant. The alternative worth considering: keep clause (c) and position the problem ramp explicitly after the ch02-ch13 exercise track, so the checkpoints are the exercises themselves rather than a reader self-report. That is cleaner architecture and more work.

WHAT TO FARM FROM FENCING. It is removed from the delivered tree and its statement, spike, consistency check and attempt log all stay in the repo under sources/. Four reusable things:

1. THE BEFORE-AND-AFTER PAIR IN ONE PROBLEM. fencing PROBLEM.md:43-51 asks for a model of the broken system, a model of the fixed one, and an account of what changed, checking each property against both. No problem on the ramp has that shape, and it is the only shape that teaches a property is wrong rather than a model is wrong.
2. THE HEADLINE FINDING. sources/spikes/fencing/REPORT.md records that the obvious property is false in the FENCED system too. "Your property passed and it was still the wrong property" is a lesson nothing else here teaches.
3. A CLOCK AS A STEP SOURCE. MaxTime = 5 in the spike cfgs. That is step sources 3 by the pinned rubric, one above the ramp current top.
4. TWO INDEPENDENT CORRECT MODELS EXISTED. The spike wrote 8 variables of raw TLA+ with a hand-rolled pc. Frank wrote 5 variables of PlusCal with a generated one, different decomposition entirely, 4 EXCEPTs each. That is measured evidence that this system admits real modelling choice, which is what CHOICES.md exists to protect, and it is worth keeping as a worked example rather than discarding with the problem.

WHY FENCING ITSELF COULD NOT TAKE A RAMP SLOT. It would raise representation 2 to 3 and step sources 2 to 3 in one problem, which is two new highs and violates clause (b) prime. That is a placement sketch rather than the record tla-gdka owes, since four of six dimensions were estimated from the artifact without reading the two pinned rubric drawers.

SEQUENCING I WOULD PROPOSE, each step one new high:
  08  state space 0 to 1     the first model that needs bounding
  09  representation 2 to 3  a program counter, which is PlusCal
  10  step sources 2 to 3    a clock, farmed from fencing idea 3
  11  form left open 1 to 2  the before-and-after pair, farmed from idea 1
  12  state space 1 to 2     a model that needs a VIEW or SYMMETRY
  13  property count 2 to 3
Refinement and INSTANCE sit above all of it and want their own run, since nothing in the set touches chapter 13 yet.

That ordering is a proposal and rests on H1 being the biggest hole. If Frank disagrees about which gap matters most, the order changes and nothing else does.

AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: reopens a locked decision and needs Frank on the reading gate before any problem gets authored.

Files: PRACTICE-PLAN.md, authoring/, harness/sequence.sh
notes:
---
FRANK RULED 2026-10-02 on two of the open questions, and asked for the other two restated.

N2, THE CHEAT SHEET: KEEP IT. His words: "I think its ok to have it, this isnt for memorization, its for application and skill." So publishing chapter N own cheat sheet beside its statement stands, collapsed behind a note as tla-jaob.1 shipped it. That also settles the posture for the references question on tla-jaob by analogy, though not the question itself.

N5, THE LOAD VECTOR AND THE RAMP: THEY MATTER. "Agreed, they matter." So tla-t8jz and tla-ahxl resolve toward UN-RETIRING rather than retiring the gates. Whoever works those two should read this and the direction drawer first, since my written recommendation on both beads argued the other way before the audience changed.

N4, THE READING GATE, is still open and he asked for it restated. The question is whether the field is a RULE or a NOTE:
- A rule: tla-h1ki is a real P1 bug, six of seven problems declare ch11 while their references use EXCEPT which is ch12, six labels need fixing, and the vocabulary needs a ch12 value it cannot currently express.
- A note telling a reader what a problem assumes: nothing is mislabeled for someone who read all of learntla, tla-h1ki closes as dissolved, and clause (c) comes out of the sequence invariant.
My recommendation is the note.

MAJORITY-VOTE IS PULLED, per his "pull it and farm it for ideas". Removed from ~/tla-practice/problems/ 2026-10-02. All 10 files stay under curated/majority-vote/ as the record, and the delivered pair is in the 2026-10-02-fresh-start backup. tla-fr50 closes.

WHAT WAS FARMED FROM IT, and there is more here than from fencing.

FOUR NAMED TECHNIQUES, from curated/majority-vote/notes/TECHNIQUES.md:
1. Turning the input into part of the state.
2. Replacing a collection with a summary of it.
3. Carrying a strengthening alongside the property you care about.
4. Bounding an infinite domain from outside the module.

Number 4 is the one to take first. It is the state-space dimension, which is H1 of this plan, the hole where the ramp has never left level 0. majority-vote already carries the technique the ramp lacks.

THE REPRESENTATION COLLAPSE, and CHOICES.md calls it "the decision the problem exists for". The statement talks about positions. Every read position is cancelled or standing, a cancellation pairs two, all standing ones share a value. The published specification carries NO POSITIONS. It carries cnt, how many stand, and cand, the value they share (Majority.tla:26-27). So the obvious representation collapses to two scalars.

FOUR WORKABLE REPRESENTATIONS FOR ONE QUESTION: a counter, a set, a bag, a pair list. With real analysis rather than a list. "The pair list is the only one of the four that can express no position takes part in more than one cancellation as written. All three cost state that grows with the sequence length rather than with the count."

AND THE SENTENCE WORTH BUILDING A PROBLEM AROUND, CHOICES.md: "I dont think any of these is the right answer. The counter is the smallest state that supports the correctness statement the author wanted. A bigger representation is the right answer for a different statement."

That is the form-left-open dimension at a level the ramp does not reach, and it is a better lesson than anything in the seven: the right representation depends on which statement you are trying to make, not on which representation is better. Four candidates, all workable, each able to say something the others cannot.

SO THE REVISED SEQUENCING PROPOSAL. My earlier order put state space 0 to 1 first and the before-and-after pair at position 11. Both farmed sources now point at the same two slots, so:
  08  state space 0 to 1     bounding an infinite domain from outside the module, farmed from majority-vote technique 4
  09  representation 2 to 3  a program counter, which is PlusCal
  10  form left open 1 to 2  several workable representations, one statement, farmed from majority-vote
  11  step sources 2 to 3    a clock, farmed from fencing
  12  form left open 2 to 3  the before-and-after pair, farmed from fencing
  13  state space 1 to 2     a model needing a VIEW or SYMMETRY
Still a proposal, still resting on H1 being the biggest hole.

ALSO WORTH KEEPING: the CHOICES.md format itself. It reads the published specification as a set of decisions somebody made, says for each what it picked and what else was on the table and what the pick costs and buys, and opens with "Your model reading differently shouldn not read as your model reading wrong." That is the artifact that protects real modelling choice and it should be the template for every future problem.

---
N4 GETS SHARPER, found 2026-10-02 while the tla-6mrz worker corrected my brief about ORDER.

I told that worker ORDER "holds seven bare names, one per line, where the line number IS the number." Wrong. scripts/number-problems.sh:119-126 skips blank lines, # comments, and exactly two markers that occupy a POSITION in the sequence without consuming a NUMBER:

  checkpoint: ch13
  checkpoint: refinement

That is D4 clause (c) implemented in the ORDER file format. The reading gate is not just a field on a problem, it is two positional markers in the delivered sequence.

SIX SCRIPTS KNOW ABOUT THEM AND NOTHING USES THEM. grep for the marker returns scripts/number-problems.sh, scripts/deliver-problems.sh, harness/sequence.sh, harness/test-number-problems.sh, harness/test-deliver-problems.sh and harness/test-sequence.sh. grep -c over the live ~/tla-practice/problems/ORDER returns 0.

So the mechanism Frank is being asked to rule on is implemented in six files and wired to nothing. Another built-and-never-wired instance, the same shape as the load vector gates in tla-ahxl.

WHAT THAT DOES TO THE DECISION. It makes the note answer cheaper and the rule answer more expensive than I said.

If the gate is a NOTE: the two markers come out of ORDER parsing in all six files, the skip list in number-problems.sh shrinks, clause (c) comes out of the sequence invariant, and tla-h1ki closes as dissolved. Nothing regresses, because nothing ever used them.

If the gate is a RULE: somebody has to decide where the two checkpoints go in a seven-problem sequence that currently declares every problem ch11, fix the six mislabelled problems, and add a ch12 value the vocabulary cannot express. And the first real use of a mechanism built a month ago arrives with no test of it in a delivered tree.

My recommendation is unchanged and now better evidenced: make it a note.

ALSO CORRECTED: ORDER widens past two digits at scripts/number-problems.sh:174-176, so the %02d I described is a floor rather than the format.
---
CYCLE 5 OPENED 2026-10-03. drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_20ad6fe9661059e6d830b053 carries the findings; drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_4cd7acae35ef634cf4ebbabb is now cycle 5, soundness RED, four markers.

F1. THE RAMP IS NOT WEDGED, and I told Frank it was. harness/sequence.sh --search reasons over 13 vector records. Six of those 13 are exactly the problems D5 withdrew on 2026-09-04: buyclub, consign, custody, pilot, qsl, seedlib. Every blocked candidate at position 8 is a withdrawn problem and not one is a ramp rung. Measured: a scratch tree holding the floor plus the seven authored-to-rung problems, VECTOR_ROOT pointed at it, returns the live ORDER and exits 0. True state is seven rungs built and position 8 unauthored.

Why it slipped: the scan reads every VECTOR.md above a reference/FREEZE.sha256 under authoring/ and pilot/ (harness/sequence.sh:58-62). Withdrawal is recorded in each record's prose and in the ORDER file, neither of which the scanner reads.

F2. SOFTENING CLAUSE (a) REACHES 10 OF 13, NOT 13. Brute force over all 13 plus the floor, five settings. V0 current = 7 (reproduces the script exactly, which is the control). V1 soften (a) = 10, adding consign, buyclub, pilot. V2 relax (b') only = 13. V3 both = 13. V4 K=2 with (a) hard = 10. Probe at scratchpad/ramp-probe.py.

So K=2 buys nothing, and (a) is the binding constraint only up to position 10.

F3. THE ONLY SETTING THAT ORDERS ALL 13 DROPS THE RAMP. V2 reaches 13 by admitting assay-office at position 1, which rises on representation, property kind and step sources at once from the floor. That is the cliff (b') exists to forbid and it is D4's whole grounding. So (b') is not negotiable, and no complete order over the existing 13 exists at any acceptable setting.

F4. WHAT BLOCKS THE THREE V1 CANNOT PLACE. Running max after V1's ten is repr 2, kind 3, count 2, sources 2, space 1, form 3. qsl needs count +1 and space +1 together, so (b'). seedlib needs count +1 and sources +1 together, so (b'). custody needs space +2, so (b), and four dimensions rise. Minimum single-dimension rungs to unblock all three: count 2 to 3, space 1 to 2 (qsl legal), sources 2 to 3 (seedlib legal), repr 2 to 3 and space 2 to 3 (custody legal). Five rungs, which is five problems.

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE SEQUENCING PROPOSAL ABOVE. It strengthens it. Positions 08 to 13 author six fresh rungs, which is what F3 says the ramp needs, and it never touches the reserve. D5 already said the reserve is a per-rung call with Frank and never the plan. So the proposal was right and my framing of why was wrong: these rungs are not a repair for a wedge, they are the next six rungs of a ramp that is working as designed.

N4 IS NOW MARKER C1 and still my recommendation: make the reading gate a note. Nothing in F1 to F4 changes that argument.

C2 IS NEW AND IT IS CENTRAL'S TO PROPOSE, NOT FRANK'S: does --search keep scanning the withdrawn set? My read is yes, keep the set and label it, because D5 allows a per-rung draw on the reserve and silently dropping them would hide that option. What has to change is the report. "no valid order over 13 problems" should distinguish ramp rungs from reserve candidates, and the hole line should say "nothing authored for position 8 yet" rather than naming six withdrawn problems as failures.
CORRECTION 2026-10-08, measured by central, not recalled.

H2 as written says 'Representation caps at 2, so PlusCal never appears.' The second half is FALSE. Three of the seven ramp references carry a PlusCal translation:

  grep -rl 'BEGIN TRANSLATION' authoring/<rung>/reference/
  bonded-store 2 files, laytime 2 files, assay-office 2 files
  river-call, floor-malting, herbarium-sheet, estate-notice 0

Each count is the .tla plus its -commented.tla, so three distinct rungs. All three carry a pc token.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ABSENT is the multi-label algorithm. All three translations are a single unlabelled while (TRUE), so the pc has one value and does no work. A reader never has to reason about where in a procedure a process is.

So the representation hole is not 'introduce PlusCal'. It is 'introduce a program counter that takes more than one value'. A problem authored to the old reading could add PlusCal and move nothing.

INSTANCE is still zero across all seven, measured the same way, so H4 stands unchanged.

title: The audience is someone who finished learntla, not Frank
description:
Frank, 2026-10-02, after being laid off the previous day: skilling up specifically for CrossnoKaye is in the rearview. The goal is now "creating an expanding and interesting artifact for other people studying TLA+. The exercises that we have that match learntla are awesome, this should be the post graduate course."

So the audience changes from one person to anyone who has finished learntla, and the artifact changes from a private practice tree to a published course. That invalidates premises all over PRACTICE-PLAN.md, which names Frank as the audience throughout.

WHAT THE PUBLISHED SITE ACTUALLY IS TODAY. mkdocs.yml site_description reads "A 107-puzzle progressive curriculum for learning TLA+ and PlusCal by doing" and docs/curriculum/ holds tier-0 through tier-7 plus judgments, apalache and final. That is puzzles/, the v1 set, which the post-mortem drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_78e0afcd8f0f7bb925f61ef0 says died of QG rule 2. The public face of the project is the failed curriculum.

WHAT IS NOT PUBLISHED. find docs -iname "*exercise*" returns nothing, so the ch02 through ch13 exercise sets, the part Frank calls awesome and the part the printed-command gate covers with 221 assertions, are invisible. So are the seven batch-2 problems and fencing, which live in authoring/ and in the unversioned ~/tla-practice/.

PREMISES IN PRACTICE-PLAN.md THAT THE AUDIENCE CHANGE BREAKS:
- "One step ahead. Build one problem ahead of me, never thirty." Built for a single reader who gates the next problem. A published course cannot ship one problem.
- "The reaction log." REACTIONS.md is Frank-s own complaint channel. A stranger has no way to send one and no reason to.
- The door test, D1 of the difficulty-progression cycle: "the learner reads a statement until they either start modelling or bounce, and a bounce is a complaint against the previous rung." Grounded in Frank, 2026-09-04: "I am the target audience ... if 16 was twice as hard as 17 he would come and say so." Strangers do not come and say so.
- "Validation. It splits in two, and the split is about what I can actually judge." One judge.
- The yardstick in sources/own-systems.md ranks workflow, two-store, lifecycle, expiry and rollout because those are the shapes CrossnoKaye-s platform contained. Every family verdict in sources/README.md is scored against that ranking. The anchor moved.

PREMISES THE CHANGE RESCUES, and this is the part worth noticing:
- The difficulty ramp matters MORE, not less. Frank could self-select past a badly placed problem. A stranger reading in order cannot. D4-s K=1 rule is already stated over the delivered sequence rather than over one person-s history, so it transfers. That argues against the retirement in tla-t8jz and tla-ahxl rather than for it.
- The reading gate becomes essential. A post-graduate course after learntla has to say which chapter a problem needs. tla-h1ki is the live defect there, six of seven references needing a chapter-12 construct while all seven declare chapter 11.
- tla-16je stops being hypothetical. Publishing five unlicensed repositories specs to strangers is redistribution for real. The prose pipeline sidesteps it, since the spike is our own spec.
- The grader stays dead and gets deader. 69 to 71 percent over-validation, and a stranger has nobody to appeal to.

THE ONE DECISION THAT BLOCKS PUBLISHING. The exercise/answer split is a delivery convention, not a structure. scripts/deliver-exercises.sh:20-23 hands over EXERCISES.md and starters/ and withholds references/ and reports/. A public repo publishes exercises/ch11/references/ next to the statement. Options: publish the references deliberately (my recommendation, since isolation served the retired grader and the retired blind panel rather than the learner), or move references behind their own top-level directory with a README so a reader chooses to open it, which is learntla-s shape. Not two repos.

THIS IS ABOVE-BEAD WORK AND SHOULD PROBABLY BE A DESIGN CYCLE. Filed as a bead so it is not lost, and because an unrecorded direction change cost this project 26 days the last time, see drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_d613ee38c5d64215673a4023.

AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: direction change, needs Frank on the references question before anything restructures.

Files: PRACTICE-PLAN.md, mkdocs.yml, sources/own-systems.md, sources/README.md
notes:
RULED BY FRANK 2026-10-15, and the question this bead asks is now answered.

"For now, let's keep me as the only audience, and file a P1 for later to shift
this to being a more general purpose tool for others."

So the audience is Frank, the artifact stays a private practice tree, and
PRACTICE-PLAN.md's premises STAND rather than being invalidated. The
published-course question is deferred whole, with its own bead and its own
priority, at tla-byyo.

NOT CLOSED, AND DEMOTED TO P2 INSTEAD, because two children carry real work
that outlives the question: tla-jaob.2 (the ramp above position 07) and
tla-jaob.3 (the twelve exercise H1s using two shapes). Closing with --force
would orphan both under a closed parent. This bead is now a shell holding
them.

THE CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING. tla-ahxl is unblocked. It measures 76 percent of
the full gate enforcing rules PRACTICE-PLAN.md:159-168 retires, and the only
reason not to act on those retirements was that THIS bead said to distrust the
document recording them. It is the largest mechanical win in the backlog and
it was blocked here for twelve days.

title: scripts/deliver-exercises.sh hardcodes an upper chapter bound of 13
description:
Found by the tla-i3zu worker 2026-10-01, outside its Files: line so it was reported rather than fixed.

scripts/deliver-exercises.sh:71 reads:

  if [ "$CHAPTER_NUM" -lt 2 ] || [ "$CHAPTER_NUM" -gt 13 ]; then

That is the second hand-maintained chapter bound in the project. tla-i3zu removed the first one, harness/test-printed-commands.sh:191, which was a literal CHAPTERS=(02 ... 11) and silently stopped covering ch.12 and ch.13 when they landed.

THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS NOW CORRECT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS P2 AND NOT P1. The gate derives its chapter list from exercises/ch??/ carrying an EXERCISES.md, so an exercises/ch14/ gets FOUND. Delivery then refuses it with rc=1 and the gate fails loudly. That is the opposite of the silent drop this bound would have caused before tla-i3zu, so nothing is going to go unnoticed. Measured, from the same worker probing templates/:

  $ bash scripts/deliver-exercises.sh templates .probe/dest
  rc=1
  Usage: scripts/deliver-exercises.sh <chapter> [dest-root]
    chapter    integer 2-13, the chapter to deliver exercises for

THE WORK. Landing ch.14 needs this line widened, and widening it by hand reintroduces exactly the shape tla-i3zu removed. So derive the bound or drop it.

Deriving an upper bound here is a DIFFERENT change from deriving a list, which is why the worker filed it separately rather than folding it in. Delivery takes one chapter as an argument and has no reason to know the set. The honest options:

1. Drop the upper bound and keep the lower one. The script already fails on a directory that is not there, so the bound buys an earlier error message and nothing else. Simplest, and I lean this way.
2. Derive it by checking exercises/ch<N>/ exists. Same effect as option 1 with a better message.
3. Keep a bound and gate it against the derived list, so the two cannot disagree. Most machinery for the least gain.

The usage text at the same site also names "integer 2-13" and has to move with whatever is chosen.

RED: INVARIANT: delivering a chapter directory that exists under exercises/ and carries an EXERCISES.md succeeds, with no upper bound written into the script.

title: corpus/MANIFEST.md carries counts derived from manifest.tsv and nothing checks them
description:
harness/test-corpus-manifest.sh gates corpus/manifest.tsv and never reads corpus/MANIFEST.md. grep -n MANIFEST.md harness/test-corpus-manifest.sh returns nothing.

MANIFEST.md carries at least two tables whose numbers are a function of the TSV:

- the level distribution (L1 24, L2 17, L3 24, L4 33, L5 45), which awk over column 6 reproduces exactly today
- the funnel (666 modules, 211 specs, 127 candidate groups, 143 systems, 131 describable), where describable is column 7 and reproduces exactly today

Both agree with the TSV as of 0122d31. Nothing keeps them agreeing. Add a row to the TSV, or correct one level after reading a module, and the prose goes stale silently.

THIS IS THE DRIFT THAT PRODUCED tla-t64z. PRACTICE-PLAN.md carried a funnel as six numbers with no rows behind them, the rows were lost, and the level-3 count sat wrong in the live plan for 26 days while every decision downstream rested on it. MANIFEST.md exists because of exactly that, and it reintroduced the same shape one layer down: derived numbers in prose with no gate.

WHAT TO ADD. A check in harness/test-corpus-manifest.sh that recomputes each table MANIFEST.md states from manifest.tsv and compares. The level table and the describable count are the two that are cleanly derivable. The modules, specs and candidate-groups counts came from passes over a corpus clone rather than from the TSV, so those are not derivable offline and the check should say so rather than pretend.

Conventions: gate-don-t-advise. A correctness invariant must never depend on a human rereading two tables.

RED: INVARIANT: every count in corpus/MANIFEST.md that is derivable from corpus/manifest.tsv equals the value recomputed from the TSV.

notes:
---
SHA CORRECTION. The close reason cites 2c5f4ec for GREEN and 06497d9 for the budget. git pull --rebase flattened the --no-ff merge before the push, so on main those are 93d83d4 and 4c3d64c. Pushed in b732cb8..4eb3731. The old SHAs still exist as dangling objects but are not ancestors of main.

Second time this bit in one night, and the lesson is recorded on tla-frpu too: push before closing, or cite the branch commit rather than the merge.

GREEN and merged at 2c5f4ec, budget 06497d9. Contract drawer drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_63b916e32e13e2d904f3a890.

harness/test-corpus-manifest.sh reads corpus/MANIFEST.md now and recomputes every count in it the TSV can answer. 19 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped, up from 7 passed and 1 skipped. 500 new lines and 17 planted controls where there were 6.

THE RED IS THE BUG STATED AS OUTPUT. With md_mismatches stubbed to return nothing, the suite printed 'ok corpus/MANIFEST.md: every derivable count agrees with the TSV' alongside 11 FAIL control md-* lines reading 'accepted, so the check is blind to it'. A checker reading nothing reporting agreement is exactly the defect.

WHAT IS GATED. All 5 Levels rows. The licence table driven from TSV licence values plus row count. The corpus table clone SHA and licence per repository, 16 rows by 2 columns, plus a check that the TSV agrees with itself before either is trusted. The funnel systems and describable stages. The rebuilt distinct-systems and describable in 'what moved'. The five level-3 survivors as a multiset of repo and tlc_seconds. And 20 prose counts, including the whole survival chain I added hours earlier.

WHAT IS NOT, EACH AS A PRINTED SKIP. Nine skip lines name what went unchecked and why: the funnel modules 666 / specs 211 / candidate groups 127 counted over the 54 MB clone, the corpus table .tla column, the lost 2026-09 recorded funnel, the per-spec Checkability figures, the clone-wide totals, PRACTICE-PLAN.md own numbers, the shortened survivor system names, the Left out bullet, and the honest residual: 'any count in a sentence no claim above names (prose has no coverage net, only the tables do)'.

TWO CONTROLS I DID NOT ASK FOR, AND THEY ARE WHAT MAKES MARKDOWN PARSING HONEST. md-reword deletes a claimed sentence and the gate FAILS with 'band floor: not found, so the sentence was reworded and the check went blind', because each prose claim must match exactly once. md-newtable appends a numeric table and the gate FAILS naming it, which is coverage-of-coverage for tables.

34 out-of-suite perturbations beyond the 11 controls. 34 of 34 bite, zero blind, real pair 0 mismatches.

NO STALE NUMBER ANYWHERE, which confirms and extends my 2026-10-01 measurement: the level table, describable 131, the survival chain, the licence table (MIT 116, NONE FOUND 19, Apache-2.0 8), 92 unattempted, 16 repositories, 5 unlicensed repositories, 19 unlicensed systems, and all 16 per-repo SHAs and licences.

MY BRIEF WAS WRONG IN TWO PLACES AND THE WORKER SAID SO. It preferred design 1, parse the markdown, while separately requiring the level-3 survival chain be gated. That chain is prose at corpus/MANIFEST.md:112-117, so a pure table parser would have reported green while omitting the numbers this bead most cares about. The worker took a hybrid and explained why. Its first version was 6.4s, 9.1x, which tripped the BUDGET DRIFT warning, so it collapsed the markdown and TSV reads into one awk pass each and memoized the TSV facts in the parent.

Full gate green, 18 suites, 296.4s.

description:

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. PRACTICE-PLAN.md:114-115 says the old plan^s door test "kept saying a mis-ordered problem is one I would complain about, and it never built anywhere for the complaint to go". The door test is D1 of the difficulty-progression cycle, and it is the ONE human signal in the whole verification design: "the learner reads a statement until they either start modelling or bounce, and a bounce is a complaint against the previous rung". With no place for the complaint, the door test is an advisory, which is the shape gate-don^t-advise exists to catch.

Frank has now worked fencing and majority-vote is in progress (tla-fr50), so reactions exist and have nowhere to go.

title: The vector author cannot touch the statement or reference it cites
description:
Goal: keep the author who assigns a problem's difficulty out of any position to
reshape the problem. The direction-change drawer names the hazard: "Scoping a
statement is the lever that lets an author hit a number, and that is the
load-vector failure returning through a different door."

From D4 of `drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_0721f0abe841f73eb9def38d`.

The consistency checker is the one reader in the prose pipeline that sees
statement and models together, so it looks like the obvious vector author.
`sources/problems/fencing/CONSISTENCY.md:1-6` confirms it reads both. It is also
able to send findings back that change the statement, which is exactly the
position the hazard forbids. So the vector is a separate reader that writes
nothing but `VECTOR.md`.

RED: INVARIANT: the commit that adds a VECTOR.md touches no file under that package's statement/ or reference/.

This is a git-shaped invariant rather than a filesystem one, so the gate reads
history. Worth knowing before you start: batch 2 would FAIL this retroactively.
Its step 4 wrote the statement and `VECTOR.md` in one pass
(`drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_6d349977cc3dcf7f0a97aacb`, step 4), which was
sound there because batch 2 wrote the reference FIRST and derived the statement
by stripping it, so its statement author had seen the reference by construction.
The prose pipeline inverts that order.

So the gate needs a scope. Either it applies only to packages built after this
lands, or it carries an explicit grandfather list of the twelve batch-2 packages.
Pick one and say why. A gate that reports twelve historical failures on every run
gets ignored, which is worse than not having it.

title: A frozen reference covers every model the statement asks for
description:
Goal: a frozen reference that cannot answer the statement's own task list is a
reference in name only. `fencing` asks for a model of the first version, a model
of the second, and an account of what the numbers change. A reference holding
only the fixed system leaves part 3 unreferenced, and part 3 is where the
spike's headline finding lives.

prose. `~/tla-practice/problems/fencing/PROBLEM.md:43-51` numbers its three
requirements in English, and counting "models required" off that reliably is not
a grep.

reads, which costs every statement a new section and risks leaking shape to the
learner, or the gate checks a weaker claim that is still worth having, for

take it.

`authoring/bonded-store/reference/FREEZE.sha256`, so no format change is needed.

title: attempts/ and released/ mirror problems/ by name, and numbering breaks the mirror
description:
`~/tla-practice/README.md` steps 2 to 4 tell a learner to copy their work into
`attempts/<name>/`, and say the reference is released to `released/<name>/`. That
is the same name `problems/<name>/` carries, so the three trees mirror each other
by convention with nothing enforcing it.

`tla-0lwx` numbers `problems/` and leaves the other two alone, by Frank's call of
2026-09-18. So the mirror breaks the moment it lands, and
`problems/01_bonded-store/` sits beside `attempts/bonded-store/`.

There is prior art for the numbered form already in the tree.
`attempts/withdrawn-2026-09-04/` holds `00-permit-review-critique` through
`05-consign`, two digits with a dash. That convention went out with batch 1 and
nothing replaced it.

## Three things to settle

What `attempts/` does. Following `problems/` means an attempt directory gets
renamed whenever the ramp is reordered, which moves work Frank has already done.
Not following leaves the mirror broken. A third option is to name an attempt for
the problem's bare name and never number it, which keeps attempts stable and makes
the mirror explicit rather than positional. I lean to the third, and I don't think
the case is strong enough to call it without Frank.

What `released/` does. It is empty today, so it costs nothing to settle now and a
lot to settle after it fills.

Whether `attempts/withdrawn-2026-09-04/` is touched. I would leave it. It is an
archive of a withdrawn batch, and its names record what those problems were called
at the time.

## One thing that will bite whoever takes this

`~/tla-practice/README.md` has no source in this repo. Nothing here generates it and
no script writes it, so it is hand-maintained in a tree that is not under version
control. Steps 2 to 4 name the directory shape directly and need rewriting whatever
gets decided.

Files: scripts/number-problems.sh
notes:
FRANK RULED 2026-10-18: OPTION 1, follow the numbering. attempts/ and released/ mirror problems/ including the number prefix, "it makes it easier to track". So an attempt directory gets renamed when the ramp reorders, and that cost is accepted. I had leaned to option 3 and was overruled. attempts/withdrawn-2026-09-04/ is an archive and is not in scope. ~/tla-practice/README.md steps 2 to 4 need rewriting and have no source in this repo.
CORRECTION to the close reason above: the successor is tla-xbbb, not tla-wqn6. I wrote the id before filing it and bd assigned a different one.

Each tree answers to the ORDER sitting BESIDE it, so an attempt batch keeps its own frozen copy and a later reorder of problems/ORDER leaves finished work alone. Frank: 'I am comfortable with each of your calls on this.' The numbered names still mirror problems/, which is what his original ruling was about. title: Build a rollout problem from the Argo candidates
description:
Rollout is the fifth of the five shapes this engineer needs, and it turned out to be the
densest source measured: 440 titles scanned, 32 opened, 26 modelable. Evidence in
sources/rollout.md.

It also came closest to being missed. A first pass searched the word rollout inside
general trackers and found one instance in 24. The supply lives in trackers whose entire
subject matter is rollout, where nobody has any reason to write the word.

Four candidates named, in the order the survey ranked them.

argo-cd 29410, a step marked complete against stale per-member status. One cause produces
two failures, an inverted ordering and a member silently left behind, which is unusual and
makes it the richest of the four.

argo-rollouts 2235, four timestamped writes leaving every routed destination at zero pods.
The sharpest safety violation and the smallest specification.

knative serving 16649, a monotone pointer latching an under-scaled revision. The only
irreversible failure found anywhere in the pass.

ocm 1346, a member in neither shard during a two-write rebalance. The purest instance of
neither old nor new.

Argo CD ApplicationSet ProgressiveSync is the closest match to his own platform: one
commit rolled across per-cluster cohorts under a concurrency cap, which is cloud-state with
the names changed.

Two things the survey established about size. Three members is enough and often two,
because the bug is always one member in a state the controller does not believe it is in
and the rest of the fleet is scenery. What costs is version depth rather than fleet width,
so a candidate needing a rollback window or a third commit is the expensive one.

Holding the cause back is cheap here. 18 of 26 are a heading-level deletion, and 46% carry
no diagnosis at all because the template extracts a symptom and a repro from reporters who
never found the cause.

Every one of these was judged from prose with nothing built. Spike before committing.

title: The manifest's prose column detects a README, not a description of the system
description:
corpus/manifest.tsv marks prose yes when the system's directory holds a README or the
module carries a header comment of eight lines or more. That is a test for a file
existing, not for the thing PRACTICE-PLAN.md needs.

What the plan needs is an independent prose description of the system, so a statement can
be checked against something the statement's author did not write. Sampling five level 1
and 2 rows marked prose yes:

- Majority, a real description of the algorithm and what it computes
- SlidingPuzzles, a Wikipedia link and TLC state counts
- N-Queens, an email from Stephan Merz about where the spec came from
- CigaretteSmokers, a Wikipedia link
- GameOfLife, a Wikipedia link

One of five. The reader on slice 3 flagged the same over-firing on bibliographic-stub
READMEs and I did not weight it enough when assembling.

MissionariesAndCannibals is the sharpest case. Its README describes the spec, not the
puzzle: "This is a very simple TLA+ spec that can be read by someone knowing nothing
about TLA+."

I do not think this sinks anything. For a famous system Wikipedia is an independent
description, and a README that links it is delegating rather than failing. The column is
just answering a different question from the one that matters.

So the fix is to record where a description lives rather than whether a file exists.
Something like authored, delegated, or none, with the pointer. The 21 rows at levels 1
and 2 currently reading prose yes are inflated as a count of usable descriptions.

This also affects the plan's own figure. PRACTICE-PLAN.md says prose ships with 50 of 67
and treats the other 17 as the problem cases. If the real distinction is authored against
delegated, that split needs recounting before it is used to decide what goes last.

title: Checkability is unknown for 132 of 211 specs, which ship no model
description:
The manifest's checkable column reads unattempted for most rows. Only 79 of 211 specs ship
a .cfg for their own module, so TLC was never run on the rest.

That is a gap in the sweep rather than a fact about those specs, and the column says so
rather than reading no. Establishing checkability for the other 132 means writing a model
for each: constants, a state constraint where the state space is unbounded, and a decision
about what to check.

Two things the sweep did measure are worth keeping in view. Of the 79 attempted, 15 hit
the 45 second budget and 13 failed to parse. And parse failures fell from 27 to 13 once
CommunityModules went on the module path, so a third of these specs do not stand alone and
a curated problem has to ship the library modules alongside the specification.

I would not do this for all 132. The plan builds one problem ahead rather than thirty, so
the cheap version is to fill this column for a system at the moment it gets picked, and
let the rest stay honestly blank.

title: Two shipped claims about floor malting's conjunct coverage are wrong
description:
The dead-conjunct sweep deleted each of 21 top-level conjuncts in turn and ran all
eight obligations together over the frozen reference and 25 variants, 572 runs. Seven
conjuncts changed no row. Five of those are dead only because the matrix has no
variant aimed at them, which is a fact about the instrument, so this bead is about
the two that contradict something already written down.

ONE. The commented reference says of requirement 1 that "S02 breaks the stage half
instead and lands on the line above, so the two conjuncts get separate arrows". The
arrow is a source location, not coverage. Delete the stage half and S02 still returns
rc=13, caught by the same rule's count half, because S02 opens at the marker rather
than at zero. The comment needs correcting, and it probably cannot be fixed by adding
a variant: an opening with wrong stages and well-formed counts breaks
`CountBelongsToTheFloor` first and the invariant wins at rc=12, which the author
already recorded at S20.

TWO. `reports/step2-variants.md:377-386` finds requirement 5's LATE-side conjunct
load-bearing and reads that as answering qsl's finding 3. It is the EARLY side that
carries nothing here, and S08 is the variant built for it, but S08 also mats a piece
into malt so the late side catches it first. One new variant closes it: kiln
unconditionally only where the count is below the lower mark.

Also worth knowing, though not a defect. Three deletions turn a verdict into
something that is not one. Dropping `CountBelongsToTheFloor`'s ceiling turns S03 into
a 300 second timeout, since nothing then bounds the count. Dropping its `\in Nat` half
turns S20 into rc=75. Dropping `TurningAddsOne`'s on-the-floor guard turns S10 into
rc=75.

title: Requirement 3's duty conjunct is dead weight against the declared set
description:
Requirement 3 says a lot that is out of the store has its place frozen and its duty
frozen. The reference's `LeavingIsFinal` carries both conjuncts. The duty conjunct
earns nothing.

Measured over the frozen reference and all 27 seeded variants, three requirements
declared together the way a learner declares them. Frank's place-only form
`OutStaysOut == [][\A l \in Lots: (place[l] \in {"released","movedOn"}) => (place[l] =
place'[l])]_place` gives an identical result to the shipped set on all 28 modules,
same token and same exit code. Deleting the duty conjunct and leaving the subscript
alone gives the identical result too, which is the same answer reached from different
text. Two controls fail where they should, so the agreement is not a blind battery.

The mechanism is not the obvious one. Central first argued the duty conjunct is
implied by requirement 1, since the biconditional makes duty a function of place and
a frozen place freezes duty. That reasoning is WRONG. Measured alone, the duty
conjunct catches S10, S11, S13, S14 and S20, and requirement 1 catches only S10 of
those. What actually covers the other four is requirement 3's OWN place conjunct.
So the conjunct is redundant against requirement 1 plus the place conjunct together,
never against requirement 1 alone.

Same defect family as tla-fg57, from the other end. Requirement 2 carries two arms
that are both load-bearing and reads as one property for a reason that turned out to
be the vector. Requirement 3 carries two conjuncts where one is dead. Both are a
property carrying two things that are not one thing, and Frank found the first and
then the second.

SECOND DEFECT, in the same analysis. `reports/step2-variants.md` finding 3 states
that no variant can exercise the duty clause alone. Four do. Its argument assumes any
duty change on an out lot leaves the lot released-and-unpaid or movedon-and-paid, and
a step that moves the place at the same time gives movedon-and-unpaid, which the
biconditional accepts. That finding needs correcting whether or not the conjunct goes.

What to decide, and it is not obvious. Dropping the conjunct makes requirement 3 a
place-only rule and the statement simpler. Keeping it means saying why a redundant
conjunct is worth writing, which is a real pedagogical position and not a bad one.
What is not defensible is the current state, where the statement asks for it and
nothing says it is redundant.

Frank raised this working the problem, 2026-09-05.

title: Requirement 2 is bundled to keep the vector legal, not because it is one rule
description:
Bonded-store's requirement 2 carries two arms under one property. The reference's
whole recorded reason is that they are "two halves of one movement rule rather than
two rules", which is a taxonomy claim.

Corpus practice does not support it. Of 28 published action properties carrying an
implication, 25 are single-arm. The closest analogue, BufferedRandomAccessFile.tla,
splits eight guarded implications into eight named properties on eight config lines.
The two genuine bundles found both bundle arms of AC4, one numbered requirement from
the atomic-commitment literature, in a file that names its other five requirements
separately. The working boundary is whether the arms answer to one requirement name.
Requirement 2's arms constrain different source states and different target sets.

The split is also free, mechanically. It catches everything the bundle catches across
28 modules, and `[][P /\ Q]_v` and `[][P]_v /\ [][Q]_v` are the same formula since
the stuttering disjunct distributes. It buys better logs, since the failing arm gets
named.

Here is the part that matters. Splitting takes the reference config from four
obligation lines to five, which crosses the property-count band from level 1 to level
2, and `harness/sequence.sh --check` then fails: two dimensions rise at once,
representation and property count. So the arms are joined to keep a number in a table
legal.

That is the finding, and it is bigger than this rung. If the ramp can bend a problem's
shape, the ramp is authoring the material. Either the count rubric should measure
something the author would not otherwise trade against, or a rung should be allowed to
declare a split that does not count as a rise.

comments.text: 2026-09-05: requirement 3 turns out to carry the mirror of this defect, filed as tla-oljv.
