title: Stage 4 §6b.1-2 — scaffold tla-practice/ + tla-answers/ with STRUCTURAL isolation
description:
Goal: Frank works the problems through a live Claude configuration rather than reading static
text — it presents the problem, answers questions, and drives review. He raised the leakage risk
himself, and it is the whole design constraint.

INSTRUCTION ISOLATION IS NOT ISOLATION (§6b.1). Telling an agent not to look at the answers DOES
NOT WORK — an agent debugging a harness failure will `cat` the reference, and it will be right to.
Isolation must be structural.

  Leak vector                                              Fix
  filesystem — reference readable from the working tree    two directories, not one
  context bleed — one agent both answers and holds it      two agents, different filesystem views
  git history — reference ever committed alongside         separate repo, never co-committed
  grader output — "missing conjunct 3 of the reference"    return a verdict object, never a diff
  TRAINING DATA — the model already knows burned problems  UNCLOSABLE. This is the operational
                                                           reason §5.7 screening is not optional.

ARCHITECTURE (§6b.2):
  tla-practice/ — statements, Frank's attempts, the harness CLIENT, its own .claude/. This is
                  where Frank and the tutor live.
  tla-answers/  — references, seeded variants, expected state counts, post-hoc commentary.
                  SEPARATE REPO, not co-located, denied in tla-practice/.claude/settings.json.

Files: (new repos ~/repos/tla-practice and ~/repos/tla-answers — outside this repo)

RED: INVARIANT: from inside tla-practice/, no path under tla-answers/ is readable — verified by an
actual attempted read, never by reading the settings file and believing it.
acceptance_criteria: Both repos exist; the deny rule is present AND demonstrated by a failed read attempt; no commit ever contains files from both.

title: Stage 2 §5.7 + §5.7b — the two independent screens: mechanism collision, and puzzle-versus-system
description:
Goal: two INDEPENDENT screens over every candidate problem. A candidate can pass one cleanly and
still be useless, which is why they are two screens and not one.

§5.7 MECHANISM COLLISION — "has someone already solved this?"
  gh api -X GET search/code -f q='<SystemName> language:tla' --jq '.total_count'
  Treat >3 hits as BURNED. Then the step that catches the misses: GREP THE MECHANISM, NOT THE
  NAME, against the tlaplus/Examples README table. "Warehouse robot coordination" is
  MisraReachability + mutual exclusion; "seat reservation" is the allocator; "leader failover"
  is Paxos. NAME NOVELTY IS NOT MECHANISM NOVELTY.

§5.7b PUZZLE-VERSUS-SYSTEM — "is it even the right KIND of thing?"
  THE SCREEN: if you hand the learner the legal moves, is there anything left to model? If no,
  it is a puzzle. Cut it, or add agents and failure until it isn't.

               | Puzzle                  | System
  legal moves  | given by the domain     | the thing you have to decide
  the question | is the goal reachable?  | is this design correct?
  who works    | TLC searches            | you model, TLC checks
  difficulty   | state-space size        | abstraction choice

  Why this is not pedantry: every puzzle in tlaplus/Examples — Die Hard, Tower of Hanoi,
  N-Queens, missionaries and cannibals, the sliding block puzzle — is flagged BEGINNER. Not
  because they are small, but because the modeling was pre-done by whoever wrote the rules. And
  "puzzles where the state space is handed to you and the work is search" is the FIRST of the
  four categories the corpus survey found the entire public corpus consists of. It is the
  category this project is defined against.

  LOCAL REPRESENTATION CHOICES DO NOT RESCUE A PUZZLE. A puzzle usually still offers real
  choices — change-ringing offers bells→positions vs positions→bells (inverse functions; picking
  wrong makes half the constraints awkward), and explicit visited-row history vs noticing that a
  repeated row IS a repeated state so TLC's own dedup enforces no-repeats for free. Genuine and
  interesting, but LOCAL — about transcribing a given action set tidily, not deciding what the
  actions are. Good taste, not modeling judgment, and only the second is what we teach.

  RESCUE PATTERN: add agents and fallibility, converting search into specification.

  TEETH: restaurant seating FAILS as "seat this party optimally" (bin-packing) and PASSES as
  "model the host stand with walk-ins and reservations arriving concurrently". Same domain,
  different statement — THE SCREEN IS WHAT TELLS YOU WHICH FRAMING YOU WROTE. So it runs at
  STATEMENT time (§6 step 4) as well as at domain-selection time; passing once does not
  immunize a domain.

§5.7 is mechanizable. §5.7b is a JUDGMENT RUBRIC — ship it as a checklist that the statement
author and the leakage checker both run, not as a script pretending to decide it.

Feed in the §2.2 pre-screen suspicions so the screen is not run blind (restaurant seating →
bin-packing; library holds / community garden / airline standby → the Resource Allocator in
different dress; orchestra auditions → tournament ranking, so at most one of the two survives;
change-ringing → fails §5.7b, rescuable but not in batch one; beekeeping → possibly too fuzzy
to state crisply enough for §3.2).

Independent of the verdict channel — no TLC involved — so it can start immediately.

Files: harness/screen.sh, harness/PUZZLE-SCREEN.md

RED: GIVEN "restaurant seating: seat this party optimally", WHEN the §5.7b rubric is applied,
THEN it is rejected as a puzzle; and GIVEN "model the host stand with walk-ins and reservations
arriving concurrently", THEN the same rubric accepts it as a system.
acceptance_criteria: screen.sh reports burned/clear by name AND mechanism; PUZZLE-SCREEN.md carries the rubric with the restaurant-seating pair as its worked example; both cited from the §9.6 statement-author brief.
close_reason: harness/screen.sh (§5.7) + PUZZLE-SCREEN.md (§5.7b rubric); 71 assertions green on merged main. §9.6/§9.7 briefs now cite both.

title: Stage 2 §5.6 — comment-pass gate (the naive stripper deletes the spec)
description:
Goal: enforce §3.8 — comments are added in a SEPARATE post-freeze pass, because comments written
alongside a spec bend the spec toward the commentary. The gate: strip comments from the frozen
and the commented versions, diff, require identical.

WRINKLE THAT BREAKS THE NAIVE IMPLEMENTATION: in PlusCal specs the algorithm lives inside
`(* --algorithm ... *)`. A naive comment stripper DELETES THE SPEC and the gate then compares two
empty files and passes. The stripper must preserve the block containing --algorithm /
--fair algorithm, and the \* BEGIN/END TRANSLATION markers.

CLEANER GATE FOR PLUSCAL: re-run pcal after commenting and require the TRANSLATION block to be
BYTE-IDENTICAL. Comments inside the algorithm block are not carried into the generated TLA+, so
any change at all means the pass touched the algorithm. Prefer this where the spec is PlusCal.

Independent of the verdict channel — this is text processing, not TLC — so it can start
immediately, in parallel with §5.1.

Files: harness/comment-gate.sh

RED: GIVEN a PlusCal spec whose algorithm lives inside (* --algorithm ... *), WHEN comment-gate.sh
strips comments, THEN the algorithm block survives and the gate compares real specs — a naive
stripper that deletes it must FAIL this test.
acceptance_criteria: PlusCal algorithm block preserved; BEGIN/END TRANSLATION markers preserved; pcal re-run path implemented; a commented-and-also-edited spec is rejected.
close_reason: harness/comment-gate.sh, two required checks (strip-and-diff + pcal re-translation); 25 assertions green on merged main. RED reproducible via COMMENT_GATE_STRIPPER=naive.

title: Stage 2 §5.5 — seeded-bug matrix: the only mechanical defense against Inv == TRUE
description:
Goal: state "this spec catches this bug" mechanically — rc==12 against the variant AND rc==0
against the reference. This is the ONLY mechanical defense against a learner writing
`Inv == TRUE`, which otherwise passes every check that asks "does your property hold".

CAVEAT TO RECORD IN THE CODE, not just here: only ~10.9% of real faulty student specs are one
mutation away from correct — real mistakes are multi-step — and 39.3% of single mutations are
semantically INERT. Mutants of our own reference are systematically unlike real learner errors.
This is a BOOTSTRAP, not a proxy for learner behaviour. The comment belongs in seeded-bugs.sh so
the next reader cannot mistake it for a validated instrument.

Diff counterexamples via ALIAS + -dumpTrace json: normalize state BEFORE dumping, and diff the
ACTION-NAME SEQUENCE PLUS TRACE LENGTH, which are stable. Concrete values vary with the learner's
representation and must NOT be diffed — diffing them would penalize exactly the representational
freedom §3.2 exists to protect.

Files: harness/seeded-bugs.sh

RED: GIVEN a reference spec, a seeded variant, and a learner property, WHEN seeded-bugs.sh runs,
THEN it passes only on rc==0-against-reference AND rc==12-against-variant — and `Inv == TRUE`
fails the matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix runner working; Inv==TRUE rejected; trace diffing compares action-name sequence + length only; the 10.9%/39.3% caveat is a comment in the file.
notes: FILES LINE CORRECTED at close: the bead declared only harness/seeded-bugs.sh, but the work legitimately spans harness/seeded-bugs.sh AND harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/. The dispatch brief granted both; the bead line did not. An under-declared Files: line makes the fan-out detector treat the footprint as smaller than it is, which is the direction that causes collisions rather than missed parallelism. Actual footprint: harness/seeded-bugs.sh, harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/.
close_reason: harness/seeded-bugs.sh + 22 files, merged to main; rules hazard recorded in 95fcdf1. 37 assertions green, and all eight suites green together at 292 (21+25+71+26+57+43+12+37). STAGE 2 IS COMPLETE — tla-kl5.11, the pilot, is unblocked. Central verified the three load-bearing behaviours directly: a good property returns BUGS_CAUGHT, Inv == TRUE returns PROPERTY_TOO_WEAK (the bead's RED), and an inert variant set returns VARIANT_INERT for a GOOD and a BAD property ALIKE — which is the attribution property that keeps a defect in our own variant set off the learner's bill. The phase ordering is what carries that: the instrument is checked before the submission, and mutation M3 shows that removing the inert check makes AlwaysTrue come back PROPERTY_TOO_WEAK, the right exit code attributed to the wrong party. Ten mutations all turn the suite red, including M5, which proves the trace comparator does not diff concrete values — diffing them would report two identical behaviours in different representations as divergent, the exact section 3.2 penalty this project forbids. Worker also independently confirmed the here-string SIGPIPE correction and converted five live pipes in its own selftest; harness/test-pipefail.sh now scans 15 shell files including both of its new ones.

title: CI downloads tla2tools.jar from 'latest' — pin the TLC release
description:
.github/workflows/verify-puzzles.yml downloads:

  https://github.com/tlaplus/tlaplus/releases/latest/download/tla2tools.jar

`latest` means a new TLC release silently changes verification behavior with no commit to this repo. For a project whose whole premise is mechanically verified specs, the checker version is part of the contract and must be pinned.

Fix: pin the release tag, and ideally checksum the jar.

Good news that makes pinning cheap rather than restrictive: TLC's state counts for a completed exhaustive run are extremely stable. Measured identical (883 generated / 343 distinct / depth 19) across workers 1/4/8, three fingerprint polynomials, and THREE TLC releases spanning roughly seven years (2.15, 2.19, 2026.03.04). Symmetry-reduced runs were likewise identical (21/10) across all three versions. So pinning costs nothing in practice and buys reproducibility.

Note for any future Apalache track: Apalache 0.60.0 reportedly requires Java 25, while this workflow runs Java 21 — a second JDK would be needed.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow pins a specific tla2tools release tag (ideally checksummed) instead of tracking latest.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-06 — THE PROBLEM IS BIGGER THAN 'PIN THE RELEASE'. Three different TLCs are in play and no two agree.

  CI today:  https://.../releases/latest/download/tla2tools.jar  ->  v1.7.4, published 2024-08-05.
             'latest' skips v1.8.0 because v1.8.0 is flagged PRERELEASE (verified: gh api
             repos/tlaplus/tlaplus/releases/latest -> v1.7.4). So CI has been running a 2024
             build this whole time.
  Local:     ~/lib/tla2tools.jar, TLC2 Version 2026.03.04.183147 (rev 52c0195), file dated Mar 5.
             This matches NO tagged release — it is a nightly/dev build. There is no 'nightly'
             release tag either (gh api .../releases/tags/nightly -> 404).
  Newest:    v1.8.0 'The Clarke release', prerelease=true, published 2026-07-31, TLC2 Version
             2026.07.31.184830.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the real finding: EVERY empirical constant in V2-PLAN.md section 5 — the
exit-code table, the frozen-mapping probe, the total==0 dead-action predicate, the 0-initial-states
gate behavior — was verified against a build that CANNOT BE OBTAINED FROM ANY RELEASE URL. The
plan says 'do re-verify if you change TLC versions'; it did not anticipate that the verified
version is unreachable, so the constants are currently unreproducible by anyone but this machine.

MITIGATING EVIDENCE: the tla-kl5.3 survey independently re-ran the rc table and the frozen-mapping
probe on 2026.07.31.184830 (v1.8.0) and reported both holding. So v1.8.0 is corroborated for the
constants that matter most, by a run that was not looking for that result.

NOT JUST A CI FIX ANYMORE: pinning CI without moving local leaves two versions; moving local
without re-verifying leaves the constants asserted against a build nobody runs. Needs a decision
on which version is canonical for the project, then a re-verification pass against it.
close_reason: CI pinned to v1.8.0 in commit 43b4d2e, and the smoke check now ASSERTS the version string rather than logging it behind || true — a pin nobody checks is precisely how this drifted unnoticed. Investigation found the problem was larger than the bead assumed: releases/latest/download/ resolved to v1.7.4 (2024-08-05) because GitHub's 'latest' skips prereleases and v1.8.0 is flagged as one, so CI had been running a 2024 build while every empirical constant in V2-PLAN.md section 5 was verified against a 2026 nightly that matches no tagged release at all. Frank chose v1.8.0 'The Clarke release' (TLC2 2026.07.31.184830) as canonical. The local-side half — swapping ~/lib/tla2tools.jar and re-verifying the section-5 constants against it — is deferred to tla-wl7, because four workers were running TLC against the current jar at decision time and swapping mid-flight would have invalidated their verification.

title: verify-puzzle.sh should classify by TLC exit code, not stdout greps; and must pin -workers 1
description:
scripts/verify-puzzle.sh classifies TLC results by grepping stdout. TLC has a clean, stable exit-code channel that makes every one of those greps unnecessary and immune to message-wording drift across releases.

Measured on TLC 2026.03.04 / tla2tools 1.8.0:
  0   success ("No error has been found")
  10  ASSUME or -postCondition evaluated FALSE
  11  deadlock
  12  safety violation (INVARIANT)
  13  liveness / action-property violation (PROPERTY, incl. refinement)
  150 parse or semantic failure
  151 config failure
  255 file not found

Switching to $? is faster, more precise (13 vs 12 distinguishes a property from an invariant violation, which grep cannot), and does not break when TLC rewords a message.

RELATED HAZARD, same file: the script does not pass -workers. It gets 1 by default today, but counterexample traces are NOT deterministic above one worker — measured, same spec and version, five runs at -workers 8 produced three different traces (trace LENGTH was stable at 4, the path was not). Any check that diffs a counterexample must pin -workers 1 explicitly rather than rely on the default.

Recommended invocation shape:
  tlc -workers 1 -deadlock -noGenerateSpecTE -nowarning \
      -coverage 1 -dumpTrace json trace.json \
      -metadir "$SCRATCH/states" Harness.tla -config Harness.cfg
(-metadir keeps states/ out of the tree; -noGenerateSpecTE stops the *_TTrace_*.tla litter already accumulating in puzzles/T01-the-light-switch/solution/.)
acceptance_criteria: verify-puzzle.sh branches on $? rather than grepping TLC stdout, and passes -workers 1 explicitly.
notes: Now depends on tla-kl5.4 (harness §5.1 verdict channel), which owns the canonical rc table and the -workers 1 constraint. Rewire verify-puzzle.sh to consume harness/verdict.sh rather than reimplementing the table — §5.1 says 'replace stdout greps with exit codes THROUGHOUT', and this bead is the v1-facing half of that.
close_reason: Rewired in commit 1dcb164, merged to main at 66cba9c. verify-puzzle.sh no longer runs TLC at all — it delegates to harness/verdict.sh and maps that one table onto v1's verdict vocabulary, so -workers 1 is pinned by INHERITANCE rather than repetition, with a structural assertion gating that no direct TLC call returns. Suite grew 2 to 33 assertions; full 107-dir corpus sweep byte-identical pre and post (115 lines, diff clean). Both banned-idiom sites DELETED outright, closing half of tla-4u0. THE GREPS WERE NOT MERELY INELEGANT — they produced two outright FALSE PASSES: rc=10 (failing ASSUME) and rc=151 (cfg naming an undefined operator) both reported PASS-OTHER at exit 0. And the headline finding, central-verified: V2-PLAN.md section 5.1's rc table was SIX CODES SHORT (14, 75, 76, 77, 152, 153), read straight from the pinned jar's own enum via javap on tlc2.output.EC$ExitStatus. rc=75 FAILURE_SPEC_EVAL is LIVE on the corpus — puzzles/T29-unchanged/solution/Clock_buggy.tla exits 75 with 'Successor state is not completely specified by action Tick', which central reproduced. The old chain classified it PASS-VIOLATION only because it matched the Trace exploration line of the *_TTrace_*.tla file TLC emits alongside the error — and the canonical invocation suppresses that file with -noGenerateSpecTE, so adopting the canonical invocation while keeping the greps would have silently deleted the only thing the verdict rested on. That is this bead's thesis demonstrated on live data.

title: Wire the 8 canonical script/ stubs (or mark N/A) and fill canonical_commands
description:
/loom-adopt P2 scaffolded loom's 8 canonical script-convention entry points into scripts/ on 2026-08-05: bootstrap, setup, update, server, test, lint, cibuild, deploy. Every one is still the unedited `exit 2` 'not implemented' stub.

Because they are unwired, .claude/project-constitution.md deliberately leaves canonical_commands EMPTY (except deploy='mkdocs gh-deploy'). Recording scripts/test there today would assert a canonical command that fails by design.

Existing bespoke scripts that plausibly map:
  scripts/test-verify-puzzle.sh -> test
  scripts/build-docs.sh         -> cibuild (or build)
  mkdocs gh-deploy              -> deploy (already migrated)

For each of the 8: either wire the real command, or mark it genuinely not-applicable by replacing the body with `echo "<verb>: N/A for this project type" && exit 0` per templates/scripts/README.md. Then fill the matching canonical_commands verb in the constitution.

NOTE: if the v2 rebuild lands (new problem set built on learntla.com), revisit which verbs matter — 'test' likely becomes 'run TLC over every problem's reference solution and its seeded-broken variants'.
acceptance_criteria: No scripts/<verb> is left as an unedited exit-2 stub, and every wired verb has a matching non-empty canonical_commands entry.
notes: CONCRETE CONTENT FOR scripts/test AS OF 2026-08-06. The v2 harness now ships three real suites, and per loom's gate-don't-advise rule they must be wired to a gate rather than left as commands someone remembers to run: ./harness/test-verdict.sh (21 assertions), ./harness/comment-gate.sh --self-test (25), ./harness/screen.sh --selftest (71). 117 assertions total, all green on main, all runnable offline — screen.sh --selftest uses a gh stub and a cached README fixture. Wiring these into scripts/test and then filling canonical_commands.test is now the highest-value part of this bead: until it happens, three test suites that took a full agent-wave to write are advisory-only.
close_reason: All 8 loom stubs wired, none marked N/A; canonical_commands filled. Merged to main at c892a4e. Central verified the gate on main: 'bash scripts/test' runs 10 suites and 292 assertions in 124s, all green. Worker deliberately INVERTED liza_base's fast-default and justified it: the full run is ~121s and the fast tier is only 108 of 292 assertions (37%), so defaulting to fast would make canonical_commands.test name a command running a third of the gate — the same class of lie as naming one that fails by design. It also watched the FAIL path fire before trusting it, and that surfaced a real fragility it then fixed: a mis-resolved repo root produced ten separate rc=127 failures instead of one clear message, so test/lint/cibuild now fail closed if harness/ and scripts/ are not both under the resolved root. Central independently confirmed three live findings: gen-curriculum-map.sh:5 hardcodes an absolute cd into the main checkout, build-docs.sh:408 tells learners to curl releases/latest (the exact 2024-resolving trap tla-5b4 removed from CI), and the remote has only refs/heads/main while pages.yml publishes via upload-pages-artifact — so the previously-recorded 'mkdocs gh-deploy' canonical would have created a branch nothing serves from. Each is filed as its own bead. Worker did NOT execute scripts/setup, verified by reading + shellcheck + bash -n + curl -sIL on the pinned URL (HTTP 200, content-length 4486015 matching); the local jar is untouched.

title: Method doc — loci-from-audio + encode-then-test protocol
description:
Goal: Write the learning-protocol method doc (D7).
Files: docs/appendix/pangram/method.md
Steps: 1. Why it works + honest caveats (cite the tla-ucw research drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_ebd286000153c745c946963e; evidence is GRADE-low, spec-mapping is extrapolation). 2. ENCODE protocol — encode from an ORAL narration of the spec (NOT screen-reading: De Beni/Moe/Cornoldi reading d~=-0.76 vs oral d~=+0.93), section-to-locus map (EXTENDS->CONSTANTS->VARIABLES->TypeOK->Init->each Action->Next/Spec->Properties), one imago agens per section encoding its res, fixed stock-character lexicon for abstract operators. 3. CONSOLIDATE protocol — spaced write-from-blank reconstruction vs TLC; palace is the cue fallback; STOP re-building the palace after first successful recall (Karpicke and Smith 2012: elaboration and retrieval are separate mechanisms). 4. Reference the operator-card + the reconstruction harness.
Acceptance: protocol followable end-to-end; cites the research drawer + key sources.
Grounding: design doc (D7).

title: Reconstruction harness (Tier-1) — blank-a-spec then TLC-check
description:
Goal: Build the reconstruction harness — blank a specimen and TLC-check the learner's from-blank reconstruction; reuse scripts/verify-puzzle.sh.

title: Research: art-of-memory / connected-discourse loci → concrete spec-as-narrative encoding guidance
description:
Design-cycle research spawn (C4) for the 'pangram-set + spaced-recall TLA+ mastery method' design cycle (design-doc drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_8af15aed4e3d4a625f8d5ec5; grounded in exploration drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_781911016d78a8fc67d62269, finding F10).

QUESTION: The exploration's first deep-research round leaned on the EXPERIMENTAL psychology of method-of-loci (word-list paradigm), under-weighting loci's PARADIGMATIC home — memorizing connected, coherent DISCOURSE (orators' speeches). Does the classical art-of-memory literature (Yates 1966 'The Art of Memory'; Rhetorica ad Herennium; Cicero De Oratore; Quintilian) plus any modern empirical work on loci-for-connected-discourse yield CONCRETE, ACTIONABLE encoding guidance for memorizing a coherent TLA+ spec AS A NARRATIVE SEQUENCE?

DELIVER: (1) how orators chunked/sequenced connected discourse via loci (the actual technique, not just that they did it); (2) a translation to spec-as-narrative — how to chunk a ~typical TLA+ specimen's token sequence into loci-able units; (3) any empirical efficacy data on loci for connected/coherent (not list) material; (4) concrete recommendations that feed the C3 learning-protocol spec (the loci/chain encoding method + operator-card design). Peer-reviewed + primary classical sources required.

GROUNDS: C3 (learning-protocol spec) of the design cycle. Findings → capture as a decision/research drawer in tla_puzzles/decisions; close bead; record back into the design-doc C3 marker.

title: Audit ~106 puzzles for QG rule-2 violations (smuggled + mis-demoed)
description:
Goal: Produce a comprehensive findings drawer cataloging every QG rule-2 violation across the ~106 fully-implemented puzzles. Read-only research bead — no code changes here.

Files (read-only):
- puzzles/*/README.md (lesson + worked example + puzzle text)
- puzzles/*/solution/*.tla (actual constructs used)
- docs/curriculum/*/T??.md, R??.md, J??.md (per-puzzle pages with builds-on chain)
- bd labels (concept tags per puzzle, if present)
- QUALITY_GATE.md (the rule definitions)

Scope: only fully-implemented puzzles (~106). Skip stubs/scaffolds.

Method (per puzzle):
1. Identify the claimed "one new thing" from the lesson section.
2. Extract every TLA+/PlusCal construct used in the solution.
3. Compute should-already-know set = union of constructs introduced by all puzzles in the transitive `builds-on` chain.
4. Smuggled = (constructs in solution) − (claimed new concept) − (should-already-know set).
5. Mis-demoed check — for each construct the lesson claims to introduce: does the worked example demonstrate it canonically and non-gratuitously? Flag self-contradicting demos (e.g., T04's `goto`s that say "use this to divert flow" but mostly go to the next sequential label).
6. Note when a demo deliberately uses a non-idiomatic form for pedagogical purposes — that's allowed IF the lesson annotates it as such, otherwise it's a violation.

Output: one MemPalace drawer in `tla_puzzles/curriculum`, table-shaped:
| puzzle | claimed concept | smuggled[] | mis-demoed[] | severity (low/med/high) | suggested fix shape (extract upstream / new puzzle / inline-explain / annotate-as-demonstrative) |

Steps:
1. Enumerate fully-implemented puzzles (filter the puzzles/ dir, drop stubs).
2. Walk per puzzle through the method above (consider parallel sub-agents per tier).
3. Cross-check T04 entries against existing diagnosis drawer (drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_94e328409a3c5ac27ba69d27) — they should agree.
4. File the findings drawer.
5. Add bd notes on this bead linking to the drawer ID.

Acceptance:
- Every fully-implemented puzzle has a row.
- T04 entries match the prior diagnosis drawer (self = smuggled, goto = mis-demoed).
- Findings drawer ID recorded in bd notes on this bead.
- Findings inform the per-fix beads filed afterward (those beads are NOT created here).

title: verify-puzzle.sh: copy helper modules to scratch dir
description: Tier 6 audit (tla-3vt.6) surfaced that verify-puzzle.sh copies only <base>.tla + .cfg to its scratch dir, omitting helper modules (e.g., AbstractCard.tla, Counter.tla, OrderStates.tla, Timer.tla, CounterA.tla, RingCount.tla, AbstractLight.tla, AbstractSignal.tla). When TLC tries to resolve a multi-module spec it errors with 'Cannot find source file for module ...', but the elif chain in verify-puzzle.sh falls through to PASS-OTHER (rc=0 because pcal-rc check passes and the script eventually hits 'Finished in'). Net effect: T51, T52, T54-T59 (and likely Tier 5 specs that are multi-module) are NOT actually verified by the gate — they all currently report PASS-OTHER instead of being rejected. Direct TLC runs in each solution/ dir confirm the puzzles themselves are correct. Two possible fixes: (a) copy the entire solution/ dir to scratch (simplest), or (b) detect cross-module FAIL via 'Cannot find source file' / 'Parsing or semantic analysis failed' patterns.

title: INVENTORY.md field 5 is a line number into a file people edit, and that rotted twice today
description:
Filed 2026-10-22 after causing the second instance in one session.

THE SHAPE. drill/INVENTORY.md field 5 is spelled
exercises/chNN/CHEATSHEET.md:LINE and points at the '- Construct:' entry a row
came from. Any edit that inserts a line above an entry moves it, and the
pointer then names a DIFFERENT construct rather than failing to resolve. That is
the bad direction: a dangling pointer is obvious and a shifted one is not.

TWICE IN ONE DAY, in two different fields of the same file.

Field 7's Rule B citations were line numbers into
.claude/rules/tla-practice.md. The tla-ll9o worker measured SEVENTEEN of 19
pointing at a line that no longer carried the figure, with @169 the only
survivor, and replaced them with SECTION anchors. Its stated reason: a line
number into a file people still edit has cost this project twice.

Field 5 then rotted the same afternoon. tla-446a inserted twelve 'House shape'
lines into ch03, ch07, ch08 and ch09 and moved 26 entries, which gen-sheet.sh
caught as 52 findings and refused to regenerate on. Repaired at 76faca6 by
joining on field 4, the construct NAME.

WHY FIELD 5 CANNOT TAKE THE FIELD 7 FIX. Section anchors worked for field 7
because the survey has numbered sections. Field 5 points at ONE construct entry
inside a '## Constructs introduced' list, so there is no finer heading to name.

TWO OPTIONS AND THE SECOND IS CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS.

1. Make field 5 the construct NAME rather than the line, spelled
   exercises/ch03/CHEATSHEET.md#--algorithm-block or similar. The name is the
   join key gen-sheet.sh already uses and it does not move. The cost is that a
   renamed construct now dangles rather than shifting, which is the direction
   you want.
2. Keep the line number and gate it. The repair script written for 76faca6 is
   most of a checker already: for each row, resolve field 4 in the named sheet
   and assert the line agrees. It is about 40 lines and it would have caught
   this before the commit rather than at the next full registry pass.

Recommendation is BOTH, in that order, because option 1 removes the failure mode
and option 2 catches a stale pointer whatever the spelling. Option 2 alone
leaves a correct-but-fragile field that reddens every time somebody edits a
sheet, which trains people to regenerate rather than to think.

NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH tla-aj8c. That bead is blocked on the gated bijection
between inventory rows and the 105 cheat-sheet construct entries. Field 5 IS
that bijection's join. So whoever opens the bijection to a second row source is
already in this code, and these two should probably be worked together.

Files: drill/INVENTORY.md, scripts/gen-sheet.sh, harness/test-sheet.sh
Acceptance: a sheet edit that moves a construct entry either cannot invalidate
field 5, or reddens a suite before it reaches a commit. The repair script from
76faca6 is in the session transcript and is the starting point.

recorded in .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md under the
gate-that-never-read-the-tree hazard, and the first one found while the hole was

THE HOLE. harness/test-pipefail.sh scans roots 'harness scripts chapter .github
drill recall'. scripts/lint's roots now read 'scripts harness drill recall swipe
completion chapter exercises sources core-language-docs'. So core-language-docs
is linted and not pipefail-checked.

IT IS CURRENTLY EMPTY, and that is why this is P3. That tree holds exactly one
shell file, core-language-docs/snippets/run-all.sh, which is centrally owned and
clean. So nothing is wrong today. The hole is that the moment a second shell
file lands there, the ban on '| grep -q', '| grep -m' and '| head' stops
covering it, and the gate reports green having read none of it.

WHY THAT BAN MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Worst case is not a false FAIL. Three
of the 24 sites found in the original sweep were GUARDS rather than assertions,
including the SYMMETRY/VIEW soundness check in harness/refinement.sh, where a
141 lets an unsound temporal reduction through unflagged. The failure direction
there is a false PASS on a correctness gate.

DO NOT ADD THE ONE ROOT. The fix shape that works, recorded in the same hazard
section: scan every candidate surface by hand FIRST, then widen to all the clean
ones at once. On 2026-10-18 the narrow fix would have left four more holes,
because swipe, completion, chapter, exercises and sources were all uncovered and
all already clean, 89 files to 134. Compare the two root lists and close the
whole gap.

AND NAME WHAT STAYS OUT, with its count, in a comment beside the root list.
harness/test-spelling.sh already does this, which is the only reason its
scripts/ hole was a two-line fix rather than a rediscovery.

NOTE THE SELECTION RULE IS ALREADY RIGHT. test-pipefail.sh selects by SHEBANG
rather than extension and scans the tree, so a file that does not exist yet is
covered the moment it lands. The roots are the only thing narrow about it.

title: Five more files still say TLC breaks the div contract, and one of them is the registry note
description:
Follows tla-dwp7, whose brief named three sites carrying the false account
that TLC breaks the Naturals.tla div contract. Its worker found nine and
fixed the four in its footprint. These five are the remainder.

  swipe/README.md:527-543
  swipe/level1/ITEMS.tsv:151-153
  swipe/level2/ITEMS.tsv:104-105
  harness/test-swipe-subscript.sh:199-200
  scripts/test:543-556 and :1635-1640

None is a red gate. All are comments, which is why they sat through a green
registry.

THE ONE WORTH READING FIRST is scripts/test. Its registry note still
describes the level 0 tripwire as asserting that the identity is broken,
which is now the opposite of what that suite does, and it also carries "76
reviewed sites over 83 occurrences" when the gate computes 89 and 96. A
registry note is where somebody looks to find out what a suite is for.

WHAT THE CORRECT ACCOUNT IS, so nobody re-derives it. TLC does not break the
contract. (-17) \div 5 is -4, (-17) % 5 is 3, and the identity holds. The -3
is operator precedence: prefix minus is 12-12, \div is 13-13, % is 10-11, so
-17 \div 5 parses as -(17 \div 5) and -17 % 5 parses as (-17) % 5, and the
two halves of the identity check were grouped differently. Same asymmetry on
exponent. The real divergence is the negative DIVISOR, upstream tlaplus#721,
and the level 0 tripwire now sits there.

swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv is the model to follow. It heads its block
PARENTHESIZE EVERY NEGATIVE LITERAL, carries the precedence account with the
^ case, and says plainly that three items were replaced on a premise that did
not hold.

WATCH harness/div-sites.tsv. Editing a comment that contains \div changes an
inventory window, and the gate reddens naming the rows. The tla-dwp7 worker
hit this on nine windows. That is the gate working, not a defect, and it
means this bead's footprint probably includes harness/div-sites.tsv.

title: The spelling gate can match inside a longer word, and its file exemptions pin a count rather than a word
description:
Two latent issues the tla-fkqs worker measured and did not fix, because
neither has a live site today and both want a decision rather than a patch.

ONE. `analyse` matches inside the American plural `analyses`. Measured:
grep -onIiE -- "analysing|analysed|analyse" over a file reading "The analyses
of the data." returns 1:analyse. There are no analyses sites in the tree, so
the gate is green, but correct American prose trips it the day somebody
writes it. Fixing it needs word-boundary logic the file's header deliberately
rejects, and the header's reasoning should be re-read before anyone adds it.

The same shape is why learnt, kerb, programme, enrol and distil cannot be
carried at all: the British form sits inside a longer American word or a name.
That is recorded beside the list. The difference here is the direction. Those
five would produce false findings on words that exist in the tree. This one
produces a false finding on a word that does not, yet.

TWO. EXEMPT_FILES pins a COUNT, not a word. If somebody removes a British
word from an exempted file and adds a different one, the count stays and the
new site passes unseen. Narrow, pre-existing, and the fix is to pin the word
beside the count.

title: The practice README names three of the seven delivered directories
description:
Found by the tla-xbbb worker on 2026-10-18 while building the first gate that reads practice/README.md.

The delivered tree ~/tla-practice holds seven directories a learner can land in: attempts, completion, drill, exercises, problems, recall and released. The README names three of them. completion, drill, exercises and recall are never mentioned at all.

So a learner who opens the tree sees four directories the document that explains the tree does not know about. Three of those four are whole practice channels with their own runners.

WHY THE NEW GATE DOES NOT FAIL ON IT. harness/test-deliver-practice-root.sh checks that every path the README names RESOLVES. It cannot check the other direction, which is whether a directory that exists is named, because whether a channel belongs in this document is an editorial call rather than a fact about the tree. The suite prints it as a nudge every run and stays green, which is the gate-don't-advise line drawn on the correct side: this one wants a human to weigh in.

THE QUESTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT is not 'add four paragraphs'. It is whether this README is the map of the whole practice tree or the instructions for working a problem. It opens 'Where Frank works problems', which reads like the second, and then it describes attempts and released, which are problem machinery. If it is the second, the right fix may be a line saying the other channels have their own READMEs rather than four sections nobody maintains.

title: The repo documents TLC's truncating div as though it were the contract
description:
Points 1 and 2 of tla-7n7e, which closed on 2026-10-18 when its RED line was
gated. The description called neither urgent and the gate was the part with
risk in it.

POINT 1. Is TLC's truncating \div upstream's known behavior, or a real
divergence from the bundled Naturals.tla's own comment? Read the Java,
tlc2.module.Naturals or Integers, rather than reasoning from the comment, and
check the tlaplus issue tracker.

The tla-7n7e worker found one thing that bears on this and does not settle it.
module-docs/Integers.md:16 already describes \div as "integer division
(truncates toward zero)". That is TLC's behavior rather than the module's
contract, so this repo's own docs have recorded the divergence the whole time
while the bead called it unrecorded. What that tells us is that somebody wrote
the observed behavior down without noticing it contradicted the jar's own
stated identity. It does not tell us what upstream thinks.

POINT 2. Should .claude/rules/tla-practice.md carry it? That file surveys
published specifications rather than the toolchain, so probably not. A bd
memory is filed already. The live question is whether module-docs/Integers.md
should say the contract and the behavior disagree, rather than silently
documenting the behavior as though it were the contract.

WHY THIS IS P3 AND NOT CLOSED. Nothing shipped is exposed, and
harness/test-div-contract.sh now stops a new site arriving unreviewed. The
tripwire in harness/test-swipe-level0.sh asserts the identity is still broken,
so a TLC that FIXES \div turns that suite red on purpose and this bead becomes
urgent the moment it does.

Files: module-docs/Integers.md, .claude/rules/tla-practice.md

RED: INVARIANT: module-docs/Integers.md states that TLC's \div disagrees with the identity its own bundled Naturals.tla asserts, rather than documenting the behavior as though it were the contract.
close_reason: Merged on main 2026-10-20, worker commit 3d4e79b. POINT 1 IS SETTLED AND THE ANSWER IS NEITHER OPTION THE BEAD OFFERED: there is no truncating \div. (-17) \div 5 is -4, (-17) % 5 is 3, and 5 * ((-17) \div 5) + ((-17) % 5) is -17, so the identity holds. Central reproduced every line independently through tlc2.REPL. The -3 the repo carried since 2026-10-17 is operator precedence: the jar's own tla2sany/parser/Operators table puts prefix minus at 12-12, \div at 13-13 and % at 10-11, so -17 \div 5 parses as -(17 \div 5) and -17 % 5 parses as (-17) % 5, and the two halves of the identity check were grouped differently. Same asymmetry on exponent, -2 ^ 2 is -4 against (-2) ^ 2 is 4. Upstream tlaplus#893 states the precedence value. BOTH SOURCES REACHED: the bytecode shows Integers.Divide taking idiv then decrementing when the signs differ and q*b is not a, which is floor division by construction, and Mod doing irem, adding b when negative, and raising unless b is positive; and eleven tracker queries found tlaplus#721, open since 2022, which is about a negative DIVISOR rather than a dividend, where the module's witness interval 0..(b-1) is empty and TLC answers anyway. POINT 2: module-docs/Integers.md had TWO wrong rows, and the second was wrong in the other direction since % does not take the dividend's sign. Both fixed, contract quoted, precedence trap shown with its groupings, negative divisor named as the uncovered case. The worker did NOT write 'the contract and the behavior disagree', because they agree inside the range the contract scopes itself to, and writing it would have shipped a second falsehood. .claude/rules/tla-practice.md stays out and the worker argued it rather than accepting the bead's guess. The bd memory is corrected. Filed tla-dwp7 for three sites outside the footprint that still carry the false account, the worst being a tripwire in harness/test-swipe-level0.sh written in the unparenthesized form, so it evaluates -12 # -17, passes, and can never fire. Verified: div-contract 26, build-docs reading 314, exercises 94, chapter 47, spelling 20, pipefail 25, lint clean over 147, build-docs clean with the new section on the page.

title: No gate stops a spike reaching for a spec from one of the five unlicensed repositories
description:
Refiled from tla-16je, which Frank closed on 2026-10-18 because its premise
was retired by the 2026-09-06 direction change. This is the part that
survives, and it is much smaller.

WHAT THE OLD BEAD ASKED. 19 of 143 candidate systems came from five
repositories carrying no LICENSE, LICENCE or COPYING file, and the plan at
the time shipped the human-authored specification in a subfolder of every
curated problem. So the question was whether to mail the authors, link out,
or drop the 19.

WHY THAT QUESTION IS GONE. Curation was retired on 2026-09-06, recorded in
PRACTICE-PLAN.md as of fb2d3f6. Problems now come from external prose and the
SPIKE is the example implementation, which this project writes. Measured at
0122d31 on 2026-10-01: a grep over curated/, authoring/, pilot/ and
exercises/ for muratdem, will62794, DrTLAPlus, mongo-repl and ongardie
returns nothing. Not one of the five unlicensed repositories has a spec in
this repo. The one spec this project does redistribute, curated/majority-vote/
example/, is the Boyer-Moore MJRTY spec at licence MIT, and the delivered copy
under ~/tla-practice/problems/majority-vote/ ships no spec at all.

WHAT STILL HAS A QUESTION IN IT. corpus/manifest.tsv records 19 systems as
licence NONE FOUND and nothing stops a future spike from reaching for one.
ongardie/raft.tla is the canonical Raft spec and is the one most likely to be
wanted.

So the gate is the whole bead: a check that fails if a spec from a NONE FOUND
system appears under any tree this project ships from. That is cheap, it fires
at the moment the question becomes live rather than years before, and it does
not require settling the licensing question today.

THE SURFACE THAT GETS MISSED, per the CLAUDE.md rule that a claim of absence
names its search: ~/tla-practice/ is not a git repo and no repo-level search
reaches it. The delivery-verify channel from tla-mjvx is where that half
belongs, not here.

title: The no-count note now only fires where its wording is wrong
description:
Flagged by the tla-1sh7.8 worker in its own report, and I confirmed it by
driving the merged runner.

After ff86f3b the note survives in exactly one place: under a value that
never evaluated. There it reads

    you typed   CASE Parking.a = 2 -> 1
      Attempted to evaluate a CASE with no conditions true.
      line 19, col 10 to line 19, col 32 of module Yours
      (no count: TLC will not count that value, so it is not a set)

The CASE produced no value at all, so "that value" has no referent and "it is
not a set" describes nothing. Before the bead the note also fired on values
that did evaluate, where the wording was at least true, so the fix moved it
onto the one case it does not fit.

The brief told the worker to leave that branch alone and it did, which was
right. Part 4 pins the note as current behavior and M4's control depends on
it, so changing it is a deliberate edit to two assertions rather than a
one-line tweak.

WHAT I WOULD DO. Drop the note on this branch too. Where the value never
evaluated, TLC's own sentence already says what happened, and the note adds a
claim about a set that nobody was asking about. That leaves the note with no
callers, which is the honest outcome: it was written to explain a skipped
count, and after tla-1sh7.8 there is no case where a reader needs that
explained.

THE ALTERNATIVE. Reword it to something true on this branch, along the lines
of "no value, so no count". I would not take that, because it spends a line
restating what the sentence above it already said. It is the option worth
having if somebody thinks the block reads as truncated without a closing line.

title: Delivered prose carries em dashes and semicolons, which frank-writing forbids
description:
Found by central on 2026-10-17 while verifying tla-1sh7.14. Not acted on: the fix is a rewrite of prose somebody else wrote, and the scope is a ruling rather than an edit.

THE PROSE THAT REACHES FRANK. recall/README.md is delivered to ~/tla-practice/recall and carries 7 em dashes and 7 semicolons. All 14 are prose rather than code or transcript, read by eye at lines 272, 284, 296, 374, 375, 461, 514, 589, 649, 654, 686, 687, 844 and 852. git blame attributes 11 to 39913c5 and 3 to cd11c6a, both dispatched-worker commits from 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-17, neither of them central's.

~/.claude/CLAUDE.md puts READMEs squarely in frank-writing's scope, and the skill is absolute on both marks: never an em dash, never a semicolon.

THE SEARCH THIS CLAIM NAMES. Swept: every tracked file except docs/ (generated) and puzzles/ (v1), and the 7 markdown files at depth 2 of the delivered tree. NOT discriminated prose from code in the other delivered hits, so these four are counts and not yet defects: tla-practice/README.md 1 and 1, REACTIONS.md 1 em dash, attempts/LOG-TEMPLATE.md 2, drill/SHEET.md 24 semicolons which are probably PlusCal statement terminators. drill/README.md is clean at 0 and 0.

THE WIDER COUNT, for scope rather than as a list of defects: 2,742 lines carry an em dash over 123 tracked files. 918 of them are in sources/, which is quoted corpus material and not Frank's prose at all. 609 are in harness/, which the global CLAUDE.md does cover, since code comments count as prose. 467 are at the root in the planning documents.

SO THE RULING IS WHERE THE WORK IS. Three candidate scopes, smallest first:
1  recall/README.md alone, 14 sites, which is the one file that is both delivered and verified prose.
2  plus the delivered tree's other four files, once somebody reads the 28 remaining hits and says which are prose.
3  plus harness/ comments, 609 lines, which is a different size of job.

NO GATE EXISTS FOR ANY OF IT. grep over harness/ and scripts/ finds no check on either mark, and the comment gate does not look for them. Loom's gate-don't-advise convention says a correctness invariant should not depend on anybody remembering, and 'never an em dash' is as mechanical as a check gets. A one-line gate over scope 1 would hold whatever is cleaned, and it would have caught both worker commits.

Files: recall/README.md, harness/comment-gate.sh (optional), scripts/test (optional)
notes:
CENTRAL 2026-10-20, a fresh measurement and a fourth question, folded in from tla-576z which is closed as a duplicate of this.

Re-measured at 64c0db2, counting OCCURRENCES rather than lines: 677 em dashes across 45 files under harness/, and 14 files under scripts/ carry at least one. The bead's 609 lines in harness/ and this 677 are the same finding counted two ways.

THE FOURTH QUESTION, which this bead does not ask and should. Scope 3 assumes the rule covers harness comments. It does, on the current wording: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md says code comments count as prose, a comment explaining an invariant is writing, and it is read by people. But if the answer is that the rule is about prose a reader outside the repo sees, then CLAUDE.md needs the carve-out written into it, because the next worker will ask again. The tla-fkqs worker did ask, on 2026-10-20: it edited one assertion message in harness/test-spelling.sh and deliberately left the em dash in, because every sibling message in that file uses the same punctuation and changing one would make it diverge. That was right for a worker and it is the wrong state for the repo.

So there are three readings and the bead should pick one:
1 the rule covers these and the sweep happens, which is 677 sites and not a sed, because an em dash inside a pattern or a fixture is data rather than prose
2 the rule covers prose a reader outside the repo sees, these are internal, and CLAUDE.md says so from now on
3 the rule covers them and the sweep is not worth it, which retires the expectation along with the work

AND NOTHING GATES ANY OF IT. harness/test-spelling.sh reads British spellings only and scripts/lint is shellcheck. Whatever the ruling, the gate question is separate and worth answering in the same sitting, because an unenforced rule in CLAUDE.md is how this got to 677.

title: Measure whether hint.md's new rationale earns its prompt tokens
description:
Read a real hint prompt and decide whether hint.md's rationale earns its
tokens.

tla-1sh7.1 grew drill/study/.claude/commands/hint.md from 85 to 121 lines, and
about 30 of those are the argument for why the tiebreak points at flat. The
whole file is now cat'd into every hint prompt, on top of PROMPT.md, the
checker's output and every attempt file.

The ordering is probably fine: the operative rule and "Classify before the
first word" both precede the rationale. But nobody has looked at a real
assembled hint prompt, and the worker that wrote it said so rather than
assuming.

WHAT TO DO. Assemble one hint prompt for a real item with a real attempt,
measure its size, and read it the way the one-shot does. Then answer one
question: does the rationale change the classification, or does it only
explain a rule the model would have followed anyway? If the second, move it to
a comment block the runner skips, or to CLAUDE.md, and keep the prompt to the
operative text.

Do not cut it on size alone. The reason the rationale is there is that the old
tiebreak survived in the file for a day and fired every time, and a rule with
no argument behind it is the kind that gets reverted by the next person who
finds it surprising.

title: mutate() reports a failed mutation through stdout, so a command substitution captures the FAIL text as a path
description:
Files: harness/test-drill-runner.sh

MEASURED 2026-10-14 in tla-rzvk.2, in that suite's own RED transcript.

`mutate()` signals a failed mutation by calling `nope`, which prints to
stdout. Callers capture the function with `M7=$(mutate ...)` expecting a
path, so on failure the variable holds the FAIL text instead, and the next
`mk_tree` dies with `cp: cannot stat '  FAIL  ...'`.

It bit all eight mutants equally and it FAILS SAFE: the control row reddens
too, so a broken mutation cannot read as a passing one. That is why the
tla-rzvk.2 worker left it alone rather than widening its footprint, which was
the right call.

Worth fixing anyway, because the symptom points at `cp` rather than at the
mutation that did not apply, and someone will spend a while on the wrong file.
The fix is to send `nope` to stderr in this path, or to have `mutate` return
nonzero and let the caller check, rather than to pass a sentinel through
stdout.

Check whether the same `nope`-to-stdout-inside-a-command-substitution shape
exists in the other harness suites before fixing just this one.
close_reason: Merged on main 2026-10-20, worker commit from the tla-yxjn worktree. CLOSED AS ALREADY FIXED, by bead tla-vo5l on 2026-10-16 at worker commit 8ccd384, one day after this bead was filed on the same file and the same shape. mutate() lands the path in a global and the verdict in the return code, and all eleven call sites read 'if mutate ...; then'. The worker proved it rather than reading the close reason: it reconstructed the pre-fix guard inside today's file, broke M5's sed so it matched nothing, and measured both sides. Before, 402 passed and rc 0 identical to a clean run, with both M5 control rows passing over a mutant that was never built and one claiming rc=127 for a mutation whose point is to exit 9, because the variable held the FAIL text so no runner was ever copied. After, 400 passed 1 failed rc 1. That also settles why stderr would have been the wrong fix: nope on stderr still increments fail_count inside a subshell and the increment still dies with it, so routing the message is not the bug and the live subshell is. THE SWEEP IS THE DELIVERABLE: 151 tracked shell files selected by shebang against the 82 of the 2026-10-17 pass, reporter list derived from the tree rather than guessed, 152 non-reporter functions calling one, and mutate the only name appearing in a command substitution anywhere, both hits being the comments about the old defect. harness/test-recall-runner.sh was the worse case with M1=$(mutate ...) || M1='' and was fixed under tla-w91v. Three surfaces the sweep does not read were measured rather than named: indirect callers at one hop, backtick capture, and subshells that are not captures. No live site anywhere. A reporter reached through three hops would still slip past. What changed is two comments, both the bead's own defect class: the header said 'Eleven mutants:' over a list of ten in a suite that gates that exact failure in drill.sh's help text three times, and the M5 preamble said 'the other four' when there are eleven. Filed tla-8jlx: nothing gates this shape and an advisory is what let it sit in a second file. Verified: 402 assertions rc 0 unchanged, pipefail 25, spelling 20, lint clean over 146.

title: The delivered drill README has no source in the repo, so it is not reproducible
description:
Found by the tla-s5iz worker, 2026-10-13. ~/tla-practice/drill/README.md was written by hand by central on 2026-10-12. drill/ in this repo carries no README, so scripts/deliver-drill.sh does not deliver one, and the delivered file survives only because the script never deletes anything.

So the practice tree holds a file with no upstream. A second delivery into a fresh tree would land 32 prompts and no README, and nobody would notice until a reader opened a directory of bare PROMPT.md files with nothing explaining what they are or what was withheld.

WHAT THE DELIVERED README SAYS, which is why it matters: how to work an item, that ANSWER.md and META.md and verify/ stayed behind and where to find them, the four families, the construct list at drill/COLD-LIST.md, and which fluency channels do not exist yet. The last of those is already stale, since the reading channel now exists.

THE DECISION. Either add drill/README.md to the repo and have deliver-drill.sh deliver it, or accept that the practice tree's README is hand-maintained and say so somewhere. The first is the recommendation, because the delivered copy is already out of date and a hand-maintained file drifts by construction.

If it becomes a delivered file, note that it is the one delivered thing that is NOT a PROMPT.md, so the manifest and the shape assertion both need a decision: a README at drill/ root is one level above item depth, so it does not touch the four-entry rule.

Files: drill/README.md, scripts/deliver-drill.sh, harness/test-deliver-drill.sh

RED: GIVEN an empty destination WHEN scripts/deliver-drill.sh runs THEN the delivered tree carries a README explaining what was withheld and where it lives.
notes:
SOURCE WRITTEN 2026-10-13 in aafb94a, WIRING STILL OPEN. Scope widened to both
channels, because completion/ had the same gap in a worse form.

WHAT IS DONE. drill/README.md and completion/README.md now exist in the repo.
The drill one is the hand-written delivered text with two corrections: its
closing section said the reading and completion channels did not exist, which
is false as of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13, and it called drill/COLD-LIST.md 105
lines when the file is 112 of which 105 are constructs.

completion/README.md is new. Nine items landed in the practice tree on
2026-10-13 with no index at all and nothing stating the three-run contract
outside each item's own PROMPT.md.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the whole point of the bead. Neither delivery script
delivers either file. Both find items with a fixed-depth glob over
<family>/<NN>-<slug>, and a channel README sits one level above that, so it is
not an item and nothing picks it up. Measured: scripts/deliver-completion.sh's
manifest is PROMPT_NAME, EXPECT_NAME and WORK_NAME, and grep for README in
either script returns nothing.

THE WORK. Add a channel-README step to scripts/deliver-drill.sh and
scripts/deliver-completion.sh, delivering <channel>/README.md to the
destination root when the source has one, under the same never-overwrite rule
as everything else. Then extend harness/test-deliver-drill.sh and
harness/test-deliver-completion.sh.

WATCH THE COUNTS. Both suites assert the manifest total as a number, including
over the real tree. harness/test-deliver-completion.sh:1021 asserts
'<REAL_MANIFEST> file(s) to land' and :623 asserts the landed line. Adding one
file to the manifest moves those, and whether they are derived or hardcoded
decides how much changes. Check before editing.

ALSO. The delivered ~/tla-practice/drill/README.md is the OLD text, with the
stale channels section and the wrong line count. Delivery never overwrites, so
re-running the script will skip it and the practice tree keeps the stale copy.
That is the repair-after-delivery problem tla-oa0m is open about, and it needs
Frank's call rather than a script that overwrites his tree.

Files: drill/README.md, completion/README.md, scripts/deliver-drill.sh, scripts/deliver-completion.sh, harness/test-deliver-drill.sh, harness/test-deliver-completion.sh
THE DESIGN POINT THAT UNBLOCKS THE STALE-COPY HALF. The never-overwrite rule
is currently global, and it does not need to be. It exists because
work/Claims.tla, a learner's attempt and an attempt log are the only copy of
work that has no git behind it. A channel README holds none of that. It is
generated content whose source is now in the repo, so overwriting it loses
nothing.

So the rule wants to be per file class rather than per script: refuse to
overwrite anything the learner could have edited, and refresh anything the repo
is the source of truth for. That distinction is also what tla-oa0m needs, and
it is a smaller question than 'can a delivered chapter be repaired' because a
README has no attempt history mixed into it.

I am not making that change without Frank, because it is a rule about writing
over his tree and he has lost 39 delivered files to a guessed manifest once
already. But the argument above is the one to put to him.

HALF OF THIS BEAD IS NOW SETTLED, 2026-10-14, and the other half got sharper.

SETTLED: never-overwrite is PER FILE CLASS, not universal. Frank's drill-runner
request forced it, because three classes wanted three policies and
scripts/deliver-drill.sh now implements all three:

  PROMPT.md       never overwrite
  the runner      ALWAYS overwrite, because a fix has to reach him
  PROGRESS.tsv    never written by the delivery script at all

Landed with bead tla-t9de. The reasoning is in deliver-drill.sh's header, because
an overwrite path in a script whose header promises it never overwrites is a trap
otherwise.

STILL OPEN, AND NOW MEASURED: should PROMPT.md be refreshable?

  15 of 64 delivered prompts differ from the repo    cmp over all 64
  49 are identical

Most of the 15 are today's spelling normalisation. TWO ARE CONTENT FIXES and they
are the reason this matters:

  sequences/07-pneumatic-tube   the delivered copy still says "you'll find the
                                tube on its own doesn't hold enough to say it,
                                and you'll have to add what it needs", the
                                telegraph tla-0yis removed. It lacks the
                                published 129 that replaced it.
  modules/07-the-hoist-and-the-crates   the delivered copy still defines
                                RECURSIVE in question 1 with only the keyword
                                removed.

So Frank's practice tree serves the telegraphed version of two drills whose
telegraphs were removed today, and under never-overwrite it always will.

THE RISK OF REFRESHING IS ZERO TODAY AND WILL NOT STAY ZERO. Measured: every one
of the 64 delivered item directories holds ONLY PROMPT.md, so there is no work to
lose. But drill/README.md tells him to "write the module and its config from
scratch, in the item's own directory", so item directories WILL hold his specs
once he starts grinding. Note that overwriting PROMPT.md would not touch those
files even then. The only thing a refresh can destroy is an annotation he made to
the prompt itself.

RECOMMENDATION: a --refresh-prompts flag on deliver-drill.sh, off by default, that
overwrites PROMPT.md and nothing else, reports every file it replaced, and still
has no delete path. Default stays never-overwrite so an ordinary delivery cannot
clobber anything. Needs a test and a line in the header's three-class block.

DO NOT HAND-COPY THE 15. The rule is to use the delivery scripts, and a guessed
manifest deleted 39 delivered files on 2026-10-02.

A verified backup was taken today before the runner delivery:
~/tla-practice-backups/tla-practice-20261014-162103.tar.gz, 1368 entries both
sides, archive reads clean.

ALSO STILL OPEN HERE: drill/README.md and completion/README.md are not delivered
by any script. The delivered ~/tla-practice/drill/README.md got there by some
other route, is 2003 bytes against the repo's 2440, and still says "32 blank-page
drills, four families" against 64 in eight. It also says nothing about the runner,
which is now a file in that directory. Filed separately as tla-nc6f.

Run against ~/tla-practice behind a verified backup at tla-practice-20261014-165225.tar.gz: 15 replaced, 49 left alone, 0 of 64 now stale, nothing leaked, and the learner's LAST-SERVED untouched. title: The census carries a known false positive on a line that denies a skip
description:
harness/drill-gate.sh:1924 reads

  echo "A CACHED JOB IS VERIFIED, not skipped: same TLC build, same verdict.sh, same"

That line is a FALSE POSITIVE in harness/test-indeterminate.sh's census: it
matches SKIP_VOCAB on the word "skipped" while the sentence DENIES a skip.

It is harmless today. tla-ocpw registered drill-gate.sh on the strength of
its real --static-only admission at :1922, so the census's verdict no longer
rests on this line. What remains is a detector carrying a known false match,
which makes the next reader of that output do the same analysis again.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN tla-ocpw, and this is the part worth reading.
harness/test-drill.sh asserts the literal string at TWO sites:

  harness/test-drill.sh:399    "A CACHED JOB IS VERIFIED, not skipped"
  harness/test-drill.sh:1308   "A CACHED JOB IS VERIFIED, not skipped"

The word "skipped" sits INSIDE the asserted substring, so no rewording of the
gate removes the ERE match while leaving those assertions true. tla-ocpw's
Files: line did not carry harness/test-drill.sh, so its worker reported the
conflict rather than reaching outside its footprint. That was the right call.

So this bead carries BOTH files, which is the only way the change is
coherent. Reword the echo and the two assertions in one commit.

Pick wording that says the same thing without a SKIP_VOCAB phrase. "passed
over" and "re-run" are both available. Then confirm with the suite's own ERE
that drill-gate.sh has no remaining match other than :1922's deliberate one:

  grep -nEi -- 'skipped|did not run|could not run|never ran|was not looked for|could not be assessed|unavailable|was not checked|was not run' harness/drill-gate.sh

Files: harness/drill-gate.sh, harness/test-drill.sh

RED: GIVEN main's tree WHEN the indeterminate census scans
harness/drill-gate.sh THEN its only SKIP_VOCAB match is the deliberate
--static-only admission, and harness/test-drill.sh still reads 0 failed. A
detector carrying a known false match is the defect; one quieted by deleting
the assertion that pinned the string is the worse fix.

title: Four hazards central briefed to eight authors did not reproduce
description:
Recorded so the next brief does not repeat them. All four were central's claims, all four were refuted by an author that measured rather than believed, and two were refuted twice independently.

1. rc 255 ON A CROSS-TYPE COMPARISON. Central told every author that a string used where a model value belongs aborts TLC at rc 255. It does not. The control-state author measured string labels at rc 0 and 'Idle' /= Idle against an untyped model value at rc 0. The state-space author measured a model value against a string and against a number, both rc 0. The 255 that IS reachable is SYMMETRY over strings.

2. THE PANGRAM SPECIMEN COUNT. Central said three of the seven delivered problems carry a PlusCal translation. It is two of seven. And across the whole delivered tree 34 of 44 PlusCal specs DO carry pc, because the exercise starters are multi-label, so central's claim that Frank has never met a multi-label algorithm was wrong. He has read 34. He has never WRITTEN explicit control state in raw TLA+, which is the accurate statement and is still the gap.

title: spike-measure.sh cannot tell a useful liveness counterexample from a useless one
description:
Reported by the tla-83lg worker and by the tla-pmm2.2 spike author independently, and the tla-83lg worker argued it is a FEATURE bead rather than part of that bugfix. Central agrees.

THE GAP. For a liveness obligation, spike-measure.sh's distinct-count and depth columns are the same whether the counterexample is informative or not. The tla-pmm2.2 spike measured both its runs at 21 distinct and depth 12. The signal is the TRACE, not the row.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF tla-83lg. Nothing in the strip or tally touches it. The fix is a NEW column rather than a corrected one, and it needs a design call that bead's RED does not contain: whether spike-measure.sh starts invoking -dumpTrace, which changes its TLC invocation and its cost, and what the new column actually says.

PRIOR ART IN THIS REPO, and it is liftable. harness/refinement.sh ALREADY parses -dumpTrace JSON through python3 to tell an initial-state probe violation from genuine movement. .claude/project-constitution.md records that parsing as the reason python3 is a sanctioned secondary runtime at all, and the reason is the same one here: the alternative is scraping TLC's console text, which V2-PLAN.md section 5.1 forbids.

ONE HAZARD THE DESIGN MUST ACCOUNT FOR, measured under tla-0igq today. TLC 2026.07.31.184830's -dumpTrace json writer IGNORES a cfg's ALIAS on the LIVENESS path while honouring it for safety. So a liveness trace read through that channel carries RAW variable names. Filed upstream as tla-1bnm. Any column built on the dumped liveness trace must not assume aliased fields.

WHAT A USEFUL COLUMN MIGHT SAY, as a starting point rather than a decision: the action-name sequence and its length are present and readable on liveness traces, measured as '2 steps: Advance -> Recycle' against '1 steps: UnnamedAction'. A trace whose only action is unnamed is the useless shape.

title: Rule 10 of the fencing statement is right today and wrong once the restart variant lands
description:
The fencing statement's rule 10 says the storage service rejects a write whose number is
lower than the number on a write it has already accepted, so it accepts an equal number.
Fenced.tla rejects an equal number.

Today they cannot be told apart. FencedGE.tla is rule 10 word for word and measures
identically to Fenced.tla, rc 0 at 74 states, because the lock service never issues a
number twice.

They diverge under token reuse. With a lock service that can lose its counter, strict
comparison passes at 284 states and the off-by-one fails at 126.

The spike called that restart variant the best sub-problem in the set, so it is likely to
be built. The day it is, rule 10 becomes the wrong rule and a learner following it
faithfully writes the bug.

Nothing to fix now. The statement as delivered is correct and the check found no defect.
This is a note to whoever extends the problem: rule 10 has to change in the same commit
that adds the restart, not after.

title: Level 5 in the manifest is the softest column, and one reader scored it differently
description:
Six readers assigned levels across the corpus, one slice each. One of them scored a merged
system at level 5 whenever any member module carried an INSTANCE composed into a checked
theorem, even where the base module alone read lower. That reader flagged the choice. The
other five did not say either way.

So level 5 may be reporting the family rather than the system on some rows, and the 45 rows
sitting there are not all decided on the same rule.

The fix is not a re-run. It is to state the rule, then check the level 5 rows against it,
which is cheap because each row carries the file:line its call was made on. My read is that
the rule should follow the learner's experience: if the problem hands over the base module
alone then the base module's shape is what the learner meets.

title: [bug] The pre-commit hook re-exports issues.jsonl after staging, so every bd commit leaves the tree dirty
description:
Seen three times in one session, 2026-09-04, on commits acf62c0, 81db919 and 5fae1cc. The sequence: git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl, git commit, the hook runs bd hooks run pre-commit and re-exports, and the export differs from what was staged. git status shows M .beads/issues.jsonl again. Committing that leftover produces the same thing once more.

The diff is memory rows changing order (5fae1cc's leftover: 11 insertions, 11 deletions, every line a _type memory row). So two exports of the same state aren't byte-identical, and the hook's export races the staged one.

I think the fix is one of two. Either the hook stages what it exports (a git add after the export, inside the hook), or bd sorts memory rows on export. The second is upstream. The first is a line in .git/hooks/pre-commit and is what I'd try first.

Until then every bd: commit leaves a dirty tree. The dispatched-agents rule already tells workers to leave it, which is fine in a worktree that dies. On main it's a standing false signal in git status, and it's what made me commit twice tonight for one change.

The assertion counts are the harder half, because `scripts/test` does not aggregate one. That is the same reason `.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md` dropped its total on 2026-08-28 rather than hand-counting a new one.

title: grade.sh crashes on rc=75/76/77 instead of grading the submission INVALID
description:
`grade.sh`'s `classify` (`:389-405`) routes 150, 151, 255 and 124 to INVALID on the submission
phase, but lets 75, 76 and 77 fall through to `die_harness`.

Those three are learner-facing. `verdict.sh`'s header (bead `tla-i9m`) records them as SPEC_EVAL_
FAILURE, SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE and LIVENESS_EVAL_FAILURE — "the spec could not be evaluated". A
submission whose observation record has the wrong shape is a learner error, not a harness fault.

Measured: a submission defining `Observe == [hue |-> colour]` against a reference whose obligations
read `o.level` gives `HARNESS ERROR: reference obligation 1: unexpected verdict rc=75`, exit 4.

So the grader crashes instead of grading. Exit 4 is HARNESS_ERROR, which tells a learner nothing
and tells whoever is running the batch that the harness is broken when it is not.

75 is also a family rather than a single cause — four EC constants route to it, recorded during
the `tla-i9m` work — so the INVALID message should say the spec did not evaluate rather than
guessing why.

Found by the `tla-x8s` agent.

close_reason:
Merged as 55c85fa (work commit b71ec34), plus af93ed2 for Gate.tla. Design captured in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_89795ff4c47c0358e2ea81e9.

A structureless spec — one variable, any permitted value at any time, no transitions, no causality — passed with zero witnesses against the shipped reference, and its operator was entirely honest, so this was never about lying. Root cause: every obligation was a single-state predicate, and no single-state predicate can constrain a transition relation. References may now state Step_*(o,p) obligations judged as a boxed action subscripted on Observe and declared PROPERTY. The _Observe subscript closes tla-nyrb's atomicity direction by construction. The frozen-operator trapdoor inside that fix is gated by a three-layer landmark check rather than a header note.

Four smaller defects landed with it: REPO_ROOT resolved from the caller's cwd so grading inside another repo ran that repo's verdict channel; rc=75/76/77 crashed the grader instead of grading the submission INVALID; the constants fragment went in unvalidated; and a selftest helper hardcoded one problem's directories. 58 assertions to 86.

title: §5.6's hand procedure dirties the .cfg it is checking
description:
§5.6 describes the PlusCal gate as "re-run `pcal` after commenting and require the TRANSLATION
block byte-identical". Followed literally, in the directory holding the artifact, that dirties the
`.cfg`: `pcal` prepends `\* Add statements after this line.` to it. Measured during the pilot's
step 7, md5 `a3c92eb6…` before and `0616a66c…` after.

For a frozen artifact that is a write to a file under hash. The pilot's freeze survived only
because the gate was run on copies.

**`harness/comment-gate.sh` already gets this right** — it stages copies, and running it against
the frozen pair leaves `sha256sum -c FREEZE.sha256` clean. So this is a documentation gap, not a
harness bug. The plan describes a procedure more dangerous than the component that implements it,
and a reader who follows the plan by hand corrupts what they are checking.

Fix: §5.6 should say the re-translation runs on a copy, and point at `comment-gate.sh` rather than
describing a hand procedure that nobody should run.

Found running the tla-kl5.11 pilot, step 7, by the comment-pass agent.

title: cd "" succeeds, so the || exit guard on REPO_ROOT does not close the hazard
description:
Six suites open with `REPO_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` and then `cd "$REPO_ROOT"`.
`tla-5r7` added `|| exit 1` to close SC2164, which handles a cd that fails.

It does not handle the case that actually happens. If `git rev-parse` fails, `REPO_ROOT` is the
empty string, and `cd ""` returns 0 without moving. So the guard passes and the suite runs from
whatever directory it was invoked in.

Cheap to close with an emptiness guard on `REPO_ROOT` before the cd. Reported by the `tla-5r7`
worker as out of scope for a lint bead, which it was.

title: T54 teaches INSTANCE without WITH — the idiom the v2 harness refuses
description:
`puzzles/T54-refinement-concrete-spec/README.md:118` and `:150` teach:

    L0 == INSTANCE AbstractCard        \* no WITH clause yet -- variable names match
    Refines == L0!Spec

**The spec is not wrong.** The variable names do match, so the implicit same-name substitution is
the mapping the author intended, and TLC verifies it. This is not a bug report against T54's
correctness.

**The problem is that it normalizes an idiom the v2 harness refuses.** V2-PLAN.md §5.4 lists
omitting `WITH` as a verified trap: the substitution is silent, and when names DON'T line up it
yields a different, usually wrong mapping that still passes. `harness/refinement.sh` (tla-kl5.7)
therefore returns `IMPLICIT_MAPPING` / rc=25 for exactly this shape — so a learner who followed
T54's own worked example and submitted it to the v2 harness would be refused, by teaching
material this repo ships.

The parenthetical "(no WITH clause yet — variable names match)" shows the author knew the
substitution was implicit and relied on it deliberately. That is precisely the habit worth not
teaching: it works until the names diverge, and then it fails silently.

OPTIONS, needs a decision rather than a default:
  (a) Rewrite T54 to state the mapping explicitly (`WITH card <- card, ...`) and add a sentence
      on why explicitness matters even when names match. Smallest change, keeps the puzzle.
  (b) Keep the implicit form and add a callout naming the hazard, so the learner meets the trap
      with a warning attached rather than as a silent norm.
  (c) Leave it. T54 is v1 and v2 replaces the curriculum, so it may not be worth touching.

(c) is defensible ONLY if v1 is genuinely retired. Until then this repo publishes a worked example
that its own new harness rejects, and the v1 site is still live.

CONTEXT: found by tla-kl5.7's corpus-validation pass over the 7 refinement puzzles on main.
5 returned REFINES; T58-refinement-debugging returns REFINEMENT_VIOLATED **by design** — its
README is about reading a refinement-violation trace, so that one is correct and needs nothing.

acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded on (a)/(b)/(c); if (a) or (b), T54 updated and the v2 harness no longer refuses its own worked example.
