title: Report the three TLAiBench harness defects (and the frozen-mapping trapdoor) upstream
description:
The tla-kl5.3 survey of github.com/tlaplus/TLAiBench (MIT, single-author, HEAD 742cfd5) turned
up three real defects while reading the harness. Full evidence is in
drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_6251f5ad5930c77a531e9917 §9. We benefited from reading their code;
reporting what we found is the reciprocal move, and one of the three makes the benchmark's
headline capability not work at all.

THE THREE:

1. The GenAIScript driver NEVER CHECKS THE FULL REFINEMENT. genaisrc/translate.genai.mts:150-152
   passes traceRefFile/traceCfgFile — the STAGE-1 files — to phase 6's three checks.
   refTLAFile/refCFGFile are declared at :132-133 and appear once more inside a prompt string at
   :137, never in a check.
2. Copy-pasted error guards in the same file (:111, :141) test `synthesize` instead of
   `traceRefinement` / `fullRefinement`, so a failed refinement synthesis goes undetected.
3. The Python port fixes (1) and then cannot pass: translate.py:1042-1053 correctly uses
   ref_tla_file/ref_cfg_file, but asserts Gold!Stats (diameter=7 — the TRACE stage's number) on a
   full state space whose diameter is 8. Verified: a CORRECT refinement mapping is rejected at
   rc=10.

Joint consequence, worth stating in the issue: the full-refinement stage appears never to have
passed end-to-end for DieHard — unexercised in one driver, unsatisfiable in the other.

WORTH RAISING SEPARATELY, and more interesting than the bugs: the benchmark has the
FROZEN-MAPPING TRAPDOOR open. A refinement module with `WITH big <- 0, small <- 0` passes both
the plain check and Gold!Refinement at rc=0. Since the LLM under test authors its own refinement
module AND its own .cfg, a model emitting a constant mapping scores a pass. The fix is cheap and
we have it working: name the mapped expression, assert as an ordinary INVARIANT that it never
leaves its initial value, and require TLC to VIOLATE it — a passing probe is a failing
refinement check.

LANE: --issue-only is probably right to start. The diameter fix is one character but the right
number depends on their intent for the two stages, which is undocumented — so ask rather than
PR a guess. The trapdoor finding is a design conversation, not a patch.

PRIVACY: redact everything project-specific. Nothing about v2, the curriculum, Frank, or this
repo goes upstream. The findings stand entirely on their own evidence.

Files: (none in this repo — output is an upstream issue)

AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: needs-decision — filing publicly under Frank's name needs his sign-off first.
acceptance_criteria: Findings reviewed by Frank, redacted of project specifics, and filed as an upstream issue; watch-bead spawned.

title: Stage 6 §8.5 — final screening sweep over every shipped problem
description:
Goal: re-run §5.7 over EVERY shipped problem, by MECHANISM as well as by name.

Why it runs again at the end: problems authored months apart drift, and a mechanism that was
clear when batch 1 was written may have been published in the interval. The screen is cheap; a
burned problem shipped is not.

Also re-run §5.7b at STATEMENT level. §5.7b says explicitly that passing once does not immunize a
domain, because the same domain yields a puzzle or a system depending on how the statement is
worded — and statements get revised between batches under §7.1.

Re-skin burned problems STRUCTURALLY, not nominally (§2.1 S1). Renaming snowcats to bookshelves
changes nothing if the structure is identical — that is the v1 lesson verbatim.

title: Stage 6 §8.1 — coverage audit, and it runs LAST
description:
Goal: enumerate learntla core constructs, find the uncovered ones, and add AT MOST 2-3 problems.
Four of the 60 are already reserved for exactly this (§2.1).

§3.1 IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THIS BEAD: COVERAGE IS AN END-OF-RUN AUDIT, NEVER THE PROBLEM-LIST
GENERATOR. Organizing by construct produces problems whose purpose is "this one exercises CHOOSE",
which is contrived by construction — and is how v1 failed one level up. DO NOT LET THE AUDIT
RESHAPE THE SET. If the audit wants to add more than three problems, that is a signal to question
the audit, not the set.

Audit which CELLS of the §2.1 grid are filled as well as which constructs are hit. The cell audit
is the one that keeps §3.1 honest — construct coverage is the metric that seduces you back into
v1's failure mode.

Record what was left uncovered and why. No silent caps.

Files: (the assembled set — outside this repo)

title: Stage 6 §8.2-3 — interleave ordering and back-load pure TLA+
description:
Goal: two ordering rules applied to the finished set.

INTERLEAVE (§8.2, §3.4). Never consecutive problems of one idiom. Interleave confusable
near-neighbours: invariant vs inductive invariant · type invariant vs safety property · WF vs SF ·
[]<> vs <>[] · refinement mapping vs auxiliary variable · atomicity split at the read vs at the
write. The §2.1 grid makes this CHECKABLE rather than a judgment call — walking diagonally means
no two consecutive problems share a situation OR a task shape.
Evidence: preregistered cluster RCT, 54 classes, unannounced test one month later — interleaved
61% vs blocked 38%, d=0.83. Mechanism, verbatim: "interleaved practice requires students to
choose a strategy and not merely execute a strategy."

BACK-LOAD PURE TLA+ (§8.3). ~25 of 60, concentrated in the FINAL THIRD so there is a real
transition rather than a sprinkle. Column F is inherently pure TLA+ (8); back-load ~17 more across
A/B/D. Include a few problems only natural in pure TLA+ — refinement mappings, non-algorithmic
system contracts.
This must NOT become "all PlusCal, then all TLA+": that is blocked practice at the coarsest grain
(§3b), and it means hitting ~25 consecutive problems in an unfamiliar notation months after last
reading the material.

Files: (the assembled set — outside this repo)

RED: INVARIANT: no two consecutive problems in the final ordering share a situation (S1-S9) or a
task shape (A-F).
acceptance_criteria: Final ordering satisfies the no-two-consecutive invariant mechanically; ~25 pure-TLA+ problems concentrated in the final third.

title: Add forward-reference + data-structure-introduction principles to QUALITY_GATE.md rule 2
description:
Goal: Document the two methodological principles locked during the tla-0w8.1 audit (2026-05-06) so future puzzle authors and audits have a clear standard.

Audit findings: drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_45aa23d4d99a54513e81d6d0
Tribal fact: bd remember qg-rule-2-audit-principle-locked-2026-05-06

Principle 1 — Forward-reference allowed for advanced concepts:
A puzzle MAY use an advanced TLA+ construct in passing (check-only forward reference) without violating Gate 2 IF the construct gets formal treatment in a later puzzle. Example: T03 uses <>(...) in its Check section; <> is formally introduced in T42. T03 passes Gate 2 because the forward reference resolves.
Limitation: forward-reference does NOT apply when the construct is required by the puzzle's solution (would be smuggling), only when it appears in checks/asides.

Principle 2 — Strict vs Pragmatic Gate 2 (data-structure introduction = one concept):
- Introduce a NEW data structure with all essential ops (T09 records: constructor+dot+EXCEPT; T10 sequences: literal+Append+Head+Tail+Len) → PASS as ONE concept (pragmatic reading; the structure itself is the concept).
- Add more ops to an EXISTING data structure (T11 \o+SubSeq added to sequences from T10; T22 IF-expr+CASE added to existing expression language) → REVISE — split into two concepts (strict reading).

Touches:
- QUALITY_GATE.md — add principles as clarifications under section 2 (Minimal Novelty); reference the 2026-05-06 audit as source.

Acceptance:
- QUALITY_GATE.md text updated.
- Cross-reference to drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_45aa23d4d99a54513e81d6d0 included.
- No code changes; pure documentation.

title: File upstream bd issue: flip export.path and export.git-add defaults
description:
The bd CLI ships with `export.path=issues.jsonl` (bare relative filename) and `export.git-add=true` defaults. The combination causes the secondary export pipeline to write /issues.jsonl at the repo root and stage it via low-level plumbing (git update-index --add --cacheinfo) that bypasses .gitignore. Three projects have hit this: liza_base (2026-04-29 ROOT CAUSE TRACED + RESOLVED), tla-puzzles (2026-05-05 tla-8ed canonical fix applied), loom (2026-05-04 loom-bm2 worktree-bypass workaround). Each project has applied the local config flip `bd config set export.git-add false` rather than waiting on upstream. File an upstream issue against the beads project (https://github.com/steveyegge/beads or wherever the bd CLI lives) asking that the defaults flip to (a) export.path=.beads/issues.jsonl (canonical path) and (b) export.git-add=false. See drawer tla_puzzles/decisions tla-8ed close 2026-05-05 (drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_69a03cc034f2d6b195bd475b) and liza_base/findings ROOT CAUSE TRACED 2026-04-29 for the diagnosis.

Acceptance: upstream issue or PR filed; URL recorded in the closing drawer of this bead.

Fresh bd init reproducer is clean; 7 tla-puzzles commits made BEFORE the export.git-add=false flip in this session also showed no stray. Historical bug was real; current bd is not buggy.
